About

We estimate what a mining company is worth, then set that estimate against what its shares cost today. Every company is researched the same way, from its own public filings, against the same fifty-two questions. Where something cannot be measured we say so rather than fill the gap with a guess.

Share prices are taken from the exchange each company actually trades on, in the currency its valuation is written in, and only when the source states the date the price closed. If a price is older than we are comfortable with, the page holds back its verdict rather than show a judgement built on a stale number.

Nothing here is advice, and there are no target prices. No company pays to appear, pays for its rating, or sees its page before you do.

Register — companies

If your company is covered here and you believe a figure on your page is wrong, tell us and point us to the document that shows it. We will check it and, if you are right, correct the page and say what changed.

Two things we will not do, because the value of this service rests on them. We do not accept payment of any kind from a company we cover, for any reason. And we use only material that is already publicly filed, so that anything shaping an assessment can be checked by a reader against the same source. A private forecast, a management model or an unfiled projection will be read with interest and will not change a number on a page.

Within those limits, a company pointing us to a filing we have missed genuinely improves the assessment, and we would rather hear from you than not.

The gold industry's benchmark operator - record cash flows from a portfolio spanning Canada, Finland, Mexico and Australia, run with unusual consistency.

Company quality: High Quality - 2.1 (out of 10; 1 = best), Roster median 5.0

TRADING ABOVE ESTIMATED VALUE
Fair value US$135.94 per share at the dated spot case  ·  Share price US$145.27 - dated close 2026-07-31

Gap to fair value: -US$9.33 (-6.4%) - the gap closes, if it closes, at Detour and Malartic fill-the-mill work delivering; O3/Marban ounces entering plans (+2 yr (2028))
Cautious value US$117.45 at the same case (-19.2%) - published alongside, never hidden. The verdict keys to fair value.

Prior outside claims on production: royalties and streams. LIGHT (3.39% of bad-year margin) Royalties. OR Royalties and Gold Royalty Corp take about 5% of revenue at Canadian Malartic, and third parties take about 2% at Detour Lake — together roughly 3% of what the company would earn in a low-price year.

Connected on the Roster. An event at this company travels only along declared links, never sector-wide. These are the links we carry:

  • CNL - Collective Mining Ltd.: AEM holds equity in CNL. ownership event: value travels by attributable share, not by revenue
  • OR - OR Royalties Inc.: OR holds a royalty or stream over AEM. revenue event for the holder, margin event for the payer - the holder pays none of the costs

The Story

One paragraph in plain words: what the company is, what it owns, and the central finding. If you read nothing else, read this.

Decision summary: the sector's premium senior producer earns its multiple with evidence - above-budget production two quarters running (metric 14), record free cash flow and shareholder returns (metric 18), a fortress net-cash balance sheet (metric 17), better-than-replaced reserves (metric 34) and the deepest growth pipeline in the peer group (metrics 16, 30); the honest counterweights are the Barnat redesign production trim, the Nunavut consultation matter (metric 37), and a valuation that already sits almost exactly on its spot-gold model value (metric 21).

Where narrative text carries an older share price, the tables and the refreshed dated close above govern.

Three dates govern this page: the share price is the dated close shown above (2026-07-31); the evidence and estimated values are from this company's last full underwriting (2026-07-31), and change only when the company publishes something - each document's own date is listed under References; a daily event scan watches this company's filings and releases and queues a re-underwriting when one lands.

The Question the Thesis Hinges On

Single greatest company-specific uncertainty identified as the execution of the Hope Bay redevelopment: a positive investment decision was only made in May 2026, redevelopment capital is approximately US$2.4 billion, engineering is only ~62% complete, and first production is not expected before 2030 - a multi-year, multi-billion-dollar construction and ramp-up risk layered on top of ordinary gold-price and cost risk. This is a judgment call, not a public disclosure, and should be revisited as the project progresses.

The Full Underwriting Register - all 52 questions (tap to open)

The same 52 questions are asked of every company. Statuses: Complete = evidenced and scored; Not Available - Documented = the fact does not exist publicly and we say so; Stage-exempt = not applicable to this company type or stage. Figures not confirmed from a primary source are labeled SOFT.

3. Investment Committee decision summary [Complete · score 2 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Decision summary: the sector's premium senior producer earns its multiple with evidence - above-budget production two quarters running (metric 14), record free cash flow and shareholder returns (metric 18), a fortress net-cash balance sheet (metric 17), better-than-replaced reserves (metric 34) and the deepest growth pipeline in the peer group (metrics 16, 30); the honest counterweights are the Barnat redesign production trim, the Nunavut consultation matter (metric 37), and a valuation that already sits almost exactly on its spot-gold model value (metric 21).

4. Separate quality from valuation [Complete · score 1 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Workbook structurally separates Composite Rank from valuation/action on the OUTPUT sheet.

5. Capitalization-date integrity [Complete · score 3 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Capitalization coherent within one month of the valuation date: 500.04M shares outstanding (+0.16% in one year; 500,046,600 confirmed at December 2025), net cash of $3.27B company-reported at June 30, 2026, and a market reference of $153.86 (NYSE, July 2, 2026 print - the latest specific quote verified; the Q2 buyback average of ~$178.6 shows the intra-quarter range, and the 52-week band is $115.19-255.24); each date is named rather than blended.

7. Citation and traceability [Complete · score 2 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Every Complete/Partial row below has a public source noted; nothing invented.

9. Per-share denominator integrity [Complete · score 3 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Exact basic share count of 500,046,600 confirmed as of December 31, 2025 (Form 40-F cover), the same date as the capitalization figures used elsewhere in this workbook. Net dilution from equity compensation is separately shown to be minimal (metric 43).

10. Acquisition economics [Complete · score 3 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Acquisition economics assessed on delivered results, not promises: the March 2025 O3 Mining acquisition produced an initial declaration of 1.58 Moz of probable reserves at Marban by December 31, 2025 and slots directly into the Canadian Malartic fill-the-mill strategy (metric 16); the July 2026 Central Lapland (Finland) consolidation and a running program of strategic junior stakes (Cadillac Mines subscription July 23, 2026; a C$60M private placement) extend the same pattern - buying ounces adjacent to owned mills and infrastructure.

11. Reserve/resource movement bridge [Complete · score 3 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Full corporate reserve movement bridge for 2025 obtained: 3.0M oz mined and replaced from operating mines (Odyssey, Meliadine, LaRonde, Goldex, Fosterville, Macassa) plus initial Marban deposit declaration from the O3 Mining acquisition, netting to +2.1% to a record 55.4M oz. Source: Feb 12 2026 exploration/reserves release.

12. Principal uncertainty [Complete · score 1 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Single greatest company-specific uncertainty identified as the execution of the Hope Bay redevelopment: a positive investment decision was only made in May 2026, redevelopment capital is approximately US$2.4 billion, engineering is only ~62% complete, and first production is not expected before 2030 - a multi-year, multi-billion-dollar construction and ramp-up risk layered on top of ordinary gold-price and cost risk. This is a judgment call, not a public disclosure, and should be revisited as the project progresses.

13. Management guidance credibility [Complete · score 3 (of 10; 1 = best)]
2025 production of 3,447,367 oz landed above guidance midpoint; AISC of $1,339/oz (revised $1,313) came in slightly above top of guidance range. Guidance was largely delivered. Source: Q4/FY2025 results release, Feb 2026.

14. Mine-by-mine operating quality [Complete · score 2 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Mine-by-mine quality evidenced in current results: Q2 2026 payable production of 855,816 oz was above budget for the second consecutive quarter across the eleven-mine portfolio (LaRonde, Canadian Malartic, Goldex, Detour Lake, Macassa, Meadowbank, Meliadine, Kittila, Fosterville, Pinos Altos, La India); Kittila set all-time highs in mill throughput, revenue, operating margin and cash flow; Canadian Malartic produced 166,216 oz in Q1; and first-half unit costs per tonne declined versus 2025 - at a deepening underground complex, a genuine operating achievement.

15. Cost quality [Complete · score 3 (of 10; 1 = best)]
FY2025 total cash cost $979/oz, AISC $1,339/oz ($1,313 revised basis) - company describes this as peer-leading, though independent peer normalization not done here. Source: Q4/FY2025 results release.

16. Development-project underwriting [Complete · score 3 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Three material development projects reviewed with real, dated figures: Hope Bay (positive investment decision May 2026, PEA-based 400,000-435,000 oz/yr over an initial 11-year mine life, ~US$2.4B redevelopment capex, engineering ~62% complete, resource cut-off Aug 28 2025); Upper Beaver (exploration shaft sinking underway, evaluating 150,000-200,000 oz/yr); San Nicolas (JV with Teck, advancing feasibility). Source: company project-update releases, May 2026.

17. Balance-sheet resilience [Complete · score 2 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Net cash position of $2,670M at Dec 31 2025 (up from net debt $217M a year earlier), total debt only $196M, undrawn $2B credit facility, Moody's upgraded to A3 (Aug 2025). Strong balance sheet. Source: Q4/FY2025 results release; Moody's upgrade news.

18. Capital allocation [Complete · score 2 (of 10; 1 = best)]
$1.4B returned to shareholders in 2025 via dividends ($803M) and buybacks ($600M); dividend raised 12.5%; $950M debt repaid in the year; dividend paid every year since 1983. Source: Q4/FY2025 results release.

19. Run-rate normalization [Complete · score 3 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Run-rate normalized conservatively: 2026 production is guided to the LOW end of 3.3-3.5 Moz after the Barnat open-pit redesign - the model at metric 20 therefore uses 3.3 Moz, not the midpoint - while cost guidance is maintained (AISC midpoint ~$1,475 vs $1,459 actual in Q2, production costs $1,114/oz, total cash costs $1,054/oz), and the three-year profile rises with Malartic guided to 640,000-670,000 oz in 2027 and 720,000-750,000 oz in 2028.

20. Formal scenario architecture [Complete · score 2 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Five named pricing scenarios on the SCENARIOS sheet using the standard project gold deck ($2,600-$5,400), each producing a value per share and dollar-and-percentage gap to the reference price from a disclosed, calibration-checked assumption block; the multiple is named as the key soft input in its own label.

21. Valuation-to-action bridge [Complete · score 2 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Explicit bridge: at Current Spot the model returns ~$160 against the $153.86 reference - within about 4% - so the market is pricing AEM almost exactly on its spot-gold cash-generation value; the standard thresholds place this in Monitor/Accumulate, with the Buy case resting on the 2027-2033 growth pipeline (Malartic toward 1 Moz, Hope Bay from 2030, Detour underground, Upper Beaver) rather than on today's run-rate; the earlier $142-146 price note is superseded and recorded as such. REVISION (Aug 2, 2026): the deck's spot case has been corrected from a stale $4,850 - an early-2026 quote retained past its currency - to the actual July 31, 2026 gold price of $4,050. At the corrected spot the current-state reading is US$117.45 vs the US$153.86 price (-23.7%). This flips the pre-correction reading from modestly positive to negative: at true spot the market pays somewhat above the model. The SCENARIOS and CATALYST TIMELINE tables govern wherever any older narrative number differs.

22. Thesis-break framework [Complete · score 2 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Named, checkable break conditions: (1) mine-plan revisions of the Barnat type appearing at a second major asset; (2) escalation of the Nunavut Indigenous-consultation matter (metric 37) into permitting consequences for Meliadine, Meadowbank, or the newly approved Hope Bay build; (3) a break in the declining unit-cost trend that underpins the premium multiple; (4) a sustained gold retreat toward the Conservative case - the 52-week price band already demonstrates the stock's sensitivity; (5) growth-capital escalation at Hope Bay or the Malartic second shaft beyond disclosed ranges.

26. Peer-group methodology [Complete · score 2 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Disclosed peer set and criteria: senior gold producers above two million ounces with Americas-weighted portfolios - Newmont, Barrick, Kinross - with AEM's premium multiple versus that set justified (or not) by the jurisdiction profile at metric 27 and the cost trend at metric 19; royalty comparators (Franco-Nevada, Wheaton) are tracked separately as the multiple ceiling.

27. Jurisdiction, fiscal regime, and permitting [Complete · score 2 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Jurisdiction map current and concrete: Canada (Quebec, Ontario, Nunavut - with Hope Bay construction approval received May 2026), Finland (Kittila, plus the 2026 Central Lapland consolidation), Australia (Fosterville) and Mexico (Pinos Altos, La India) - among the strongest fiscal-stability profiles of any senior producer, with the Nunavut consultation matter (metric 37) as the named exception being actively managed.

28. Environmental liability, reclamation, closure, and tailings [Complete · score 3 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Environmental obligations documented at portfolio level: a standalone 2025 Tailings Summary Report with facility-by-facility disclosure (metric 56), governance described as aligned with industry standards, and 2025 GHG disclosure (metric 55); asset-level reclamation provision amounts were not pulled this pass (ledger).

29. Reserve/resource quality [Complete · score 2 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Reserve base large, growing, and quality-evidenced at asset level: 55.4 Moz proven and probable (+2% year over year, net of ~3.4 Moz of depletion - genuine replacement), measured and indicated resources 47.1 Moz (+10%), inferred 41.8 Moz (+15%); asset detail includes Odyssey's 6.0 Moz P&P at 3.14 g/t, Marban's initial 1.58 Moz probable, and the Hope Bay base supporting 400,000-435,000 oz/yr over an initial 11-year life from 2030.

30. Exploration effectiveness [Complete · score 2 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Exploration effectiveness proven where it matters most - next to owned infrastructure: East Gouldie inferred resources grew 62% year over year to 7.4 Moz, the new Eclipse zone declared an initial 0.6 Moz within reach of planned underground development, and the 2026 Malartic program ($32.6M, 190,700 m, up to 20 rigs) plus the Detour Lake underground West Extension continue the pattern of converting drilling into mill feed rather than press releases.

31. Ownership, royalties, streams, and joint ventures [Complete · score 3 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Ownership and partner map documented: San Nicolas (copper-zinc, Mexico) held 50/50 with Teck through a wholly-owned subsidiary; a deliberate minority-stake pipeline in juniors (Cadillac Mines, July 2026; Prism Resources early-warning updates; a C$60M placement); and royalty encumbrances on owned ground disclosed transparently - including the 3-5% NSR royalties on Canadian Malartic and 5% on East Gouldie payable to OR Royalties, a real cost item cross-checked against the payee's own filings in this project.

32. Commodity-price, FX, and inflation assumption governance [Complete · score 3 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Full, dated, asset-specific commodity price and FX assumptions disclosed for year-end 2025: reserves based on $1,600/oz gold (exceptions named per asset, e.g. $1,500 Detour Lake open pit, $2,000 Amaruq/Pinos Altos, $1,300 San Nicolas), $24/oz silver, $3.80/lb copper, $1.20/lb zinc; resources based on $2,000/oz gold base case. FX of C$1.34, A$1.52, EUR0.91, MXN18.00 per US$1. Source: 2025 Form 40-F / year-end reserves release.

33. Tax, royalties, and fiscal losses [Complete · score 3 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Tax position quantified from results: $2.73B of taxes paid over the trailing twelve months on $5.34B of earnings (book effective rate ~33-34%), spread across Canadian federal/provincial, Finnish, Australian and Mexican regimes; no material tax disputes identified in the releases reviewed.

34. Production profile, depletion, and replacement [Complete · score 2 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Production profile and replacement both evidenced: 3,447,367 oz produced in 2025 with guidance achieved, 2026 guided to the low end of 3.3-3.5 Moz (cause named at metric 19), a rising three-year profile at the cornerstone asset, and 2025 reserves UP 2% after absorbing full depletion - replacement above 100% at portfolio level, with the Odyssey reconciliation detail at metric 54.

35. Operating reliability [Complete · score 3 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Operating reliability quantified: total recordable injury frequency improved to 4.8 from 5.2 in 2024, production has beaten budget two consecutive quarters, and Kittila's records came with declining unit costs; the Barnat pit redesign is the disclosed reliability blemish - a mine-plan correction at the largest complex, honestly weighed rather than netted against the beats.

36. Safety, workforce, and labor [Complete · score 4 (of 10; 1 = best)]
TRIFR improved to 4.8 from 5.2, but a fatal incident involving a contractor occurred at Fosterville in early December 2025 - scored down from what the cost/production numbers alone would suggest, reflecting that outcome. Source: 2025 Form 40-F.

37. Community relations and social licence [Complete · score 3 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Social licence assessed on both sides of the ledger: a 2025 federal investigation found gaps in Indigenous consultation (FPIC) practices relating to Whale Tail/Nunavut - a real adverse finding recorded as such - while the response is also documented: the Q2 2026 report explicitly describes progressing reconciliation initiatives with Indigenous communities, and Nunavut regulators granted Hope Bay construction approval in May 2026, indicating the relationship remains functional; this metric stays on the watch list at metric 22.

38. Disclosure quality, reporting integrity, and governance [Complete · score 2 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Company's 2025 Form 40-F confirms: internal control over financial reporting assessed effective as of Dec 31 2025 with a clean Ernst & Young attestation; no accounting restatements or clawback recoveries during the year; no off-balance-sheet arrangements; Code of Business Conduct and Ethics in place with no waivers for the CEO/CFO/controller; Audit Committee has multiple named independent financial experts.

39. Infrastructure, utilities, logistics, and business continuity [Complete · score 3 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Infrastructure and logistics exposure named and priced: the Nunavut operations (Meadowbank/Amaruq, Meliadine, now the Hope Bay build) depend on seasonal sealift resupply and arctic logistics - a structural, recurring exposure - against which the Abitibi, Finnish and Australian assets sit on mature road-and-grid infrastructure.

40. Cybersecurity, operational technology, and data integrity [Not Available - Documented]
Checked the 2025 Form 40-F risk-factor list and sustainability disclosures: "information technology issues" is named as a generic risk factor, but no control-maturity detail, incident history, or technical posture is disclosed anywhere in the public filings, consistent with standard practice for companies this size. Not expected to become available through further public search.

41. Hedging, derivatives, and counterparty risk [Complete · score 3 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Approximately 56% of 2026 diesel exposure hedged at an average $0.69/litre benchmark against a 2026 guidance assumption of $0.78/litre; company states current hedges are not factored into forward guidance. Concrete, dated, quantified hedging disclosure. Source: Q4/FY2025 results release.

42. Working capital, cash conversion, and liquidity quality [Complete · score 3 (of 10; 1 = best)]
FY2024 audited balance sheet: total current assets $2,805.3 million vs. total current liabilities $1,512.0 million, giving positive working capital of $1,293.3 million and a current ratio of 1.86x (down from 2.09x at Dec 31 2023, still healthy). Source: 2024 audited consolidated financial statements. Same one-year-lag caveat as metric 33 applies.

43. Dilution, equity compensation, and capital-structure overhang [Complete · score 2 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Dilution effectively zero and reversing: shares outstanding rose just 0.16% in a year to 500.04M despite ongoing RSU/option grants, while the company repurchased 2.24M shares for $400M in Q2 2026 alone within record quarterly shareholder returns of $625M and a $0.45 quarterly dividend - cash dividends paid every year since 1983.

44. Debt structure, covenants, and refinancing [Complete · score 2 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Clear debt paydown history through 2025 (senior notes redeemed at maturity), total long-term debt down to $196M, Moody's A3 stable rating, $2B undrawn facility. Source: quarterly results releases, 2025.

45. Litigation, regulatory, and contingent liabilities [Complete · score 3 (of 10; 1 = best)]
The identified regulatory matter is the Nunavut FPIC investigation (metric 37); beyond it, no material litigation or contingent liability against the company was identified in the 2025-2026 disclosures reviewed, and no tax disputes surfaced in a year in which $2.73B of taxes were paid.

46. Insurance adequacy [Not Available - Documented]
Checked the 2025 Form 40-F, AIF references, and sustainability reports: no insurance program terms, limits, deductibles, or carriers are disclosed. This is standard - insurance program detail is essentially never public for any issuer. Not expected to become available through further public search.

47. Concentration, correlation, and single-point-of-failure risk [Complete · score 3 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Concentration profile healthy for a senior: eleven mines across two reporting segments, with the largest complex (Canadian Malartic, 575,000-605,000 oz guided for 2026) around 17-18% of company production - no single-asset dependence - though country weighting is heavily Canadian, a deliberate jurisdictional choice whose flip side is metric 27's strength.

48. Revenue realization, offtake, and payable metal [Complete · score 2 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Per Note 1 of the FY2024 audited financial statements, Agnico Eagle "sells its gold production into the world market" as a direct seller of doré/bullion - it is not a streaming or royalty company and has no third-party offtake or payable-metal deduction structure comparable to a junior producer selling concentrate. This materially simplifies revenue-realization risk relative to peers with smelter/refinery offtake contracts.

49. Forecast governance and model governance [Complete · score 2 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Forecast governance demonstrated in both directions: 2025 guidance was achieved; when the Barnat redesign trimmed the 2026 outlook, the company said so mid-year with the cause named while MAINTAINING cost guidance and transparently RAISING growth capital for Hope Bay and Malartic - guidance treated as a commitment, revisions treated as news.

50. Management incentives and conflicts [Complete · score 3 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Incentive architecture documented: a formal incentive-compensation recoupment (clawback) policy, performance-linked incentive structures, equity-based programs whose grants have produced near-zero net dilution (metric 43), and behavioral alignment evidenced by record shareholder returns and a 43-year unbroken dividend; per-executive quantum not itemized this pass (ledger).

51. Corporate structure, subsidiary mapping, and entity-level solvency [Complete · score 3 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Corporate structure mapped at the level that matters: country subsidiaries beneath a Canadian parent, the San Nicolas joint venture held through a wholly-owned subsidiary alongside Teck, two clean reporting segments, and no variable-interest or off-balance-sheet complexity identified in the filings reviewed.

52. Reserve-price sensitivity, cut-off migration, and economic-envelope robustness [Complete · score 3 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Company discloses quantified reserve price sensitivity: a 10% higher gold price would increase gold in proven-and-probable reserves by approximately 9.0%; a 10% lower price would decrease it by approximately 8.7%. Source: Feb 12 2026 exploration/reserves release.

53. Technical-report currency, competent-person reliance, and study obsolescence [Complete · score 3 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Technical-report currency verified on the live documents: the Hope Bay 2026 study rests on a drill database cut to August 28, 2025 - current for a May 2026 construction approval - and the February 12, 2026 reserve/resource and three-year-guidance releases carry the Malartic technical detail; no stale cornerstone reports identified.

54. Geological reconciliation, grade control, metallurgical accounting, and reserve performance [Complete · score 2 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Model-to-mine reconciliation evidenced directly from operator disclosure: positive reconciliation in Odyssey underground production and reserve-model improvements drove reserve replacement at the Odyssey mine to 90%, while continued positive open-pit reconciliation at Canadian Malartic ADDED 115,000 oz to open-pit reserves in 2025 - ore bodies outperforming their block models, the single strongest technical-integrity signal a producer can show.

55. Water balance, water security, climate resilience, and extreme weather [Complete · score 3 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Climate and environmental quantification disclosed: 2025 GHG emissions of 1.36M tonnes CO2e at an intensity of 0.39 t/oz, with arctic-operations climate experience embedded in the Nunavut logistics record (metric 39); site-level water-security disclosure remains thin relative to the tailings reporting and is retained in the ledger.

56. Tailings-facility integrity, geotechnical stability, and emergency preparedness [Complete · score 2 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Tailings integrity disclosed at a standard most producers do not meet: a dedicated 2025 Tailings Summary Report with facility-by-facility disclosure across the Canadian and international portfolio, aligned with industry governance frameworks - the benchmark disclosure format this metric exists to reward.

57. Valuation-method hierarchy, asset-level NAV governance, discount-rate discipline, and double-counting prevention [Complete · score 3 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Valuation architecture disclosed on the SCENARIOS sheet (which replaces the NAV_MODEL sheet referenced in an earlier pass - that sheet does not exist in this workbook and the stale pointer is corrected here): a calibration-checked cash-generation multiple model with the multiple named as the key soft input; per the split requirement, at Current Spot roughly $34 per share (~21% of value) is gold-price dependence above the Long-Term Normalized case, with the 12x multiple carrying the quality/growth premium that metrics 14, 19 and 30 must keep earning. CORRECTION LOG: spot case restated $4,850 to $4,050 (actual July 31, 2026) on August 2, 2026; every table and the staircase chart reflects the corrected, dated case.

58. Underwriting conclusion governance, recommendation authorization, confidence calibration, and report-release control [Complete · score 2 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Release control satisfied: every metric carries a resolved status, the gate computes PASS from statuses alone, confidence and rank range are formula-driven, and publication authority rests with the accountable analyst named on INPUTS.

59. Management track record and role-specific competence [Complete · score 2 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Role-specific leadership verified: President and CEO Ammar Al-Joundi - CEO since February 2022 after seven years as President, with a mining-finance career including CFO of Agnico Eagle and senior finance leadership at Barrick Gold - has delivered guidance achievement, record free cash flow, the net-cash transition and record shareholder returns on his watch; depth of bench is evidenced in the operator's own words (the long-tenured Kittila management team) and in succession practice at a company that has paid dividends under every leadership generation since 1983.

Glossary - every term, in plain words (tap to open)

Estimated value - What our model calculates one share is worth from documented evidence at a stated metal price and date. An estimate, not a prediction of where the stock will trade.

Cautious value (safety floor) - The deliberately careful of the two published values: stress-grade assumptions throughout. If the price is below even this number, the discount needs no generosity to see.

Fair value (market-based) - The second published value: what the company is worth using the yardstick the market actually applies to companies of this type across the Roster, with growth on its documented calendar. The verdict keys to this value.

Discount / premium at today's price - The gap between an estimated value and what a share costs today. Green (discount) = the share costs less than the value. Red (premium) = the price already exceeds the value.

Share price - What the market currently charges for one share, always shown with the date of the quote.

Trading below / near / above estimated value - The relationship between price and FAIR value. Below = the market charges less than the estimate (a discount). Above = the price already assumes future events (a pre-payment). Near = within a few percent.

The five-case deck - Value computed at five fixed cases of the company's own commodity price - Stress, Conservative Base, the dated Spot, Long-Term Normalized, Upside. We never forecast the metal; you bring your own view.

Value milestones - A calendar of dated events. Value steps only when an event lands and its inputs are released; the share price line is never forecast. Each step is a checkable claim.

Catalyst - A dated, verifiable event - a study, a permit, a financing - that releases new model inputs.

Pre-payment - When today's price already contains tomorrow's documents. Not automatically bad - but you should know you are doing it.

Quality tier / recalibrated rank - Company quality alone, from a 7-factor panel, placed on a 1-10 ladder where the Roster median is 5.0. It deliberately ignores price.

Symposium Top - The highest quality tier on the Roster ladder - the best-evidenced enterprises among an already elite set.

The Roster - The fixed set of companies covered - the presenting companies of a leading annual natural-resource investing symposium, itself a pre-selected elite of the roughly 2,000-3,000 mining companies worldwide, so every tier is standing among the select.

Release gate - A report is published only when every one of the 52 questions reaches a terminal answer - evidenced, documented as absent, or stage-exempt. No gaps hidden.

SOFT - A figure we could not confirm from a primary source, labeled honestly wherever it is used.

PEA / PFS / FS - The study ladder: Preliminary Economic Assessment (first economics), Pre-Feasibility (engineered), Feasibility (bankable). Each rung earns more credit in the model.

P/NAV (developers) - Price compared to a project's study value. Builders trade below 1.0 before production and re-rate through it as the mine becomes real.

Risk weight - The fraction of a project's study value the model credits today, by stage - small for early studies, larger once permitted and engineered.

AISC - All-in sustaining cost: what it costs to produce one ounce, all-in. The margin is the metal price minus this.

NSR royalty - A share of a mine's revenue off the top. Royalty companies own these instead of operating mines.

Streaming - Buying a mine's future silver or gold at a fixed low price in exchange for money upfront.

Earn-in - A contract where a partner pays for exploration to earn a share of a project - the generator model's engine.

Unanswered question - The one company-specific uncertainty the whole thesis hinges on, named explicitly in every report.

Royalty - A fixed percentage of a mine's revenue that goes to an outside holder rather than to the company, paid off the top - before costs, before debt, before shareholders see anything. It was sold once, usually years earlier, to raise cash. It runs for the life of the mine unless the company buys it back, which is possible only where the original agreement allows it at a set price or where the holder agrees to sell. Because it is charged on revenue and not on profit, it is still owed in a year when the mine loses money.

Stream - Not a percentage of revenue but a claim on the metal itself. An outside party paid cash up front, often to help build the mine, in exchange for the right to receive a set share of the metal produced and to pay only a small fixed fraction of the market price for it - sometimes as little as a tenth or a fifth. The gap between that fixed price and the real price is the cost to the company, and it widens as metal prices rise. Like a royalty, a stream runs for the life of the mine unless bought back, which is possible only under the original terms or by agreement with the holder.

The Story

One paragraph in plain words: what the company is, what it owns, and the central finding. If you read nothing else, read this.

INVESTMENT COMMITTEE SUMMARY (July 31, 2026). First Majestic is the marquee primary-silver producer: four underground mines in Mexico (Santa Elena, 70%-held Los Gatos, San Dimas, La Encantada), a second-quarter report released ON the valuation date showing record revenue of US$415.5 million (+53%), EBITDA of US$252.3 million (+110%), free cash flow of US$194.6 million and a US$1.25 billion treasury, and production guidance raised for the second consecutive year. The underwriting tension is the purest expression of the expensive-marquee pattern in this project: the operations are performing, the balance sheet is a fortress, and the current-state model still values the company below its share price in ALL FIVE silver cases - the first such result in the project - because the market is paying today for the silver-torque brand, the Jerritt Canyon restart, two mill expansions and the Santo Nino and Navidad portals, none of which produce yet.

Where narrative text carries an older share price, the tables and the refreshed dated close above govern.

Three dates govern this page: the share price is the dated close shown above (2026-07-28); the evidence and estimated values are from this company's last full underwriting (2026-07-31), and change only when the company publishes something - each document's own date is listed under References; a daily event scan watches this company's filings and releases and queues a re-underwriting when one lands.

The Question the Thesis Hinges On

Single greatest company-specific uncertainty identified as the Jerritt Canyon situation: all mining and processing activity was suspended in April 2023, remained largely dormant through 2025 (only 342 oz of gold recovered via in-circuit recovery efforts), and a restart program was only recently announced, with re-opening of the Smith-SSX underground mines targeted for Q2 2026 - a real, multi-year suspended-asset situation, smaller in scale than Pan American's Escobal but the same fundamental risk category.

INVESTMENT COMMITTEE SUMMARY (July 31, 2026). First Majestic is the marquee primary-silver producer: four underground mines in Mexico (Santa Elena, 70%-held Los Gatos, San Dimas, La Encantada), a second-quarter report released ON the valuation date showing record revenue of US$415.5 million (+53%), EBITDA of US$252.3 million (+110%), free cash flow of US$194.6 million and a US$1.25 billion treasury, and production guidance raised for the second consecutive year. The underwriting tension is the purest expression of the expensive-marquee pattern in this project: the operations are performing, the balance sheet is a fortress, and the current-state model still values the company below its share price in ALL FIVE silver cases - the first such result in the project - because the market is paying today for the silver-torque brand, the Jerritt Canyon restart, two mill expansions and the Santo Nino and Navidad portals, none of which produce yet.

Second-quarter costs printed BELOW guidance. The asterisk: AISC guidance was itself raised 4% at the midpoint alongside the production raise, and the longer record includes the original Jerritt Canyon operating period that ended in suspension - the same asset now being restarted under this guidance framework.

15. Cost quality [Complete · score 4 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Cost quality is high on execution and structurally elevated on level. Second-quarter cash cost of US$18.06 and AISC of US$25.68 per attributable payable silver-equivalent ounce both came in below guidance, and management discloses the drivers with unusual candour: revised full-year AISC of US$27.69-28.77 is 4% above the original range primarily because royalties and workforce profit-sharing are CONTRACTUALLY LINKED to the silver price and the Mexican peso strengthened - costs that rise with revenue, a built-in margin governor. On the fixed 2025 assumption basis the company itself shows Q2 AISC would have been US$22.72, 13% lower, which is honest disclosure of how the AgEq denominator moves the optics. An AISC in the high-twenties remains among the highest absolute cost structures of any producer in this project, and it is what makes the stress case brutal.

The clean way through: first-half production of 7.3 million silver and 69,001 gold ounces sits at the revised guidance midpoints, so the physical run-rate is exactly on plan and the revenue volatility is price and timing, not operations.

A buyer at US$15.03 is paying today for the complete five-year plan delivered on schedule, plus the silver-torque premium the name has always commanded.

Glossary - every term, in plain words (tap to open)

Estimated value - What our model calculates one share is worth from documented evidence at a stated metal price and date. An estimate, not a prediction of where the stock will trade.

Cautious value (safety floor) - The deliberately careful of the two published values: stress-grade assumptions throughout. If the price is below even this number, the discount needs no generosity to see.

Fair value (market-based) - The second published value: what the company is worth using the yardstick the market actually applies to companies of this type across the Roster, with growth on its documented calendar. The verdict keys to this value.

Discount / premium at today's price - The gap between an estimated value and what a share costs today. Green (discount) = the share costs less than the value. Red (premium) = the price already exceeds the value.

Share price - What the market currently charges for one share, always shown with the date of the quote.

Trading below / near / above estimated value - The relationship between price and FAIR value. Below = the market charges less than the estimate (a discount). Above = the price already assumes future events (a pre-payment). Near = within a few percent.

The five-case deck - Value computed at five fixed cases of the company's own commodity price - Stress, Conservative Base, the dated Spot, Long-Term Normalized, Upside. We never forecast the metal; you bring your own view.

Value milestones - A calendar of dated events. Value steps only when an event lands and its inputs are released; the share price line is never forecast. Each step is a checkable claim.

Catalyst - A dated, verifiable event - a study, a permit, a financing - that releases new model inputs.

Pre-payment - When today's price already contains tomorrow's documents. Not automatically bad - but you should know you are doing it.

Quality tier / recalibrated rank - Company quality alone, from a 7-factor panel, placed on a 1-10 ladder where the Roster median is 5.0. It deliberately ignores price.

Symposium Top - The highest quality tier on the Roster ladder - the best-evidenced enterprises among an already elite set.

The Roster - The fixed set of companies covered - the presenting companies of a leading annual natural-resource investing symposium, itself a pre-selected elite of the roughly 2,000-3,000 mining companies worldwide, so every tier is standing among the select.

Release gate - A report is published only when every one of the 52 questions reaches a terminal answer - evidenced, documented as absent, or stage-exempt. No gaps hidden.

SOFT - A figure we could not confirm from a primary source, labeled honestly wherever it is used.

PEA / PFS / FS - The study ladder: Preliminary Economic Assessment (first economics), Pre-Feasibility (engineered), Feasibility (bankable). Each rung earns more credit in the model.

P/NAV (developers) - Price compared to a project's study value. Builders trade below 1.0 before production and re-rate through it as the mine becomes real.

Risk weight - The fraction of a project's study value the model credits today, by stage - small for early studies, larger once permitted and engineered.

AISC - All-in sustaining cost: what it costs to produce one ounce, all-in. The margin is the metal price minus this.

NSR royalty - A share of a mine's revenue off the top. Royalty companies own these instead of operating mines.

Streaming - Buying a mine's future silver or gold at a fixed low price in exchange for money upfront.

Earn-in - A contract where a partner pays for exploration to earn a share of a project - the generator model's engine.

Unanswered question - The one company-specific uncertainty the whole thesis hinges on, named explicitly in every report.

Royalty - A fixed percentage of a mine's revenue that goes to an outside holder rather than to the company, paid off the top - before costs, before debt, before shareholders see anything. It was sold once, usually years earlier, to raise cash. It runs for the life of the mine unless the company buys it back, which is possible only where the original agreement allows it at a set price or where the holder agrees to sell. Because it is charged on revenue and not on profit, it is still owed in a year when the mine loses money.

Stream - Not a percentage of revenue but a claim on the metal itself. An outside party paid cash up front, often to help build the mine, in exchange for the right to receive a set share of the metal produced and to pay only a small fixed fraction of the market price for it - sometimes as little as a tenth or a fifth. The gap between that fixed price and the real price is the cost to the company, and it widens as metal prices rise. Like a royalty, a stream runs for the life of the mine unless bought back, which is possible only under the original terms or by agreement with the holder.

References - the documents behind the evidence (tap to open)

The Story

One paragraph in plain words: what the company is, what it owns, and the central finding. If you read nothing else, read this.

INVESTMENT COMMITTEE SUMMARY (July 31, 2026). Argenta Silver owns 100% of El Quevar in Salta, Argentina - 56,709 hectares of which less than three percent has been explored, anchored by the Yaxtche deposit's genuinely elite resource: 45.3 million ounces indicated at 482 grams silver plus 4.1 million inferred at 417, with over 100,000 metres of historical drilling and existing roads and camp behind it. The 2025-26 campaign transformed the frame: 22,000 metres across 68 holes since May 2025, the program upsized twice to 45,000 metres, step-outs like 446 grams over 28 metres a full 120 metres beyond the resource boundary and a 4,982-gram emerging-target hit, the footprint up 20%, Mani-Copan delivering surface-grade silver 500 metres south, a drill-confirmed gold-copper discovery at Carmen that may MERGE with Yaxtche at depth, twenty-plus district targets defined, and a January C$23 million bought deal funding it all through June 2027 with metallurgy reporting by Q3 2026. At C$0.47 the market pays roughly a fifth ahead of the resource-based model at spot - the district story pre-paid one document early, on grades that justify the attention.

Where narrative text carries an older share price, the tables and the refreshed dated close above govern.

Three dates govern this page: the share price is the dated close shown above (2026-08-01); the evidence and estimated values are from this company's last full underwriting (2026-07-31), and change only when the company publishes something - each document's own date is listed under References; a daily event scan watches this company's filings and releases and queues a re-underwriting when one lands.

The Question the Thesis Hinges On

Single greatest company-specific uncertainty identified as conversion of a genuinely high-grade but still lightly-explored resource into a construction-ready project: only about 1-3% of the 56,709-hectare property has been historically explored, meaning the current resource, however high-grade, represents a small fraction of the property's tested potential - real upside, but also real uncertainty about whether the current results generalize across the broader land package.

Glossary - every term, in plain words (tap to open)

Estimated value - What our model calculates one share is worth from documented evidence at a stated metal price and date. An estimate, not a prediction of where the stock will trade.

Cautious value (safety floor) - The deliberately careful of the two published values: stress-grade assumptions throughout. If the price is below even this number, the discount needs no generosity to see.

Fair value (market-based) - The second published value: what the company is worth using the yardstick the market actually applies to companies of this type across the Roster, with growth on its documented calendar. The verdict keys to this value.

Discount / premium at today's price - The gap between an estimated value and what a share costs today. Green (discount) = the share costs less than the value. Red (premium) = the price already exceeds the value.

Share price - What the market currently charges for one share, always shown with the date of the quote.

Trading below / near / above estimated value - The relationship between price and FAIR value. Below = the market charges less than the estimate (a discount). Above = the price already assumes future events (a pre-payment). Near = within a few percent.

The five-case deck - Value computed at five fixed cases of the company's own commodity price - Stress, Conservative Base, the dated Spot, Long-Term Normalized, Upside. We never forecast the metal; you bring your own view.

Value milestones - A calendar of dated events. Value steps only when an event lands and its inputs are released; the share price line is never forecast. Each step is a checkable claim.

Catalyst - A dated, verifiable event - a study, a permit, a financing - that releases new model inputs.

Pre-payment - When today's price already contains tomorrow's documents. Not automatically bad - but you should know you are doing it.

Quality tier / recalibrated rank - Company quality alone, from a 7-factor panel, placed on a 1-10 ladder where the Roster median is 5.0. It deliberately ignores price.

Symposium Top - The highest quality tier on the Roster ladder - the best-evidenced enterprises among an already elite set.

The Roster - The fixed set of companies covered - the presenting companies of a leading annual natural-resource investing symposium, itself a pre-selected elite of the roughly 2,000-3,000 mining companies worldwide, so every tier is standing among the select.

Release gate - A report is published only when every one of the 52 questions reaches a terminal answer - evidenced, documented as absent, or stage-exempt. No gaps hidden.

SOFT - A figure we could not confirm from a primary source, labeled honestly wherever it is used.

PEA / PFS / FS - The study ladder: Preliminary Economic Assessment (first economics), Pre-Feasibility (engineered), Feasibility (bankable). Each rung earns more credit in the model.

P/NAV (developers) - Price compared to a project's study value. Builders trade below 1.0 before production and re-rate through it as the mine becomes real.

Risk weight - The fraction of a project's study value the model credits today, by stage - small for early studies, larger once permitted and engineered.

AISC - All-in sustaining cost: what it costs to produce one ounce, all-in. The margin is the metal price minus this.

NSR royalty - A share of a mine's revenue off the top. Royalty companies own these instead of operating mines.

Streaming - Buying a mine's future silver or gold at a fixed low price in exchange for money upfront.

Earn-in - A contract where a partner pays for exploration to earn a share of a project - the generator model's engine.

Unanswered question - The one company-specific uncertainty the whole thesis hinges on, named explicitly in every report.

Royalty - A fixed percentage of a mine's revenue that goes to an outside holder rather than to the company, paid off the top - before costs, before debt, before shareholders see anything. It was sold once, usually years earlier, to raise cash. It runs for the life of the mine unless the company buys it back, which is possible only where the original agreement allows it at a set price or where the holder agrees to sell. Because it is charged on revenue and not on profit, it is still owed in a year when the mine loses money.

Stream - Not a percentage of revenue but a claim on the metal itself. An outside party paid cash up front, often to help build the mine, in exchange for the right to receive a set share of the metal produced and to pay only a small fixed fraction of the market price for it - sometimes as little as a tenth or a fifth. The gap between that fixed price and the real price is the cost to the company, and it widens as metal prices rise. Like a royalty, a stream runs for the life of the mine unless bought back, which is possible only under the original terms or by agreement with the holder.

The Story

One paragraph in plain words: what the company is, what it owns, and the central finding. If you read nothing else, read this.

INVESTMENT COMMITTEE SUMMARY (July 31, 2026). Amarc is the project's majors-funded district generator: three British Columbia porphyry copper-gold districts, each near power, highway and rail, each carrying a different partnership state. At JOY in the Toodoggone, Freeport-McMoRan earned 60% by accelerating C$35 million, then ELECTED a C$75 million Stage 2 for ten more points - the partner's own arithmetic pricing the district near three-quarters of a billion - after the 2024 AuRORA high-grade copper-gold-silver discovery, its 2025 expansion, the TWINS discovery and a confirmed THIRD porphyry system; three rigs run the C$20 million 2026 program with Amarc as paid contractor. At DUKE, Boliden sole-funded C$30 million and converted to a 60:40 joint venture whose modest C$4 million 2026 program is metric 12's neutral signal, with Amarc holding a 180-day C$2.66 million election. IKE in the south remains 100%. FY2026 exploration of C$19.2 million was almost entirely partner money. At C$0.92, the market pays roughly a sixth BELOW the partner-arithmetic model at spot copper - the generator discount applied even where the majors have already published their price.

Glossary - every term, in plain words (tap to open)

Estimated value - What our model calculates one share is worth from documented evidence at a stated metal price and date. An estimate, not a prediction of where the stock will trade.

Cautious value (safety floor) - The deliberately careful of the two published values: stress-grade assumptions throughout. If the price is below even this number, the discount needs no generosity to see.

Fair value (market-based) - The second published value: what the company is worth using the yardstick the market actually applies to companies of this type across the Roster, with growth on its documented calendar. The verdict keys to this value.

Discount / premium at today's price - The gap between an estimated value and what a share costs today. Green (discount) = the share costs less than the value. Red (premium) = the price already exceeds the value.

Share price - What the market currently charges for one share, always shown with the date of the quote.

Trading below / near / above estimated value - The relationship between price and FAIR value. Below = the market charges less than the estimate (a discount). Above = the price already assumes future events (a pre-payment). Near = within a few percent.

The five-case deck - Value computed at five fixed cases of the company's own commodity price - Stress, Conservative Base, the dated Spot, Long-Term Normalized, Upside. We never forecast the metal; you bring your own view.

Value milestones - A calendar of dated events. Value steps only when an event lands and its inputs are released; the share price line is never forecast. Each step is a checkable claim.

Catalyst - A dated, verifiable event - a study, a permit, a financing - that releases new model inputs.

Pre-payment - When today's price already contains tomorrow's documents. Not automatically bad - but you should know you are doing it.

Quality tier / recalibrated rank - Company quality alone, from a 7-factor panel, placed on a 1-10 ladder where the Roster median is 5.0. It deliberately ignores price.

Symposium Top - The highest quality tier on the Roster ladder - the best-evidenced enterprises among an already elite set.

The Roster - The fixed set of companies covered - the presenting companies of a leading annual natural-resource investing symposium, itself a pre-selected elite of the roughly 2,000-3,000 mining companies worldwide, so every tier is standing among the select.

Release gate - A report is published only when every one of the 52 questions reaches a terminal answer - evidenced, documented as absent, or stage-exempt. No gaps hidden.

SOFT - A figure we could not confirm from a primary source, labeled honestly wherever it is used.

PEA / PFS / FS - The study ladder: Preliminary Economic Assessment (first economics), Pre-Feasibility (engineered), Feasibility (bankable). Each rung earns more credit in the model.

P/NAV (developers) - Price compared to a project's study value. Builders trade below 1.0 before production and re-rate through it as the mine becomes real.

Risk weight - The fraction of a project's study value the model credits today, by stage - small for early studies, larger once permitted and engineered.

AISC - All-in sustaining cost: what it costs to produce one ounce, all-in. The margin is the metal price minus this.

NSR royalty - A share of a mine's revenue off the top. Royalty companies own these instead of operating mines.

Streaming - Buying a mine's future silver or gold at a fixed low price in exchange for money upfront.

Earn-in - A contract where a partner pays for exploration to earn a share of a project - the generator model's engine.

Unanswered question - The one company-specific uncertainty the whole thesis hinges on, named explicitly in every report.

Royalty - A fixed percentage of a mine's revenue that goes to an outside holder rather than to the company, paid off the top - before costs, before debt, before shareholders see anything. It was sold once, usually years earlier, to raise cash. It runs for the life of the mine unless the company buys it back, which is possible only where the original agreement allows it at a set price or where the holder agrees to sell. Because it is charged on revenue and not on profit, it is still owed in a year when the mine loses money.

Stream - Not a percentage of revenue but a claim on the metal itself. An outside party paid cash up front, often to help build the mine, in exchange for the right to receive a set share of the metal produced and to pay only a small fixed fraction of the market price for it - sometimes as little as a tenth or a fifth. The gap between that fixed price and the real price is the cost to the company, and it widens as metal prices rise. Like a royalty, a stream runs for the life of the mine unless bought back, which is possible only under the original terms or by agreement with the holder.

The Story

One paragraph in plain words: what the company is, what it owns, and the central finding. If you read nothing else, read this.

INVESTMENT COMMITTEE SUMMARY (July 31, 2026). Aldebaran is the project's fair-for-the-stage giant: 80% of Altar in San Juan, Argentina (Sibanye-Stillwater holds 20%) - a cluster of large porphyries whose October 2025 PEA (SRK) mapped a 48-year, 60,000-tonne-per-day open-pit-plus-block-cave operation producing over 121,000 tonnes of copper-equivalent annually in its first twenty years, with an after-tax NPV(8%) of US$2.0 billion and a 20.5% IRR at US$4.35 copper - the modest return-on-scale that is the file's central tension. The 2026 story is focus: the Nuton option was terminated (November 2025), the non-core northern portfolio is being spun out as Centauri Minerals (drill permit received, US$25 million subscription-receipt financing closed July 23, listing planned this year), and the 2025-26 field season collects the infill and geotechnical data for the PFS. On roughly 185 million shares, the C$2.77 quote sits almost exactly at the model's dated-spot value with a ten-percent risk weight - the market pricing a PEA-stage Argentine porphyry precisely at its documents, with every future document a step up.

Where narrative text carries an older share price, the tables and the refreshed dated close above govern.

Three dates govern this page: the share price is the dated close shown above (2026-08-01); the evidence and estimated values are from this company's last full underwriting (2026-07-31), and change only when the company publishes something - each document's own date is listed under References; a daily event scan watches this company's filings and releases and queues a re-underwriting when one lands.

Single greatest company-specific uncertainty identified as converting a genuinely enormous but only moderately-returning resource into a bankable project: the October 2025 PEA showed a real, large after-tax NPV of US$2 billion over a 48-year mine life, but a comparatively modest 20.5% IRR - a real, disclosed combination of scale and return that is less immediately compelling on a returns basis than several smaller but higher-IRR projects reviewed elsewhere in this project (e.g. Bravo Mining's 49% IRR, #18 on this list), worth weighing directly rather than being impressed by absolute NPV alone.

The contingent inventory is transactional: the Sibanye joint-venture agreement's terms (the 20% partner's rights at each decision gate), the Centauri arrangement agreement's conditions through closing, the terminated Nuton option's clean exit, and ordinary-course provincial obligations. The Sibanye document is the one this underwriting most wishes were public in full.

Consistent with standard practice, no insurance program terms are disclosed in any public source reviewed this pass.

The recent Centauri Minerals spin-out (metric 10) further concentrates Aldebaran's remaining business almost entirely on the single Altar project, having separated the exploration-stage non-core Argentine assets into their own vehicle - a real, deliberate move toward single-asset focus rather than diversification. 49. Forecast governance and model governance [Complete · score 3 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Forecast governance has a clean recent record at study cadence: the PEA delivered in its stated window, filed on SEDAR+ with the termination disclosure in the same release, the spin-out executing on its announced timetable (agreement June 1, financing closed July 23, listing targeted this year), and the field program running to its stated PFS-data purpose. The record is short and document-based - exactly what a developer's should be - with the PFS date itself the next kept-or-missed test.

50. Management incentives and conflicts [Complete · score 3 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Incentives run through single-asset tenure: John Black has led Aldebaran since the 2018 Altar acquisition - eight years on one project - with management equity riding the same document chain as the register and the spin-out giving insiders the same Centauri exposure as everyone else. No insider selling of note was identified. The tenure is conviction evidence and concentration risk in one fact, consistent with the file's whole shape.

51. Corporate structure, subsidiary mapping, and entity-level solvency [Complete · score 2 (of 10; 1 = best)]
A real, specific, and unusually well-documented corporate structure: Aldebaran is itself a subsidiary of Regulus Resources Inc., holds an 80% interest in Altar (with Sibanye-Stillwater retaining 20%, metric 31), and has just completed the structural separation of its non-core Argentine exploration assets into the newly formed Centauri Minerals (metric 10).

52. Reserve-price sensitivity, cut-off migration, and economic-envelope robustness [Complete · score 4 (of 10; 1 = best)]
The economic envelope is the file's defining tension made numeric: a 20.5% IRR at the PEA's US$4.35 base is thin for Argentine porphyry risk - the envelope works, but without the headroom that lets a PFS absorb capital inflation - while the spot-copper case (the company's own supplementary calculation) shows what the current price environment adds. The 48-year life is the offsetting asset: envelopes this long survive cycles that kill shorter ones.

The October 2025 PEA is genuinely current and was prepared by named, credible independent consultants (SRK Consulting, Knight Piesold); an updated resource estimate incorporating more than 40,000 metres of subsequent infill drilling is targeted for Q3 2026, meaning the technical basis is being actively refreshed, not left stale.

No operating reconciliation exists at study stage. The PEA's inferred-inclusive basis is the relevant data-quality caveat, carried at metrics 20 and 29; the 2025-26 infill program is the conversion work.

55. Water balance, water security, climate resilience, and extreme weather [Complete · score 3 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Water and climate exposure is high-cordilleran: the project's water supply belongs to its own future engineering in a snowpack-fed basin, glacier-law screening applies as to every San Juan project at elevation, and the PEA's Knight Piesold tailings and water work is the current evidence base. No identified conflict with agricultural users at this remove; the EIA era will test it properly.

56. Tailings-facility integrity, geotechnical stability, and emergency preparedness [Complete · score 3 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Tailings design is study-stage and actively being de-risked: the PEA carries a conventional facility sized for a 48-year, 60,000-tonne-per-day life, and the current field season's geotechnical drilling WITHIN the planned tailings footprint is exactly the pre-PFS diligence the metric wants to see. No facility exists yet to classify; the design philosophy (smaller footprint via block cave) is disclosed.

The valuation hierarchy is explicit: 80% of the Altar PEA's NPV, scaled through a SOFT linear slope per dollar of copper anchored at the study's base case, risked at 0.10 for PEA-stage economics, plus a SOFT treasury estimate - with the Centauri distribution, the updated resource, the PFS, any RIGI application and the entire partner dynamic carried at ZERO as the anti-double-counting offset, released only on the dated staircase. The company's own spot-price NPV calculation is noted at metric 52 and deliberately not adopted.

Conclusion governance is satisfied for release: every scored metric resolved, the two not-applicable items and single absence documented, the SOFT treasury and slope labeled, and the central finding - a fair-for-the-stage price on a giant whose next two years are documents, not discoveries - stated identically in summary, bridge and hierarchy. Authorized with the PFS timetable and the Sibanye relationship as the standing watch items.

Glossary - every term, in plain words (tap to open)

Estimated value - What our model calculates one share is worth from documented evidence at a stated metal price and date. An estimate, not a prediction of where the stock will trade.

Cautious value (safety floor) - The deliberately careful of the two published values: stress-grade assumptions throughout. If the price is below even this number, the discount needs no generosity to see.

Fair value (market-based) - The second published value: what the company is worth using the yardstick the market actually applies to companies of this type across the Roster, with growth on its documented calendar. The verdict keys to this value.

Discount / premium at today's price - The gap between an estimated value and what a share costs today. Green (discount) = the share costs less than the value. Red (premium) = the price already exceeds the value.

Share price - What the market currently charges for one share, always shown with the date of the quote.

Trading below / near / above estimated value - The relationship between price and FAIR value. Below = the market charges less than the estimate (a discount). Above = the price already assumes future events (a pre-payment). Near = within a few percent.

The five-case deck - Value computed at five fixed cases of the company's own commodity price - Stress, Conservative Base, the dated Spot, Long-Term Normalized, Upside. We never forecast the metal; you bring your own view.

Value milestones - A calendar of dated events. Value steps only when an event lands and its inputs are released; the share price line is never forecast. Each step is a checkable claim.

Catalyst - A dated, verifiable event - a study, a permit, a financing - that releases new model inputs.

Pre-payment - When today's price already contains tomorrow's documents. Not automatically bad - but you should know you are doing it.

Quality tier / recalibrated rank - Company quality alone, from a 7-factor panel, placed on a 1-10 ladder where the Roster median is 5.0. It deliberately ignores price.

Symposium Top - The highest quality tier on the Roster ladder - the best-evidenced enterprises among an already elite set.

The Roster - The fixed set of companies covered - the presenting companies of a leading annual natural-resource investing symposium, itself a pre-selected elite of the roughly 2,000-3,000 mining companies worldwide, so every tier is standing among the select.

Release gate - A report is published only when every one of the 52 questions reaches a terminal answer - evidenced, documented as absent, or stage-exempt. No gaps hidden.

SOFT - A figure we could not confirm from a primary source, labeled honestly wherever it is used.

PEA / PFS / FS - The study ladder: Preliminary Economic Assessment (first economics), Pre-Feasibility (engineered), Feasibility (bankable). Each rung earns more credit in the model.

P/NAV (developers) - Price compared to a project's study value. Builders trade below 1.0 before production and re-rate through it as the mine becomes real.

Risk weight - The fraction of a project's study value the model credits today, by stage - small for early studies, larger once permitted and engineered.

AISC - All-in sustaining cost: what it costs to produce one ounce, all-in. The margin is the metal price minus this.

NSR royalty - A share of a mine's revenue off the top. Royalty companies own these instead of operating mines.

Streaming - Buying a mine's future silver or gold at a fixed low price in exchange for money upfront.

Earn-in - A contract where a partner pays for exploration to earn a share of a project - the generator model's engine.

Unanswered question - The one company-specific uncertainty the whole thesis hinges on, named explicitly in every report.

Royalty - A fixed percentage of a mine's revenue that goes to an outside holder rather than to the company, paid off the top - before costs, before debt, before shareholders see anything. It was sold once, usually years earlier, to raise cash. It runs for the life of the mine unless the company buys it back, which is possible only where the original agreement allows it at a set price or where the holder agrees to sell. Because it is charged on revenue and not on profit, it is still owed in a year when the mine loses money.

Stream - Not a percentage of revenue but a claim on the metal itself. An outside party paid cash up front, often to help build the mine, in exchange for the right to receive a set share of the metal produced and to pay only a small fixed fraction of the market price for it - sometimes as little as a tenth or a fifth. The gap between that fixed price and the real price is the cost to the company, and it widens as metal prices rise. Like a royalty, a stream runs for the life of the mine unless bought back, which is possible only under the original terms or by agreement with the holder.

The Story

One paragraph in plain words: what the company is, what it owns, and the central finding. If you read nothing else, read this.

IC summary: the most intellectually distinguished royalty compounder in the universe at its growth inflection - record Q2 2026 attributable royalty revenue of ~$30.0M (vs $12.7M a year earlier) across copper (Chapada stream), potash, the newly acquired Lithium Royalty Corp portfolio (four operating royalties, Finniss restarting, guided to C$40-60M by decade end), LIORC iron ore, and a ramping electricity-royalty platform now being partially monetized to Northampton and Apollo funds; the pre-revenue Silicon/Merlin gold royalty on AngloGold ground sits behind it all. The uncomfortable, honest finding: at C$58.41 the price exceeds this model's conservative value at EVERY deck case - the market pays a substantial premium for the growth and optionality book beyond what cautious appraisal supports. Superb enterprise; visibly expensive - the mirror image of the cheap-and-rough cases elsewhere in the universe.

Real, current, and quantified royalty-revenue growth by segment: Q2 2026 record attributable royalty revenue of approximately $30.0 million, more than double the $12.7 million reported in Q2 2025, with base-metals (primarily copper, via the Chapada stream) revenue of $9.4 million reflecting higher realized prices and delivery timing, and potash revenue of $5.0 million reflecting higher realized prices and volumes - genuine, segment-level, and dated revenue detail rather than a single blended figure.

13. Management guidance credibility [Not Applicable - Operator's Risk]
As a royalty and streaming company, Altius does not operate mines itself, so conventional production guidance does not apply directly; the company instead reports and guides on attributable royalty revenue by segment (metric 11), which it has grown substantially in every recent quarter reviewed.

14. Mine-by-mine operating quality [Not Applicable - Operator's Risk]
No operating mine exists for the company itself; mine-level operating detail belongs to the underlying operators (e.g. Lundin Mining at Chapada, Silvercorp Metals at Curipamba).

15. Cost quality [Not Applicable - Operator's Risk]
The company has no mining production costs of its own; it does disclose a real cost-of-sales figure specific to the Chapada copper stream ($2.6 million for Q2 2026, excluding depletion) - a real, specific, stream-level cost line rather than a company-wide production cost.

16. Development-project underwriting [Not Applicable - Operator's Risk]
No development-stage project belongs to Altius directly; it holds a real, dated 2% NSR royalty on Silvercorp Metals' Curipamba project, which is itself under active construction and on track for completion in July 2027 - a real, specific, forward-looking royalty on someone else's development project.

Real, strong balance-sheet detail: $89.3 million outstanding under a term credit facility as of December 31, 2025, against strong and growing quarterly royalty revenue (metric 11) - real, disclosed, and moderate leverage; a real, recent C$181.5 million equity raise was also identified, providing additional real, dated capital though also real, disclosed dilution risk flagged by at least one independent source. Months of cash runway and funding gap to the next milestone were not separately quantified this pass, per the sharpened requirement for this metric.

18. Capital allocation [Complete · score 3 (of 10; 1 = best)]
A real, long-established, and currently active capital-return program: a quarterly dividend of $0.10/share (with a Dividend Reinvestment Plan available to Canadian-resident shareholders since 2020), alongside a renewed Normal Course Issuer Bid allowing repurchase of up to approximately 4.02% of shares outstanding - among the most established, longest-running shareholder-return track records found at any company in this project, running alongside continued acquisitive growth (metric 10), not instead of it.

19. Run-rate normalization [Complete · score 2 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Reported-to-sustainable: the record Q2 decomposes cleanly - LRC lithium added ($6.4M), Chapada copper timing and prices ($9.4M), potash pricing ($5.0M), electricity ramp with Sequoia I first production ($6.1M incl. interest), LIORC steady ($1.6M) - an annualized run-rate near C$118M against FY2025's C$69.9M ($1.51/share); the growth is acquisition-plus-ramp, each component named and durable.

Shared five-case deck applied through the diversified-royalty adaptation (attributable revenue scaled as gold-equivalent), with the flagged simplification that potash, lithium, iron and electricity do not track gold - the deck exists for cross-company comparability; the non-revenue book is carried separately at appraisal.

21. Valuation-to-action bridge [Complete · score 2 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Valuation-to-action bridge - the cohort's first clear EXPENSIVE-QUALITY verdict: model value at spot C$30.06 vs C$58.41 (-C$24.63, -48.5%), and even the +3-5yr success staircase reaches only C$40.83 at spot (-30.1%); the price embeds either a much larger Silicon/Merlin than conservatively appraised, structurally higher multiples, or momentum. The action question inverts the usual one: not whether the company is good (it is) but what you are being asked to pay for goodness.
