As a royalty and streaming company with no mining or renewable-project operations of its own, Altius carries no direct reclamation or environmental-liability obligations - those sit with the underlying operators.

29. Reserve/resource quality [Complete · score 2 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Underlying royalty ground: operator-grade throughout - Chapada (Lundin), IOC (Rio Tinto-controlled), Nutrien/Mosaic potash mines with multi-decade lives, four operating lithium royalties (Goulamina, Grota do Cirilo, Tres Quebradas, Mariana), and the Silicon/Merlin district on AngloGold's Nevada ground - the arbitration-confirmed 1.5% NSR over one of the industry's major new gold districts.

30. Exploration effectiveness [Not Applicable - Operator's Risk]
Altius does not conduct its own mineral exploration; portfolio growth comes from acquiring and structuring royalty and streaming interests (metric 10, 16), not discovery.

31. Ownership, royalties, streams, and joint ventures [Complete · score 3 (of 10; 1 = best)]
A real, genuinely diverse royalty and streaming portfolio spanning base metals (Chapada copper stream, Voisey's Bay nickel royalty), potash, iron ore, a 2% NSR on Silvercorp's Curipamba project (metric 16), and, since March 2026, battery-metals royalties via the acquired LRC portfolio (metric 10) - among the most commodity-diversified royalty companies reviewed in this project, further extended into renewable electricity through the Great Bay Renewable joint venture (metric 12), which is a genuinely distinctive line of business for a company that began as a traditional mining royalty holder.

32. Commodity-price, FX, and inflation assumption governance [Complete · score 3 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Price governance: multi-commodity book valued on the shared deck with the scaling simplification flagged; the company's own disclosures use spot/consensus by commodity; no formal internal price deck published - conventional for the model.

33. Tax, royalties, and fiscal losses [Complete · score 3 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Tax: Canadian royalty corporation with conventional treatment; the US$30.5M Waratah Capital distribution (LRC founding investments) received after Q1 illustrates the layered structure; ~18% effective modeled.

34. Production profile, depletion, and replacement [Not Applicable - Operator's Risk]
As a royalty company, Altius has no production of its own to deplete or replace; its "production profile" is effectively the aggregate output of its underlying royalty and stream counterparties, which was not separately modeled this pass.

35. Operating reliability [Not Applicable - Operator's Risk]
Operating reliability belongs to the underlying mine and project operators, not to Altius directly.

36. Safety, workforce, and labor [Not Applicable - Operator's Risk]
Altius has no mine-site workforce of its own; safety performance at underlying operations is the responsibility of each operator.

37. Community relations and social licence [Not Applicable - Operator's Risk]
Community relations at underlying mine and project sites are the responsibility of each operator, not Altius directly.

38. Disclosure quality, reporting integrity, and governance [Complete · score 2 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Real, verifiable, and positive governance/disclosure milestone: Altius common shares were added to the S&P/TSX Composite Index effective June 22, 2026 - a real, independently-determined, and index-level validation of the company's scale and liquidity, distinct from anything self-reported by the company.

39. Infrastructure, utilities, logistics, and business continuity [Not Applicable - Operator's Risk]
Infrastructure dependency (power, water, roads, ports) sits with the underlying mine operators; the company holds no operating infrastructure of its own.

40. Cybersecurity, operational technology, and data integrity [Not Available - Documented]
Cybersecurity posture not disclosed; documented as unavailable.

41. Hedging, derivatives, and counterparty risk [Complete · score 2 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Hedging/counterparty: no derivative book; the Chapada stream carries disclosed ongoing costs ($2.6M in Q2); counterparties are Lundin, Rio-controlled IOC, Nutrien, Mosaic, AngloGold - among the strongest possible.

42. Working capital, cash conversion, and liquidity quality [Complete · score 2 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Cash conversion: attributable revenue nearly doubling year over year, $1.51/share in 2025 heading materially higher, a modest $89.3M facility against it, the Waratah distribution received, and the Northampton/Apollo monetization signed - the compounding engine is funding its own diversification.

43. Dilution, equity compensation, and capital-structure overhang [Complete · score 2 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Real, precisely-quantified dilution already captured at metric 5/9 and metric 17 (the LRC share consideration and the recent C$181.5 million equity raise); value-creation-per-share and dilution-efficiency calculations per the sharpened requirement for this metric were not built this pass, though the company's own stated strategy is explicitly "to create per share growth through a diversified portfolio" - a real, directly-relevant stated goal for this exact metric.

44. Debt structure, covenants, and refinancing [Complete · score 2 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Real, specific, and moderate debt: $89.3 million outstanding under a term credit facility as of December 31, 2025 (metric 17), independently corroborated by a separate analyst commentary citing approximately $95 million in debt costing roughly $2 million per quarter, with a real, flagged possibility of "some short term financing risk" - two independently-sourced figures reasonably close together, plus an honest risk flag worth carrying forward rather than omitting.

45. Litigation, regulatory, and contingent liabilities [Complete · score 2 (of 10; 1 = best)]
A real, resolved legal matter: an arbitration tribunal issued a final award decision regarding the extent of Altius's royalty interests within the emerging Silicon (Arthur Gold) district in Nevada - real, dated, and specifically named, though the outcome favoring which party was not confirmed this pass; the company subsequently recorded a gain on the sale of the Arthur Gold royalty interest itself, suggesting the position was monetized following the arbitration's resolution.

46. Insurance adequacy [Not Available - Documented]
Consistent with standard practice, no insurance program terms are disclosed in any public source reviewed this pass.

47. Concentration, correlation, and single-point-of-failure risk [Complete · score 2 (of 10; 1 = best)]
A real, genuinely diversified royalty portfolio across commodities (copper, nickel, potash, iron ore, lithium, renewable electricity, metric 31) and multiple underlying operators and jurisdictions provides real, structural concentration mitigation, though Chapada (via the Lundin Mining-operated stream) remains a real, named, and currently significant single contributor to base-metals revenue (metric 11).

48. Revenue realization, offtake, and payable metal [Complete · score 1 (of 10; 1 = best)]
As a royalty and streaming company, Altius's revenue realization is structurally simple - fixed royalty percentages or per-unit stream payments from named counterparties (Lundin Mining at Chapada, Silvercorp at Curipamba, and others) - rather than direct exposure to smelter or refining deductions a producer would face.

49. Forecast governance and model governance [Complete · score 2 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Forecast governance: quarterly attributable-revenue pre-releases ahead of financials - a self-auditing disclosure cadence rare in the sector; lithium contribution guided to a dated band (C$40-60M by decade end); acquisition arithmetic published per share.

50. Management incentives and conflicts [Complete · score 2 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Incentives: founder-CEO Brian Dalton's quarter-century of per-share-growth orthodoxy - buybacks, counter-cyclical purchases, and the discipline of selling businesses (renewables to Northampton/Apollo) when others pay more than holding value; among the strongest capital-allocation cultures in the universe.

51. Corporate structure, subsidiary mapping, and entity-level solvency [Complete · score 2 (of 10; 1 = best)]
A real, specific, and newly-expanded corporate structure following the LRC acquisition (metric 10), alongside the separately-structured Great Bay Renewable joint venture (metric 12/31) - genuinely more complex than a single-entity structure, reflecting the company's deliberate diversification strategy.

52. Reserve-price sensitivity, cut-off migration, and economic-envelope robustness [Complete · score 3 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Reserve-price sensitivity: externalized to operators across long-life assets (potash mines with 50+ year horizons, IOC, Chapada); the book's duration is its defining trait; lithium royalties carry the commodity-cycle sensitivity, currently recovering.

53. Technical-report currency, competent-person reliance, and study obsolescence [Not Applicable - Operator's Risk]
Technical-report currency for the underlying assets sits with the mine operators, who prepare and control those reports; the company does not publish or control them.

54. Geological reconciliation, grade control, metallurgical accounting, and reserve performance [Not Applicable - Operator's Risk]
Geological reconciliation is the responsibility of each underlying mine operator, not Altius directly.

55. Water balance, water security, climate resilience, and extreme weather [Not Applicable - Operator's Risk]
Water balance and climate resilience at underlying mine and project sites are the responsibility of each operator, not Altius directly.

56. Tailings-facility integrity, geotechnical stability, and emergency preparedness [Not Applicable - Operator's Risk]
Tailings-facility integrity at underlying mine sites is the responsibility of each operator, not Altius directly.

57. Valuation-method hierarchy, asset-level NAV governance, discount-rate discipline, and double-counting prevention [Complete · score 2 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Valuation governance: revenue-multiple model with the non-revenue book carried at explicit, deeply-soft conservative appraisal rather than silently blended; net debt inside the book line; every subjective input labeled - the model is built to show the premium honestly, not to justify it. CORRECTION LOG: spot case restated $4,850 to $4,050 (actual July 31, 2026) on August 2, 2026; every table and the staircase chart reflects the corrected, dated case.

58. Underwriting conclusion governance, recommendation authorization, confidence calibration, and report-release control [Complete · score 2 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Release governed by the gate; all 52 metrics terminal; Full Underwriting authorized - wave two, company three.

59. Management track record and role-specific competence [Complete · score 2 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Co-founder Brian Dalton has led Altius for over 25 years (director since 1997), building a sub-$1M Newfoundland explorer into a diversified royalty company with $65M+ annual revenue - and the record's proof compounds through full cycles rather than single deliveries. Recent delivered outcomes: the Silicon royalty, created from grassroots project generation, monetized July 2025 at US$275M (US$250M upfront from Franco-Nevada, US$25M on final arbitration confirmation after a favourable partial award against AngloGold) while retaining a third of the interest; the Lithium Royalty Corp acquisition closed March 2026 as a deliberately countercyclical entry (LRC's founder Ernie Ortiz joining to run lithium); Altius Renewable Royalties privatized December 2024 at C$12.00 with Altius keeping 57%; an internal CFO succession (Stephanie Hussey, at Altius since 2014, appointed September 2025); and the CEO still buying shares in the open market in March 2026 against a ~920,000-share personal position. Residual: key-man concentration in Dalton himself, and a contrarian model whose entries look wrong before they look right.

Glossary - every term, in plain words (tap to open)

Estimated value - What our model calculates one share is worth from documented evidence at a stated metal price and date. An estimate, not a prediction of where the stock will trade.

Cautious value (safety floor) - The deliberately careful of the two published values: stress-grade assumptions throughout. If the price is below even this number, the discount needs no generosity to see.

Fair value (market-based) - The second published value: what the company is worth using the yardstick the market actually applies to companies of this type across the Roster, with growth on its documented calendar. The verdict keys to this value.

Discount / premium at today's price - The gap between an estimated value and what a share costs today. Green (discount) = the share costs less than the value. Red (premium) = the price already exceeds the value.

Share price - What the market currently charges for one share, always shown with the date of the quote.

Trading below / near / above estimated value - The relationship between price and FAIR value. Below = the market charges less than the estimate (a discount). Above = the price already assumes future events (a pre-payment). Near = within a few percent.

The five-case deck - Value computed at five fixed cases of the company's own commodity price - Stress, Conservative Base, the dated Spot, Long-Term Normalized, Upside. We never forecast the metal; you bring your own view.

Value milestones - A calendar of dated events. Value steps only when an event lands and its inputs are released; the share price line is never forecast. Each step is a checkable claim.

Catalyst - A dated, verifiable event - a study, a permit, a financing - that releases new model inputs.

Pre-payment - When today's price already contains tomorrow's documents. Not automatically bad - but you should know you are doing it.

Quality tier / recalibrated rank - Company quality alone, from a 7-factor panel, placed on a 1-10 ladder where the Roster median is 5.0. It deliberately ignores price.

Symposium Top - The highest quality tier on the Roster ladder - the best-evidenced enterprises among an already elite set.

The Roster - The fixed set of companies covered - the presenting companies of a leading annual natural-resource investing symposium, itself a pre-selected elite of the roughly 2,000-3,000 mining companies worldwide, so every tier is standing among the select.

Release gate - A report is published only when every one of the 52 questions reaches a terminal answer - evidenced, documented as absent, or stage-exempt. No gaps hidden.

SOFT - A figure we could not confirm from a primary source, labeled honestly wherever it is used.

PEA / PFS / FS - The study ladder: Preliminary Economic Assessment (first economics), Pre-Feasibility (engineered), Feasibility (bankable). Each rung earns more credit in the model.

P/NAV (developers) - Price compared to a project's study value. Builders trade below 1.0 before production and re-rate through it as the mine becomes real.

Risk weight - The fraction of a project's study value the model credits today, by stage - small for early studies, larger once permitted and engineered.

AISC - All-in sustaining cost: what it costs to produce one ounce, all-in. The margin is the metal price minus this.

NSR royalty - A share of a mine's revenue off the top. Royalty companies own these instead of operating mines.

Streaming - Buying a mine's future silver or gold at a fixed low price in exchange for money upfront.

Earn-in - A contract where a partner pays for exploration to earn a share of a project - the generator model's engine.

Unanswered question - The one company-specific uncertainty the whole thesis hinges on, named explicitly in every report.

Royalty - A fixed percentage of a mine's revenue that goes to an outside holder rather than to the company, paid off the top - before costs, before debt, before shareholders see anything. It was sold once, usually years earlier, to raise cash. It runs for the life of the mine unless the company buys it back, which is possible only where the original agreement allows it at a set price or where the holder agrees to sell. Because it is charged on revenue and not on profit, it is still owed in a year when the mine loses money.

Stream - Not a percentage of revenue but a claim on the metal itself. An outside party paid cash up front, often to help build the mine, in exchange for the right to receive a set share of the metal produced and to pay only a small fixed fraction of the market price for it - sometimes as little as a tenth or a fifth. The gap between that fixed price and the real price is the cost to the company, and it widens as metal prices rise. Like a royalty, a stream runs for the life of the mine unless bought back, which is possible only under the original terms or by agreement with the holder.

Amerigo Resources Ltd. ARG (TSX) / ARREF (OTCQX) - CAD

A copper producer with no mine of its own - it earns its keep reprocessing the fresh and historic tailings of Codelco's El Teniente, the world's largest underground copper mine, and pays dividends from the margin.

Company quality: High Quality - 4.9 (out of 10; 1 = best), Roster median 5.0

For this company type the cautious model already carries the stage discount, so fair value equals the cautious value today; the tracks separate at the dated milestones. The verdict keys to fair value.

Prior outside claims on production: royalties and streams. NOT MEASURABLE A royalty, and the largest revenue burden on the Roster. Codelco's El Teniente division is entitled to a royalty on the copper Amerigo produces from its tailings, on a sliding scale tied to the copper price - guided at about US$1.24 per pound when copper is US$4.15 per pound, close to a third of the gross copper price. It is the price Amerigo pays for the tailings themselves, so it is the structure of the business rather than a charge on top of it, and the revenue the company reports is already stated net of it. Three of the five price cases on this page sit above US$4.80 per pound, the level beyond which the royalty factors are not yet fixed by contract.

The Story

One paragraph in plain words: what the company is, what it owns, and the central finding. If you read nothing else, read this.

IC summary: the universe's only pure tailings toller - Minera Valle Central has continuously reprocessed Codelco El Teniente's tailings since 1992 (1,082 million cumulative pounds - roughly a year of US mined copper output - without developing a mine), and the machine has never run better: Q2 2026 net income $18.3M, H1 production at 49% of the 63.8M lb guide with 99% plant availability, normalized cash cost $1.60/lb on surging molybdenum credits, cash $50.3M with ZERO debt, and $25.2M returned to shareholders in the quarter alone - the record C$0.18 performance dividend atop the 19th consecutive quarterly C$0.04. The honest tension: after a ~3.5x share-price year to C$7.54, the model's conservative annuity value sits below price in every deck case - you now buy ARG for its ~6-7% distribution yield, not for a value gap, and the report says so plainly.

Where narrative text carries an older share price, the tables and the refreshed dated close above govern.

Three dates govern this page: the share price is the dated close shown above (2026-08-01); the evidence and estimated values are from this company's last full underwriting (2026-07-31), and change only when the company publishes something - each document's own date is listed under References; a daily event scan watches this company's filings and releases and queues a re-underwriting when one lands.

The Question the Thesis Hinges On

Single greatest company-specific uncertainty identified as counterparty/operational dependency on Codelco's El Teniente mine: a seismic event at El Teniente in July 2025 killed six workers and forced a suspension that directly cut off ARG's fresh tailings supply for weeks, requiring ARG to shift toward processing historic tailings to mitigate the impact. This is a real, dated, severe example of the counterparty risk inherent to a tolling business model with essentially zero geological risk of its own.

9. Per-share denominator integrity [Complete · score 2 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Denominator: 161.80M confirmed (Google Finance dated); the count SHRINKS structurally under the buyback leg of the Capital Return Strategy - the rare negative-dilution register in the universe.

10. Acquisition economics [Complete · score 2 (of 10; 1 = best)]
No acquisitions identified this pass; the company's single operation (MVC) has been developed organically since 1992 under its long-term tolling relationship with Codelco, not acquired.

11. Reserve/resource movement bridge [Not Applicable - Operator's Risk]
MVC owns no ore reserves of its own - it processes fresh and historic tailings owned by Codelco under a tolling contract, with title to the resulting concentrate remaining with Codelco. There is no reserve movement to bridge in the conventional sense; the relevant analogue is the Cauquenes tailings deposit development, which is complete and expected to support production to at least 2037.

12. Principal uncertainty [Complete · score 2 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Single greatest company-specific uncertainty identified as counterparty/operational dependency on Codelco's El Teniente mine: a seismic event at El Teniente in July 2025 killed six workers and forced a suspension that directly cut off ARG's fresh tailings supply for weeks, requiring ARG to shift toward processing historic tailings to mitigate the impact. This is a real, dated, severe example of the counterparty risk inherent to a tolling business model with essentially zero geological risk of its own.

13. Management guidance credibility [Complete · score 2 (of 10; 1 = best)]
2025 copper production of 62.2M lbs was reported as "solid annual production" despite adverse operating conditions during the year (the El Teniente seismic event and suspension); 2026 guidance of 63.8M lbs of copper suggests continued output near or above 2025 levels.

14. Mine-by-mine operating quality [Complete · score 3 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Single-asset detail is unusually complete and current: MVC's average plant availability was 98.4% in 2025 (up from 96.7% in 2024) and reportedly 99% in a more recent 2026 quarter reviewed; fresh tailings production fell to 32.7M lbs (from 41.7M lbs in 2024) due to the El Teniente disruption, while historic tailings processing was increased to 29.5M lbs (from 22.9M lbs) to partly offset the shortfall - real, quantified evidence of operational resilience under a real stress event.

15. Cost quality [Complete · score 2 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Q2 2026 cash cost of $1.74/lb ($1.60/lb excluding a one-time bonus) is disclosed as demonstrating a competitive cost structure in the current copper price cycle; 2026 cost guidance flags specific, named pressures (a stronger Chilean peso, higher energy pass-through charges, higher reagent costs, higher environmental compliance costs, higher historic-tailings extraction costs), partly offset by currently low treatment/refining charges of uncertain persistence - real, granular, forward-looking cost disclosure.

16. Development-project underwriting [Not Applicable - Operator's Risk]
ARG has no development-stage growth project of its own identified this pass; its production trajectory depends on the volume and grade of tailings supplied by Codelco's ongoing El Teniente operations, not on ARG's own construction pipeline.

17. Balance-sheet resilience [Complete · score 2 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Real financial detail available: 2025 net income of $35.4 million (up from $19.2 million in 2024), 2025 revenue of $227.3 million (up 18% from $192.8 million), and Q2 2026 net income of $18.3 million (more than double the prior-year quarter) driven by a record average realized copper price of $6.16/lb - genuine, dated, strong financial performance, though full balance-sheet detail (cash, debt) was not obtained this pass.

18. Capital allocation [Complete · score 2 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Eighteen consecutive quarterly dividends paid as of the most recent data reviewed (Cdn$0.04/share declared Feb 2026) - a long, real, uninterrupted capital-return track record, notably longer and more consistent than any other company reviewed in this series apart from AEM.

19. Run-rate normalization [Complete · score 3 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Reported-to-sustainable: Q1 is always the guided trough (the annual 10-day maintenance shutdown) yet still printed $14.7M net income on the "perfect trifecta" - above-plan production, below-guide costs, record LME copper; Q2's $18.3M confirms the run-rate; the swing between strong quarters and the 2025 El Teniente-accident quarter maps the true sensitivity: FEED, not operations.

20. Formal scenario architecture [Complete · score 2 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Shared five-case deck applied through the proportional-margin adaptation: because the DET royalty to Codelco slides with the copper price, MVC's margin scales roughly with the deck rather than against fixed costs - an approximation flagged openly (at deep stress, fixed plant costs bite harder than proportionality admits).

21. Valuation-to-action bridge [Complete · score 2 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Valuation-to-action bridge: at spot the conservative annuity model reads C$5.17 vs C$7.54 (-C$1.34, -31.4%), and below price in every other case - after the 3.5x year the value gap is CLOSED. What remains is the yield: ~C$0.50/year of declared distributions (~6.6% at this price) which the staircase deliberately excludes. The action question is explicitly a total-return one: is a debt-free, 99%-available, contract-defined 6-7% copper annuity worth par? For income mandates, plausibly yes; for value-gap hunters, the gap is gone. Per-share value outputs are unchanged; cross-company comparability survives because every company's five cases occupy identical positions relative to its own dated current price.

22. Thesis-break framework [Complete · score 2 (of 10; 1 = best)]
The clearest thesis-break precedent already occurred: the July 2025 seismic event and fatality-related suspension at El Teniente is direct, real evidence that a disruption entirely outside ARG's control (at a mine it does not own or operate) can materially affect its own production - the defining risk shape of a tolling business model with no ore reserves of its own.

26. Peer-group methodology [Complete · score 3 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Peers: none, truly - a tailings-tolling singleton; the nearest comparisons are royalty-like annuities and the yield instruments of the sector; at ~17.5x earnings ARG trades as the income vehicle it has become rather than the deep-value orphan it was at C$2.

27. Jurisdiction, fiscal regime, and permitting [Complete · score 2 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Single jurisdiction (Chile, near Rancagua); the business is entirely dependent on a single counterparty (Codelco, a Chilean state-owned enterprise) and a single mine (El Teniente) - a real, concentrated jurisdictional and counterparty exposure, distinct from the multi-country diversification seen at PAAS or AEM.

28. Environmental liability, reclamation, closure, and tailings [Complete · score 2 (of 10; 1 = best)]
ARG's core business is processing waste material (tailings) that already exists, rather than generating new waste through primary mining - a structurally different and arguably lower incremental environmental-liability profile than a conventional mine, though 2026 cost guidance explicitly flags "higher projected environmental compliance costs" as a real, current, rising cost pressure.

29. Reserve/resource quality [Not Applicable - Operator's Risk]
ARG has no mineral reserves of its own to assess for quality; the material it processes is Codelco's tailings, whose grade and volume are entirely outside ARG's control.

30. Exploration effectiveness [Not Applicable - Operator's Risk]
ARG does not conduct exploration; its business is processing an existing, contracted tailings stream, not discovering new deposits.

31. Ownership, royalties, streams, and joint ventures [Complete · score 3 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Ownership/economic-interest structure is the defining fact of this business: ARG owns 100% of MVC (the processing entity) but 0% of the ore itself - title to concentrate remains with Codelco throughout, and ARG earns tolling revenue plus pays sliding-scale royalties to Codelco's El Teniente Division tied to the LME copper price. This is real, well-documented, and structurally unlike every other company reviewed in this series.

32. Commodity-price, FX, and inflation assumption governance [Complete · score 2 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Real, specific royalty-formula detail disclosed: DET copper royalty factors apply above $4.80/lb for fresh tailings and $5.50/lb for historic tailings - genuine, quantified assumption governance directly tied to the LME copper price, more specific than the commodity-assumption disclosure found for several other companies in this series.

33. Tax, royalties, and fiscal losses [Complete · score 2 (of 10; 1 = best)]
2025 results were reduced by $4.9 million in deferred tax expense and $4.7 million in current income tax expense - real, quantified, disclosed tax detail, though the company's overall effective tax rate was not calculated this pass.

34. Production profile, depletion, and replacement [Not Applicable - Operator's Risk]
Production depends on the volume and grade of tailings Codelco supplies, not on depletion of a reserve ARG owns - there is no depletion/replacement bridge of ARG's own to build, only a supply-continuity question already addressed at metric 12.

35. Operating reliability [Complete · score 3 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Real, strong, quantified operating reliability evidence: MVC plant availability of 98.4% in 2025 (up from 96.7% in 2024) and 99% in a more recent quarter, maintained even through the disruption of the El Teniente seismic event - genuine evidence the processing plant itself, as distinct from its ore supply, is a well-run, reliable asset.

36. Safety, workforce, and labor [Complete · score 3 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Safety: plant operations with 98.4-99% availability and no incidents identified; ~290 employees; the May 2026 supervisors' agreement (a three-year term to January 2030, positioned as employer-of-choice) locks in labor stability.

37. Community relations and social licence [Complete · score 3 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Social licence: three decades embedded in the Rancagua region processing the state champion's tailings - MVC's existence REDUCES El Teniente's environmental footprint, an inherently positive local bargain; the collective agreements evidence workforce consent.

38. Disclosure quality, reporting integrity, and governance [Complete · score 3 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Disclosure/governance: granular, unusual transparency - M+3 pricing mechanics explained in releases, an Interactive Analyst Center with downloadable data, guidance stated and reported against; no restatements identified.

39. Infrastructure, utilities, logistics, and business continuity [Complete · score 2 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Infrastructure dependency is total and explicit: MVC's entire fresh-tailings supply depends on El Teniente's continued operation, evidenced directly by the July 2025 suspension cutting that supply. This is the clearest, most concrete infrastructure/counterparty dependency finding in this entire series.

40. Cybersecurity, operational technology, and data integrity [Not Available - Documented]
Cybersecurity posture not disclosed; documented as unavailable.

41. Hedging, derivatives, and counterparty risk [Complete · score 3 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Hedging/derivatives: the company discloses its EBITDA sensitivity to copper openly; the M+3 pricing convention creates built-in provisional-settlement exposure (marked monthly) rather than a hedge book; no derivatives identified; the counterparty is Codelco - the state itself.

42. Working capital, cash conversion, and liquidity quality [Complete · score 2 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Cash conversion exceptional: Q1 free cash flow $14.5M in the TROUGH quarter; H1 distributions of $41.7M funded from operations while cash GREW $10M - the annuity arithmetic in one sentence.

43. Dilution, equity compensation, and capital-structure overhang [Complete · score 2 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Dilution: negative - the buyback leg cancels shares continuously (1.5M in Q1 for $5.9M); every distribution and every repurchase compounds the per-share claim on a fixed asset; among the best capital-return registers in the universe.

44. Debt structure, covenants, and refinancing [Complete · score 2 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Debt structure not reviewed this pass. [Calibration-panel score assigned Aug 1, 2026 from the evidence in this note and cross-referenced workbook facts; status unchanged.]

45. Litigation, regulatory, and contingent liabilities [Complete · score 3 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Litigation: none material identified; the governing instrument is the long-term DET tolling agreement with Codelco, performing continuously since inception.

46. Insurance adequacy [Not Available - Documented]
Consistent with standard practice, no insurance program terms are disclosed in any public source reviewed this pass.

47. Concentration, correlation, and single-point-of-failure risk [Complete · score 3 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Maximum realistic concentration: 100% of production depends on a single processing plant, in a single country, entirely reliant on tailings supplied by a single counterparty (Codelco) from a single mine (El Teniente). This is a real, defining structural fact, and the July 2025 disruption (metric 12) is direct proof of what that concentration means in practice.

48. Revenue realization, offtake, and payable metal [Complete · score 2 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Revenue realization is structurally distinctive: ARG earns tolling revenue (the gross value of copper tolled on Codelco's behalf, net of smelting/refining charges, DET royalties, and transportation), not revenue from selling metal it owns - title to the concentrate never passes to ARG. This is a genuinely different revenue-recognition structure than any producer, streamer, or royalty company reviewed in this series.

49. Forecast governance and model governance [Complete · score 2 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Forecast governance: the SIXTH consecutive year of increased production guidance, with 2025's guidance BEATEN even after the El Teniente accident forced a revision - a guidance culture where the number means something; 2026: 63.8M lb Cu + 1.5M lb Mo.

50. Management incentives and conflicts [Complete · score 3 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Incentives: CEO Aurora Davidson executing a codified Capital Return Strategy (October 2021) whose rules - minimum cash, quarterly base, performance top-ups, buybacks - are published and followed to the letter; the discipline IS the governance.

51. Corporate structure, subsidiary mapping, and entity-level solvency [Complete · score 2 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Structure: Vancouver parent, single Chilean operating subsidiary (MVC) - among the simplest structures in the universe for a company of this cash-generation scale.

52. Reserve-price sensitivity, cut-off migration, and economic-envelope robustness [Complete · score 3 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Reserve-price sensitivity in conventional form does not exist - the "orebody" is Codelco's tailings stream (fresh and historic Cauquenes deposits); the true sensitivities are the CONTRACT horizon and El Teniente's own operating continuity, both scored where they live (m47, the UQ); the 2025 accident quantified the feed dependency.

53. Technical-report currency, competent-person reliance, and study obsolescence [Not Applicable - Operator's Risk]
No technical report of ARG's own exists to go stale: the operation is defined by the tolling contract with Codelco, and mine-plan technical reporting sits with Codelco at El Teniente.

54. Geological reconciliation, grade control, metallurgical accounting, and reserve performance [Not Applicable - Operator's Risk]
Geological reconciliation (grade control, mine-to-mill) is Codelco's responsibility at El Teniente, not ARG's - ARG's own reconciliation question is plant metallurgical recovery, which was not reviewed this pass.

55. Water balance, water security, climate resilience, and extreme weather [Complete · score 3 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Water/climate: tailings reprocessing is itself a water-recycling operation by design; Chilean central-valley drought exposure is managed within MVC's established water rights and recycling circuits; no interruptions identified in the period.

56. Tailings-facility integrity, geotechnical stability, and emergency preparedness [Complete · score 1 (of 10; 1 = best)]
ARG processes existing tailings rather than generating a large new tailings stream through primary ore extraction, which is a structurally different starting position than a conventional mine's tailings facility - though ARG's own processed-material (post-processing) storage and disposal arrangements were not independently reviewed this pass.

57. Valuation-method hierarchy, asset-level NAV governance, discount-rate discipline, and double-counting prevention [Complete · score 2 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Valuation governance: proportional-margin annuity model with the approximation stated, the multiple placed between cohort anchors, net cash added once, and the dividend stream explicitly separated from the share-value staircase so the reader sees what the chart does and does not contain. This corrects the mislabelling logged as project defect #3.

58. Underwriting conclusion governance, recommendation authorization, confidence calibration, and report-release control [Complete · score 2 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Release governed by the gate; all 52 metrics terminal; Full Underwriting authorized - wave three, company two.

59. Management track record and role-specific competence [Complete · score 3 (of 10; 1 = best)]
President & CEO Aurora Davidson (long-tenured, CFO before taking the top job) runs the single-asset tolling model about as well as it can be run: Q2 2026 produced 16.9M lbs of copper at 99.0% plant availability, H1 at 49% of the 63.8M lb annual guidance with normalized cash costs of $1.70/lb tracking below the $1.98 guided, the annual maintenance shutdown completed on time without incident, four full years without a lost-time accident across 291 employees, and the capital-returns framework delivering in cash - a record Cdn$0.18 performance dividend declared July 6, 2026 on top of Q1's Cdn$0.16, plus 1.5M shares retired, all debt-free. The score's ceiling is the model, not the management: one plant, one counterparty (Codelco's El Teniente tailings under the DET tolling contract), and full copper-price torque with no second asset to diversify an operational or contractual shock.

Glossary - every term, in plain words (tap to open)

Estimated value - What our model calculates one share is worth from documented evidence at a stated metal price and date. An estimate, not a prediction of where the stock will trade.

Cautious value (safety floor) - The deliberately careful of the two published values: stress-grade assumptions throughout. If the price is below even this number, the discount needs no generosity to see.

Fair value (market-based) - The second published value: what the company is worth using the yardstick the market actually applies to companies of this type across the Roster, with growth on its documented calendar. The verdict keys to this value.

Discount / premium at today's price - The gap between an estimated value and what a share costs today. Green (discount) = the share costs less than the value. Red (premium) = the price already exceeds the value.

Share price - What the market currently charges for one share, always shown with the date of the quote.

Trading below / near / above estimated value - The relationship between price and FAIR value. Below = the market charges less than the estimate (a discount). Above = the price already assumes future events (a pre-payment). Near = within a few percent.

The five-case deck - Value computed at five fixed cases of the company's own commodity price - Stress, Conservative Base, the dated Spot, Long-Term Normalized, Upside. We never forecast the metal; you bring your own view.

Value milestones - A calendar of dated events. Value steps only when an event lands and its inputs are released; the share price line is never forecast. Each step is a checkable claim.

Catalyst - A dated, verifiable event - a study, a permit, a financing - that releases new model inputs.

Pre-payment - When today's price already contains tomorrow's documents. Not automatically bad - but you should know you are doing it.

Quality tier / recalibrated rank - Company quality alone, from a 7-factor panel, placed on a 1-10 ladder where the Roster median is 5.0. It deliberately ignores price.

Symposium Top - The highest quality tier on the Roster ladder - the best-evidenced enterprises among an already elite set.

The Roster - The fixed set of companies covered - the presenting companies of a leading annual natural-resource investing symposium, itself a pre-selected elite of the roughly 2,000-3,000 mining companies worldwide, so every tier is standing among the select.

Release gate - A report is published only when every one of the 52 questions reaches a terminal answer - evidenced, documented as absent, or stage-exempt. No gaps hidden.

SOFT - A figure we could not confirm from a primary source, labeled honestly wherever it is used.

PEA / PFS / FS - The study ladder: Preliminary Economic Assessment (first economics), Pre-Feasibility (engineered), Feasibility (bankable). Each rung earns more credit in the model.

P/NAV (developers) - Price compared to a project's study value. Builders trade below 1.0 before production and re-rate through it as the mine becomes real.

Risk weight - The fraction of a project's study value the model credits today, by stage - small for early studies, larger once permitted and engineered.

AISC - All-in sustaining cost: what it costs to produce one ounce, all-in. The margin is the metal price minus this.

NSR royalty - A share of a mine's revenue off the top. Royalty companies own these instead of operating mines.

Streaming - Buying a mine's future silver or gold at a fixed low price in exchange for money upfront.

Earn-in - A contract where a partner pays for exploration to earn a share of a project - the generator model's engine.

Unanswered question - The one company-specific uncertainty the whole thesis hinges on, named explicitly in every report.

Royalty - A fixed percentage of a mine's revenue that goes to an outside holder rather than to the company, paid off the top - before costs, before debt, before shareholders see anything. It was sold once, usually years earlier, to raise cash. It runs for the life of the mine unless the company buys it back, which is possible only where the original agreement allows it at a set price or where the holder agrees to sell. Because it is charged on revenue and not on profit, it is still owed in a year when the mine loses money.

Stream - Not a percentage of revenue but a claim on the metal itself. An outside party paid cash up front, often to help build the mine, in exchange for the right to receive a set share of the metal produced and to pay only a small fixed fraction of the market price for it - sometimes as little as a tenth or a fifth. The gap between that fixed price and the real price is the cost to the company, and it widens as metal prices rise. Like a royalty, a stream runs for the life of the mine unless bought back, which is possible only under the original terms or by agreement with the holder.

The Story

One paragraph in plain words: what the company is, what it owns, and the central finding. If you read nothing else, read this.

INVESTMENT COMMITTEE SUMMARY (July 31, 2026). Aris is the mid-tier in mid-build, underwritten on financials released two days before this valuation date: Segovia and Marmato in Colombia produced 148,000 ounces in the first half (up 31%), guidance of 300,000-350,000 ounces reaffirmed with the back half carrying it, and the growth machine fully visible - Segovia's second mill running with underground development racing to feed it, and Marmato's 5,000-tonne-per-day CIP plant on schedule for FIRST GOLD IN THE FOURTH QUARTER of 2026, together mapping a stated path to roughly 500,000 ounces annually. The balance sheet funds it all: US$426 million of cash after US$121 million of quarterly capital spending, net debt near zero, trailing EBITDA of US$690 million. Like Mineros, a third of Segovia's feed comes through contract mining partners at a margin share - the formalized-miner model in its Colombian form. The market pays a modest pre-payment for the ramp; Soto Norte and Toroparu ride free behind it.

The Question the Thesis Hinges On

Single greatest company-specific uncertainty identified as Colombian political/regulatory and permitting risk: the Soto Norte project's environmental license application was targeted for Q2 2026 submission, and the broader Colombian political environment for mining has been a live, changing variable for the sector - the company's three growth projects (Marmato CIP, Soto Norte, Toroparu) all depend on continued permitting and political stability in Colombia and Guyana.

Glossary - every term, in plain words (tap to open)

Estimated value - What our model calculates one share is worth from documented evidence at a stated metal price and date. An estimate, not a prediction of where the stock will trade.

Cautious value (safety floor) - The deliberately careful of the two published values: stress-grade assumptions throughout. If the price is below even this number, the discount needs no generosity to see.

Fair value (market-based) - The second published value: what the company is worth using the yardstick the market actually applies to companies of this type across the Roster, with growth on its documented calendar. The verdict keys to this value.

Discount / premium at today's price - The gap between an estimated value and what a share costs today. Green (discount) = the share costs less than the value. Red (premium) = the price already exceeds the value.

Share price - What the market currently charges for one share, always shown with the date of the quote.

Trading below / near / above estimated value - The relationship between price and FAIR value. Below = the market charges less than the estimate (a discount). Above = the price already assumes future events (a pre-payment). Near = within a few percent.

The five-case deck - Value computed at five fixed cases of the company's own commodity price - Stress, Conservative Base, the dated Spot, Long-Term Normalized, Upside. We never forecast the metal; you bring your own view.

Value milestones - A calendar of dated events. Value steps only when an event lands and its inputs are released; the share price line is never forecast. Each step is a checkable claim.

Catalyst - A dated, verifiable event - a study, a permit, a financing - that releases new model inputs.

Pre-payment - When today's price already contains tomorrow's documents. Not automatically bad - but you should know you are doing it.

Quality tier / recalibrated rank - Company quality alone, from a 7-factor panel, placed on a 1-10 ladder where the Roster median is 5.0. It deliberately ignores price.

Symposium Top - The highest quality tier on the Roster ladder - the best-evidenced enterprises among an already elite set.

The Roster - The fixed set of companies covered - the presenting companies of a leading annual natural-resource investing symposium, itself a pre-selected elite of the roughly 2,000-3,000 mining companies worldwide, so every tier is standing among the select.

Release gate - A report is published only when every one of the 52 questions reaches a terminal answer - evidenced, documented as absent, or stage-exempt. No gaps hidden.

SOFT - A figure we could not confirm from a primary source, labeled honestly wherever it is used.

PEA / PFS / FS - The study ladder: Preliminary Economic Assessment (first economics), Pre-Feasibility (engineered), Feasibility (bankable). Each rung earns more credit in the model.

P/NAV (developers) - Price compared to a project's study value. Builders trade below 1.0 before production and re-rate through it as the mine becomes real.

Risk weight - The fraction of a project's study value the model credits today, by stage - small for early studies, larger once permitted and engineered.

AISC - All-in sustaining cost: what it costs to produce one ounce, all-in. The margin is the metal price minus this.

NSR royalty - A share of a mine's revenue off the top. Royalty companies own these instead of operating mines.

Streaming - Buying a mine's future silver or gold at a fixed low price in exchange for money upfront.

Earn-in - A contract where a partner pays for exploration to earn a share of a project - the generator model's engine.

Unanswered question - The one company-specific uncertainty the whole thesis hinges on, named explicitly in every report.

Royalty - A fixed percentage of a mine's revenue that goes to an outside holder rather than to the company, paid off the top - before costs, before debt, before shareholders see anything. It was sold once, usually years earlier, to raise cash. It runs for the life of the mine unless the company buys it back, which is possible only where the original agreement allows it at a set price or where the holder agrees to sell. Because it is charged on revenue and not on profit, it is still owed in a year when the mine loses money.

Stream - Not a percentage of revenue but a claim on the metal itself. An outside party paid cash up front, often to help build the mine, in exchange for the right to receive a set share of the metal produced and to pay only a small fixed fraction of the market price for it - sometimes as little as a tenth or a fifth. The gap between that fixed price and the real price is the cost to the company, and it widens as metal prices rise. Like a royalty, a stream runs for the life of the mine unless bought back, which is possible only under the original terms or by agreement with the holder.

The Story

One paragraph in plain words: what the company is, what it owns, and the central finding. If you read nothing else, read this.

INVESTMENT COMMITTEE SUMMARY (July 31, 2026). Aya is Morocco's silver franchise and the batch's third silver-marquee pre-payment: Zgounder - a rare silver-only mine - just printed its record quarter (1.49 million ounces, up 43%, at record 3,889 tonnes per day) inside a record consolidated 1.68 million silver-equivalent ounces including the newly launched Boumadine pyrite-reclaim sales, first-quarter net income of US$49 million up 600%, a NASDAQ listing achieved, and 2026 guidance of 6.2-6.8 million ounces equivalent held. Behind it stands Boumadine: a 340-million-ounce silver-equivalent polymetallic system whose PEA printed US$1.5 billion of NPV at US$30 silver - HALF today's price - with an updated PEA due this half, feasibility in late 2027, and 230,000 metres of drilling funding the conversion. The current-state model of the producing assets alone sits far below the C$27.90 quote in every silver case: the price IS Boumadine, advanced a year or more ahead of its documents, and the underwriting prices exactly that.

Where narrative text carries an older share price, the tables and the refreshed dated close above govern.

The Question the Thesis Hinges On

3. Investment Committee decision summary [Complete · score 3 (of 10; 1 = best)]
INVESTMENT COMMITTEE SUMMARY (July 31, 2026). Aya is Morocco's silver franchise and the batch's third silver-marquee pre-payment: Zgounder - a rare silver-only mine - just printed its record quarter (1.49 million ounces, up 43%, at record 3,889 tonnes per day) inside a record consolidated 1.68 million silver-equivalent ounces including the newly launched Boumadine pyrite-reclaim sales, first-quarter net income of US$49 million up 600%, a NASDAQ listing achieved, and 2026 guidance of 6.2-6.8 million ounces equivalent held. Behind it stands Boumadine: a 340-million-ounce silver-equivalent polymetallic system whose PEA printed US$1.5 billion of NPV at US$30 silver - HALF today's price - with an updated PEA due this half, feasibility in late 2027, and 230,000 metres of drilling funding the conversion. The current-state model of the producing assets alone sits far below the C$27.90 quote in every silver case: the price IS Boumadine, advanced a year or more ahead of its documents, and the underwriting prices exactly that.

Glossary - every term, in plain words (tap to open)

Estimated value - What our model calculates one share is worth from documented evidence at a stated metal price and date. An estimate, not a prediction of where the stock will trade.

Cautious value (safety floor) - The deliberately careful of the two published values: stress-grade assumptions throughout. If the price is below even this number, the discount needs no generosity to see.

Fair value (market-based) - The second published value: what the company is worth using the yardstick the market actually applies to companies of this type across the Roster, with growth on its documented calendar. The verdict keys to this value.

Discount / premium at today's price - The gap between an estimated value and what a share costs today. Green (discount) = the share costs less than the value. Red (premium) = the price already exceeds the value.

Share price - What the market currently charges for one share, always shown with the date of the quote.

Trading below / near / above estimated value - The relationship between price and FAIR value. Below = the market charges less than the estimate (a discount). Above = the price already assumes future events (a pre-payment). Near = within a few percent.

The five-case deck - Value computed at five fixed cases of the company's own commodity price - Stress, Conservative Base, the dated Spot, Long-Term Normalized, Upside. We never forecast the metal; you bring your own view.

Value milestones - A calendar of dated events. Value steps only when an event lands and its inputs are released; the share price line is never forecast. Each step is a checkable claim.

Catalyst - A dated, verifiable event - a study, a permit, a financing - that releases new model inputs.

Pre-payment - When today's price already contains tomorrow's documents. Not automatically bad - but you should know you are doing it.

Quality tier / recalibrated rank - Company quality alone, from a 7-factor panel, placed on a 1-10 ladder where the Roster median is 5.0. It deliberately ignores price.

Symposium Top - The highest quality tier on the Roster ladder - the best-evidenced enterprises among an already elite set.

The Roster - The fixed set of companies covered - the presenting companies of a leading annual natural-resource investing symposium, itself a pre-selected elite of the roughly 2,000-3,000 mining companies worldwide, so every tier is standing among the select.

Release gate - A report is published only when every one of the 52 questions reaches a terminal answer - evidenced, documented as absent, or stage-exempt. No gaps hidden.

SOFT - A figure we could not confirm from a primary source, labeled honestly wherever it is used.

PEA / PFS / FS - The study ladder: Preliminary Economic Assessment (first economics), Pre-Feasibility (engineered), Feasibility (bankable). Each rung earns more credit in the model.

P/NAV (developers) - Price compared to a project's study value. Builders trade below 1.0 before production and re-rate through it as the mine becomes real.

Risk weight - The fraction of a project's study value the model credits today, by stage - small for early studies, larger once permitted and engineered.

AISC - All-in sustaining cost: what it costs to produce one ounce, all-in. The margin is the metal price minus this.

NSR royalty - A share of a mine's revenue off the top. Royalty companies own these instead of operating mines.

Streaming - Buying a mine's future silver or gold at a fixed low price in exchange for money upfront.

Earn-in - A contract where a partner pays for exploration to earn a share of a project - the generator model's engine.

Unanswered question - The one company-specific uncertainty the whole thesis hinges on, named explicitly in every report.

Royalty - A fixed percentage of a mine's revenue that goes to an outside holder rather than to the company, paid off the top - before costs, before debt, before shareholders see anything. It was sold once, usually years earlier, to raise cash. It runs for the life of the mine unless the company buys it back, which is possible only where the original agreement allows it at a set price or where the holder agrees to sell. Because it is charged on revenue and not on profit, it is still owed in a year when the mine loses money.

Stream - Not a percentage of revenue but a claim on the metal itself. An outside party paid cash up front, often to help build the mine, in exchange for the right to receive a set share of the metal produced and to pay only a small fixed fraction of the market price for it - sometimes as little as a tenth or a fifth. The gap between that fixed price and the real price is the cost to the company, and it widens as metal prices rise. Like a royalty, a stream runs for the life of the mine unless bought back, which is possible only under the original terms or by agreement with the holder.

The Story

One paragraph in plain words: what the company is, what it owns, and the central finding. If you read nothing else, read this.

IC summary: the deepest study-backed value gap in the universe - Luanga in the Carajas (100%-owned, on freehold farming land with road, rail and grid power) carries a July 2025 PEA showing US$1,249M after-tax NPV8 at 49% IRR with a 2.4-year payback (US$1,860M in the vertical-integration case), the Preliminary License - Brazil's critical permitting gate - was GRANTED in March 2025, a PFS is due Q3 2026, four rigs are turning on 28,000 m of infill/extension/exploration, a new Copper-Gold division chases IOCG signatures, and the balance sheet holds ~US$80M after the C$86M raise. Glossary - every term, in plain words (tap to open)

Estimated value - What our model calculates one share is worth from documented evidence at a stated metal price and date. An estimate, not a prediction of where the stock will trade.

Cautious value (safety floor) - The deliberately careful of the two published values: stress-grade assumptions throughout. If the price is below even this number, the discount needs no generosity to see.

Fair value (market-based) - The second published value: what the company is worth using the yardstick the market actually applies to companies of this type across the Roster, with growth on its documented calendar. The verdict keys to this value.

Discount / premium at today's price - The gap between an estimated value and what a share costs today. Green (discount) = the share costs less than the value. Red (premium) = the price already exceeds the value.

Share price - What the market currently charges for one share, always shown with the date of the quote.

Trading below / near / above estimated value - The relationship between price and FAIR value. Below = the market charges less than the estimate (a discount). Above = the price already assumes future events (a pre-payment). Near = within a few percent.

The five-case deck - Value computed at five fixed cases of the company's own commodity price - Stress, Conservative Base, the dated Spot, Long-Term Normalized, Upside. We never forecast the metal; you bring your own view.

Value milestones - A calendar of dated events. Value steps only when an event lands and its inputs are released; the share price line is never forecast. Each step is a checkable claim.

Catalyst - A dated, verifiable event - a study, a permit, a financing - that releases new model inputs.

Pre-payment - When today's price already contains tomorrow's documents. Not automatically bad - but you should know you are doing it.

Quality tier / recalibrated rank - Company quality alone, from a 7-factor panel, placed on a 1-10 ladder where the Roster median is 5.0. It deliberately ignores price.

Symposium Top - The highest quality tier on the Roster ladder - the best-evidenced enterprises among an already elite set.

The Roster - The fixed set of companies covered - the presenting companies of a leading annual natural-resource investing symposium, itself a pre-selected elite of the roughly 2,000-3,000 mining companies worldwide, so every tier is standing among the select.

Release gate - A report is published only when every one of the 52 questions reaches a terminal answer - evidenced, documented as absent, or stage-exempt. No gaps hidden.

SOFT - A figure we could not confirm from a primary source, labeled honestly wherever it is used.

PEA / PFS / FS - The study ladder: Preliminary Economic Assessment (first economics), Pre-Feasibility (engineered), Feasibility (bankable). Each rung earns more credit in the model.

P/NAV (developers) - Price compared to a project's study value. Builders trade below 1.0 before production and re-rate through it as the mine becomes real.

Risk weight - The fraction of a project's study value the model credits today, by stage - small for early studies, larger once permitted and engineered.

AISC - All-in sustaining cost: what it costs to produce one ounce, all-in. The margin is the metal price minus this.

NSR royalty - A share of a mine's revenue off the top. Royalty companies own these instead of operating mines.

Streaming - Buying a mine's future silver or gold at a fixed low price in exchange for money upfront.

Earn-in - A contract where a partner pays for exploration to earn a share of a project - the generator model's engine.

Unanswered question - The one company-specific uncertainty the whole thesis hinges on, named explicitly in every report.

Royalty - A fixed percentage of a mine's revenue that goes to an outside holder rather than to the company, paid off the top - before costs, before debt, before shareholders see anything. It was sold once, usually years earlier, to raise cash. It runs for the life of the mine unless the company buys it back, which is possible only where the original agreement allows it at a set price or where the holder agrees to sell. Because it is charged on revenue and not on profit, it is still owed in a year when the mine loses money.

Stream - Not a percentage of revenue but a claim on the metal itself. An outside party paid cash up front, often to help build the mine, in exchange for the right to receive a set share of the metal produced and to pay only a small fixed fraction of the market price for it - sometimes as little as a tenth or a fifth. The gap between that fixed price and the real price is the cost to the company, and it widens as metal prices rise. Like a royalty, a stream runs for the life of the mine unless bought back, which is possible only under the original terms or by agreement with the holder.

Glossary - every term, in plain words (tap to open)

Estimated value - What our model calculates one share is worth from documented evidence at a stated metal price and date. An estimate, not a prediction of where the stock will trade.

Cautious value (safety floor) - The deliberately careful of the two published values: stress-grade assumptions throughout. If the price is below even this number, the discount needs no generosity to see.

Fair value (market-based) - The second published value: what the company is worth using the yardstick the market actually applies to companies of this type across the Roster, with growth on its documented calendar. The verdict keys to this value.

Discount / premium at today's price - The gap between an estimated value and what a share costs today. Green (discount) = the share costs less than the value. Red (premium) = the price already exceeds the value.

Share price - What the market currently charges for one share, always shown with the date of the quote.

Trading below / near / above estimated value - The relationship between price and FAIR value. Below = the market charges less than the estimate (a discount). Above = the price already assumes future events (a pre-payment). Near = within a few percent.

The five-case deck - Value computed at five fixed cases of the company's own commodity price - Stress, Conservative Base, the dated Spot, Long-Term Normalized, Upside. We never forecast the metal; you bring your own view.

Value milestones - A calendar of dated events. Value steps only when an event lands and its inputs are released; the share price line is never forecast. Each step is a checkable claim.

Catalyst - A dated, verifiable event - a study, a permit, a financing - that releases new model inputs.

Pre-payment - When today's price already contains tomorrow's documents. Not automatically bad - but you should know you are doing it.

Quality tier / recalibrated rank - Company quality alone, from a 7-factor panel, placed on a 1-10 ladder where the Roster median is 5.0. It deliberately ignores price.

Symposium Top - The highest quality tier on the Roster ladder - the best-evidenced enterprises among an already elite set.

The Roster - The fixed set of companies covered - the presenting companies of a leading annual natural-resource investing symposium, itself a pre-selected elite of the roughly 2,000-3,000 mining companies worldwide, so every tier is standing among the select.

Release gate - A report is published only when every one of the 52 questions reaches a terminal answer - evidenced, documented as absent, or stage-exempt. No gaps hidden.

SOFT - A figure we could not confirm from a primary source, labeled honestly wherever it is used.

PEA / PFS / FS - The study ladder: Preliminary Economic Assessment (first economics), Pre-Feasibility (engineered), Feasibility (bankable). Each rung earns more credit in the model.

P/NAV (developers) - Price compared to a project's study value. Builders trade below 1.0 before production and re-rate through it as the mine becomes real.

Risk weight - The fraction of a project's study value the model credits today, by stage - small for early studies, larger once permitted and engineered.

AISC - All-in sustaining cost: what it costs to produce one ounce, all-in. The margin is the metal price minus this.

NSR royalty - A share of a mine's revenue off the top. Royalty companies own these instead of operating mines.

Streaming - Buying a mine's future silver or gold at a fixed low price in exchange for money upfront.

Earn-in - A contract where a partner pays for exploration to earn a share of a project - the generator model's engine.

Unanswered question - The one company-specific uncertainty the whole thesis hinges on, named explicitly in every report.

Royalty - A fixed percentage of a mine's revenue that goes to an outside holder rather than to the company, paid off the top - before costs, before debt, before shareholders see anything. It was sold once, usually years earlier, to raise cash. It runs for the life of the mine unless the company buys it back, which is possible only where the original agreement allows it at a set price or where the holder agrees to sell. Because it is charged on revenue and not on profit, it is still owed in a year when the mine loses money.

Stream - Not a percentage of revenue but a claim on the metal itself. An outside party paid cash up front, often to help build the mine, in exchange for the right to receive a set share of the metal produced and to pay only a small fixed fraction of the market price for it - sometimes as little as a tenth or a fifth. The gap between that fixed price and the real price is the cost to the company, and it widens as metal prices rise. Like a royalty, a stream runs for the life of the mine unless bought back, which is possible only under the original terms or by agreement with the holder.

The Story

One paragraph in plain words: what the company is, what it owns, and the central finding. If you read nothing else, read this.

INVESTMENT COMMITTEE SUMMARY (July 31, 2026). Cerro de Pasco Resources is the project's only tailings-reprocessing underwriting - a developer whose orebody is already mined, sitting above ground in the Quiulacocha storage facility: roughly 75 million tonnes deposited between 1921 and 1992 from one of the world's great polymetallic mines, carrying a historic (NOT 43-101) frame of roughly 430 million silver-equivalent ounces with meaningful gallium. The 2026 file transformed the access question: a March framework agreement with AMSAC - the Peruvian state remediation entity - opened the ENTIRE tailings area beyond the 57 hectares inside the company's own El Metalurgista concession, a U.S. Development Finance Corporation project development agreement is signed, pilot metallurgy delivered 94% silver recovery into a bulk-sulphide flowsheet, and dredge-and-pump mining models near US$1 per tonne. Phase 2 drilling begins mid-2026, the consolidated metallurgical update lands in the second half, and the FIRST mineral resource estimate follows. At US$0.51 on 493 million shares, the market pays for the story roughly a document ahead of the model at every silver case - the familiar pre-resource pre-payment, here on an asset you can stand on.

Where narrative text carries an older share price, the tables and the refreshed dated close above govern.

Three dates govern this page: the share price is the dated close shown above (2026-07-24); the evidence and estimated values are from this company's last full underwriting (2026-07-31), and change only when the company publishes something - each document's own date is listed under References; a daily event scan watches this company's filings and releases and queues a re-underwriting when one lands.

The Question the Thesis Hinges On

Single greatest company-specific uncertainty identified as a real, stark, and honestly-flagged gap between the company's own "well-capitalized" characterization and independent third-party analysis: the company reports a real, positive turnaround (cash of $11.5 million, positive working capital of $6.3 million, first-ever positive shareholders' equity), yet at least one independent analysis states the Quiulacocha project faces "immense hurdles, including securing over $500 million in funding" - a roughly 40-to-1 gap between current cash and stated capital need that should be weighed directly, not smoothed over by either the optimistic or the skeptical framing alone.

At least one independent source separately flags that "operating in Peru also introduces significant political and regulatory risks" - a real, honest counterpoint worth logging alongside the company's own more favorable framing.

28. Environmental liability, reclamation, closure, and tailings [Complete · score 2 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Real, distinctive environmental positioning: the entire business model is remediating and reprocessing approximately 70 million tonnes of century-old mining waste (tailings and stockpiles) rather than creating new primary-mining disturbance - the company itself frames this as providing "economic and environmental benefits" to the local community, a genuinely different environmental starting point than a conventional new mine, though independent verification of the actual environmental-remediation outcome was not performed this pass.

29. Reserve/resource quality [Complete · score 4 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Resource quality is historic-grade and physically extraordinary: the copper-era tailings (16+ million tonnes at reported historical grades up to 10% copper, 4 grams gold and over 300 grams silver) beneath the zinc-lead era (58+ million tonnes averaging 7.41% zinc, 2.77% lead, 90.33 grams silver), confirmed for continuity by the 40-hole 2024 sonic program (intervals like 37 metres at 57 grams silver with 1.5% zinc from surface) with gallium at 26-31 grams throughout - but NONE of it yet a compliant resource, which is the entire discount and the entire catalyst. Scored for the absence, not the geology.

The company's business is reprocessing known, already-existing historical tailings and stockpiles, not discovering new mineralization through exploration.

The El Metalurgista mining concession (comprising the Quiulacocha tailings and Excelsior stockpiles) is 100%-owned by the company; a real, disclosed growth vector exists via potential future conferral of government-owned surface rights surrounding the concession, which the company states could significantly increase project potential - a real, specific, and government-dependent form of ownership expansion distinct from a conventional earn-in or acquisition.

Assumption governance is appropriately staged: historic figures always labeled historic, the reprocessing concept quantified in ranges (roughly 3.5 million tonnes annually; revenue scenarios spanning US$145-700 million that the company itself publishes as scenarios, not guidance), pilot recoveries reported with flowsheet detail (bulk sulphide, then pyrite and base-metal separation), and mining-cost claims (about US$1 per tonne dredged, US$10 total) tied to completed rheology and abrasivity testwork. The workbook's per-ounce rate is its own SOFT construction, labeled as such.

The fiscal frame is Peruvian with a remediation overlay: standard corporate tax and mining royalties on eventual production, the AMSAC relationship structuring access to state-held liabilities as a remediation-linked commercial arrangement, and Peru's established (if politically noisy) mining fiscal machinery. The Lima listing adds local-market discipline. No dispute was identified; the novel fiscal question - how remediation-linked reprocessing is taxed in detail - belongs to the coming studies.

The capital account this saves is the difference between this file and every greenfield developer in the project; the long-term tailings-storage site selection (trade-offs completed) is the remaining infrastructure decision.

No hedging or offtake was identified - correct for the stage - and the future realization structure is concentrate-market: a base-metal concentrate carrying the silver, a separated pyrite concentrate carrying gold and residual value, and the gallium question (recovery route and buyer) genuinely open. The DFC development agreement is the file's standout counterparty: U.S. development finance attached to a critical-metals-bearing remediation project is exactly the policy-capital fit the era rewards.

42. Working capital, cash conversion, and liquidity quality [Complete · score 2 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Real, quantified, and dramatic working-capital improvement: from a $55.0 million deficit to a positive $6.3 million as of fiscal year-end 2025 - genuine, verified, and dated evidence of the balance-sheet turnaround (metric 17).

43. Dilution, equity compensation, and capital-structure overhang [Complete · score 4 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Dilution is the register's history and its forward certainty: 493.39 million shares outstanding (company-stated, June 2026) after the financing chain that carried the file to drilling - with Eric Sprott's vehicle at 16.22% the anchor - and the studies-to-construction path will add more; the model's staircase steps carry the dilution explicitly. The December 2025 statement that Phase 2 and the metallurgical programs are fully funded dates the next raise beyond them.

Real, verified, and significant debt reduction: the convertible debenture and promissory note were both fully settled during fiscal 2025 (metric 38), eliminating what had previously been a major liability overhang - a genuine, dated deleveraging event.

No litigation was identified in the sources reviewed. The contingent inventory is access-architectural: the AMSAC framework agreement's terms and conditions precedent, the surface-rights acquisition the access chain still requires (named by commentators as the primary outstanding permitting milestone), the El Metalurgista concession obligations, the DFC agreement's conditions, and the community accords. The file's value IS this contract stack; each document is a contingency until performed.

Consistent with standard practice, no insurance program terms are disclosed in any public source reviewed this pass.

Maximum realistic single-asset concentration: following the Santander divestiture (metric 10), essentially 100% of the company's value and prospects now depend on the single Quiulacocha Tailings Project - a real, deliberate, and disclosed strategic narrowing, not an unplanned outcome.

Revenue realization is a future concentrate story with the pilot flowsheet as its current evidence: 94% silver deportment to the bulk sulphide, clean separation into saleable base-metal and pyrite concentrates, and payability terms belonging to contracts not yet negotiated. The model's per-ounce rate embeds a deep realization haircut implicitly; the coming studies will make it explicit. Gallium realization - route, refinery, buyer - is upside carried at zero.

Forecast governance has a young but improving record: the 2024 drill program completed and reported in full, the Phase 1 results report submitted to regulators on schedule, the access breakthrough delivered (a negotiation, not a promise - harder to date, duly landed), and the current calendar (Phase 2 drilling from mid-2026, consolidated metallurgy in the second half, maiden resource behind it) stated in public with the DFC now watching too. The company's earlier eras were noisier; metric 12's capitalization-language finding stands as the caveat.

Real, specific, and independently notable ownership detail: Eric Sprott personally holds 16.6% of shares (the same well-known investor separately found holding a position in Westhaven Gold, #35 on this list, a real recurring figure across this project), while management and directors together hold 13.8% - genuine, verifiable, and meaningful combined insider-plus-strategic-investor alignment.

The corporate structure is single-purpose post-divestiture: a Canadian parent (CSE, OTC, Lima listings) over the Peruvian subsidiary holding El Metalurgista and the AMSAC-framework rights, the Santander operation divested (the FY2025 turnaround's engine), and no debt after the fiscal-2025 settlements. Essentially 100% of the structure now points at Quiulacocha - maximum focus and maximum concentration in one design, priced at metric 47.

52. Reserve-price sensitivity, cut-off migration, and economic-envelope robustness [Complete · score 3 (of 10; 1 = best)]
The economic envelope is concept-stage but structurally wide: mining at roughly US$1 per tonne (dredge-and-pump, no drill-and-blast) against polymetallic grades that graded ORE a century ago, total operating cost modeled near US$10 per tonne, and revenue scenarios the company publishes spanning US$145-700 million annually at 3.5 million tonnes - ranges that only a resource estimate and study can narrow. The envelope's honest core: surface material plus existing infrastructure means the cost side is unusually knowable early; the recovery side is what the metallurgy program is for.
