Technical currency is the discount's other half: no compliant resource estimate, no economic study - the file runs on historic figures, a completed Phase 1 dataset, pilot metallurgy and engineering trade-offs - with the first resource estimate explicitly sequenced behind the second-half 2026 metallurgical consolidation. Scored for the absence; the entire 2026-27 calendar exists to cure it, and curing it is the investment case.

Water and climate exposure is high-Andean and inherited: the site sits at altitude in a historic mining basin with abundant water (an operating advantage for dredging), the project's own water story is remediation-positive (reprocessing removes the contamination source feeding legacy drainage), and climate exposure is conventional cordilleran. The environmental baseline work feeding the future EIA is in progress; no constraint on the current program was identified.

The entire project is itself a tailings-remediation and reprocessing initiative (metric 28) - directly and centrally relevant to this metric, since the company's core activity is managing existing tailings risk rather than creating new tailings storage from scratch, though independent geotechnical verification of the existing facility's condition was not performed this pass.

The valuation hierarchy is explicit and deliberately primitive: the historic silver-equivalent frame at a SOFT per-ounce rate scaling with silver, plus treasury - with the expanded AMSAC area beyond the historic frame, the gallium, the pyrite-gold stream, the DFC's financing capacity, and every study carried at ZERO as the anti-double-counting offset, released only on the dated staircase as documents convert historic to compliant. Authorized with the H2 metallurgical consolidation and maiden resource as the standing checkpoints.

Glossary - every term, in plain words (tap to open)

Estimated value - What our model calculates one share is worth from documented evidence at a stated metal price and date. An estimate, not a prediction of where the stock will trade.

Cautious value (safety floor) - The deliberately careful of the two published values: stress-grade assumptions throughout. If the price is below even this number, the discount needs no generosity to see.

Fair value (market-based) - The second published value: what the company is worth using the yardstick the market actually applies to companies of this type across the Roster, with growth on its documented calendar. The verdict keys to this value.

Discount / premium at today's price - The gap between an estimated value and what a share costs today. Green (discount) = the share costs less than the value. Red (premium) = the price already exceeds the value.

Share price - What the market currently charges for one share, always shown with the date of the quote.

Trading below / near / above estimated value - The relationship between price and FAIR value. Below = the market charges less than the estimate (a discount). Above = the price already assumes future events (a pre-payment). Near = within a few percent.

The five-case deck - Value computed at five fixed cases of the company's own commodity price - Stress, Conservative Base, the dated Spot, Long-Term Normalized, Upside. We never forecast the metal; you bring your own view.

Value milestones - A calendar of dated events. Value steps only when an event lands and its inputs are released; the share price line is never forecast. Each step is a checkable claim.

Catalyst - A dated, verifiable event - a study, a permit, a financing - that releases new model inputs.

Pre-payment - When today's price already contains tomorrow's documents. Not automatically bad - but you should know you are doing it.

Quality tier / recalibrated rank - Company quality alone, from a 7-factor panel, placed on a 1-10 ladder where the Roster median is 5.0. It deliberately ignores price.

Symposium Top - The highest quality tier on the Roster ladder - the best-evidenced enterprises among an already elite set.

The Roster - The fixed set of companies covered - the presenting companies of a leading annual natural-resource investing symposium, itself a pre-selected elite of the roughly 2,000-3,000 mining companies worldwide, so every tier is standing among the select.

Release gate - A report is published only when every one of the 52 questions reaches a terminal answer - evidenced, documented as absent, or stage-exempt. No gaps hidden.

SOFT - A figure we could not confirm from a primary source, labeled honestly wherever it is used.

PEA / PFS / FS - The study ladder: Preliminary Economic Assessment (first economics), Pre-Feasibility (engineered), Feasibility (bankable). Each rung earns more credit in the model.

P/NAV (developers) - Price compared to a project's study value. Builders trade below 1.0 before production and re-rate through it as the mine becomes real.

Risk weight - The fraction of a project's study value the model credits today, by stage - small for early studies, larger once permitted and engineered.

AISC - All-in sustaining cost: what it costs to produce one ounce, all-in. The margin is the metal price minus this.

NSR royalty - A share of a mine's revenue off the top. Royalty companies own these instead of operating mines.

Streaming - Buying a mine's future silver or gold at a fixed low price in exchange for money upfront.

Earn-in - A contract where a partner pays for exploration to earn a share of a project - the generator model's engine.

Unanswered question - The one company-specific uncertainty the whole thesis hinges on, named explicitly in every report.

Royalty - A fixed percentage of a mine's revenue that goes to an outside holder rather than to the company, paid off the top - before costs, before debt, before shareholders see anything. It was sold once, usually years earlier, to raise cash. It runs for the life of the mine unless the company buys it back, which is possible only where the original agreement allows it at a set price or where the holder agrees to sell. Because it is charged on revenue and not on profit, it is still owed in a year when the mine loses money.

Stream - Not a percentage of revenue but a claim on the metal itself. An outside party paid cash up front, often to help build the mine, in exchange for the right to receive a set share of the metal produced and to pay only a small fixed fraction of the market price for it - sometimes as little as a tenth or a fifth. The gap between that fixed price and the real price is the cost to the company, and it widens as metal prices rise. Like a royalty, a stream runs for the life of the mine unless bought back, which is possible only under the original terms or by agreement with the holder.

The Story

One paragraph in plain words: what the company is, what it owns, and the central finding. If you read nothing else, read this.

INVESTMENT COMMITTEE SUMMARY (July 31, 2026). Copper Giant - the renamed Libero Copper - owns Mocoa in Putumayo, Colombia: a Jurassic porphyry that has now passed the billion-tonne threshold at 1,120 million tonnes inferred grading 0.51% copper-equivalent - 12.7 billion pounds CuEq, including 7.7 billion pounds of copper and a full billion pounds of molybdenum - continuous from surface past a thousand vertical metres, one of the very few independent near-surface copper-molybdenum systems of global scale. The 2026 machine is running: 23,000 metres of directional drilling (the project's largest campaign, up 80%, fully funded from C$23 million), conversion of 30-50% of inferred to indicated under APEX, metallurgy under Frank Wright and SGS already printing 92% copper and 97% molybdenum rougher recoveries above the resource model's assumptions, geotech and hydrogeology in motion - and in May the company formally COMMENCED the PEA with a multi-scenario scope and a stated roadmap to prefeasibility. The company itself names Colombia risk openly in its own materials. At C$0.72 the market pays about a cent and a half per in-situ pound - roughly fair for a pre-PEA inferred giant in a hard postcode, with the delivered PEA the crossing everything points at.

Where narrative text carries an older share price, the tables and the refreshed dated close above govern.

Three dates govern this page: the share price is the dated close shown above (2026-07-27); the evidence and estimated values are from this company's last full underwriting (2026-07-31), and change only when the company publishes something - each document's own date is listed under References; a daily event scan watches this company's filings and releases and queues a re-underwriting when one lands.

The Question the Thesis Hinges On

Single greatest company-specific uncertainty identified as one the company itself names openly: its own investor materials list Colombia's August 2026 presidential election directly alongside technical milestones (drilling, PEA) as a "key upcoming milestone" - an unusually transparent acknowledgment that political risk sits on comparable footing with geological and technical risk for this specific project, rather than being relegated to generic risk-factor language.

Environmental obligations are the file's defining sensitivity: Mocoa sits in Putumayo's Andean-Amazon piedmont - among the most environmentally scrutinized settings in Colombian mining - where the project's history under prior operators included real community and environmental opposition, and where the current program's social re-engagement is as material as its drilling. Baseline environmental and hydrogeological work is disclosed as running; no current proceeding was identified. The eventual EIA is the file's true summit, years and documents away.

29. Reserve/resource quality [Complete · score 2 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Resource quality is the asset: 1,120 million tonnes inferred at 0.51% CuEq with a molybdenum kicker few porphyries carry (a billion pounds at 0.039% - meaningful by-product economics at current molybdenum prices), continuity demonstrated from surface beyond a thousand metres, and district targets interpreted as additional porphyry centres still untested. The entire inventory is INFERRED - the category is the discount - and the 2026 program's 30-50% conversion objective is aimed at precisely that.

Frank Giustra's Fiore backing (~11%) anchors the register. Residuals define the score: the entire resource is inferred, the economics are pre-study, and the deposit sits 10 km from Mocoa town in Putumayo - a Colombian social-permitting setting whose real test arrives with a mine plan, not a drill program.

Glossary - every term, in plain words (tap to open)

Estimated value - What our model calculates one share is worth from documented evidence at a stated metal price and date. An estimate, not a prediction of where the stock will trade.

Cautious value (safety floor) - The deliberately careful of the two published values: stress-grade assumptions throughout. If the price is below even this number, the discount needs no generosity to see.

Fair value (market-based) - The second published value: what the company is worth using the yardstick the market actually applies to companies of this type across the Roster, with growth on its documented calendar. The verdict keys to this value.

Discount / premium at today's price - The gap between an estimated value and what a share costs today. Green (discount) = the share costs less than the value. Red (premium) = the price already exceeds the value.

Share price - What the market currently charges for one share, always shown with the date of the quote.

Trading below / near / above estimated value - The relationship between price and FAIR value. Below = the market charges less than the estimate (a discount). Above = the price already assumes future events (a pre-payment). Near = within a few percent.

The five-case deck - Value computed at five fixed cases of the company's own commodity price - Stress, Conservative Base, the dated Spot, Long-Term Normalized, Upside. We never forecast the metal; you bring your own view.

Value milestones - A calendar of dated events. Value steps only when an event lands and its inputs are released; the share price line is never forecast. Each step is a checkable claim.

Catalyst - A dated, verifiable event - a study, a permit, a financing - that releases new model inputs.

Pre-payment - When today's price already contains tomorrow's documents. Not automatically bad - but you should know you are doing it.

Quality tier / recalibrated rank - Company quality alone, from a 7-factor panel, placed on a 1-10 ladder where the Roster median is 5.0. It deliberately ignores price.

Symposium Top - The highest quality tier on the Roster ladder - the best-evidenced enterprises among an already elite set.

The Roster - The fixed set of companies covered - the presenting companies of a leading annual natural-resource investing symposium, itself a pre-selected elite of the roughly 2,000-3,000 mining companies worldwide, so every tier is standing among the select.

Release gate - A report is published only when every one of the 52 questions reaches a terminal answer - evidenced, documented as absent, or stage-exempt. No gaps hidden.

SOFT - A figure we could not confirm from a primary source, labeled honestly wherever it is used.

PEA / PFS / FS - The study ladder: Preliminary Economic Assessment (first economics), Pre-Feasibility (engineered), Feasibility (bankable). Each rung earns more credit in the model.

P/NAV (developers) - Price compared to a project's study value. Builders trade below 1.0 before production and re-rate through it as the mine becomes real.

Risk weight - The fraction of a project's study value the model credits today, by stage - small for early studies, larger once permitted and engineered.

AISC - All-in sustaining cost: what it costs to produce one ounce, all-in. The margin is the metal price minus this.

NSR royalty - A share of a mine's revenue off the top. Royalty companies own these instead of operating mines.

Streaming - Buying a mine's future silver or gold at a fixed low price in exchange for money upfront.

Earn-in - A contract where a partner pays for exploration to earn a share of a project - the generator model's engine.

Unanswered question - The one company-specific uncertainty the whole thesis hinges on, named explicitly in every report.

Royalty - A fixed percentage of a mine's revenue that goes to an outside holder rather than to the company, paid off the top - before costs, before debt, before shareholders see anything. It was sold once, usually years earlier, to raise cash. It runs for the life of the mine unless the company buys it back, which is possible only where the original agreement allows it at a set price or where the holder agrees to sell. Because it is charged on revenue and not on profit, it is still owed in a year when the mine loses money.

Stream - Not a percentage of revenue but a claim on the metal itself. An outside party paid cash up front, often to help build the mine, in exchange for the right to receive a set share of the metal produced and to pay only a small fixed fraction of the market price for it - sometimes as little as a tenth or a fifth. The gap between that fixed price and the real price is the cost to the company, and it widens as metal prices rise. Like a royalty, a stream runs for the life of the mine unless bought back, which is possible only under the original terms or by agreement with the holder.

Glossary - every term, in plain words (tap to open)

Estimated value - What our model calculates one share is worth from documented evidence at a stated metal price and date. An estimate, not a prediction of where the stock will trade.

Cautious value (safety floor) - The deliberately careful of the two published values: stress-grade assumptions throughout. If the price is below even this number, the discount needs no generosity to see.

Fair value (market-based) - The second published value: what the company is worth using the yardstick the market actually applies to companies of this type across the Roster, with growth on its documented calendar. The verdict keys to this value.

Discount / premium at today's price - The gap between an estimated value and what a share costs today. Green (discount) = the share costs less than the value. Red (premium) = the price already exceeds the value.

Share price - What the market currently charges for one share, always shown with the date of the quote.

Trading below / near / above estimated value - The relationship between price and FAIR value. Below = the market charges less than the estimate (a discount). Above = the price already assumes future events (a pre-payment). Near = within a few percent.

The five-case deck - Value computed at five fixed cases of the company's own commodity price - Stress, Conservative Base, the dated Spot, Long-Term Normalized, Upside. We never forecast the metal; you bring your own view.

Value milestones - A calendar of dated events. Value steps only when an event lands and its inputs are released; the share price line is never forecast. Each step is a checkable claim.

Catalyst - A dated, verifiable event - a study, a permit, a financing - that releases new model inputs.

Pre-payment - When today's price already contains tomorrow's documents. Not automatically bad - but you should know you are doing it.

Quality tier / recalibrated rank - Company quality alone, from a 7-factor panel, placed on a 1-10 ladder where the Roster median is 5.0. It deliberately ignores price.

Symposium Top - The highest quality tier on the Roster ladder - the best-evidenced enterprises among an already elite set.

The Roster - The fixed set of companies covered - the presenting companies of a leading annual natural-resource investing symposium, itself a pre-selected elite of the roughly 2,000-3,000 mining companies worldwide, so every tier is standing among the select.

Release gate - A report is published only when every one of the 52 questions reaches a terminal answer - evidenced, documented as absent, or stage-exempt. No gaps hidden.

SOFT - A figure we could not confirm from a primary source, labeled honestly wherever it is used.

PEA / PFS / FS - The study ladder: Preliminary Economic Assessment (first economics), Pre-Feasibility (engineered), Feasibility (bankable). Each rung earns more credit in the model.

P/NAV (developers) - Price compared to a project's study value. Builders trade below 1.0 before production and re-rate through it as the mine becomes real.

Risk weight - The fraction of a project's study value the model credits today, by stage - small for early studies, larger once permitted and engineered.

AISC - All-in sustaining cost: what it costs to produce one ounce, all-in. The margin is the metal price minus this.

NSR royalty - A share of a mine's revenue off the top. Royalty companies own these instead of operating mines.

Streaming - Buying a mine's future silver or gold at a fixed low price in exchange for money upfront.

Earn-in - A contract where a partner pays for exploration to earn a share of a project - the generator model's engine.

Unanswered question - The one company-specific uncertainty the whole thesis hinges on, named explicitly in every report.

Royalty - A fixed percentage of a mine's revenue that goes to an outside holder rather than to the company, paid off the top - before costs, before debt, before shareholders see anything. It was sold once, usually years earlier, to raise cash. It runs for the life of the mine unless the company buys it back, which is possible only where the original agreement allows it at a set price or where the holder agrees to sell. Because it is charged on revenue and not on profit, it is still owed in a year when the mine loses money.

Stream - Not a percentage of revenue but a claim on the metal itself. An outside party paid cash up front, often to help build the mine, in exchange for the right to receive a set share of the metal produced and to pay only a small fixed fraction of the market price for it - sometimes as little as a tenth or a fifth. The gap between that fixed price and the real price is the cost to the company, and it widens as metal prices rise. Like a royalty, a stream runs for the life of the mine unless bought back, which is possible only under the original terms or by agreement with the holder.

The Story

One paragraph in plain words: what the company is, what it owns, and the central finding. If you read nothing else, read this.

INVESTMENT COMMITTEE SUMMARY (July 31, 2026). Contango Silver & Gold is three companies stapled together mid-transformation: a 30% non-operating stake in the Kinross-run Manh Choh direct-ship-ore mine that funds everything; the March 26, 2026 merger of equals with Dolly Varden Silver that added the 65-million-ounce-silver Kitsault Valley district in British Columbia and renamed the company; and an Alaska development pipeline (fully-owned Lucky Shot, FAST-41-tracked Johnson Tract) targeting 200,000 gold-equivalent ounces plus 5 million silver ounces within five years. The underwriting tension: 2026 is deliberately the trough year (40,000-45,000 ounce guidance after a harsh-winter first quarter) before the guided 2027 doubling to 75,000-80,000 ounces from the higher-grade South Pit - and Manh Choh's short direct-ship life means the pipeline is not optional growth but mandatory replacement. The current-state model prices the trough year; the staircase prices whether the replacement machine works.

Where narrative text carries an older share price, the tables and the refreshed dated close above govern.

Three dates govern this page: the share price is the dated close shown above (2026-08-01); the evidence and estimated values are from this company's last full underwriting (2026-07-31), and change only when the company publishes something - each document's own date is listed under References; a daily event scan watches this company's filings and releases and queues a re-underwriting when one lands.

The Question the Thesis Hinges On

Single greatest company-specific uncertainty identified as non-operator dependency layered with a genuine near-term production dip: Contango holds only a 30% JV interest in Manh Choh (Kinross operates the other 70% and controls mine-plan decisions), and the company's own guidance shows 2026 production falling to 40,000-45,000 oz (from 60,200 oz in 2025) as mining transitions from the North Pit to the higher-grade South Pit, before recovering to a guided 75,000-80,000 oz in 2027 - a real, disclosed, multi-year dip-then-recovery pattern investors must accept on faith in Kinross's execution.

Glossary - every term, in plain words (tap to open)

Estimated value - What our model calculates one share is worth from documented evidence at a stated metal price and date. An estimate, not a prediction of where the stock will trade.

Cautious value (safety floor) - The deliberately careful of the two published values: stress-grade assumptions throughout. If the price is below even this number, the discount needs no generosity to see.

Fair value (market-based) - The second published value: what the company is worth using the yardstick the market actually applies to companies of this type across the Roster, with growth on its documented calendar. The verdict keys to this value.

Discount / premium at today's price - The gap between an estimated value and what a share costs today. Green (discount) = the share costs less than the value. Red (premium) = the price already exceeds the value.

Share price - What the market currently charges for one share, always shown with the date of the quote.

Trading below / near / above estimated value - The relationship between price and FAIR value. Below = the market charges less than the estimate (a discount). Above = the price already assumes future events (a pre-payment). Near = within a few percent.

The five-case deck - Value computed at five fixed cases of the company's own commodity price - Stress, Conservative Base, the dated Spot, Long-Term Normalized, Upside. We never forecast the metal; you bring your own view.

Value milestones - A calendar of dated events. Value steps only when an event lands and its inputs are released; the share price line is never forecast. Each step is a checkable claim.

Catalyst - A dated, verifiable event - a study, a permit, a financing - that releases new model inputs.

Pre-payment - When today's price already contains tomorrow's documents. Not automatically bad - but you should know you are doing it.

Quality tier / recalibrated rank - Company quality alone, from a 7-factor panel, placed on a 1-10 ladder where the Roster median is 5.0. It deliberately ignores price.

Symposium Top - The highest quality tier on the Roster ladder - the best-evidenced enterprises among an already elite set.

The Roster - The fixed set of companies covered - the presenting companies of a leading annual natural-resource investing symposium, itself a pre-selected elite of the roughly 2,000-3,000 mining companies worldwide, so every tier is standing among the select.

Release gate - A report is published only when every one of the 52 questions reaches a terminal answer - evidenced, documented as absent, or stage-exempt. No gaps hidden.

SOFT - A figure we could not confirm from a primary source, labeled honestly wherever it is used.

PEA / PFS / FS - The study ladder: Preliminary Economic Assessment (first economics), Pre-Feasibility (engineered), Feasibility (bankable). Each rung earns more credit in the model.

P/NAV (developers) - Price compared to a project's study value. Builders trade below 1.0 before production and re-rate through it as the mine becomes real.

Risk weight - The fraction of a project's study value the model credits today, by stage - small for early studies, larger once permitted and engineered.

AISC - All-in sustaining cost: what it costs to produce one ounce, all-in. The margin is the metal price minus this.

NSR royalty - A share of a mine's revenue off the top. Royalty companies own these instead of operating mines.

Streaming - Buying a mine's future silver or gold at a fixed low price in exchange for money upfront.

Earn-in - A contract where a partner pays for exploration to earn a share of a project - the generator model's engine.

Unanswered question - The one company-specific uncertainty the whole thesis hinges on, named explicitly in every report.

Royalty - A fixed percentage of a mine's revenue that goes to an outside holder rather than to the company, paid off the top - before costs, before debt, before shareholders see anything. It was sold once, usually years earlier, to raise cash. It runs for the life of the mine unless the company buys it back, which is possible only where the original agreement allows it at a set price or where the holder agrees to sell. Because it is charged on revenue and not on profit, it is still owed in a year when the mine loses money.

Stream - Not a percentage of revenue but a claim on the metal itself. An outside party paid cash up front, often to help build the mine, in exchange for the right to receive a set share of the metal produced and to pay only a small fixed fraction of the market price for it - sometimes as little as a tenth or a fifth. The gap between that fixed price and the real price is the cost to the company, and it widens as metal prices rise. Like a royalty, a stream runs for the life of the mine unless bought back, which is possible only under the original terms or by agreement with the holder.

Centaurus is the project's most complete developer arriving at its decision moment: Jaguar - a tier-one nickel sulphide deposit in Brazil's Carajas (1.2 million tonnes contained nickel, 52 Mt reserve) taken from Vale acquisition in 2019 through a value-engineered Feasibility Study (US$735 million post-tax NPV, 34% IRR, 1.8-year payback) to FULLY PERMITTED with mining lease, environmental approvals, installation licence, and - as of July 15, 2026 - an approved national-grid high-voltage connection at half the transmission cost. A binding Glencore offtake covers a third of output, Brazil's development bank has a US$190 million letter of intent, ten institutions have offered up to US$320 million, and the Tucuma-proven project director is aboard. Everything is assembled EXCEPT the money: the Final Investment Decision is targeted for the end of the third quarter of 2026 against a Glencore contract that can terminate if it slips - the entire underwriting compresses into one dated funding event.

Where narrative text carries an older share price, the tables and the refreshed dated close above govern.

21. Valuation-to-action bridge [Complete · score 3 (of 10; 1 = best)]
The valuation-to-action bridge is asymmetric around one event: at the dated spot nickel price the risked model sits roughly 80% ABOVE the quote, clears it at base, long-term and upside, and falls below only at stress - the market is pricing meaningful FID failure probability into a project that is permitted, granted grid access, offtaken and letter-of-intent financed. The bridge to action is therefore the September quarter itself: FID on time converts the discount; FID missed hands Glencore a termination right and re-prices the story as another stranded feasibility.

22. Thesis-break framework [Complete · score 1 (of 10; 1 = best)]
The clearest thesis-break condition is failure to convert either the US$320 million non-binding debt offers or the BNDES letter of intent into a signed, binding funding package (metric 12/17) - without that, the already-once-delayed FID (metric 12) cannot proceed regardless of how strong the underlying project economics are.

26. Peer-group methodology [Complete · score 3 (of 10; 1 = best)]
The peer frame is the ex-Indonesia nickel-development set - a thin cohort after the price winter culled it - where Jaguar's claim is bottom-quartile operating cost via grid power and Carajas infrastructure, plus Brazil's 15% regional tax rate. The in-project comparator is NICU: the same commodity on the same restated deck, where the Sudbury restart trades at extreme pre-payment while this fully-permitted FS-stage builder trades at a discount to its risked model - the project's clearest same-commodity mispricing pair, in opposite directions.

27. Jurisdiction, fiscal regime, and permitting [Complete · score 3 (of 10; 1 = best)]

28. Environmental liability, reclamation, closure, and tailings [Complete · score 2 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Real, strong, and specific ESG characteristics disclosed: Jaguar is designed to run on 100% renewable energy, giving it a genuinely low-carbon footprint for a nickel sulphide operation - directly relevant given nickel's carbon intensity is an active concern for battery-supply-chain buyers; the company markets this explicitly as a competitive advantage.

29. Reserve/resource quality [Complete · score 2 (of 10; 1 = best)]
The May 2025 updated JORC Proved and Probable Ore Reserve of 52.0 million tonnes (0.4% nickel cut-off) is real, current, and independently classified under JORC standards (the Australian reserve/resource reporting code) - genuinely current technical confidence for a project already through Feasibility Study.

30. Exploration effectiveness [Complete · score 2 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Real, current exploration activity at the separate, earlier-stage Boi Novo copper-gold project: multiple copper-in-soil anomalies exceeding 2 kilometres in extent were identified at the Rio Novo target, building a real drill-target pipeline ahead of a planned Q3 2026 drilling campaign - genuine exploration progress distinct from Jaguar's development-stage work.

Glossary - every term, in plain words (tap to open)

Estimated value - What our model calculates one share is worth from documented evidence at a stated metal price and date. An estimate, not a prediction of where the stock will trade.

Cautious value (safety floor) - The deliberately careful of the two published values: stress-grade assumptions throughout. If the price is below even this number, the discount needs no generosity to see.

Fair value (market-based) - The second published value: what the company is worth using the yardstick the market actually applies to companies of this type across the Roster, with growth on its documented calendar. The verdict keys to this value.

Discount / premium at today's price - The gap between an estimated value and what a share costs today. Green (discount) = the share costs less than the value. Red (premium) = the price already exceeds the value.

Share price - What the market currently charges for one share, always shown with the date of the quote.

Trading below / near / above estimated value - The relationship between price and FAIR value. Below = the market charges less than the estimate (a discount). Above = the price already assumes future events (a pre-payment). Near = within a few percent.

The five-case deck - Value computed at five fixed cases of the company's own commodity price - Stress, Conservative Base, the dated Spot, Long-Term Normalized, Upside. We never forecast the metal; you bring your own view.

Value milestones - A calendar of dated events. Value steps only when an event lands and its inputs are released; the share price line is never forecast. Each step is a checkable claim.

Catalyst - A dated, verifiable event - a study, a permit, a financing - that releases new model inputs.

Pre-payment - When today's price already contains tomorrow's documents. Not automatically bad - but you should know you are doing it.

Quality tier / recalibrated rank - Company quality alone, from a 7-factor panel, placed on a 1-10 ladder where the Roster median is 5.0. It deliberately ignores price.

Symposium Top - The highest quality tier on the Roster ladder - the best-evidenced enterprises among an already elite set.

The Roster - The fixed set of companies covered - the presenting companies of a leading annual natural-resource investing symposium, itself a pre-selected elite of the roughly 2,000-3,000 mining companies worldwide, so every tier is standing among the select.

Release gate - A report is published only when every one of the 52 questions reaches a terminal answer - evidenced, documented as absent, or stage-exempt. No gaps hidden.

SOFT - A figure we could not confirm from a primary source, labeled honestly wherever it is used.

PEA / PFS / FS - The study ladder: Preliminary Economic Assessment (first economics), Pre-Feasibility (engineered), Feasibility (bankable). Each rung earns more credit in the model.

P/NAV (developers) - Price compared to a project's study value. Builders trade below 1.0 before production and re-rate through it as the mine becomes real.

Risk weight - The fraction of a project's study value the model credits today, by stage - small for early studies, larger once permitted and engineered.

AISC - All-in sustaining cost: what it costs to produce one ounce, all-in. The margin is the metal price minus this.

NSR royalty - A share of a mine's revenue off the top. Royalty companies own these instead of operating mines.

Streaming - Buying a mine's future silver or gold at a fixed low price in exchange for money upfront.

Earn-in - A contract where a partner pays for exploration to earn a share of a project - the generator model's engine.

Unanswered question - The one company-specific uncertainty the whole thesis hinges on, named explicitly in every report.

Royalty - A fixed percentage of a mine's revenue that goes to an outside holder rather than to the company, paid off the top - before costs, before debt, before shareholders see anything. It was sold once, usually years earlier, to raise cash. It runs for the life of the mine unless the company buys it back, which is possible only where the original agreement allows it at a set price or where the holder agrees to sell. Because it is charged on revenue and not on profit, it is still owed in a year when the mine loses money.

Stream - Not a percentage of revenue but a claim on the metal itself. An outside party paid cash up front, often to help build the mine, in exchange for the right to receive a set share of the metal produced and to pay only a small fixed fraction of the market price for it - sometimes as little as a tenth or a fifth. The gap between that fixed price and the real price is the cost to the company, and it widens as metal prices rise. Like a royalty, a stream runs for the life of the mine unless bought back, which is possible only under the original terms or by agreement with the holder.

Glossary - every term, in plain words (tap to open)

Estimated value - What our model calculates one share is worth from documented evidence at a stated metal price and date. An estimate, not a prediction of where the stock will trade.

Cautious value (safety floor) - The deliberately careful of the two published values: stress-grade assumptions throughout. If the price is below even this number, the discount needs no generosity to see.

Fair value (market-based) - The second published value: what the company is worth using the yardstick the market actually applies to companies of this type across the Roster, with growth on its documented calendar. The verdict keys to this value.

Discount / premium at today's price - The gap between an estimated value and what a share costs today. Green (discount) = the share costs less than the value. Red (premium) = the price already exceeds the value.

Share price - What the market currently charges for one share, always shown with the date of the quote.

Trading below / near / above estimated value - The relationship between price and FAIR value. Below = the market charges less than the estimate (a discount). Above = the price already assumes future events (a pre-payment). Near = within a few percent.

The five-case deck - Value computed at five fixed cases of the company's own commodity price - Stress, Conservative Base, the dated Spot, Long-Term Normalized, Upside. We never forecast the metal; you bring your own view.

Value milestones - A calendar of dated events. Value steps only when an event lands and its inputs are released; the share price line is never forecast. Each step is a checkable claim.

Catalyst - A dated, verifiable event - a study, a permit, a financing - that releases new model inputs.

Pre-payment - When today's price already contains tomorrow's documents. Not automatically bad - but you should know you are doing it.

Quality tier / recalibrated rank - Company quality alone, from a 7-factor panel, placed on a 1-10 ladder where the Roster median is 5.0. It deliberately ignores price.

Symposium Top - The highest quality tier on the Roster ladder - the best-evidenced enterprises among an already elite set.

The Roster - The fixed set of companies covered - the presenting companies of a leading annual natural-resource investing symposium, itself a pre-selected elite of the roughly 2,000-3,000 mining companies worldwide, so every tier is standing among the select.

Release gate - A report is published only when every one of the 52 questions reaches a terminal answer - evidenced, documented as absent, or stage-exempt. No gaps hidden.

SOFT - A figure we could not confirm from a primary source, labeled honestly wherever it is used.

PEA / PFS / FS - The study ladder: Preliminary Economic Assessment (first economics), Pre-Feasibility (engineered), Feasibility (bankable). Each rung earns more credit in the model.

P/NAV (developers) - Price compared to a project's study value. Builders trade below 1.0 before production and re-rate through it as the mine becomes real.

Risk weight - The fraction of a project's study value the model credits today, by stage - small for early studies, larger once permitted and engineered.

AISC - All-in sustaining cost: what it costs to produce one ounce, all-in. The margin is the metal price minus this.

NSR royalty - A share of a mine's revenue off the top. Royalty companies own these instead of operating mines.

Streaming - Buying a mine's future silver or gold at a fixed low price in exchange for money upfront.

Earn-in - A contract where a partner pays for exploration to earn a share of a project - the generator model's engine.

Unanswered question - The one company-specific uncertainty the whole thesis hinges on, named explicitly in every report.

Royalty - A fixed percentage of a mine's revenue that goes to an outside holder rather than to the company, paid off the top - before costs, before debt, before shareholders see anything. It was sold once, usually years earlier, to raise cash. It runs for the life of the mine unless the company buys it back, which is possible only where the original agreement allows it at a set price or where the holder agrees to sell. Because it is charged on revenue and not on profit, it is still owed in a year when the mine loses money.

Stream - Not a percentage of revenue but a claim on the metal itself. An outside party paid cash up front, often to help build the mine, in exchange for the right to receive a set share of the metal produced and to pay only a small fixed fraction of the market price for it - sometimes as little as a tenth or a fifth. The gap between that fixed price and the real price is the cost to the company, and it widens as metal prices rise. Like a royalty, a stream runs for the life of the mine unless bought back, which is possible only under the original terms or by agreement with the holder.

Prior outside claims on production: royalties and streams. LIGHT (0.96% of bad-year margin) One claim on production, newly measured. An outside company, Gold Royalty Corp, is entitled to all of the copper produced from the Rupice mine area at Vares, paying DPM 30 per cent of the market copper price for it. Copper is a minor metal at that mine - about 2 per cent of its revenue over the life of the mine - so the effect on the company as a whole is small: roughly 0.48 per cent of revenue, or about 1.0 per cent of what would be left over in a bad year for metal prices. It will grow as Vares reaches full output and the Ada Tepe mine finishes. The mines in Bulgaria pay state royalties as well, but those are a feature of the country rather than something the company sold, and are counted separately.

Glossary - every term, in plain words (tap to open)

Estimated value - What our model calculates one share is worth from documented evidence at a stated metal price and date. An estimate, not a prediction of where the stock will trade.

Cautious value (safety floor) - The deliberately careful of the two published values: stress-grade assumptions throughout. If the price is below even this number, the discount needs no generosity to see.

Fair value (market-based) - The second published value: what the company is worth using the yardstick the market actually applies to companies of this type across the Roster, with growth on its documented calendar. The verdict keys to this value.

Discount / premium at today's price - The gap between an estimated value and what a share costs today. Green (discount) = the share costs less than the value. Red (premium) = the price already exceeds the value.

Share price - What the market currently charges for one share, always shown with the date of the quote.

Trading below / near / above estimated value - The relationship between price and FAIR value. Below = the market charges less than the estimate (a discount). Above = the price already assumes future events (a pre-payment). Near = within a few percent.

The five-case deck - Value computed at five fixed cases of the company's own commodity price - Stress, Conservative Base, the dated Spot, Long-Term Normalized, Upside. We never forecast the metal; you bring your own view.

Value milestones - A calendar of dated events. Value steps only when an event lands and its inputs are released; the share price line is never forecast. Each step is a checkable claim.

Catalyst - A dated, verifiable event - a study, a permit, a financing - that releases new model inputs.

Pre-payment - When today's price already contains tomorrow's documents. Not automatically bad - but you should know you are doing it.

Quality tier / recalibrated rank - Company quality alone, from a 7-factor panel, placed on a 1-10 ladder where the Roster median is 5.0. It deliberately ignores price.

Symposium Top - The highest quality tier on the Roster ladder - the best-evidenced enterprises among an already elite set.

The Roster - The fixed set of companies covered - the presenting companies of a leading annual natural-resource investing symposium, itself a pre-selected elite of the roughly 2,000-3,000 mining companies worldwide, so every tier is standing among the select.

Release gate - A report is published only when every one of the 52 questions reaches a terminal answer - evidenced, documented as absent, or stage-exempt. No gaps hidden.

SOFT - A figure we could not confirm from a primary source, labeled honestly wherever it is used.

PEA / PFS / FS - The study ladder: Preliminary Economic Assessment (first economics), Pre-Feasibility (engineered), Feasibility (bankable). Each rung earns more credit in the model.

P/NAV (developers) - Price compared to a project's study value. Builders trade below 1.0 before production and re-rate through it as the mine becomes real.

Risk weight - The fraction of a project's study value the model credits today, by stage - small for early studies, larger once permitted and engineered.

AISC - All-in sustaining cost: what it costs to produce one ounce, all-in. The margin is the metal price minus this.

NSR royalty - A share of a mine's revenue off the top. Royalty companies own these instead of operating mines.

Streaming - Buying a mine's future silver or gold at a fixed low price in exchange for money upfront.

Earn-in - A contract where a partner pays for exploration to earn a share of a project - the generator model's engine.

Unanswered question - The one company-specific uncertainty the whole thesis hinges on, named explicitly in every report.

Royalty - A fixed percentage of a mine's revenue that goes to an outside holder rather than to the company, paid off the top - before costs, before debt, before shareholders see anything. It was sold once, usually years earlier, to raise cash. It runs for the life of the mine unless the company buys it back, which is possible only where the original agreement allows it at a set price or where the holder agrees to sell. Because it is charged on revenue and not on profit, it is still owed in a year when the mine loses money.

Stream - Not a percentage of revenue but a claim on the metal itself. An outside party paid cash up front, often to help build the mine, in exchange for the right to receive a set share of the metal produced and to pay only a small fixed fraction of the market price for it - sometimes as little as a tenth or a fifth. The gap between that fixed price and the real price is the cost to the company, and it widens as metal prices rise. Like a royalty, a stream runs for the life of the mine unless bought back, which is possible only under the original terms or by agreement with the holder.

The Story

One paragraph in plain words: what the company is, what it owns, and the central finding. If you read nothing else, read this.

IC summary: the critical-minerals royalty company mid-metamorphosis - the legacy Kestrel coking-coal royalty is running off exactly as telegraphed while base metals surge past it: H1 2026 portfolio contribution of $31.3M (Q1 +105%, Q2 +60% year over year) led by a RECORD Voisey's Bay cobalt quarter ($10.0M on 196 tonnes at $28.30/lb, with mine life extended to 2044), Mantos Blancos and Mimbula copper streams building, Four Mile uranium steady, and net debt cut from $124.6M to $74.9M in twelve months. The market prices the caterpillar, not the butterfly: ~0.8x NAV against royalty peers near 1.9x. At GBP 1.30 the model reads -10.0% at spot with the re-rating tied to a dated, visible event - the completion of the coal runoff.

Real, dated, and offsetting portfolio transactions: acquired the Mimbula royalty interest, directly driving net debt from $82.3 million to $124.6 million and leverage from 1.5x to 2.5x (metric 5) by mid-2025; separately sold the Dugbe royalty for $16.5 million in proceeds, explicitly earmarked to help deleverage the balance sheet built up from the Mimbula purchase - a real, disclosed buy-and-sell rebalancing within the same year, not one-directional growth.

The company has no direct mining production costs; it does disclose the average realized sales price for its uranium royalty payments, which rose to $7.47/lb in H1 2025 from $6.59/lb in H1 2024 (metric 30) - a real, specific, favorable price trend for that particular royalty stream.

A real, named development-stage royalty asset with current, specific technical progress: the Phalaborwa rare earths project (operated by Rainbow Rare Earths, in which Ecora holds a 0.85% Gross Revenue Royalty, rising to 1.10% if commercial production has not begun by July 1, 2028) reported that pilot-plant test work has optimized and simplified the process flow sheet as part of an ongoing Definitive Feasibility Study - real, current, and specific third-party technical progress on a royalty Ecora will benefit from once production begins.

17. Balance-sheet resilience [Complete · score 2 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Real, disclosed, and moderate corporate financial strength despite the recent leverage increase: analyst commentary describes Ecora's balance sheet as "strong" and positioned to further diversify the portfolio through acquisitions, and the company maintains a formulaic dividend policy (metric 18) rather than one requiring precarious cash preservation. Months of cash runway and funding gap to the next milestone were not separately quantified this pass, per the sharpened requirement for this metric.

18. Capital allocation [Complete · score 2 (of 10; 1 = best)]
A real, formulaic, and currently active dividend policy: the company targets paying out 25-35% of free cash flow as dividends, with a final 2025 dividend of 1.40 cents per share approved at the June 4, 2026 AGM (payable July 31, 2026) - a genuinely different capital-return structure than the flat-per-share approach used by several other royalty companies reviewed in this project, directly tying shareholder payouts to actual cash generation rather than a fixed commitment.

19. Run-rate normalization [Complete · score 2 (of 10; 1 = best)]
The real, disclosed H1 2025 revenue collapse (down 68% year-over-year) directly attributable to Kestrel's production timing shift (metric 12), followed by a real full-year 2025 recovery to net income of $22.2 million and EPS of $0.089 (versus a loss the prior year), is itself direct, dated evidence of why this metric matters - the interim results alone would have badly understated the company's actual annual performance.

Dilution: 249.45M shares essentially static - only periodic small treasury-share transfers for compensation identified; the balance-sheet repair is being done with cash flow, not paper.

44. Debt structure, covenants, and refinancing [Complete · score 2 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Real, specific, and recently-increased debt: net debt rose from $82.3 million to $124.6 million (leverage from 1.5x to 2.5x) following the Mimbula acquisition (metric 5/10), with the company explicitly stating that H2 cash flow, plus the real $16.5 million Dugbe sale proceeds, "should drive further deleveraging" - a real, disclosed, and time-bound deleveraging plan, not an open-ended concern.

45. Litigation, regulatory, and contingent liabilities [Complete · score 3 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Litigation: none material identified; the Dugbe royalty sale ($16.5M upfront plus up to $3.5M contingent) closed cleanly; portfolio agreements conventional.

46. Insurance adequacy [Not Available - Documented]
Consistent with standard practice, no insurance program terms are disclosed in any public source reviewed this pass.

47. Concentration, correlation, and single-point-of-failure risk [Complete · score 2 (of 10; 1 = best)]
A real, genuinely diversified royalty portfolio across more than ten named commodities and multiple continents (metric 27/31) provides real, structural concentration mitigation, though the real, disclosed H1 2025 revenue volatility tied to a single asset (Kestrel, metric 12) shows that diversification does not fully eliminate single-counterparty timing risk.

48. Revenue realization, offtake, and payable metal [Complete · score 1 (of 10; 1 = best)]
As a royalty and streaming company, Ecora's revenue realization is structurally simple - fixed royalty percentages or per-unit stream payments from named counterparties (Cameco, Rainbow Rare Earths, and others, metric 16/30/31) - rather than direct exposure to smelter or refining deductions a producer would face.

49. Forecast governance and model governance [Complete · score 2 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Forecast governance: cobalt guidance stated (500-560t for 2026) and held; Kestrel tonnage and timing guided in advance (1.0-1.2mt, H2-weighted) and delivering; a published 2026-2030 forward outlook frames the transition - unusually auditable for the sector.

50. Management incentives and conflicts [Complete · score 3 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Incentives: professional management under UK governance executing a stated multi-year strategy without deviation; compensation not proxy-deep-dived - scored mid; the strategy's discipline (selling non-core gold to fund critical-minerals deleveraging) is itself alignment evidence.

51. Corporate structure, subsidiary mapping, and entity-level solvency [Complete · score 2 (of 10; 1 = best)]
A real, unusually long and distinctive corporate history: the company was originally founded in 1967 as "Diversified Bank Shares Limited," a financial entity with no original connection to mining, before its eventual transformation into a natural-resource royalty company and its most recent rename to Ecora Royalties PLC (metric 38) - a genuinely unusual corporate lineage compared to every other company reviewed in this project.

52. Reserve-price sensitivity, cut-off migration, and economic-envelope robustness [Complete · score 3 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Reserve-price sensitivity: the royalty model externalizes cut-off risk to operators; the portfolio's duration evidence is positive - Voisey's Bay extended to 2044, Mantos expanding, Mimbula expanding - operators are investing INTO Ecora's royalty ground.

53. Technical-report currency, competent-person reliance, and study obsolescence [Not Applicable - Operator's Risk]
Technical-report currency for the underlying assets sits with the mine operators, who prepare and control those reports; the company does not publish or control them.

54. Geological reconciliation, grade control, metallurgical accounting, and reserve performance [Not Applicable - Operator's Risk]
Geological reconciliation is the responsibility of each underlying mine operator, not Ecora directly.

55. Water balance, water security, climate resilience, and extreme weather [Not Applicable - Operator's Risk]
Water balance and climate resilience at underlying mine and project sites are the responsibility of each operator, not Ecora directly.

56. Tailings-facility integrity, geotechnical stability, and emergency preparedness [Not Applicable - Operator's Risk]
Tailings-facility integrity at underlying mine sites is the responsibility of each operator, not Ecora directly.

57. Valuation-method hierarchy, asset-level NAV governance, discount-rate discipline, and double-counting prevention [Complete · score 2 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Valuation governance: single-method contribution-multiple model; net debt subtracted once; the GEO-equivalence simplification, the 11x multiple and the run-rate estimate all flagged soft; the peer-NAV gap reported as documented context, not adopted as the model. Glossary - every term, in plain words (tap to open)

Estimated value - What our model calculates one share is worth from documented evidence at a stated metal price and date. An estimate, not a prediction of where the stock will trade.

Cautious value (safety floor) - The deliberately careful of the two published values: stress-grade assumptions throughout. If the price is below even this number, the discount needs no generosity to see.

Fair value (market-based) - The second published value: what the company is worth using the yardstick the market actually applies to companies of this type across the Roster, with growth on its documented calendar. The verdict keys to this value.

Discount / premium at today's price - The gap between an estimated value and what a share costs today. Green (discount) = the share costs less than the value. Red (premium) = the price already exceeds the value.

Share price - What the market currently charges for one share, always shown with the date of the quote.

Trading below / near / above estimated value - The relationship between price and FAIR value. Below = the market charges less than the estimate (a discount). Above = the price already assumes future events (a pre-payment). Near = within a few percent.

The five-case deck - Value computed at five fixed cases of the company's own commodity price - Stress, Conservative Base, the dated Spot, Long-Term Normalized, Upside. We never forecast the metal; you bring your own view.

Value milestones - A calendar of dated events. Value steps only when an event lands and its inputs are released; the share price line is never forecast. Each step is a checkable claim.

Catalyst - A dated, verifiable event - a study, a permit, a financing - that releases new model inputs.

Pre-payment - When today's price already contains tomorrow's documents. Not automatically bad - but you should know you are doing it.

Quality tier / recalibrated rank - Company quality alone, from a 7-factor panel, placed on a 1-10 ladder where the Roster median is 5.0. It deliberately ignores price.

Symposium Top - The highest quality tier on the Roster ladder - the best-evidenced enterprises among an already elite set.

The Roster - The fixed set of companies covered - the presenting companies of a leading annual natural-resource investing symposium, itself a pre-selected elite of the roughly 2,000-3,000 mining companies worldwide, so every tier is standing among the select.

Release gate - A report is published only when every one of the 52 questions reaches a terminal answer - evidenced, documented as absent, or stage-exempt. No gaps hidden.

SOFT - A figure we could not confirm from a primary source, labeled honestly wherever it is used.

PEA / PFS / FS - The study ladder: Preliminary Economic Assessment (first economics), Pre-Feasibility (engineered), Feasibility (bankable). Each rung earns more credit in the model.

P/NAV (developers) - Price compared to a project's study value. Builders trade below 1.0 before production and re-rate through it as the mine becomes real.

Risk weight - The fraction of a project's study value the model credits today, by stage - small for early studies, larger once permitted and engineered.

AISC - All-in sustaining cost: what it costs to produce one ounce, all-in. The margin is the metal price minus this.

NSR royalty - A share of a mine's revenue off the top. Royalty companies own these instead of operating mines.

Streaming - Buying a mine's future silver or gold at a fixed low price in exchange for money upfront.

Earn-in - A contract where a partner pays for exploration to earn a share of a project - the generator model's engine.

Unanswered question - The one company-specific uncertainty the whole thesis hinges on, named explicitly in every report.

Royalty - A fixed percentage of a mine's revenue that goes to an outside holder rather than to the company, paid off the top - before costs, before debt, before shareholders see anything. It was sold once, usually years earlier, to raise cash. It runs for the life of the mine unless the company buys it back, which is possible only where the original agreement allows it at a set price or where the holder agrees to sell. Because it is charged on revenue and not on profit, it is still owed in a year when the mine loses money.

Stream - Not a percentage of revenue but a claim on the metal itself. An outside party paid cash up front, often to help build the mine, in exchange for the right to receive a set share of the metal produced and to pay only a small fixed fraction of the market price for it - sometimes as little as a tenth or a fifth. The gap between that fixed price and the real price is the cost to the company, and it widens as metal prices rise. Like a royalty, a stream runs for the life of the mine unless bought back, which is possible only under the original terms or by agreement with the holder.

Glossary - every term, in plain words (tap to open)

Estimated value - What our model calculates one share is worth from documented evidence at a stated metal price and date. An estimate, not a prediction of where the stock will trade.

Cautious value (safety floor) - The deliberately careful of the two published values: stress-grade assumptions throughout. If the price is below even this number, the discount needs no generosity to see.

Fair value (market-based) - The second published value: what the company is worth using the yardstick the market actually applies to companies of this type across the Roster, with growth on its documented calendar. The verdict keys to this value.

Discount / premium at today's price - The gap between an estimated value and what a share costs today. Green (discount) = the share costs less than the value. Red (premium) = the price already exceeds the value.

Share price - What the market currently charges for one share, always shown with the date of the quote.

Trading below / near / above estimated value - The relationship between price and FAIR value. Below = the market charges less than the estimate (a discount). Above = the price already assumes future events (a pre-payment). Near = within a few percent.

The five-case deck - Value computed at five fixed cases of the company's own commodity price - Stress, Conservative Base, the dated Spot, Long-Term Normalized, Upside. We never forecast the metal; you bring your own view.

Value milestones - A calendar of dated events. Value steps only when an event lands and its inputs are released; the share price line is never forecast. Each step is a checkable claim.

Catalyst - A dated, verifiable event - a study, a permit, a financing - that releases new model inputs.

Pre-payment - When today's price already contains tomorrow's documents. Not automatically bad - but you should know you are doing it.

Quality tier / recalibrated rank - Company quality alone, from a 7-factor panel, placed on a 1-10 ladder where the Roster median is 5.0. It deliberately ignores price.

Symposium Top - The highest quality tier on the Roster ladder - the best-evidenced enterprises among an already elite set.

The Roster - The fixed set of companies covered - the presenting companies of a leading annual natural-resource investing symposium, itself a pre-selected elite of the roughly 2,000-3,000 mining companies worldwide, so every tier is standing among the select.

Release gate - A report is published only when every one of the 52 questions reaches a terminal answer - evidenced, documented as absent, or stage-exempt. No gaps hidden.

SOFT - A figure we could not confirm from a primary source, labeled honestly wherever it is used.

PEA / PFS / FS - The study ladder: Preliminary Economic Assessment (first economics), Pre-Feasibility (engineered), Feasibility (bankable). Each rung earns more credit in the model.

P/NAV (developers) - Price compared to a project's study value. Builders trade below 1.0 before production and re-rate through it as the mine becomes real.

Risk weight - The fraction of a project's study value the model credits today, by stage - small for early studies, larger once permitted and engineered.

AISC - All-in sustaining cost: what it costs to produce one ounce, all-in. The margin is the metal price minus this.

NSR royalty - A share of a mine's revenue off the top. Royalty companies own these instead of operating mines.

Streaming - Buying a mine's future silver or gold at a fixed low price in exchange for money upfront.

Earn-in - A contract where a partner pays for exploration to earn a share of a project - the generator model's engine.

Unanswered question - The one company-specific uncertainty the whole thesis hinges on, named explicitly in every report.

Royalty - A fixed percentage of a mine's revenue that goes to an outside holder rather than to the company, paid off the top - before costs, before debt, before shareholders see anything. It was sold once, usually years earlier, to raise cash. It runs for the life of the mine unless the company buys it back, which is possible only where the original agreement allows it at a set price or where the holder agrees to sell. Because it is charged on revenue and not on profit, it is still owed in a year when the mine loses money.

Stream - Not a percentage of revenue but a claim on the metal itself. An outside party paid cash up front, often to help build the mine, in exchange for the right to receive a set share of the metal produced and to pay only a small fixed fraction of the market price for it - sometimes as little as a tenth or a fifth. The gap between that fixed price and the real price is the cost to the company, and it widens as metal prices rise. Like a royalty, a stream runs for the life of the mine unless bought back, which is possible only under the original terms or by agreement with the holder.

The Story

One paragraph in plain words: what the company is, what it owns, and the central finding. If you read nothing else, read this.

INVESTMENT COMMITTEE SUMMARY (July 31, 2026). Empress is the project's micro-cap royalty CREATOR: rather than buying existing royalties at auction, Alexandra Woodyer Sherron's team writes new streams onto small producers' assets at the moment they need construction capital - US$10 million into Sierra Antapite's Peruvian expansion, US$5 million finishing Tahuehueto's build (the LUCA mine this project underwrote in wave six), US$3.5 million carrying Manica to production in Mozambique, the Galaxy gold stream in South Africa, and the Pinos NSR in Mexico. The model just proved itself: first-quarter revenue of US$9.06 million against US$2.70 million a year earlier, gross profit of US$6.75 million, record 2025 behind it, and 2026 guidance of 7,045-7,430 gold-equivalent ounces reiterated - stated at deliberately conservative US$4,000 gold and US$70 silver conversions. At C$1.00 on 134 million shares the market pays roughly a sixth below the model's dated-spot value - the micro-cap royalty discount in a sector where scale itself is the multiple.

Where narrative text carries an older share price, the tables and the refreshed dated close above govern.

The model is a GEO-margin construction: guided gold-equivalent ounces times the gold case at a stream-level gross margin (transfer payments netted), less corporate costs, taxed and multiplied at a royalty-company rating discounted for micro-cap scale - the same family as NRC and ECOR, with the guidance conservatism (GEOs stated at US$4,000 gold and US$70 silver) noted as a built-in cushion.

The valuation-to-action bridge shows the micro-cap royalty discount plainly: modelled value sits about 18% ABOVE the quote at the dated spot gold case, above at long-term and upside, modestly below at base, further below only at stress - a royalty cash-flow stream trading beneath its own arithmetic because 134 million shares of TSX-Venture float cannot buy the sector's scale multiple. The action logic is growth-into-rerating: each delivered guidance year and each new stream compounds toward the size where royalty paper reprices.

22. Thesis-break framework [Complete · score 1 (of 10; 1 = best)]
The clearest thesis-break condition is one or more of the "ramping up or nearing production" mines underlying Empress's royalty and stream portfolio failing to stay on schedule or deliver as promised - a real, independently-flagged risk (metric 12/16), not a hypothetical one, since Empress has no direct operational lever to fix an underperforming counterparty mine.

26. Peer-group methodology [Complete · score 3 (of 10; 1 = best)]
The peer frame is the junior royalty tier (Gold Royalty, Elemental Altus lineage, Vox), where sub-US$150 million royalty companies persistently trade at deep NAV discounts to the FNV-WPM tier's premiums - the sector's best-documented size effect. In-project, the comparison set is exact: FNV at the premium extreme (the project's 2.0 benchmark), NRC's Indigenous platform at 2.4, ECOR's portfolio at 2.2 - and Empress the smallest and highest-torque of the family, priced accordingly.

27. Jurisdiction, fiscal regime, and permitting [Complete · score 4 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Jurisdictional exposure is deliberately frontier-weighted: producing assets in Peru, Mexico (two), Mozambique and South Africa - a portfolio built where capital is scarce and stream pricing therefore generous, which is the strategy's engine and its risk in one design. Mozambique's post-2024 political volatility and Mexico's permitting freeze are the live files; the royalty structure insulates from operating cost inflation but not from operator interruption, priced at metric 47.

28. Environmental liability, reclamation, closure, and tailings [Not Applicable - Operator's Risk]
As a royalty and streaming company with no mining operations of its own, Empress carries no direct reclamation or environmental-liability obligations - those sit with each underlying operator.

29. Reserve/resource quality [Complete · score 4 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Resource foundations beneath the portfolio are small-producer grade: Sierra Antapite's high-grade Peruvian veins, Tahuehueto's epithermal system (whose reserve currency this project scored at LUCA's metric 53), Manica's greenstone oxides, Galaxy's Barberton-belt underground - real deposits with modest published statements and limited independent verification at the royalty level. The metric scores the portfolio's documentary thinness, not the operators' geology; stream diligence files are private by nature.

30. Exploration effectiveness [Not Applicable - Operator's Risk]
Empress does not conduct its own mineral exploration; portfolio growth comes from originating and structuring royalty and streaming positions, not discovery.

31. Ownership, royalties, streams, and joint ventures [Complete · score 2 (of 10; 1 = best)]
A real, distinctive structural relationship not seen at every royalty company reviewed in this project: a stated strategic partnership with Endeavour Financial, explicitly described as giving Empress access to global investment opportunities plus mining-finance expertise, deal-structuring capability, and capital-markets access - a real, named, and specific sourcing advantage beyond the company's own internal resources.

32. Commodity-price, FX, and inflation assumption governance [Complete · score 3 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Assumption governance is genuinely conservative where it counts: GEO guidance stated at US$4,000 gold and US$70 silver conversions (below both dated spot prices - the guidance understates ounces if metals hold), the delivery-versus-sales timing distinctions disclosed carefully, and the reliance on operator forecasts (including non-public information the company holds under confidentiality) stated plainly with its limits. The workbook's margin and multiple are its own SOFT constructions, labeled.

33. Tax, royalties, and fiscal losses [Complete · score 3 (of 10; 1 = best)]
The fiscal frame is multi-jurisdictional at one remove: streams and royalties are taxed at the Canadian parent on receipts, with withholding and transfer arrangements per asset country embedded in the netted margins, and no dispute identified. The royalty structure's fiscal virtue - no exposure to operator-level cost or tax escalation beyond the contract - is intact across all five paying assets.

34. Production profile, depletion, and replacement [Complete · score 2 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Real, specific, and forward-dated production guidance: 2026 guidance of 7,045 to 7,430 attributable Gold Equivalent Ounces, explicitly signaling further growth supported by "ongoing production from key assets" - genuine, quantified forward planning, not vague forward-looking language.

35. Operating reliability [Not Applicable - Operator's Risk]
Operating reliability belongs to the underlying mine and project operators in Empress's royalty and stream portfolio, not Empress directly.

36. Safety, workforce, and labor [Not Applicable - Operator's Risk]
Empress has no mine-site workforce of its own; safety performance at underlying operations is the responsibility of each operator.

37. Community relations and social licence [Not Applicable - Operator's Risk]
Community relations at underlying mine and project sites are the responsibility of each operator, not Empress directly.

38. Disclosure quality, reporting integrity, and governance [Complete · score 2 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Disclosure practice is strong for the tier: quarterly results with per-asset revenue context, GEO guidance with its conversion assumptions and timing caveats stated, the operator-dependence risk described honestly (including the confidentiality-bound information asymmetry), stream amendments disclosed as they occur (the Tahuehueto stream updates through Luca's turnaround), and an unusually communicative investor program. The record supports the creation model's core claim: this team documents its deals.

39. Infrastructure, utilities, logistics, and business continuity [Not Applicable - Operator's Risk]
Infrastructure dependency (power, water, roads, ports) sits with the underlying mine operators; the company holds no operating infrastructure of its own.

40. Cybersecurity, operational technology, and data integrity [Not Available - Documented]
No cybersecurity disclosure was located - standard at this scale, and largely an operator-level risk in the royalty model.

41. Hedging, derivatives, and counterparty risk [Complete · score 3 (of 10; 1 = best)]
The portfolio IS the counterparty book: five small operators (Sierra Sun's private Peruvian unit, Luca, Manica's operator, Galaxy's, Pinos') whose delivery obligations are secured by stream contracts over assets, not by balance sheets - counterparty risk concentrated exactly where the pricing edge comes from. The Nebari facility adds a lender relationship (the same fund this project met at WRLG). No hedging; the streams are the exposure by design.

42. Working capital, cash conversion, and liquidity quality [Complete · score 2 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Real, positive, and quantified cash-conversion evidence: full-year 2025 positive operating cash flow of $3.7 million (metric 17), alongside a real current ratio of 2.65 (metric 5) - genuine, disclosed liquidity strength.

Dilution has been the growth currency and is decelerating: 134 million shares carry the portfolio's construction era, with strategic placements (Gleason & Sons) rather than broad raises the recent pattern, and the credit facility substituting for equity at the margin. The forward test is whether operating cash flow now funds new streams without the share count compounding faster than GEOs - the crossover the 2026 guidance year is designed to demonstrate.

A low Debt/Equity ratio of 0.15 (metric 5) indicates minimal debt-structure risk for this company at this time.

No litigation was identified in the sources reviewed. The contingent inventory is contract-structural: five stream and royalty agreements whose security packages, delivery cure mechanics and amendment histories (Tahuehueto's through Luca's restructuring era) are the company's real asset register, plus the Nebari facility's covenants. Each contract performed through 2025-26, including the one this project independently stress-read from the operator's side at LUCA.

46. Insurance adequacy [Not Available - Documented]
Consistent with standard practice, no insurance program terms are disclosed in any public source reviewed this pass.

Portfolio concentration is real but genuinely diversified for the size: five paying assets across four countries, with revenue weighted to Sierra Antapite and Tahuehueto - two assets carrying most of the book, either's interruption material, neither fatal. Among the project's royalty underwritings this sits between ECOR's breadth and a single-asset stream, scored accordingly.

48. Revenue realization, offtake, and payable metal [Complete · score 1 (of 10; 1 = best)]
As a royalty and streaming company, Empress's revenue realization is structurally simple - fixed royalty percentages or stream payments from underlying counterparties - rather than direct exposure to smelter or refining deductions a producer would face.

49. Forecast governance and model governance [Complete · score 2 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Real, specific, and dated forward guidance was issued for 2026 (GEO output, metric 34) alongside the full-year 2025 results release - genuine, quantified forecasting practice.

50. Management incentives and conflicts [Complete · score 3 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Incentives are creator-aligned: Woodyer Sherron has led since inception with the portfolio her personal track record, management equity rides the rerating case, strategic holders (Gleason & Sons increasing through results) anchor the register, and option grants are disclosed as issued. No insider selling of note was identified. The concentration note: the deal pipeline is substantially one team's relationships - key-person exposure the tier always carries.

51. Corporate structure, subsidiary mapping, and entity-level solvency [Complete · score 2 (of 10; 1 = best)]
The corporate structure is royalty-clean: a Canadian parent holding stream and royalty contracts directly, no operating subsidiaries with their liabilities, the Nebari facility the single debt instrument at a 0.15 debt-to-equity ratio, and the exploration-royalty shelf (Coldstream and peers) carried at zero cost. Entity solvency is straightforward and improving with the revenue ramp.

52. Reserve-price sensitivity, cut-off migration, and economic-envelope robustness [Complete · score 3 (of 10; 1 = best)]
The economic envelope is the royalty model's structural gift: stream margins insulated from operator cost inflation by contract (transfer payments fixed or formulaic), gross profit of US$6.75 million on US$9.06 million of Q1 revenue evidencing the margin capture, and the guidance conservatism adding a metals cushion on top. The envelope's soft spot is corporate scale: fixed costs consume a larger revenue share than at any senior, which is precisely what growth cures.

Technical-report currency for the underlying assets sits with the mine operators, who prepare and control those reports; the company does not publish or control them.

Geological reconciliation is the responsibility of each underlying mine operator, not Empress directly.

55. Water balance, water security, climate resilience, and extreme weather [Not Applicable - Operator's Risk]
Water balance and climate resilience at underlying mine and project sites are the responsibility of each operator, not Empress directly.

56. Tailings-facility integrity, geotechnical stability, and emergency preparedness [Not Applicable - Operator's Risk]
Tailings-facility integrity at underlying mine sites is the responsibility of each operator, not Empress directly.
