The valuation hierarchy is explicit: guided GEOs at the midpoint, priced per gold case at a SOFT stream-level gross margin, less corporate costs, taxed, at a deliberately sub-sector multiple for micro-cap scale, net of SOFT facility drawings - with the exploration-royalty shelf, future stream creations, guidance conservatism and any rerating toward sector multiples all carried at ZERO as the anti-double-counting offset, released only on the dated staircase. The creation pipeline - the actual business - is by construction unpriced until signed.

Conclusion governance is satisfied for release: every scored metric resolved, the single absence documented, the SOFT margin, multiple and facility-drawing labeled, the operator-dependence asymmetry stated, and the finding - a working royalty creator trading below its own arithmetic for want of scale, with the smallest denominator and highest per-deal torque in the project's royalty family - stated identically in summary, bridge and hierarchy. Authorized with the guidance year's delivery and the next stream signing as the standing checkpoints.

CEO and President Alexandra Woodyer Sherron has been the continuous, named voice across every result reviewed in this pass, presiding over the real, verified 2025 revenue doubling and margin expansion (metric 17/19); a full independently-verified, role-specific track-record evaluation per the consultation document's standard was not performed this pass. Glossary - every term, in plain words (tap to open)

Estimated value - What our model calculates one share is worth from documented evidence at a stated metal price and date. An estimate, not a prediction of where the stock will trade.

Cautious value (safety floor) - The deliberately careful of the two published values: stress-grade assumptions throughout. If the price is below even this number, the discount needs no generosity to see.

Fair value (market-based) - The second published value: what the company is worth using the yardstick the market actually applies to companies of this type across the Roster, with growth on its documented calendar. The verdict keys to this value.

Discount / premium at today's price - The gap between an estimated value and what a share costs today. Green (discount) = the share costs less than the value. Red (premium) = the price already exceeds the value.

Share price - What the market currently charges for one share, always shown with the date of the quote.

Trading below / near / above estimated value - The relationship between price and FAIR value. Below = the market charges less than the estimate (a discount). Above = the price already assumes future events (a pre-payment). Near = within a few percent.

The five-case deck - Value computed at five fixed cases of the company's own commodity price - Stress, Conservative Base, the dated Spot, Long-Term Normalized, Upside. We never forecast the metal; you bring your own view.

Value milestones - A calendar of dated events. Value steps only when an event lands and its inputs are released; the share price line is never forecast. Each step is a checkable claim.

Catalyst - A dated, verifiable event - a study, a permit, a financing - that releases new model inputs.

Pre-payment - When today's price already contains tomorrow's documents. Not automatically bad - but you should know you are doing it.

Quality tier / recalibrated rank - Company quality alone, from a 7-factor panel, placed on a 1-10 ladder where the Roster median is 5.0. It deliberately ignores price.

Symposium Top - The highest quality tier on the Roster ladder - the best-evidenced enterprises among an already elite set.

The Roster - The fixed set of companies covered - the presenting companies of a leading annual natural-resource investing symposium, itself a pre-selected elite of the roughly 2,000-3,000 mining companies worldwide, so every tier is standing among the select.

Release gate - A report is published only when every one of the 52 questions reaches a terminal answer - evidenced, documented as absent, or stage-exempt. No gaps hidden.

SOFT - A figure we could not confirm from a primary source, labeled honestly wherever it is used.

PEA / PFS / FS - The study ladder: Preliminary Economic Assessment (first economics), Pre-Feasibility (engineered), Feasibility (bankable). Each rung earns more credit in the model.

P/NAV (developers) - Price compared to a project's study value. Builders trade below 1.0 before production and re-rate through it as the mine becomes real.

Risk weight - The fraction of a project's study value the model credits today, by stage - small for early studies, larger once permitted and engineered.

AISC - All-in sustaining cost: what it costs to produce one ounce, all-in. The margin is the metal price minus this.

NSR royalty - A share of a mine's revenue off the top. Royalty companies own these instead of operating mines.

Streaming - Buying a mine's future silver or gold at a fixed low price in exchange for money upfront.

Earn-in - A contract where a partner pays for exploration to earn a share of a project - the generator model's engine.

Unanswered question - The one company-specific uncertainty the whole thesis hinges on, named explicitly in every report.

Royalty - A fixed percentage of a mine's revenue that goes to an outside holder rather than to the company, paid off the top - before costs, before debt, before shareholders see anything. It was sold once, usually years earlier, to raise cash. It runs for the life of the mine unless the company buys it back, which is possible only where the original agreement allows it at a set price or where the holder agrees to sell. Because it is charged on revenue and not on profit, it is still owed in a year when the mine loses money.

Stream - Not a percentage of revenue but a claim on the metal itself. An outside party paid cash up front, often to help build the mine, in exchange for the right to receive a set share of the metal produced and to pay only a small fixed fraction of the market price for it - sometimes as little as a tenth or a fifth. The gap between that fixed price and the real price is the cost to the company, and it widens as metal prices rise. Like a royalty, a stream runs for the life of the mine unless bought back, which is possible only under the original terms or by agreement with the holder.

Equinox Gold Corp. EQX (NYSE American / TSX) - USD

A multi-mine gold producer carrying heavy debt, whose story hinges on the Greenstone mine ramping to plan and the Los Filos complex returning to work.

Company quality: Median - 5.0 (out of 10; 1 = best), Roster median 5.0

RE-UNDERWRITTEN AUGUST 5, 2026
The combined-entity underwriting is complete, from the Q2 2026 results and updated consolidated guidance published after market close on August 5. Production is stated on a full-year run-rate basis built from the company's own per-asset guidance, because the headline 870,000-920,000 ounce figure covers only five months of the assets acquired from Orla and would understate the business against a full post-merger share count. The last verified price is the August 1 close, so the market has not yet traded on this guidance.

Prior outside claims on production: royalties and streams. NOT MEASURABLE Partly measured, and the unmeasured part is the larger one. On the assets inherited from Orla Mining on 31 July 2026, Camino Rojo carries a 2% net smelter return royalty on oxide material, sold to Maverix Metals in October 2021 and now held by Triple Flag Precious Metals, which is not a Roster company; South Railroad carries a 3% royalty in favour of Sandstorm Gold over ground acquired with Contact Gold, and it is not yet producing; no royalty or stream has been found over Musselwhite, which is recorded as not found rather than as none, because the mine was bought from Newmont and a vendor royalty would sit in the purchase agreement rather than in news flow. Camino Rojo is about a eighth of run-rate production, so this measured burden is light against the company as a whole. The legacy Equinox assets have not yet been checked for royalties of their own, so no company-wide figure is published: a number covering an eighth of the mines would read as though the other seven-eighths were free of claims, and that has not been established. Mexican state mining duties are a feature of the country rather than something sold, and are carried separately. One further obligation is recorded outside this line because it is not a share of revenue: Orla received US$360.8 million in 2025 under an arrangement repaid in gold rather than cash, and at 31 March 2026 the amount still owed under that arrangement together with a streaming obligation stood at US$271.1 million. The 5 August results do not restate it, and the company's headline net cash figure of US$214 million is calculated from drawn debt, which does not include it. Taken at the March figure the company would be in net debt rather than net cash, a swing of about 23 US cents a share; the true figure is lower than that because four months of gold has since been delivered against it. Both ends are stated here because only both ends are documented.

The Story

One paragraph in plain words: what the company is, what it owns, and the central finding. If you read nothing else, read this.

Decision summary: the mid-tier slot's shape-shifter - two transformational mergers in thirteen months (Calibre, then Orla closing on this workbook's valuation date, metric 10) built North America's newest ~1.1 Moz/yr senior producer with >60% of production from three long-life Canadian mines and a stated path past 1.9 Moz (metric 34). The quality case is scale, diversification (metric 47) and a repaired balance sheet (metrics 17/44); the honest costs are a structurally high AISC (metric 15), serial dilution (metric 43), live Mexico/Nicaragua social-fiscal exposure (metrics 27/37) and a CEO handover mid-integration (metric 59).

Glossary - every term, in plain words (tap to open)

Estimated value - What our model calculates one share is worth from documented evidence at a stated metal price and date. An estimate, not a prediction of where the stock will trade.

Cautious value (safety floor) - The deliberately careful of the two published values: stress-grade assumptions throughout. If the price is below even this number, the discount needs no generosity to see.

Fair value (market-based) - The second published value: what the company is worth using the yardstick the market actually applies to companies of this type across the Roster, with growth on its documented calendar. The verdict keys to this value.

Discount / premium at today's price - The gap between an estimated value and what a share costs today. Green (discount) = the share costs less than the value. Red (premium) = the price already exceeds the value.

Share price - What the market currently charges for one share, always shown with the date of the quote.

Trading below / near / above estimated value - The relationship between price and FAIR value. Below = the market charges less than the estimate (a discount). Above = the price already assumes future events (a pre-payment). Near = within a few percent.

The five-case deck - Value computed at five fixed cases of the company's own commodity price - Stress, Conservative Base, the dated Spot, Long-Term Normalized, Upside. We never forecast the metal; you bring your own view.

Value milestones - A calendar of dated events. Value steps only when an event lands and its inputs are released; the share price line is never forecast. Each step is a checkable claim.

Catalyst - A dated, verifiable event - a study, a permit, a financing - that releases new model inputs.

Pre-payment - When today's price already contains tomorrow's documents. Not automatically bad - but you should know you are doing it.

Quality tier / recalibrated rank - Company quality alone, from a 7-factor panel, placed on a 1-10 ladder where the Roster median is 5.0. It deliberately ignores price.

Symposium Top - The highest quality tier on the Roster ladder - the best-evidenced enterprises among an already elite set.

The Roster - The fixed set of companies covered - the presenting companies of a leading annual natural-resource investing symposium, itself a pre-selected elite of the roughly 2,000-3,000 mining companies worldwide, so every tier is standing among the select.

Release gate - A report is published only when every one of the 52 questions reaches a terminal answer - evidenced, documented as absent, or stage-exempt. No gaps hidden.

SOFT - A figure we could not confirm from a primary source, labeled honestly wherever it is used.

PEA / PFS / FS - The study ladder: Preliminary Economic Assessment (first economics), Pre-Feasibility (engineered), Feasibility (bankable). Each rung earns more credit in the model.

P/NAV (developers) - Price compared to a project's study value. Builders trade below 1.0 before production and re-rate through it as the mine becomes real.

Risk weight - The fraction of a project's study value the model credits today, by stage - small for early studies, larger once permitted and engineered.

AISC - All-in sustaining cost: what it costs to produce one ounce, all-in. The margin is the metal price minus this.

NSR royalty - A share of a mine's revenue off the top. Royalty companies own these instead of operating mines.

Streaming - Buying a mine's future silver or gold at a fixed low price in exchange for money upfront.

Earn-in - A contract where a partner pays for exploration to earn a share of a project - the generator model's engine.

Unanswered question - The one company-specific uncertainty the whole thesis hinges on, named explicitly in every report.

Royalty - A fixed percentage of a mine's revenue that goes to an outside holder rather than to the company, paid off the top - before costs, before debt, before shareholders see anything. It was sold once, usually years earlier, to raise cash. It runs for the life of the mine unless the company buys it back, which is possible only where the original agreement allows it at a set price or where the holder agrees to sell. Because it is charged on revenue and not on profit, it is still owed in a year when the mine loses money.

Stream - Not a percentage of revenue but a claim on the metal itself. An outside party paid cash up front, often to help build the mine, in exchange for the right to receive a set share of the metal produced and to pay only a small fixed fraction of the market price for it - sometimes as little as a tenth or a fifth. The gap between that fixed price and the real price is the cost to the company, and it widens as metal prices rise. Like a royalty, a stream runs for the life of the mine unless bought back, which is possible only under the original terms or by agreement with the holder.

The Story

One paragraph in plain words: what the company is, what it owns, and the central finding. If you read nothing else, read this.

INVESTMENT COMMITTEE SUMMARY (July 31, 2026). First Mining is the batch's freshest inflection: on June 30, 2026 - one month before this valuation date - Springpole received its FEDERAL Environmental Assessment approval after an eight-and-a-half-year regulatory journey, on the strength of something genuinely novel: an independent Anishinaabe-Led Impact Assessment by Cat Lake and Lac Seul First Nations, whose communities VOTED on June 4 to authorize the project. One of Canada's largest undeveloped gold resources (updated PFS November 2025: US$2.1 billion after-tax NPV and 40% IRR at US$3,100 gold, 300,000-plus ounces annually, sub-two-year payback) now awaits only the Ontario provincial decision targeted by end of summer 2026, with feasibility mid-2027 and an eighteen-month path to a construction decision. Management's own framing of the gap - roughly $50-60 per resource ounce against $300-400 for permitted developers - is promotional but directionally real: the model below puts value above the quote in every deck case except stress, where it lands within pennies.

In-project, the instructive comparators are SGD (elite Yukon ounces pre-paid at a premium on quality) and BYN (Yukon ounces at a post-accident discount): this name holds a middle claim - approved Ontario ounces at an explorer's price - and the batch's cleanest test of whether permits alone re-rate.

The Anishinaabe-Led Impact Assessment adds a second, community-authored compliance layer the company must honour alongside the federal conditions. Nothing is built; the obligations are contractual and conditional, now finally defined rather than speculative.

Glossary - every term, in plain words (tap to open)

Estimated value - What our model calculates one share is worth from documented evidence at a stated metal price and date. An estimate, not a prediction of where the stock will trade.

Cautious value (safety floor) - The deliberately careful of the two published values: stress-grade assumptions throughout. If the price is below even this number, the discount needs no generosity to see.

Fair value (market-based) - The second published value: what the company is worth using the yardstick the market actually applies to companies of this type across the Roster, with growth on its documented calendar. The verdict keys to this value.

Discount / premium at today's price - The gap between an estimated value and what a share costs today. Green (discount) = the share costs less than the value. Red (premium) = the price already exceeds the value.

Share price - What the market currently charges for one share, always shown with the date of the quote.

Trading below / near / above estimated value - The relationship between price and FAIR value. Below = the market charges less than the estimate (a discount). Above = the price already assumes future events (a pre-payment). Near = within a few percent.

The five-case deck - Value computed at five fixed cases of the company's own commodity price - Stress, Conservative Base, the dated Spot, Long-Term Normalized, Upside. We never forecast the metal; you bring your own view.

Value milestones - A calendar of dated events. Value steps only when an event lands and its inputs are released; the share price line is never forecast. Each step is a checkable claim.

Catalyst - A dated, verifiable event - a study, a permit, a financing - that releases new model inputs.

Pre-payment - When today's price already contains tomorrow's documents. Not automatically bad - but you should know you are doing it.

Quality tier / recalibrated rank - Company quality alone, from a 7-factor panel, placed on a 1-10 ladder where the Roster median is 5.0. It deliberately ignores price.

Symposium Top - The highest quality tier on the Roster ladder - the best-evidenced enterprises among an already elite set.

The Roster - The fixed set of companies covered - the presenting companies of a leading annual natural-resource investing symposium, itself a pre-selected elite of the roughly 2,000-3,000 mining companies worldwide, so every tier is standing among the select.

Release gate - A report is published only when every one of the 52 questions reaches a terminal answer - evidenced, documented as absent, or stage-exempt. No gaps hidden.

SOFT - A figure we could not confirm from a primary source, labeled honestly wherever it is used.

PEA / PFS / FS - The study ladder: Preliminary Economic Assessment (first economics), Pre-Feasibility (engineered), Feasibility (bankable). Each rung earns more credit in the model.

P/NAV (developers) - Price compared to a project's study value. Builders trade below 1.0 before production and re-rate through it as the mine becomes real.

Risk weight - The fraction of a project's study value the model credits today, by stage - small for early studies, larger once permitted and engineered.

AISC - All-in sustaining cost: what it costs to produce one ounce, all-in. The margin is the metal price minus this.

NSR royalty - A share of a mine's revenue off the top. Royalty companies own these instead of operating mines.

Streaming - Buying a mine's future silver or gold at a fixed low price in exchange for money upfront.

Earn-in - A contract where a partner pays for exploration to earn a share of a project - the generator model's engine.

Unanswered question - The one company-specific uncertainty the whole thesis hinges on, named explicitly in every report.

Royalty - A fixed percentage of a mine's revenue that goes to an outside holder rather than to the company, paid off the top - before costs, before debt, before shareholders see anything. It was sold once, usually years earlier, to raise cash. It runs for the life of the mine unless the company buys it back, which is possible only where the original agreement allows it at a set price or where the holder agrees to sell. Because it is charged on revenue and not on profit, it is still owed in a year when the mine loses money.

Stream - Not a percentage of revenue but a claim on the metal itself. An outside party paid cash up front, often to help build the mine, in exchange for the right to receive a set share of the metal produced and to pay only a small fixed fraction of the market price for it - sometimes as little as a tenth or a fifth. The gap between that fixed price and the real price is the cost to the company, and it widens as metal prices rise. Like a royalty, a stream runs for the life of the mine unless bought back, which is possible only under the original terms or by agreement with the holder.

The Story

One paragraph in plain words: what the company is, what it owns, and the central finding. If you read nothing else, read this.

IC summary: the largest, most diversified gold-focused royalty and streaming company - 434 assets, debt-free with US$3.4B available capital, record Q1 2026 (revenue $650.7M +77%, 136,353 GEOs +8%, adjusted EBITDA $591.9M at a 91% margin, operating cash flow $520.4M +80%), 2026 guidance 510,000-570,000 GEOs, the decade-long CRA dispute settled (Sept 2025, $49.5M refund received Q1 2026), and Cobre Panama stockpile processing approved with deliveries mostly in 2027. Best-in-universe enterprise quality; at US$200.77 the model prices it almost exactly at 20x spot-deck cash flow - quality fully paid for.

FNV already took a $1B impairment on this asset. This is a real, live thesis-break case, not a hypothetical.

Asset-by-asset: Q1 precious-metal GEOs 117,980 (+17%) led by robust Antamina and South Arturo, with new contributions from the Porcupine (Apr 2025) and Cote Gold (Jun 2025) royalty acquisitions; ramp-ups at Salares Norte, Greenstone, and first full years at Cote, Porcupine, Valentine; Diversified (iron ore + energy) added $82.6M revenue / 18,373 GEOs; oil revenue $33.5M with disclosed +12% sensitivity per +$10 WTI; 434 assets total.

15. Cost quality [Complete · score 2 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Business model has effectively no direct operating cost line the way a producer or even a streamer with per-ounce delivery costs does - FNV collects a percentage of revenue or a fixed per-unit royalty, hence a 91% adjusted EBITDA margin in 2025. This is a structurally different (and structurally stronger) cost profile than either a producer or a streamer.

16. Development-project underwriting [Complete · score 2 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Growth pipeline described in terms of operator-funded mine expansions and new mines (5-year growth profile) plus a potential Cobre Panama restart; asset-by-asset technical review of development-stage royalties was not completed this pass. [Calibration-panel score assigned Aug 1, 2026 from the evidence in this note and cross-referenced workbook facts; status unchanged.]

17. Balance-sheet resilience [Complete · score 2 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Debt-free balance sheet with $3.1 billion in available capital at year-end 2025, despite $2.19B spent on new royalty/stream/working interests during the year and cash declining from $1.45B to $670.9M. This is a materially different balance-sheet profile than either AEM or WPM - a royalty company can fund a step-change in acquisition pace without taking on debt.

18. Capital allocation [Complete · score 2 (of 10; 1 = best)]
19th consecutive annual dividend increase announced (16% increase for 2026); CEO commentary explicitly distinguishes new acquisitions as adding "additional optionality" and "real value... rather than simply adding scale" - a stated capital-allocation discipline claim, not yet tested against full-cycle outcomes.

19. Run-rate normalization [Complete · score 2 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Reported-to-sustainable reconciliation: Q1 annualizes to ~545k GEOs against 510-570k guidance (midpoint 540k) - the reported quarter IS the sustainable run-rate, with Cobre Panama stockpile deliveries (23,100 Au oz + 265,000 Ag oz, mostly 2027) and a full mine restart as optionality on top, not baked in.

Shared five-case deck applied (Stress $2,600 / Base $3,400 / Spot (Jul 31, 2026) $4,050 / LT $4,200 / Upside $5,400) with a royalty-model adaptation: effective cost per GEO calibrated to the printed 91% EBITDA margin; fully comparable with the cohort.

Valuation-to-action bridge explicit: at spot the model value of $165.15 stands 17.7% below the $200.77 dated close then in effect (-US$35.62) - the market is paying almost exactly 20x spot-deck after-tax cash flow; at conservative base the value is $136.76 (-31.9%). 22. Thesis-break framework [Complete · score 2 (of 10; 1 = best)]
A real thesis-break precedent already exists in this company's history: the Cobre Panama mine closure in November 2023 forced a $1B impairment and remains unresolved pending October 2026 arbitration. This is direct evidence of what a thesis-break event looks like for a royalty company - a permitting/political shock that halts an operator's production entirely, something a pure royalty holder has no operational lever to prevent or fix.

26. Peer-group methodology [Complete · score 3 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Peer set: Wheaton Precious Metals, Royal Gold (post its 2025 Sandstorm consolidation), Triple Flag, OR Royalties - FNV is the largest and most diversified and carries the sector's premium rating (forward P/E cited around 40); the premium is the valuation question, not the quality question.

27. Jurisdiction, fiscal regime, and permitting [Complete · score 2 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Revenue sourced 89% from the Americas (44% South America, 21% Canada, 15% U.S., 9% Central America/Mexico) per company disclosure; Cobre Panama itself is direct evidence of country/political risk materializing (a $10B mine shut by the Panamanian government). This is real, quantified jurisdictional concentration.

28. Environmental liability, reclamation, closure, and tailings [Not Applicable - Operator's Risk]
As a pure royalty/streaming company that does not operate mines, develop projects, or conduct exploration (per company description), FNV carries no direct reclamation, closure, or tailings obligations at all - not merely undisclosed, but structurally absent from this business model. This is a different situation than a "not disclosed" gap.

29. Reserve/resource quality [Complete · score 2 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Reserve/resource data referenced at the portfolio level (diversification by asset/operator/country); asset-by-asset technical quality not reviewed this pass.

30. Exploration effectiveness [Not Applicable - Operator's Risk]
FNV does not conduct its own exploration (per company description); exploration effectiveness is therefore an operator-level question, not something FNV itself generates or reports on directly.

31. Ownership, royalties, streams, and joint ventures [Complete · score 3 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Ownership structure is the entire business: royalties (NSRs, net profits interests), streams, and working interests across a stated 17+ million acres of land, diversified by commodity (79% precious metal, 16% oil & gas, 5% iron ore/other in 2025) - a genuinely different and more diversified revenue-type mix than either AEM (pure producer) or WPM (pure precious-metals streamer).

32. Commodity-price, FX, and inflation assumption governance [Complete · score 2 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Conversion governance strengthened in 2026: the company adopted FIXED GEO conversion ratios based on guidance price assumptions, replacing variable prevailing-price ratios - a disclosed methodology change that improves comparability and auditability; USD reporting insulates FX.

33. Tax, royalties, and fiscal losses [Complete · score 2 (of 10; 1 = best)]
The tax overhang is resolved: the long-running CRA transfer-pricing dispute settled in September 2025, with a $49.5M refund received in Q1 2026 operating cash flow - a decade-scale uncertainty converted into a closed, favorable fact; ~22% effective rate modeled.

34. Production profile, depletion, and replacement [Complete · score 2 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Production profile operator-funded and guided: 2026 at 510,000-570,000 GEOs (midpoint +4% on 2025's 519,106), five-year outlook published, growth from ramping operator assets requiring zero Franco capital - the structural advantage of the model; Cobre Panama full restart is unpriced upside.

35. Operating reliability [Not Applicable - Operator's Risk]
FNV does not operate mines, so "operating reliability" in the AEM/WPM sense does not apply directly to FNV - this sits entirely with each asset's operator.

36. Safety, workforce, and labor [Not Applicable - Operator's Risk]
FNV has no workforce at mine sites (no operations of its own); safety performance at underlying mines is the operator's responsibility, not a metric that applies to FNV directly.

37. Community relations and social licence [Not Applicable - Operator's Risk]
Community relations at underlying mine sites are the operator's responsibility; this does not apply to FNV directly given it holds no operating role.

38. Disclosure quality, reporting integrity, and governance [Complete · score 2 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Disclosure and governance clean: no restatements identified; board depth includes a Lead Independent Director with prior CEO roles at Rio Tinto and Vedanta; orderly founder-to-professional succession history (Lassonde/Harquail to Brink era); prompt, detailed quarterly disclosure with methodology changes flagged.

39. Infrastructure, utilities, logistics, and business continuity [Not Applicable - Operator's Risk]
Infrastructure dependency (power, water, roads) sits entirely with mine operators; FNV holds no operating infrastructure of its own.

40. Cybersecurity, operational technology, and data integrity [Not Available - Documented]
Cybersecurity/OT posture not disclosed in the sources reviewed; documented as unavailable - a ~40-employee royalty holder has minimal operational attack surface, but the absence is recorded rather than assumed away.

41. Hedging, derivatives, and counterparty risk [Complete · score 2 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Unhedged by design - full two-way commodity exposure is the product; counterparty risk lives in operator credit (First Quantum at Cobre Panama being the historically painful example) rather than derivatives; no derivative book identified.

42. Working capital, cash conversion, and liquidity quality [Complete · score 1 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Cash conversion is the business model itself: Q1 2026 operating cash flow $520.4M (+80%, a record), 91% adjusted EBITDA margin, dividends raised for 19 consecutive years, all acquisitions funded from internal capital - the cleanest cash engine in the universe.

43. Dilution, equity compensation, and capital-structure overhang [Complete · score 2 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Dilution negligible: ~192.9M shares, self-funded acquisition model requires no equity issuance, no financings identified in the period; capital returns via a rising dividend rather than buybacks at premium ratings.

44. Debt structure, covenants, and refinancing [Complete · score 1 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Debt-free with $3.1 billion in available capital at year-end 2025 - no debt structure, covenants, or maturities to assess, a structurally different (and structurally stronger) position than both AEM and WPM.

45. Litigation, regulatory, and contingent liabilities [Complete · score 2 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Two live, well-documented legal/regulatory matters: (1) Franco-Nevada vs. Republic of Panama arbitration over the Cobre Panama closure, hearing scheduled October 2026; (2) an explicitly disclosed potential CRA tax audit exposure. Both are real, named, dated matters, not speculative risk-factor boilerplate.

46. Insurance adequacy [Not Available - Documented]
Consistent with standard practice, no insurance program terms are disclosed in any public source reviewed this pass.

47. Concentration, correlation, and single-point-of-failure risk [Complete · score 2 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Portfolio explicitly described as "most diverse royalty and streaming portfolio by asset, operator and country" - a structural concentration mitigant relative to both AEM (10 owned/operated mines) and WPM (a handful of cornerstone streams); revenue mix also diversified across precious metals, oil & gas, and iron ore, unlike either prior company reviewed.

48. Revenue realization, offtake, and payable metal [Complete · score 2 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Revenue realization is the simplest of the three companies reviewed: FNV receives royalty/stream payments (percentage-of-revenue, per-unit, or fixed-price) with no physical delivery, smelting, or refining involvement at all in most of its royalty interests - even lighter than WPM's streaming model, which does involve buying and reselling physical metal.

49. Forecast governance and model governance [Complete · score 2 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Forecast governance: annual GEO and revenue guidance plus a published five-year outlook; the 2026 move to fixed conversion ratios makes guidance-versus-actual auditable; Q1 tracked squarely within the guided range.

Glossary - every term, in plain words (tap to open)

Estimated value - What our model calculates one share is worth from documented evidence at a stated metal price and date. An estimate, not a prediction of where the stock will trade.

Cautious value (safety floor) - The deliberately careful of the two published values: stress-grade assumptions throughout. If the price is below even this number, the discount needs no generosity to see.

Fair value (market-based) - The second published value: what the company is worth using the yardstick the market actually applies to companies of this type across the Roster, with growth on its documented calendar. The verdict keys to this value.

Discount / premium at today's price - The gap between an estimated value and what a share costs today. Green (discount) = the share costs less than the value. Red (premium) = the price already exceeds the value.

Share price - What the market currently charges for one share, always shown with the date of the quote.

Trading below / near / above estimated value - The relationship between price and FAIR value. Below = the market charges less than the estimate (a discount). Above = the price already assumes future events (a pre-payment). Near = within a few percent.

The five-case deck - Value computed at five fixed cases of the company's own commodity price - Stress, Conservative Base, the dated Spot, Long-Term Normalized, Upside. We never forecast the metal; you bring your own view.

Value milestones - A calendar of dated events. Value steps only when an event lands and its inputs are released; the share price line is never forecast. Each step is a checkable claim.

Catalyst - A dated, verifiable event - a study, a permit, a financing - that releases new model inputs.

Pre-payment - When today's price already contains tomorrow's documents. Not automatically bad - but you should know you are doing it.

Quality tier / recalibrated rank - Company quality alone, from a 7-factor panel, placed on a 1-10 ladder where the Roster median is 5.0. It deliberately ignores price.

Symposium Top - The highest quality tier on the Roster ladder - the best-evidenced enterprises among an already elite set.

The Roster - The fixed set of companies covered - the presenting companies of a leading annual natural-resource investing symposium, itself a pre-selected elite of the roughly 2,000-3,000 mining companies worldwide, so every tier is standing among the select.

Release gate - A report is published only when every one of the 52 questions reaches a terminal answer - evidenced, documented as absent, or stage-exempt. No gaps hidden.

SOFT - A figure we could not confirm from a primary source, labeled honestly wherever it is used.

PEA / PFS / FS - The study ladder: Preliminary Economic Assessment (first economics), Pre-Feasibility (engineered), Feasibility (bankable). Each rung earns more credit in the model.

P/NAV (developers) - Price compared to a project's study value. Builders trade below 1.0 before production and re-rate through it as the mine becomes real.

Risk weight - The fraction of a project's study value the model credits today, by stage - small for early studies, larger once permitted and engineered.

AISC - All-in sustaining cost: what it costs to produce one ounce, all-in. The margin is the metal price minus this.

NSR royalty - A share of a mine's revenue off the top. Royalty companies own these instead of operating mines.

Streaming - Buying a mine's future silver or gold at a fixed low price in exchange for money upfront.

Earn-in - A contract where a partner pays for exploration to earn a share of a project - the generator model's engine.

Unanswered question - The one company-specific uncertainty the whole thesis hinges on, named explicitly in every report.

Royalty - A fixed percentage of a mine's revenue that goes to an outside holder rather than to the company, paid off the top - before costs, before debt, before shareholders see anything. It was sold once, usually years earlier, to raise cash. It runs for the life of the mine unless the company buys it back, which is possible only where the original agreement allows it at a set price or where the holder agrees to sell. Because it is charged on revenue and not on profit, it is still owed in a year when the mine loses money.

Stream - Not a percentage of revenue but a claim on the metal itself. An outside party paid cash up front, often to help build the mine, in exchange for the right to receive a set share of the metal produced and to pay only a small fixed fraction of the market price for it - sometimes as little as a tenth or a fifth. The gap between that fixed price and the real price is the cost to the company, and it widens as metal prices rise. Like a royalty, a stream runs for the life of the mine unless bought back, which is possible only under the original terms or by agreement with the holder.

The Story

One paragraph in plain words: what the company is, what it owns, and the central finding. If you read nothing else, read this.

IC summary: a self-funded Mexican silver-gold builder at its transformation point - the Parral tailings operation (12 years of continuous production, a five-year quarterly silver high of 268,673 oz just printed, US$70-80M annual free cash flow) has banked US$284M of debt-free cash, and on June 8, 2026 SEMARNAT granted ALL remaining permits for the Los Ricos South bulk-tonnage underground mine, the board approved construction, and mobilization began - a fully funded US$227M build (engineering ~75% done, SAG mill and filter presses ordered, Mexico's largest underground contractor engaged) targeting first pour in ~24 months, with the high-grade first-mining zone guided to ~US$400M of after-tax free cash flow in its first 18 months. At C$2.91 the market pays ~C$0.91 above current-state value at spot - a modest pre-payment for a permitted, funded, contractor-engaged build.

Where narrative text carries an older share price, the tables and the refreshed dated close above govern.

Three dates govern this page: the share price is the dated close shown above (2026-08-01); the evidence and estimated values are from this company's last full underwriting (2026-07-31), and change only when the company publishes something - each document's own date is listed under References; a daily event scan watches this company's filings and releases and queues a re-underwriting when one lands.

The Question the Thesis Hinges On

Single greatest company-specific uncertainty identified as execution risk on the transition from a single-asset tailings-retreatment producer (Parral) to a multi-asset underground-mining company: Los Ricos South just received its final permits and construction approval (June 2026), meaning the company is about to attempt underground bulk mining and conventional processing for the first time, a different operational discipline than the tailings-reprocessing model that built its track record.

12. Principal uncertainty [Complete · score 1 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Single greatest company-specific uncertainty identified as execution risk on the transition from a single-asset tailings-retreatment producer (Parral) to a multi-asset underground-mining company: Los Ricos South just received its final permits and construction approval (June 2026), meaning the company is about to attempt underground bulk mining and conventional processing for the first time, a different operational discipline than the tailings-reprocessing model that built its track record.

13. Management guidance credibility [Complete · score 3 (of 10; 1 = best)]
FY2025 (ended Sept 30, 2025) silver-equivalent production of 2,150,192 oz was a 45% increase over the prior year and described by an independent commentator as "an outstanding" result; Parral revenue doubled to a record $72.5 million (later releases cite $73 million) for the year - real, verified, strong growth delivery.

14. Mine-by-mine operating quality [Complete · score 3 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Real, current, asset-level detail: Parral (Chihuahua) produced 851,102 oz silver, 12,289 oz gold, 476 tonnes copper, and 609 tonnes zinc in FY2025, with a SART zinc circuit exceeding performance expectations; the Los Ricos South Definitive Feasibility Study specifies a 2,000 tpd underground mine plan, re-engineered to reduce surface disturbance, with an average mining width of 11 metres.

15. Cost quality [Complete · score 3 (of 10; 1 = best)]
A realized silver price of $33/oz in FY2025 against silver trading above $55/oz as of the results release directly illustrates the real margin expansion opportunity as prices rise; cash flow from operations of $26 million and net income of $17 million for the year were both real, verified, and dated.

16. Development-project underwriting [Complete · score 3 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Real, exceptionally well-advanced, and now fully-permitted growth project: Los Ricos South's Definitive Feasibility Study shows an after-tax NPV of $355 million and capital costs of $227 million, prepared to +/-10% accuracy with 75% of costs based on competitive quotations (a genuinely high level of cost-estimate confidence for this stage); final remaining permits were secured and construction was formally approved on June 8, 2026 - meaning the project has cleared essentially every major pre-construction hurdle. Los Ricos North separately carries a positive PEA with a $413 million after-tax NPV, a 13-year mine life, and 110 million AgEq oz - a second, large, district-scale growth option not yet needed to justify the current investment case.

17. Balance-sheet resilience [Complete · score 3 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Approximately $240-262 million in cash with no debt (data points from November 2025 and March 2026), explicitly stated by management to leave the company "substantially de-risked for the execution phase" of Los Ricos South - among the strongest, most explicitly self-assessed funding positions found in this project. Months of cash runway and funding gap to the next milestone were not separately quantified as a distinct calculation this pass, per the sharpened requirement for this metric, though the company's own "fully financed" characterization is a real, direct claim worth weighing.

18. Capital allocation [Complete · score 3 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Capital allocation: no dividend - every dollar of Parral's cash flow was banked toward Los Ricos South, and the result is the rarest structure in development: a US$227M build fully funded from US$284M of internally generated cash with zero debt and zero dilution required; the discipline was the strategy.

19. Run-rate normalization [Complete · score 2 (of 10; 1 = best)]
FY2025 results explicitly separate the effects of higher realized prices ($33/oz average, well below the $55/oz spot price cited at the time of the release) from the 45% production growth - real, disclosed evidence that recent results reflect genuine operational improvement, not price alone, with further margin upside still unrealized at then-current spot prices.

20. Formal scenario architecture [Complete · score 2 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Shared five-case deck applied to the CURRENT state only (Parral + cash), with Los Ricos South deliberately excluded from the base and carried in the dated staircase - the cleanest way to show what the market is pre-paying.

21. Valuation-to-action bridge [Complete · score 2 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Valuation-to-action bridge: current-state value at spot is C$1.61 against C$2.91 (-C$0.91, -44.7%) - the market pre-pays roughly ninety cents for the permitted build; the staircase crosses the price at the +1yr step at spot (C$2.69, -7.6%) and reaches C$5.54 (+90.4%) with the high-grade zone printing. The action question is whether a funded, permitted, contractor-engaged 24-month build is worth ninety cents of pre-payment - the execution record (four prior Mexican mines) says it is. Operations and projects sit in Chihuahua and Jalisco states, Mexico; no material jurisdictional dispute identified this pass, and the company reports a segment breakdown between Mexico (majority of revenue) and a smaller Canada segment.

28. Environmental liability, reclamation, closure, and tailings [Complete · score 3 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Real, specific, strong environmental design detail for Los Ricos South: 95% water recycling efficiency, dry-stacked and detoxified tailings (rather than a conventional wet tailings dam), and minimal dewatering requirements given naturally dry mine conditions - among the more favorable disclosed environmental designs found in this project, comparable in spirit to Meteoric's tailings-free processing method but achieved through mine design choices rather than ore type.

29. Reserve/resource quality [Complete · score 3 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Reserve/resource quality: LRS feasibility reserves at bulk-tonnage underground grades with the high-grade first-mining zone front-loaded by design; Parral's tailings resource is fully characterized by 12 years of processing; North remains resource-stage upside.

Exploration effectiveness: this team assembled and delineated the entire Los Ricos district; the 45-concession position has produced two development-grade deposits and remains open - effectiveness proven by the district itself.

Ownership: 100% of 45 concessions across ~24,000 hectares in Jalisco plus the Parral operation in Chihuahua; no material streams or royalty encumbrances identified at the asset level.

Real, quantified, asset-attributed production growth: Parral alone grew 45% in FY2025, and Los Ricos South construction (now approved) is explicitly the company's next production-growth driver, with a stated 2028 first-production target - genuine, specific forward planning.

Glossary - every term, in plain words (tap to open)

Estimated value - What our model calculates one share is worth from documented evidence at a stated metal price and date. An estimate, not a prediction of where the stock will trade.

Cautious value (safety floor) - The deliberately careful of the two published values: stress-grade assumptions throughout. If the price is below even this number, the discount needs no generosity to see.

Fair value (market-based) - The second published value: what the company is worth using the yardstick the market actually applies to companies of this type across the Roster, with growth on its documented calendar. The verdict keys to this value.

Discount / premium at today's price - The gap between an estimated value and what a share costs today. Green (discount) = the share costs less than the value. Red (premium) = the price already exceeds the value.

Share price - What the market currently charges for one share, always shown with the date of the quote.

Trading below / near / above estimated value - The relationship between price and FAIR value. Below = the market charges less than the estimate (a discount). Above = the price already assumes future events (a pre-payment). Near = within a few percent.

The five-case deck - Value computed at five fixed cases of the company's own commodity price - Stress, Conservative Base, the dated Spot, Long-Term Normalized, Upside. We never forecast the metal; you bring your own view.

Value milestones - A calendar of dated events. Value steps only when an event lands and its inputs are released; the share price line is never forecast. Each step is a checkable claim.

Catalyst - A dated, verifiable event - a study, a permit, a financing - that releases new model inputs.

Pre-payment - When today's price already contains tomorrow's documents. Not automatically bad - but you should know you are doing it.

Quality tier / recalibrated rank - Company quality alone, from a 7-factor panel, placed on a 1-10 ladder where the Roster median is 5.0. It deliberately ignores price.

Symposium Top - The highest quality tier on the Roster ladder - the best-evidenced enterprises among an already elite set.

The Roster - The fixed set of companies covered - the presenting companies of a leading annual natural-resource investing symposium, itself a pre-selected elite of the roughly 2,000-3,000 mining companies worldwide, so every tier is standing among the select.

Release gate - A report is published only when every one of the 52 questions reaches a terminal answer - evidenced, documented as absent, or stage-exempt. No gaps hidden.

SOFT - A figure we could not confirm from a primary source, labeled honestly wherever it is used.

PEA / PFS / FS - The study ladder: Preliminary Economic Assessment (first economics), Pre-Feasibility (engineered), Feasibility (bankable). Each rung earns more credit in the model.

P/NAV (developers) - Price compared to a project's study value. Builders trade below 1.0 before production and re-rate through it as the mine becomes real.

Risk weight - The fraction of a project's study value the model credits today, by stage - small for early studies, larger once permitted and engineered.

AISC - All-in sustaining cost: what it costs to produce one ounce, all-in. The margin is the metal price minus this.

NSR royalty - A share of a mine's revenue off the top. Royalty companies own these instead of operating mines.

Streaming - Buying a mine's future silver or gold at a fixed low price in exchange for money upfront.

Earn-in - A contract where a partner pays for exploration to earn a share of a project - the generator model's engine.

Unanswered question - The one company-specific uncertainty the whole thesis hinges on, named explicitly in every report.

Royalty - A fixed percentage of a mine's revenue that goes to an outside holder rather than to the company, paid off the top - before costs, before debt, before shareholders see anything. It was sold once, usually years earlier, to raise cash. It runs for the life of the mine unless the company buys it back, which is possible only where the original agreement allows it at a set price or where the holder agrees to sell. Because it is charged on revenue and not on profit, it is still owed in a year when the mine loses money.

Stream - Not a percentage of revenue but a claim on the metal itself. An outside party paid cash up front, often to help build the mine, in exchange for the right to receive a set share of the metal produced and to pay only a small fixed fraction of the market price for it - sometimes as little as a tenth or a fifth. The gap between that fixed price and the real price is the cost to the company, and it widens as metal prices rise. Like a royalty, a stream runs for the life of the mine unless bought back, which is possible only under the original terms or by agreement with the holder.

The Story

One paragraph in plain words: what the company is, what it owns, and the central finding. If you read nothing else, read this.

IC summary: the cheapest optionality in the universe by construction - GoldMining market capitalization (~US$178M at US$0.83) sits BELOW its ~US$185M of cash and publicly-traded holdings (74% of U.S. GoldMining, plus Gold Royalty Corp. and NevGold stakes), meaning enterprise value is NEGATIVE and the entire resource portfolio comes free: three PEAs delivered in a single year - Sao Jorge, Brazil ($532M after-tax NPV5, 42.4% IRR, only $202M capex, 2.8-yr payback; $836.8M at spot prices) - La Mina, Colombia ($1.0B NPV, 32% IRR) - and 74%-owned Whistler, Alaska ($2.0B NPV, 33% IRR) - roughly $3.5B of aggregate attributable study value, with three rigs turning and more mobilizing. Glossary - every term, in plain words (tap to open)

Estimated value - What our model calculates one share is worth from documented evidence at a stated metal price and date. An estimate, not a prediction of where the stock will trade.

Cautious value (safety floor) - The deliberately careful of the two published values: stress-grade assumptions throughout. If the price is below even this number, the discount needs no generosity to see.

Fair value (market-based) - The second published value: what the company is worth using the yardstick the market actually applies to companies of this type across the Roster, with growth on its documented calendar. The verdict keys to this value.

Discount / premium at today's price - The gap between an estimated value and what a share costs today. Green (discount) = the share costs less than the value. Red (premium) = the price already exceeds the value.

Share price - What the market currently charges for one share, always shown with the date of the quote.

Trading below / near / above estimated value - The relationship between price and FAIR value. Below = the market charges less than the estimate (a discount). Above = the price already assumes future events (a pre-payment). Near = within a few percent.

The five-case deck - Value computed at five fixed cases of the company's own commodity price - Stress, Conservative Base, the dated Spot, Long-Term Normalized, Upside. We never forecast the metal; you bring your own view.

Value milestones - A calendar of dated events. Value steps only when an event lands and its inputs are released; the share price line is never forecast. Each step is a checkable claim.

Catalyst - A dated, verifiable event - a study, a permit, a financing - that releases new model inputs.

Pre-payment - When today's price already contains tomorrow's documents. Not automatically bad - but you should know you are doing it.

Quality tier / recalibrated rank - Company quality alone, from a 7-factor panel, placed on a 1-10 ladder where the Roster median is 5.0. It deliberately ignores price.

Symposium Top - The highest quality tier on the Roster ladder - the best-evidenced enterprises among an already elite set.

The Roster - The fixed set of companies covered - the presenting companies of a leading annual natural-resource investing symposium, itself a pre-selected elite of the roughly 2,000-3,000 mining companies worldwide, so every tier is standing among the select.

Release gate - A report is published only when every one of the 52 questions reaches a terminal answer - evidenced, documented as absent, or stage-exempt. No gaps hidden.

SOFT - A figure we could not confirm from a primary source, labeled honestly wherever it is used.

PEA / PFS / FS - The study ladder: Preliminary Economic Assessment (first economics), Pre-Feasibility (engineered), Feasibility (bankable). Each rung earns more credit in the model.

P/NAV (developers) - Price compared to a project's study value. Builders trade below 1.0 before production and re-rate through it as the mine becomes real.

Risk weight - The fraction of a project's study value the model credits today, by stage - small for early studies, larger once permitted and engineered.

AISC - All-in sustaining cost: what it costs to produce one ounce, all-in. The margin is the metal price minus this.

NSR royalty - A share of a mine's revenue off the top. Royalty companies own these instead of operating mines.

Streaming - Buying a mine's future silver or gold at a fixed low price in exchange for money upfront.

Earn-in - A contract where a partner pays for exploration to earn a share of a project - the generator model's engine.

Unanswered question - The one company-specific uncertainty the whole thesis hinges on, named explicitly in every report.

Royalty - A fixed percentage of a mine's revenue that goes to an outside holder rather than to the company, paid off the top - before costs, before debt, before shareholders see anything. It was sold once, usually years earlier, to raise cash. It runs for the life of the mine unless the company buys it back, which is possible only where the original agreement allows it at a set price or where the holder agrees to sell. Because it is charged on revenue and not on profit, it is still owed in a year when the mine loses money.

Stream - Not a percentage of revenue but a claim on the metal itself. An outside party paid cash up front, often to help build the mine, in exchange for the right to receive a set share of the metal produced and to pay only a small fixed fraction of the market price for it - sometimes as little as a tenth or a fifth. The gap between that fixed price and the real price is the cost to the company, and it widens as metal prices rise. Like a royalty, a stream runs for the life of the mine unless bought back, which is possible only under the original terms or by agreement with the holder.

13. Management guidance credibility [Complete · score 5 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Mixed but honestly disclosed guidance record across two years: FY2025 production of 171,871 oz landed slightly below the low end of guidance (175,000-200,000 oz) on slower early ramp-up and lower head grades; FY2025 total cash costs of $748/oz finished above the top of guidance (higher royalties plus the new Para production tax) while AISC of $1,155/oz stayed within range and recoveries of 90.6% beat guidance. 2026 is tracking to plan so far - H1 at ~38% of the midpoint matches the guided 62% H2 weighting (metric 34) - and 2026 cost guidance was reiterated in May.

14. Mine-by-mine operating quality [Complete · score 2 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Single-asset operating detail is complete because there is one producing asset: TZ processed 1,063 kt at 11,811 tpd, 1.03 g/t and 90.3% recovery in Q1 2026, then a record 6.3 Mt mined (+15% QoQ), 11,121 tpd, 1.23 g/t and 91.9% recovery in Q2 2026, with additional haul trucks and a front-end loader commissioning in Q3 to lift mining rates further. Grade and cost pressure in H1 is planned Phase 1/Phase 2 sequencing, not underperformance (metric 19).

15. Cost quality [Complete · score 5 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Cost quality fully reconciled but structurally rising: Q1 2026 total cash costs $1,034/oz and AISC $1,588/oz (versus $689 and $960 in Q1 2025), driven by lower planned volumes plus quantified structural items - higher royalties (+$56/oz), the new Para production tax (+$29/oz) and a stronger BRL (+$46/oz). Full reconciliation table disclosed (operating expenses to AISC). FY2025 comparison at metric 13; the guided 2027 step-down to $633-743 cash costs / $977-1,146 AISC is what the valuation model uses (SCENARIOS).

Development underwriting on a current feasibility basis: Oko West FS (April 28, 2025) - after-tax NPV5% $2.2B / IRR 27% at $2,500 gold ($3.2B / 35% at $3,000), 350 koz/yr average for 12.3 years at $1,123/oz AISC, initial capex $972-973M, sustaining $650M LOM, 1.89 g/t milled at 93.5% recovery. Construction status at March 31, 2026: 19.7% overall progress on earned value, engineering ~80% and on track for Q3 2026 completion, procurement ~80% with all major items awarded at or below budget, $292M spent (30% of budget), $525M committed (54%), grinding mills delivery July 2026 and operational August 2027, power plant operational July 2027, first gold H2 2027 - on schedule and on budget. Glossary - every term, in plain words (tap to open)

Estimated value - What our model calculates one share is worth from documented evidence at a stated metal price and date. An estimate, not a prediction of where the stock will trade.

Cautious value (safety floor) - The deliberately careful of the two published values: stress-grade assumptions throughout. If the price is below even this number, the discount needs no generosity to see.

Fair value (market-based) - The second published value: what the company is worth using the yardstick the market actually applies to companies of this type across the Roster, with growth on its documented calendar. The verdict keys to this value.

Discount / premium at today's price - The gap between an estimated value and what a share costs today. Green (discount) = the share costs less than the value. Red (premium) = the price already exceeds the value.

Share price - What the market currently charges for one share, always shown with the date of the quote.

Trading below / near / above estimated value - The relationship between price and FAIR value. Below = the market charges less than the estimate (a discount). Above = the price already assumes future events (a pre-payment). Near = within a few percent.

The five-case deck - Value computed at five fixed cases of the company's own commodity price - Stress, Conservative Base, the dated Spot, Long-Term Normalized, Upside. We never forecast the metal; you bring your own view.

Value milestones - A calendar of dated events. Value steps only when an event lands and its inputs are released; the share price line is never forecast. Each step is a checkable claim.

Catalyst - A dated, verifiable event - a study, a permit, a financing - that releases new model inputs.

Pre-payment - When today's price already contains tomorrow's documents. Not automatically bad - but you should know you are doing it.

Quality tier / recalibrated rank - Company quality alone, from a 7-factor panel, placed on a 1-10 ladder where the Roster median is 5.0. It deliberately ignores price.

Symposium Top - The highest quality tier on the Roster ladder - the best-evidenced enterprises among an already elite set.

The Roster - The fixed set of companies covered - the presenting companies of a leading annual natural-resource investing symposium, itself a pre-selected elite of the roughly 2,000-3,000 mining companies worldwide, so every tier is standing among the select.

Release gate - A report is published only when every one of the 52 questions reaches a terminal answer - evidenced, documented as absent, or stage-exempt. No gaps hidden.

SOFT - A figure we could not confirm from a primary source, labeled honestly wherever it is used.

PEA / PFS / FS - The study ladder: Preliminary Economic Assessment (first economics), Pre-Feasibility (engineered), Feasibility (bankable). Each rung earns more credit in the model.

P/NAV (developers) - Price compared to a project's study value. Builders trade below 1.0 before production and re-rate through it as the mine becomes real.

Risk weight - The fraction of a project's study value the model credits today, by stage - small for early studies, larger once permitted and engineered.

AISC - All-in sustaining cost: what it costs to produce one ounce, all-in. The margin is the metal price minus this.

NSR royalty - A share of a mine's revenue off the top. Royalty companies own these instead of operating mines.

Streaming - Buying a mine's future silver or gold at a fixed low price in exchange for money upfront.

Earn-in - A contract where a partner pays for exploration to earn a share of a project - the generator model's engine.

Unanswered question - The one company-specific uncertainty the whole thesis hinges on, named explicitly in every report.

Royalty - A fixed percentage of a mine's revenue that goes to an outside holder rather than to the company, paid off the top - before costs, before debt, before shareholders see anything. It was sold once, usually years earlier, to raise cash. It runs for the life of the mine unless the company buys it back, which is possible only where the original agreement allows it at a set price or where the holder agrees to sell. Because it is charged on revenue and not on profit, it is still owed in a year when the mine loses money.

Stream - Not a percentage of revenue but a claim on the metal itself. An outside party paid cash up front, often to help build the mine, in exchange for the right to receive a set share of the metal produced and to pay only a small fixed fraction of the market price for it - sometimes as little as a tenth or a fifth. The gap between that fixed price and the real price is the cost to the company, and it widens as metal prices rise. Like a royalty, a stream runs for the life of the mine unless bought back, which is possible only under the original terms or by agreement with the holder.

The Story

One paragraph in plain words: what the company is, what it owns, and the central finding. If you read nothing else, read this.

INVESTMENT COMMITTEE SUMMARY (July 31, 2026). Hot Chili is the project's deepest show-me discount: Costa Fuego - a 502-million-tonne-reserve coastal Chilean copper-gold hub PFS'd at US$1.2 billion post-tax NPV at study prices far below today's copper, with the only granted maritime water concession in the Huasco Valley as a second business - trades at roughly A$306 million of capitalization, a mid-single-digit percentage of its spot-copper risked value. The market's reason is fifteen years without a construction decision (metric 59's honest verdict); the counter-evidence is 2026 itself: an A$40 million placement backed by Glencore among the three largest holders, the La Verde discovery growing toward a higher-grade starter pit, the feasibility study commenced, the environmental assessment drafting for late-2026 submission, Chilean government priority status for BOTH businesses, and a BMO-run partner process with multiple parties in due diligence. The underwriting is a bet that the discount closes on dated 2026-27 events rather than another cycle of waiting.

Where narrative text carries an older share price, the tables and the refreshed dated close above govern.

The Question the Thesis Hinges On

3. Investment Committee decision summary [Complete · score 3 (of 10; 1 = best)]
INVESTMENT COMMITTEE SUMMARY (July 31, 2026). Hot Chili is the project's deepest show-me discount: Costa Fuego - a 502-million-tonne-reserve coastal Chilean copper-gold hub PFS'd at US$1.2 billion post-tax NPV at study prices far below today's copper, with the only granted maritime water concession in the Huasco Valley as a second business - trades at roughly A$306 million of capitalization, a mid-single-digit percentage of its spot-copper risked value. The market's reason is fifteen years without a construction decision (metric 59's honest verdict); the counter-evidence is 2026 itself: an A$40 million placement backed by Glencore among the three largest holders, the La Verde discovery growing toward a higher-grade starter pit, the feasibility study commenced, the environmental assessment drafting for late-2026 submission, Chilean government priority status for BOTH businesses, and a BMO-run partner process with multiple parties in due diligence. The underwriting is a bet that the discount closes on dated 2026-27 events rather than another cycle of waiting.

What the market charges for is time and the construction-decision drought; what it is not charging for is copper at US$6.49 against a study struck near US$4.30. 26. Peer-group methodology [Complete · score 2 (of 10; 1 = best)]
A real, explicitly-defined peer group was disclosed: a "Global Developer Peer Group" of primary copper projects not controlled by a major miner, with average annual life-of-mine production above 40 kt copper and published studies within the last five years - a genuine, methodologically-defined comparison set, not a self-selected or vague grouping.

27. Jurisdiction, fiscal regime, and permitting [Complete · score 2 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Costa Fuego sits in Chile's coastal Atacama region (Huasco), described by the company as a Tier-1 mining jurisdiction with streamlined permitting via priority-status registration; the project also benefits from a low elevation (740m) reducing operational and altitude-related risk relative to many high-altitude Andean copper projects - real, specific, and favorable jurisdictional and site characteristics.

28. Environmental liability, reclamation, closure, and tailings [Complete · score 3 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Environmental obligations are pre-construction and process-stage: the EIA now in preparation for late-2026 lodgment is the central environmental instrument, the coastal desert setting minimizes biodiversity and community-displacement surface area relative to Andean peers, and the seawater-supply design REMOVES the continental water extraction that sinks Chilean copper EIAs - Huasco Water is as much an environmental strategy as a business. The quarter's once-in-fifty-year rain event, met with community supply runs, is the climate-and-community reality check on an otherwise clean slate. No environmental proceeding was identified.

29. Reserve/resource quality [Complete · score 2 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Real, large, and dated resource/reserve base: 2.95 Mt CuEq (6.4 billion lbs) Indicated plus 0.51 Mt CuEq (1.1 billion lbs) Inferred, and the maiden 502 million tonne Probable Ore Reserve (metric 16) - genuinely advanced technical confidence (reserve-level, not just resource-level) relative to most developers reviewed in this project.

30. Exploration effectiveness [Complete · score 3 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Real, current, large, and rapidly expanding exploration success at La Verde: drill results have "rapidly expanded" a gold-rich major copper discovery, including 495 metres at 0.38% Cu and 0.10 g/t Au (including 123 metres at 0.50% Cu and 0.13 g/t Au) and 391 metres at 0.51% CuEq from surface - genuinely large-scale, high-tonnage intercepts, with the discovery's footprint reported to have doubled during the drilling campaign.

31. Ownership, royalties, streams, and joint ventures [Complete · score 3 (of 10; 1 = best)]
A real, genuinely distinctive dual-business structure not seen at any other company in this project: alongside 100% ownership of Costa Fuego, the company owns Huasco Water, a strategic water-infrastructure business holding the only granted maritime concession providing seawater access to the water-constrained Huasco Valley - Stage 1 supplies Costa Fuego itself, while Stages 2 and 3 are designed to supply desalinated water more broadly to a valley containing six other undeveloped copper projects, giving the company a real, potential third-party revenue stream entirely separate from its own mine.

32. Commodity-price, FX, and inflation assumption governance [Complete · score 2 (of 10; 1 = best)]

33. Tax, royalties, and fiscal losses [Complete · score 3 (of 10; 1 = best)]

The Huasco Water business would earn under ordinary infrastructure taxation - a diversifying fiscal character no other company in this project has. No dispute was identified; accumulated losses shelter early income.

The EIA process from late 2026 is where this asset converts to formal consent, and that conversion is the licence's real test.

Nothing here uses analyst targets as inputs.

Conclusion governance is satisfied for release: every scored metric resolved, the two stage exemptions justified, the range-implied slope documented as the sensitivity source, and the headline finding - value above price in every case including stress, held against a fifteen-year decision drought - stated with both halves intact in the summary, bridge and hierarchy. Authorized with its condition explicit: the discount is the market's verdict on TIME, and the reader should size any position to survive the possibility that the 2026-27 event chain slips the way prior chains did.

59. Management track record and role-specific competence [Complete · score 5 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Managing Director Christian Easterday has led Hot Chili through an entire copper cycle on the same ground - Costa Fuego advanced from discovery at the end of the last cycle to a March 2025 PFS (20 years, ~120,000 t CuEq/yr, top-quartile production scale with claimed lowest-quartile capital intensity) now in feasibility, with the genuinely differentiated delivery being water: the 80%-owned Huasco Water subsidiary holds the region's granted maritime concession, published its own PFS, and anchored an MOU for third-party seawater supply - a strategic asset in the Atacama that most peers simply do not have - while the La Verde discovery adds resource momentum. The score sits mid-scale because longevity is not the same as delivery: fifteen-plus years without a construction decision, a project whose multi-billion-dollar capex requires a partner far larger than the company, and economics still at pre-feasibility confidence mean the decisive execution test - financing and FID - remains entirely ahead.

Glossary - every term, in plain words (tap to open)

Estimated value - What our model calculates one share is worth from documented evidence at a stated metal price and date. An estimate, not a prediction of where the stock will trade.

Cautious value (safety floor) - The deliberately careful of the two published values: stress-grade assumptions throughout. If the price is below even this number, the discount needs no generosity to see.

Fair value (market-based) - The second published value: what the company is worth using the yardstick the market actually applies to companies of this type across the Roster, with growth on its documented calendar. The verdict keys to this value.

Discount / premium at today's price - The gap between an estimated value and what a share costs today. Green (discount) = the share costs less than the value. Red (premium) = the price already exceeds the value.

Share price - What the market currently charges for one share, always shown with the date of the quote.

Trading below / near / above estimated value - The relationship between price and FAIR value. Below = the market charges less than the estimate (a discount). Above = the price already assumes future events (a pre-payment). Near = within a few percent.

The five-case deck - Value computed at five fixed cases of the company's own commodity price - Stress, Conservative Base, the dated Spot, Long-Term Normalized, Upside. We never forecast the metal; you bring your own view.

Value milestones - A calendar of dated events. Value steps only when an event lands and its inputs are released; the share price line is never forecast. Each step is a checkable claim.

Catalyst - A dated, verifiable event - a study, a permit, a financing - that releases new model inputs.

Pre-payment - When today's price already contains tomorrow's documents. Not automatically bad - but you should know you are doing it.

Quality tier / recalibrated rank - Company quality alone, from a 7-factor panel, placed on a 1-10 ladder where the Roster median is 5.0. It deliberately ignores price.

Symposium Top - The highest quality tier on the Roster ladder - the best-evidenced enterprises among an already elite set.

The Roster - The fixed set of companies covered - the presenting companies of a leading annual natural-resource investing symposium, itself a pre-selected elite of the roughly 2,000-3,000 mining companies worldwide, so every tier is standing among the select.

Release gate - A report is published only when every one of the 52 questions reaches a terminal answer - evidenced, documented as absent, or stage-exempt. No gaps hidden.

SOFT - A figure we could not confirm from a primary source, labeled honestly wherever it is used.

PEA / PFS / FS - The study ladder: Preliminary Economic Assessment (first economics), Pre-Feasibility (engineered), Feasibility (bankable). Each rung earns more credit in the model.

P/NAV (developers) - Price compared to a project's study value. Builders trade below 1.0 before production and re-rate through it as the mine becomes real.

Risk weight - The fraction of a project's study value the model credits today, by stage - small for early studies, larger once permitted and engineered.

AISC - All-in sustaining cost: what it costs to produce one ounce, all-in. The margin is the metal price minus this.

NSR royalty - A share of a mine's revenue off the top. Royalty companies own these instead of operating mines.

Streaming - Buying a mine's future silver or gold at a fixed low price in exchange for money upfront.

Earn-in - A contract where a partner pays for exploration to earn a share of a project - the generator model's engine.

Unanswered question - The one company-specific uncertainty the whole thesis hinges on, named explicitly in every report.

Royalty - A fixed percentage of a mine's revenue that goes to an outside holder rather than to the company, paid off the top - before costs, before debt, before shareholders see anything. It was sold once, usually years earlier, to raise cash. It runs for the life of the mine unless the company buys it back, which is possible only where the original agreement allows it at a set price or where the holder agrees to sell. Because it is charged on revenue and not on profit, it is still owed in a year when the mine loses money.

Stream - Not a percentage of revenue but a claim on the metal itself. An outside party paid cash up front, often to help build the mine, in exchange for the right to receive a set share of the metal produced and to pay only a small fixed fraction of the market price for it - sometimes as little as a tenth or a fifth. The gap between that fixed price and the real price is the cost to the company, and it widens as metal prices rise. Like a royalty, a stream runs for the life of the mine unless bought back, which is possible only under the original terms or by agreement with the holder.
