The Story

One paragraph in plain words: what the company is, what it owns, and the central finding. If you read nothing else, read this.

INVESTMENT COMMITTEE SUMMARY (July 31, 2026). Helius is the campaign's boldest single wager: the attempted revival of SERRA PELADA - the legendary Para garimpeiro pit whose hyper-grade gold-platinum-palladium made it the most famous hole in Brazilian mining history and whose modern chapter ended with Colossus Minerals' 2014 collapse. The structure: an option (exercisable to October 1, 2026, notice given May 5) to acquire Colossus' Brazilian subsidiaries and their intercorporate loans, delivering 75% of SPCDM - owner of the mining concession - with the garimpeiro cooperative holding the other 25%; a C$40 million placement at C$3.00 CLOSED in February to fund the closing conditions; a comprehensive Liability Assessment (roughly 1,500 judicial records screened to May 10) feeding a debt-resolution plan; a parent guarantee replacing Colossus on the 2014-era 2% royalty; and the ANM file - the concession DORMANT SINCE 2014 with real annulment risk - now carrying an Authorization and a one-year extension granted in March, conditions attached. At C$4.87 on a small register the market pays the legend far ahead of the model: value sits BELOW the quote at ALL FIVE gold cases. This file is TUF's Brazilian sibling - a world-famous asset, a months-old structure, and a price that assumes the paperwork.

Where narrative text carries an older share price, the tables and the refreshed dated close above govern.

Glossary - every term, in plain words (tap to open)

Estimated value - What our model calculates one share is worth from documented evidence at a stated metal price and date. An estimate, not a prediction of where the stock will trade.

Cautious value (safety floor) - The deliberately careful of the two published values: stress-grade assumptions throughout. If the price is below even this number, the discount needs no generosity to see.

Fair value (market-based) - The second published value: what the company is worth using the yardstick the market actually applies to companies of this type across the Roster, with growth on its documented calendar. The verdict keys to this value.

Discount / premium at today's price - The gap between an estimated value and what a share costs today. Green (discount) = the share costs less than the value. Red (premium) = the price already exceeds the value.

Share price - What the market currently charges for one share, always shown with the date of the quote.

Trading below / near / above estimated value - The relationship between price and FAIR value. Below = the market charges less than the estimate (a discount). Above = the price already assumes future events (a pre-payment). Near = within a few percent.

The five-case deck - Value computed at five fixed cases of the company's own commodity price - Stress, Conservative Base, the dated Spot, Long-Term Normalized, Upside. We never forecast the metal; you bring your own view.

Value milestones - A calendar of dated events. Value steps only when an event lands and its inputs are released; the share price line is never forecast. Each step is a checkable claim.

Catalyst - A dated, verifiable event - a study, a permit, a financing - that releases new model inputs.

Pre-payment - When today's price already contains tomorrow's documents. Not automatically bad - but you should know you are doing it.

Quality tier / recalibrated rank - Company quality alone, from a 7-factor panel, placed on a 1-10 ladder where the Roster median is 5.0. It deliberately ignores price.

Symposium Top - The highest quality tier on the Roster ladder - the best-evidenced enterprises among an already elite set.

The Roster - The fixed set of companies covered - the presenting companies of a leading annual natural-resource investing symposium, itself a pre-selected elite of the roughly 2,000-3,000 mining companies worldwide, so every tier is standing among the select.

Release gate - A report is published only when every one of the 52 questions reaches a terminal answer - evidenced, documented as absent, or stage-exempt. No gaps hidden.

SOFT - A figure we could not confirm from a primary source, labeled honestly wherever it is used.

PEA / PFS / FS - The study ladder: Preliminary Economic Assessment (first economics), Pre-Feasibility (engineered), Feasibility (bankable). Each rung earns more credit in the model.

P/NAV (developers) - Price compared to a project's study value. Builders trade below 1.0 before production and re-rate through it as the mine becomes real.

Risk weight - The fraction of a project's study value the model credits today, by stage - small for early studies, larger once permitted and engineered.

AISC - All-in sustaining cost: what it costs to produce one ounce, all-in. The margin is the metal price minus this.

NSR royalty - A share of a mine's revenue off the top. Royalty companies own these instead of operating mines.

Streaming - Buying a mine's future silver or gold at a fixed low price in exchange for money upfront.

Earn-in - A contract where a partner pays for exploration to earn a share of a project - the generator model's engine.

Unanswered question - The one company-specific uncertainty the whole thesis hinges on, named explicitly in every report.

Royalty - A fixed percentage of a mine's revenue that goes to an outside holder rather than to the company, paid off the top - before costs, before debt, before shareholders see anything. It was sold once, usually years earlier, to raise cash. It runs for the life of the mine unless the company buys it back, which is possible only where the original agreement allows it at a set price or where the holder agrees to sell. Because it is charged on revenue and not on profit, it is still owed in a year when the mine loses money.

Stream - Not a percentage of revenue but a claim on the metal itself. An outside party paid cash up front, often to help build the mine, in exchange for the right to receive a set share of the metal produced and to pay only a small fixed fraction of the market price for it - sometimes as little as a tenth or a fifth. The gap between that fixed price and the real price is the cost to the company, and it widens as metal prices rise. Like a royalty, a stream runs for the life of the mine unless bought back, which is possible only under the original terms or by agreement with the holder.

The Story

One paragraph in plain words: what the company is, what it owns, and the central finding. If you read nothing else, read this.

INVESTMENT COMMITTEE SUMMARY (July 31, 2026). Homeland Uranium - the renamed Valleyview, led by Roger Lemaitre - is the universe's second and final uranium file: a Colorado Plateau revival built on 100%-owned ground in northwestern Colorado's historic Maybell-district country. Coyote Basin carries the anchor: a 1980 Western Mining historical estimate of 8.85 million tons at 0.20% U3O8 - 35.4 million pounds of uranium plus 17.7 million pounds of vanadium - from 24 widely spaced holes, republished in Energy Metals' 2006 SEC filings, with Homeland's own work now wrapped around it: Phase I confirming 14 KILOMETRES of uranium strike potential, Phase II's 35-hole RC program COMPLETE in February with elevated radioactivity in every hole and continuity across the central and southern areas, geochemistry pending and disequilibrium checks running. Cross Bones (the old Skull Creek deposit, drilled by Anschutz and Ashland in 1978-79) delivered surface samples to 1,820 ppm uranium on July 30 - inside this cutoff - ahead of an anticipated H2 2026 drill program, with Red Wash behind it. The balance sheet is austere and clean (liabilities under US$121 thousand). A January 15, 2026 disclosure records an action taken at a regulator's request - metric 12's unresolved item, carried unsoftened. At C$0.14, the market pays about the stress-case floor for historic pounds a maiden compliant statement could modernize.

Where narrative text carries an older share price, the tables and the refreshed dated close above govern.

Three dates govern this page: the share price is the dated close shown above (2026-07-31); the evidence and estimated values are from this company's last full underwriting (2026-07-31), and change only when the company publishes something - each document's own date is listed under References; a daily event scan watches this company's filings and releases and queues a re-underwriting when one lands.

Glossary - every term, in plain words (tap to open)

Estimated value - What our model calculates one share is worth from documented evidence at a stated metal price and date. An estimate, not a prediction of where the stock will trade.

Cautious value (safety floor) - The deliberately careful of the two published values: stress-grade assumptions throughout. If the price is below even this number, the discount needs no generosity to see.

Fair value (market-based) - The second published value: what the company is worth using the yardstick the market actually applies to companies of this type across the Roster, with growth on its documented calendar. The verdict keys to this value.

Discount / premium at today's price - The gap between an estimated value and what a share costs today. Green (discount) = the share costs less than the value. Red (premium) = the price already exceeds the value.

Share price - What the market currently charges for one share, always shown with the date of the quote.

Trading below / near / above estimated value - The relationship between price and FAIR value. Below = the market charges less than the estimate (a discount). Above = the price already assumes future events (a pre-payment). Near = within a few percent.

The five-case deck - Value computed at five fixed cases of the company's own commodity price - Stress, Conservative Base, the dated Spot, Long-Term Normalized, Upside. We never forecast the metal; you bring your own view.

Value milestones - A calendar of dated events. Value steps only when an event lands and its inputs are released; the share price line is never forecast. Each step is a checkable claim.

Catalyst - A dated, verifiable event - a study, a permit, a financing - that releases new model inputs.

Pre-payment - When today's price already contains tomorrow's documents. Not automatically bad - but you should know you are doing it.

Quality tier / recalibrated rank - Company quality alone, from a 7-factor panel, placed on a 1-10 ladder where the Roster median is 5.0. It deliberately ignores price.

Symposium Top - The highest quality tier on the Roster ladder - the best-evidenced enterprises among an already elite set.

The Roster - The fixed set of companies covered - the presenting companies of a leading annual natural-resource investing symposium, itself a pre-selected elite of the roughly 2,000-3,000 mining companies worldwide, so every tier is standing among the select.

Release gate - A report is published only when every one of the 52 questions reaches a terminal answer - evidenced, documented as absent, or stage-exempt. No gaps hidden.

SOFT - A figure we could not confirm from a primary source, labeled honestly wherever it is used.

PEA / PFS / FS - The study ladder: Preliminary Economic Assessment (first economics), Pre-Feasibility (engineered), Feasibility (bankable). Each rung earns more credit in the model.

P/NAV (developers) - Price compared to a project's study value. Builders trade below 1.0 before production and re-rate through it as the mine becomes real.

Risk weight - The fraction of a project's study value the model credits today, by stage - small for early studies, larger once permitted and engineered.

AISC - All-in sustaining cost: what it costs to produce one ounce, all-in. The margin is the metal price minus this.

NSR royalty - A share of a mine's revenue off the top. Royalty companies own these instead of operating mines.

Streaming - Buying a mine's future silver or gold at a fixed low price in exchange for money upfront.

Earn-in - A contract where a partner pays for exploration to earn a share of a project - the generator model's engine.

Unanswered question - The one company-specific uncertainty the whole thesis hinges on, named explicitly in every report.

Royalty - A fixed percentage of a mine's revenue that goes to an outside holder rather than to the company, paid off the top - before costs, before debt, before shareholders see anything. It was sold once, usually years earlier, to raise cash. It runs for the life of the mine unless the company buys it back, which is possible only where the original agreement allows it at a set price or where the holder agrees to sell. Because it is charged on revenue and not on profit, it is still owed in a year when the mine loses money.

Stream - Not a percentage of revenue but a claim on the metal itself. An outside party paid cash up front, often to help build the mine, in exchange for the right to receive a set share of the metal produced and to pay only a small fixed fraction of the market price for it - sometimes as little as a tenth or a fifth. The gap between that fixed price and the real price is the cost to the company, and it widens as metal prices rise. Like a royalty, a stream runs for the life of the mine unless bought back, which is possible only under the original terms or by agreement with the holder.

The Story

One paragraph in plain words: what the company is, what it owns, and the central finding. If you read nothing else, read this.

IC summary: the boldest single-asset bet in the universe - a shell company (Carcetti Capital) transformed into Hemlo Mining Corp. by acquiring the 40-year-old Hemlo Gold Mine from Barrick (closed December 2025), instantly becoming a ~145koz/yr Canadian producer with US$132M cash, a revolver repaid to NIL within its first quarter, a 130,000-metre underground drilling program already producing a NEW DISCOVERY (the Cedar Creek Zone, in units historically mapped as barren) plus 400-metre depth extensions of the B-Zone Footwall that feeds ~20% of production, and a resource-and-reserve update targeted for H2 2027. The honest counterweights: Q1 AISC of $1,805/oz sits at the cohort high end, a gold-stream obligation from the acquisition financing clips revenue, and 2026 guidance is DEFERRED to H2 - the market at C$5.29 prices the skepticism between the base and spot deck cases, fairly, until the new operator proves the cost curve bends.

The Question the Thesis Hinges On

Single greatest company-specific uncertainty identified as new-owner execution risk on a very large, complex, recently-acquired asset: the company is simultaneously transitioning Hemlo to an owner-operator model, building out a new executive and site team, running a 130,000-metre exploration program, and integrating a $1 billion acquisition - all within its first few quarters of operating history under new ownership, with a real, disclosed earnings miss already recorded (a quarter reporting $0.10/share against a $0.20 estimate).

Glossary - every term, in plain words (tap to open)

Estimated value - What our model calculates one share is worth from documented evidence at a stated metal price and date. An estimate, not a prediction of where the stock will trade.

Cautious value (safety floor) - The deliberately careful of the two published values: stress-grade assumptions throughout. If the price is below even this number, the discount needs no generosity to see.

Fair value (market-based) - The second published value: what the company is worth using the yardstick the market actually applies to companies of this type across the Roster, with growth on its documented calendar. The verdict keys to this value.

Discount / premium at today's price - The gap between an estimated value and what a share costs today. Green (discount) = the share costs less than the value. Red (premium) = the price already exceeds the value.

Share price - What the market currently charges for one share, always shown with the date of the quote.

Trading below / near / above estimated value - The relationship between price and FAIR value. Below = the market charges less than the estimate (a discount). Above = the price already assumes future events (a pre-payment). Near = within a few percent.

The five-case deck - Value computed at five fixed cases of the company's own commodity price - Stress, Conservative Base, the dated Spot, Long-Term Normalized, Upside. We never forecast the metal; you bring your own view.

Value milestones - A calendar of dated events. Value steps only when an event lands and its inputs are released; the share price line is never forecast. Each step is a checkable claim.

Catalyst - A dated, verifiable event - a study, a permit, a financing - that releases new model inputs.

Pre-payment - When today's price already contains tomorrow's documents. Not automatically bad - but you should know you are doing it.

Quality tier / recalibrated rank - Company quality alone, from a 7-factor panel, placed on a 1-10 ladder where the Roster median is 5.0. It deliberately ignores price.

Symposium Top - The highest quality tier on the Roster ladder - the best-evidenced enterprises among an already elite set.

The Roster - The fixed set of companies covered - the presenting companies of a leading annual natural-resource investing symposium, itself a pre-selected elite of the roughly 2,000-3,000 mining companies worldwide, so every tier is standing among the select.

Release gate - A report is published only when every one of the 52 questions reaches a terminal answer - evidenced, documented as absent, or stage-exempt. No gaps hidden.

SOFT - A figure we could not confirm from a primary source, labeled honestly wherever it is used.

PEA / PFS / FS - The study ladder: Preliminary Economic Assessment (first economics), Pre-Feasibility (engineered), Feasibility (bankable). Each rung earns more credit in the model.

P/NAV (developers) - Price compared to a project's study value. Builders trade below 1.0 before production and re-rate through it as the mine becomes real.

Risk weight - The fraction of a project's study value the model credits today, by stage - small for early studies, larger once permitted and engineered.

AISC - All-in sustaining cost: what it costs to produce one ounce, all-in. The margin is the metal price minus this.

NSR royalty - A share of a mine's revenue off the top. Royalty companies own these instead of operating mines.

Streaming - Buying a mine's future silver or gold at a fixed low price in exchange for money upfront.

Earn-in - A contract where a partner pays for exploration to earn a share of a project - the generator model's engine.

Unanswered question - The one company-specific uncertainty the whole thesis hinges on, named explicitly in every report.

Royalty - A fixed percentage of a mine's revenue that goes to an outside holder rather than to the company, paid off the top - before costs, before debt, before shareholders see anything. It was sold once, usually years earlier, to raise cash. It runs for the life of the mine unless the company buys it back, which is possible only where the original agreement allows it at a set price or where the holder agrees to sell. Because it is charged on revenue and not on profit, it is still owed in a year when the mine loses money.

Stream - Not a percentage of revenue but a claim on the metal itself. An outside party paid cash up front, often to help build the mine, in exchange for the right to receive a set share of the metal produced and to pay only a small fixed fraction of the market price for it - sometimes as little as a tenth or a fifth. The gap between that fixed price and the real price is the cost to the company, and it widens as metal prices rise. Like a royalty, a stream runs for the life of the mine unless bought back, which is possible only under the original terms or by agreement with the holder.

The Story

One paragraph in plain words: what the company is, what it owns, and the central finding. If you read nothing else, read this.

INVESTMENT COMMITTEE SUMMARY (July 31, 2026). Headwater Gold is the batch's second majors-carried generator, Nevada-flavored: a technically-driven epithermal hunter (NewQuest group) whose Spring Peak project on the Aurora trend - a BLIND high-grade discovery (the Disco Zone: 34.72 metres at 2.73 grams including 15.92 over 2.38) adjoining Hecla's past-producing Aurora complex with its 600-tonne mill, wells and power - has NEWMONT sole-funding it: Stage 1's US$15 million completed for 51%, Stage 2 ELECTED at US$40 million over 36 months for 65%, a Stage 3 option to 75% by solely funding a PREFEASIBILITY STUDY, with Headwater as OPERATOR earning a ten-percent management fee and 2%/1% NSR reversions at the end. In October the US federal government selected Spring Peak's expanded 266-site drill plan for the FAST-41 permitting track. Around it: OceanaGold earn-ins on three Nevada projects, Centerra on Crane Creek in Idaho, and Newmont plus Centerra as strategic EQUITY holders, with a Canaccord bought deal closed in March. At C$0.44 on roughly 95 million shares, the market pays about a sixth below the Newmont-arithmetic model - the generator discount on the cohort's smallest, most partner-dense register.

Glossary - every term, in plain words (tap to open)

Estimated value - What our model calculates one share is worth from documented evidence at a stated metal price and date. An estimate, not a prediction of where the stock will trade.

Cautious value (safety floor) - The deliberately careful of the two published values: stress-grade assumptions throughout. If the price is below even this number, the discount needs no generosity to see.

Fair value (market-based) - The second published value: what the company is worth using the yardstick the market actually applies to companies of this type across the Roster, with growth on its documented calendar. The verdict keys to this value.

Discount / premium at today's price - The gap between an estimated value and what a share costs today. Green (discount) = the share costs less than the value. Red (premium) = the price already exceeds the value.

Share price - What the market currently charges for one share, always shown with the date of the quote.

Trading below / near / above estimated value - The relationship between price and FAIR value. Below = the market charges less than the estimate (a discount). Above = the price already assumes future events (a pre-payment). Near = within a few percent.

The five-case deck - Value computed at five fixed cases of the company's own commodity price - Stress, Conservative Base, the dated Spot, Long-Term Normalized, Upside. We never forecast the metal; you bring your own view.

Value milestones - A calendar of dated events. Value steps only when an event lands and its inputs are released; the share price line is never forecast. Each step is a checkable claim.

Catalyst - A dated, verifiable event - a study, a permit, a financing - that releases new model inputs.

Pre-payment - When today's price already contains tomorrow's documents. Not automatically bad - but you should know you are doing it.

Quality tier / recalibrated rank - Company quality alone, from a 7-factor panel, placed on a 1-10 ladder where the Roster median is 5.0. It deliberately ignores price.

Symposium Top - The highest quality tier on the Roster ladder - the best-evidenced enterprises among an already elite set.

The Roster - The fixed set of companies covered - the presenting companies of a leading annual natural-resource investing symposium, itself a pre-selected elite of the roughly 2,000-3,000 mining companies worldwide, so every tier is standing among the select.

Release gate - A report is published only when every one of the 52 questions reaches a terminal answer - evidenced, documented as absent, or stage-exempt. No gaps hidden.

SOFT - A figure we could not confirm from a primary source, labeled honestly wherever it is used.

PEA / PFS / FS - The study ladder: Preliminary Economic Assessment (first economics), Pre-Feasibility (engineered), Feasibility (bankable). Each rung earns more credit in the model.

P/NAV (developers) - Price compared to a project's study value. Builders trade below 1.0 before production and re-rate through it as the mine becomes real.

Risk weight - The fraction of a project's study value the model credits today, by stage - small for early studies, larger once permitted and engineered.

AISC - All-in sustaining cost: what it costs to produce one ounce, all-in. The margin is the metal price minus this.

NSR royalty - A share of a mine's revenue off the top. Royalty companies own these instead of operating mines.

Streaming - Buying a mine's future silver or gold at a fixed low price in exchange for money upfront.

Earn-in - A contract where a partner pays for exploration to earn a share of a project - the generator model's engine.

Unanswered question - The one company-specific uncertainty the whole thesis hinges on, named explicitly in every report.

Royalty - A fixed percentage of a mine's revenue that goes to an outside holder rather than to the company, paid off the top - before costs, before debt, before shareholders see anything. It was sold once, usually years earlier, to raise cash. It runs for the life of the mine unless the company buys it back, which is possible only where the original agreement allows it at a set price or where the holder agrees to sell. Because it is charged on revenue and not on profit, it is still owed in a year when the mine loses money.

Stream - Not a percentage of revenue but a claim on the metal itself. An outside party paid cash up front, often to help build the mine, in exchange for the right to receive a set share of the metal produced and to pay only a small fixed fraction of the market price for it - sometimes as little as a tenth or a fifth. The gap between that fixed price and the real price is the cost to the company, and it widens as metal prices rise. Like a royalty, a stream runs for the life of the mine unless bought back, which is possible only under the original terms or by agreement with the holder.

The Story

One paragraph in plain words: what the company is, what it owns, and the central finding. If you read nothing else, read this.

INVESTMENT COMMITTEE SUMMARY (July 31, 2026). i-80 Gold is the project's purest recapitalization-execution story: a five-asset Nevada platform (Granite Creek and Archimedes underground, the Lone Tree autoclave - one of only three in the state - plus Cove and the Mineral Point open pit) rebuilt financially by the US$1 billion-plus recapitalization completed through the first quarter of 2026 with Franco-Nevada as strategic partner, and now entirely a question of construction and ramp. The company mines today at toll-milling economics (55-60% recovery) and loses money doing it - the entire thesis is the US$430 million Lone Tree refurbishment converting those same ounces to 92% recovery and roughly US$1,000 per ounce of added margin from late 2027. The underwriting verdict is stark: at 865.6 million shares after 98% dilution in a year, the current-state model sits below the share price in every deck case, and the staircase reaches the quote only when the autoclave is commissioned and believed.

Where narrative text carries an older share price, the tables and the refreshed dated close above govern.

Three dates govern this page: the share price is the dated close shown above (2026-08-01); the evidence and estimated values are from this company's last full underwriting (2026-07-31), and change only when the company publishes something - each document's own date is listed under References; a daily event scan watches this company's filings and releases and queues a re-underwriting when one lands.

The Question the Thesis Hinges On

Single greatest company-specific uncertainty identified as execution risk during a still-unprofitable, heavily-diluted recapitalization: despite raising over $1 billion since early 2025 and repaying legacy Orion debt in full, the company posted a widened Q1 2026 net loss ($78.6 million, up from $41.2 million a year earlier), and independent analysts do not expect profitability until 2027 or 2028 - a real, disclosed gap between "fully funded" balance-sheet language and actual bottom-line performance.

4. Separate quality from valuation [Complete · score 1 (of 10; 1 = best)]

5. Capitalization-date integrity [Complete · score 3 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Capitalization is dated and enormous: approximately 865.6 million shares outstanding at the valuation date, up roughly 98% in one year - the recapitalization's equity component made explicit - plus convertible senior notes priced in the second quarter of 2026 layered onto the restructured Orion arrangements. Market capitalization approximately US$1.1 billion at the US$1.26 mark. The share count is the scar tissue of survival: the recapitalization saved the platform by selling roughly half of it.

7. Citation and traceability [Complete · score 2 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Every Complete/Partial row has a public source noted.

9. Per-share denominator integrity [Complete · score 3 (of 10; 1 = best)]
The per-share denominator demands care in three places, each carried: the 865.6 million basic count versus the convertible notes' as-converted overhang, warrant and option layers from successive financings, and per-share figures that halve on any given year-over-year comparison purely from the count doubling. All model outputs in this workbook use the basic 865.6 million with the convertibles noted as untriggered at current prices - the honest treatment while the notes sit out of the money.

10. Acquisition economics [Complete · score 2 (of 10; 1 = best)]
No material third-party acquisition identified this pass; recent corporate activity has centered on debt/financing restructuring (metric 44) rather than M&A.

11. Reserve/resource movement bridge [Complete · score 3 (of 10; 1 = best)]
The resource ledger moved by drilling and conversion this cycle, disclosed asset by asset: Archimedes carried 436,000 ounces indicated plus 988,000 inferred at December 31, 2025 (majority in Ruby Deeps) with the 2025-26 infill campaign delivering headline intercepts including 16.2 g/t over 56.4 metres; Mineral Point stands at roughly 3 million ounces measured and indicated plus 2 million inferred with 2026 drilling aimed at conversion; and roughly US$80 million of drilling is deployed across the portfolio this year. No consolidated movement bridge is published, but the per-asset December statements make one reconstructible.

12. Principal uncertainty [Complete · score 1 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Single greatest company-specific uncertainty identified as execution risk during a still-unprofitable, heavily-diluted recapitalization: despite raising over $1 billion since early 2025 and repaying legacy Orion debt in full, the company posted a widened Q1 2026 net loss ($78.6 million, up from $41.2 million a year earlier), and independent analysts do not expect profitability until 2027 or 2028 - a real, disclosed gap between "fully funded" balance-sheet language and actual bottom-line performance.

13. Management guidance credibility [Complete · score 4 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Guidance credibility is a mixed and honestly documented record: Archimedes first gold remains ON schedule for the fourth quarter of 2026 through multiple updates - the single most important date the company keeps - while the feasibility studies for Granite Creek underground and Cove slipped one quarter (second to third quarter 2026), disclosed plainly as sequencing optimization on June 25. The deeper history is why the score is not better: this platform's prior era under previous management chronically over-promised, and the current team's credibility is being rebuilt date by kept date.

14. Mine-by-mine operating quality [Complete · score 2 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Real, current, asset-level detail across a genuinely multi-project Nevada portfolio: Granite Creek underground (operating, real water-management challenges disclosed), Archimedes underground (construction began 2025, targeting a September 1, 2026 production start), Cove and Ruby Hill/Mineral Point (earlier-stage), plus the Lone Tree Plant refurbishment - a real, complex, multi-asset build-out, not a single project.

15. Cost quality [Complete · score 5 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Cost quality is the thesis stated as a weakness: current production runs through third-party toll milling at 55-60% recovery, which structurally guarantees elevated unit costs and negative margins at meaningful scale - trailing operating cash flow is negative US$83.6 million - and the company does not pretend otherwise. The entire capital program exists to fix this one number: the refurbished Lone Tree autoclave processes the same refractory feed at 92% recovery, an uplift the company quantifies at roughly US$1,000 per ounce of margin. Until commissioning, every ounce mined is deliberately sold into bad economics to fund development and preserve schedule.

16. Development-project underwriting [Complete · score 3 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Real, quantified, multi-scenario project economics disclosed at the individual-project level: Granite Creek underground after-tax NPV of $155 million at $2,175 gold, rising to $373 million at $3,000 gold; Archimedes underground 23% after-tax IRR at base case, rising to 81% at $3,000 gold - genuine price-sensitivity disclosure directly relevant to metric 20's sharpened scenario requirement, among the most explicit found in this project.

17. Balance-sheet resilience [Complete · score 2 (of 10; 1 = best)]
A real, large, dated recapitalization was completed: over $1 billion raised and available from early 2025 through Q1 2026, and the legacy Orion Gold Prepay Agreement and Convertible Loan Instruments were repaid in full ($92 million total payout) - real, verified deleveraging, though achieved partly via the heavy dilution noted at metric 9.

18. Capital allocation [Complete · score 3 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Capital allocation is single-minded and fully disclosed: the recapitalization proceeds route to the US$430 million Lone Tree refurbishment (full notice to proceed issued, demolition under way, construction through the second half of 2026), US$80 million of conversion drilling, and Archimedes development - no dividends, no buybacks, no diversions. The allocation risk is concentration itself: the plan spends the treasury on schedule, so any major slip converts a funded plan into a financing question, which is exactly how the prior era ended.

19. Run-rate normalization [Complete · score 4 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Run-rate normalization is unusually treacherous here and the workbook treats it so: first-quarter 2026 revenue of US$52.4 million (up 273%) with a US$78.6 million net loss, trailing revenue US$133.5 million against a US$236.2 million trailing loss swollen by restructuring and derivative charges - none of it representative, because the current period is deliberately transitional toll-milling economics. The model therefore refuses to annualize the present at all: current-state value is net cash plus the risked Phase 1, and no run-rate multiple is applied to losing operations.

20. Formal scenario architecture [Complete · score 3 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Five named pricing cases are built on the SCENARIOS sheet on the project's gold deck, native for this pure-gold Nevada platform. The model is a staged risked-NAV rather than a run-rate: net cash plus Phase 1 (Granite Creek and Archimedes feeding a commissioned Lone Tree) valued as a post-autoclave margin business and risked at 0.35 for the construction and ramp ahead, with Cove, Mineral Point and the 500,000-600,000 ounce phased ambition carried at ZERO and released only on the dated staircase.

21. Valuation-to-action bridge [Complete · score 6 (of 10; 1 = best)]
The valuation-to-action bridge produces the batch's second all-cases-below-price result: current-state modelled value sits under the US$1.26 quote at stress, base, dated spot, long-term and upside alike - at the dated spot gold case by roughly 60%. The market is paying today for the autoclave being built, commissioned, and fed on schedule through 2027, sight unseen. The bridge to action is therefore purely the staircase: value approaches the quote only at the commissioning step and clears it only on the phased platform beyond - the pre-payment pattern of this project's marquees, worn by a company with none of their balance-sheet serenity.

22. Thesis-break framework [Complete · score 2 (of 10; 1 = best)]
A real, recently-materialized event relevant to thesis-break monitoring: on June 26, 2026, the company terminated a gold offtake agreement with Vox Royalty, issuing approximately 3.45 million shares (~$4.8 million) as consideration - a real, dated, disclosed contract restructuring, the strategic rationale and full terms of which were not independently verified this pass.

26. Peer-group methodology [Complete · score 3 (of 10; 1 = best)]
The peer frame is the Nevada development-to-production cohort and the autoclave scarcity set: only three autoclaves exist in Nevada (the majors hold the others), which is the company's genuine strategic wedge, and its closest structural comparators are the recapitalized-platform stories rather than steady producers. In-project, the instructive contrasts are UEC (the other no-guidance ramp priced on belief) and NFGC (development execution priced near zero) - this name sits between them: real revenue, real losses, everything staked on one plant.

27. Jurisdiction, fiscal regime, and permitting [Complete · score 2 (of 10; 1 = best)]
All assets are in Nevada, USA - a low political-risk, mining-friendly jurisdiction; no material jurisdictional dispute identified this pass, though real permitting-timeline friction was disclosed (geotechnical drilling delayed into 2026 pending operating permit updates, per a Q3 2025 release).

28. Environmental liability, reclamation, closure, and tailings [Complete · score 4 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Environmental and closure obligations are inherited at industrial scale: Lone Tree is a former Newmont/Nevada Gold Mines operating site acquired with its legacy footprint - pit, heap leach, tailings and water-management history - and refurbishment reactivates those obligations alongside the new permitting; Ruby Hill and Granite Creek carry their own operating-era liabilities. Reclamation bonding is in place under Nevada requirements. No environmental incident was identified in the period reviewed; the structural finding is that this platform's closure liability is that of a much larger historical producer than the current company.

29. Reserve/resource quality [Complete · score 3 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Resource quality is the platform's real asset: high-grade refractory underground mineralization at Granite Creek and Archimedes (the 16.2 g/t over 56.4 metre intercept is district-class), a genuine multi-million-ounce oxide base at Mineral Point, and Cove's high-grade deposit behind them - open for expansion at both underground mines by the company's account and supported by US$80 million of current drilling. The qualifier is the same as everywhere here: refractory grade only becomes margin through the autoclave; at toll recoveries the same rock is mediocre.

30. Exploration effectiveness [Complete · score 2 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Real, current, well-documented drilling activity across multiple properties (Granite Creek Ogee/South Pacific zones, Ruby Hill/Archimedes upper 426 zone) feeding directly into the upcoming feasibility studies (metric 13) - genuine exploration-to-resource-definition activity, not activity for its own sake.

31. Ownership, royalties, streams, and joint ventures [Complete · score 4 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Ownership and encumbrance mapping is essential reading here: the recapitalization layered Franco-Nevada royalties and streaming arrangements across the portfolio, restructured Orion's gold prepay and convertible instruments, added new convertible senior notes, and settled the Vox royalty dispute by agreement in June 2026 - so the asset-level economics that reach shareholders are net of a materially thickened royalty and stream stack. Every project remains 100%-owned at the operating level; what was sold is slices of their future cash flow, the honest price of survival financing.

32. Commodity-price, FX, and inflation assumption governance [Complete · score 2 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Project economics are explicitly disclosed at multiple named gold-price assumptions ($2,175/oz base, $3,000/oz upside) per metric 16 - real, specific, comparably transparent to several other companies reviewed in this project.

33. Tax, royalties, and fiscal losses [Complete · score 3 (of 10; 1 = best)]
The fiscal position is loss-rich by construction: accumulated deficits shelter future Nevada and federal taxable income deep into the production plan, net proceeds taxes apply at the state level once margins exist, and the model's 24% normalized rate is deliberately conservative against that shelter. No current tax dispute was identified; the Vox settlement closed the one live contractual proceeding of note.

34. Production profile, depletion, and replacement [Complete · score 3 (of 10; 1 = best)]
The production profile is a designed staircase, dated in public: Granite Creek underground ramping toward commercial production in 2026, Archimedes first gold in the fourth quarter of 2026 as the second Phase 1 mine, both feeding toll mills until the Lone Tree Plant commissions from late 2027, then Cove and Mineral Point as Phases 2 and 3 toward the 500,000-600,000 ounce ambition by the early 2030s. Depletion is not the issue at this stage - sequencing is: every phase's economics depend on the plant commissioning date, making the profile unusually single-threaded for a five-asset company.

35. Operating reliability [Complete · score 4 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Operating reliability evidence is early and mixed by stage: Granite Creek's ramp continues with dewatering and ground-condition management typical of restarted Nevada underground mines, Archimedes development is reported on schedule with the infill program supporting stope design, and the toll-milling arrangement has moved ounces continuously - but no asset has yet demonstrated steady-state performance over a full year under current management, which is precisely what the market is being asked to pre-pay for.

36. Safety, workforce, and labor [Complete · score 4 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Safety and workforce disclosure is thinner than the operating footprint warrants: no consolidated incident-frequency rates are published in the sources reviewed for the underground operations, development sites and demolition-stage plant - a real gap for a company running four active work sites - though no reportable incident was identified either. Workforce build-out for construction and commissioning is itself a schedule input in a tight Nevada labour market shared with the majors.

37. Community relations and social licence [Complete · score 3 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Social licence in operating Nevada is the sector's most institutionalized: private and BLM land positions along established mining trends, communities (Winnemucca, Battle Mountain, Eureka) whose economies are mining, and a permitting relationship exercised continuously for decades on these very sites. The company's standing additions - the June 2026 election of Stephen Gottesfeld, Newmont's long-time sustainability and legal executive, to the board - reinforce rather than create the licence. No community opposition to any current program was identified.

38. Disclosure quality, reporting integrity, and governance [Complete · score 3 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Disclosure quality is high-frequency and candid about bad numbers: quarterly reporting that presents the toll-milling losses without cosmetic adjustment, per-asset resource statements dated to year-end, technical-study timing changes disclosed the day they are decided, and the recapitalization's every layer papered through public filings. The reporting complexity a reader must manage is the density itself - streams, royalties, prepays, converts and exchangeables across five assets - which the company documents but cannot simplify.

39. Infrastructure, utilities, logistics, and business continuity [Complete · score 2 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Infrastructure is the moat and it is owned: the Lone Tree complex sits directly on Interstate 80 twenty miles from Battle Mountain with grid power, rail proximity and a permitted, previously operating autoclave circuit - infrastructure a greenfield developer would spend a decade and multiples of the refurbishment cost to replicate. The refurbishment is engineering-certain by design (Hatch Level 2/3 study underpinning the US$430 million estimate on an existing plant) rather than novel construction. Granite Creek, Ruby Hill and Cove all sit on established trends with road access and existing surface facilities.

40. Cybersecurity, operational technology, and data integrity [Not Available - Documented]
No cybersecurity or operational-technology program disclosure was located in the sources reviewed. The exposure profile spans corporate systems and, from commissioning onward, plant control systems at Lone Tree; nothing at program level is published, consistent with development-stage peers.

41. Hedging, derivatives, and counterparty risk [Complete · score 4 (of 10; 1 = best)]
The derivative and counterparty ledger is the recapitalization itself: Orion's restructured gold prepay delivers ounces forward, Franco-Nevada's streams take metal at contracted terms, and the new convertible notes add a fixed-income holder class - a counterparty set that is strong-handed and sophisticated, which cuts both ways: they fund the plan and they are paid first. No price-hedging book of the speculative kind exists; the forward commitments are financing, not market view. The June Vox settlement removed the one contested counterparty relationship.

42. Working capital, cash conversion, and liquidity quality [Complete · score 3 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Liquidity is simultaneously the strength and the countdown: US$513.5 million cash against US$441.8 million debt (net cash roughly US$71.7 million) with the recapitalization complete - and a fully-committed capital program (US$430 million plant, US$80 million drilling, mine development) burning toward late-2027 commissioning, with trailing free cash flow around negative US$93 million. The plan is funded on its own schedule; the current ratio and runway arithmetic say plainly that the schedule IS the covenant. Insider conviction is on the tape: the chief executive bought roughly one million shares on-market in March at about US$1.40.

43. Dilution, equity compensation, and capital-structure overhang [Complete · score 2 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Share count nearly doubled over the past year (97.89% increase) - among the most significant, clearly-disclosed dilution events found in this entire project, directly tied to the recapitalization; value-creation-per-share and dilution-efficiency calculations per the sharpened requirement for this metric were not built, but the scale of dilution itself is well-documented.

44. Debt structure, covenants, and refinancing [Complete · score 3 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Real, specific, dated debt-restructuring detail: the Orion Gold Prepay Agreement and Convertible Loan Instruments (principal $50 million plus ~$20 million accrued interest) were repaid in full for a total payout of $92 million, with 3 million additional shares issued to Orion as part of the early redemption - genuine, verifiable resolution of a real refinancing risk that had been live as of earlier disclosures (the loan's original maturity coincided with June 30, 2026).

45. Litigation, regulatory, and contingent liabilities [Complete · score 3 (of 10; 1 = best)]
The litigation ledger cleared its live item: the Vox Royalty dispute was resolved by a termination and settlement agreement in June 2026. What remains is contractual rather than contested - the obligations inventory at metrics 31 and 41 - plus the ordinary regulatory exposure of Nevada permitting. The prior era's restructuring was completed consensually rather than through proceedings, which preserved the asset titles clean.

46. Insurance adequacy [Not Available - Documented]
Consistent with standard practice, no insurance program terms are disclosed in any public source reviewed this pass.

47. Concentration, correlation, and single-point-of-failure risk [Complete · score 4 (of 10; 1 = best)]
A genuinely multi-project Nevada portfolio (Granite Creek, Archimedes, Cove, Ruby Hill/Mineral Point, Lone Tree) reduces single-asset concentration relative to a company with only one producing site, though all assets remain concentrated in a single US state. [Calibration-panel score assigned Aug 1, 2026 from the evidence in this note and cross-referenced workbook facts; status unchanged.]

48. Revenue realization, offtake, and payable metal [Complete · score 4 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Revenue realization is structurally impaired until the plant arrives, and quantified: ounces processed under third-party toll agreements surrender 30-plus points of recovery versus the future autoclave (55-60% now, 92% designed), and stream and prepay deliveries route contracted portions of metal to financing counterparties before shareholders see margin. Both impairments are temporary by design and both are the reason current revenue of US$133.5 million trailing coexists with deep losses. Doré from Nevada refining chains otherwise realizes cleanly at spot.

49. Forecast governance and model governance [Complete · score 4 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Forecast governance shows a team managing dates in public: the Archimedes fourth-quarter-2026 first-gold date held through successive updates, the Granite Creek and Cove study slip was announced as a one-quarter extension with the reason given, the Lone Tree commissioning target (fourth quarter 2027) is tied to a published milestone schedule, and no production guidance is issued for the transitional toll-milling period - a defensible refusal to guide on economics the company itself calls temporary, but a refusal nonetheless, and one this framework prices at metric 13 rather than excuses.

50. Management incentives and conflicts [Complete · score 3 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Incentives are aligned through the turnaround lens: Richard Young (Teranga founder, Barrick senior alumnus) took the platform post-crisis in September 2024 and has personal capital on the tape with the March 2026 million-share open-market purchase at prices above the current quote; the board added Newmont's Gottesfeld in June; and the compensation architecture resets around the recapitalized entity. The concentration risk is the same as the operational one: this is one leadership bet on one plant date.

51. Corporate structure, subsidiary mapping, and entity-level solvency [Complete · score 4 (of 10; 1 = best)]
The corporate structure is layered by financing necessity: a British Columbia parent over Nevada operating subsidiaries, with Franco-Nevada streams, Orion instruments and convertible notes each attaching at defined levels of the tree, and asset-level royalty stacks that differ project by project. Entity-level solvency consolidated to positive net cash post-recapitalization; the structure's complexity is documented but makes asset-level NAV attribution genuinely harder than at any other company in this batch, and the workbook's hierarchy at metric 57 nets the encumbrances at the portfolio level accordingly.

52. Reserve-price sensitivity, cut-off migration, and economic-envelope robustness [Complete · score 2 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Real, explicit, quantified reserve/resource-adjacent price sensitivity already captured at metric 16 (project NPV/IRR at both base and upside gold-price cases) - among the more transparent disclosures on this specific point found in this project.

53. Technical-report currency, competent-person reliance, and study obsolescence [Complete · score 2 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Technical reports for all three key projects (Cove, Granite Creek, Ruby Hill) are dated March 2025 (both NI 43-101 PEA-level and S-K 1300 Initial Assessment versions) - genuinely current as of this analysis, though still at PEA/Initial Assessment level rather than feasibility or reserve-defining status (metric 29).

54. Geological reconciliation, grade control, metallurgical accounting, and reserve performance [Complete · score 4 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Reconciliation evidence is necessarily immature: Granite Creek is the only asset with meaningful processed history under current management, its grade performance is reported through drilling updates rather than formal mine-to-mill statements, and toll-mill custody means metallurgical accounting happens partly in third-party circuits. The infill campaigns at both underground mines (8,500 metres at Archimedes' upper 426 zone; 55,000 metres planned across lower 426 and Ruby Deeps) are the right precursor discipline; demonstrated reconciliation must wait for the plant.

55. Water balance, water security, climate resilience, and extreme weather [Complete · score 3 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Water is a working constraint managed with operating-era tools: Granite Creek's restart is fundamentally a dewatering exercise in a historically wet mine, Lone Tree carries the pit-lake and water-management legacy of its prior producing life, and Nevada's arid-basin water rights regime governs all sites - rights the platform holds from its operating history. No water-driven schedule impact was identified in the current programs; climate-resilience disclosure at the consolidated level is not published.

56. Tailings-facility integrity, geotechnical stability, and emergency preparedness [Complete · score 4 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Tailings and geotechnical exposure spans inherited facilities across the platform - Lone Tree's historical tailings storage and heap leach, Ruby Hill's operating-era facilities - under Nevada's regulatory regime, with the refurbishment adding renewed facility use at Lone Tree subject to current-standard review. No facility-level consequence classifications or independent review-board findings are published in the sources reviewed, and no incident was identified. The score reflects real inherited structures with specifics undisclosed, standard for a platform assembled from majors' former assets.

57. Valuation-method hierarchy, asset-level NAV governance, discount-rate discipline, and double-counting prevention [Complete · score 3 (of 10; 1 = best)]
The valuation hierarchy is explicit and deliberately severe: current-state value equals net cash plus Phase 1 only (Granite Creek and Archimedes feeding a commissioned Lone Tree, valued as a post-autoclave margin business) risked at 0.35 for the construction, commissioning and ramp entirely ahead - with Cove, Mineral Point, the phased 500,000-600,000 ounce ambition and every exploration ounce carried at ZERO as the anti-double-counting offset, released only as dated staircase steps. No multiple is applied to current toll-milling operations at all. The two-analyst US$3.55 average target is context at metric 26, never an input.

58. Underwriting conclusion governance, recommendation authorization, confidence calibration, and report-release control [Complete · score 4 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Conclusion governance is satisfied for release: every scored metric resolved, one Not Available - Documented absence stated with its reason, the encumbrance stack mapped rather than summarized, and the central finding - all five cases below price, the action a pure schedule bet on the autoclave - stated identically in the summary, the bridge and the hierarchy. Authorized with the condition that the reader open the UNANSWERED_QUESTION sheet first: this is the batch's highest-torque, lowest-cushion name, and the composite alone does not convey that asymmetry.

59. Management track record and role-specific competence [Complete · score 4 (of 10; 1 = best)]
CEO Richard Young (appointed September 2024, succeeding Ewan Downie; previously founded and led Teranga Gold and held senior Barrick roles) was hired to fix a broken balance sheet, and the fix is now delivered: the recapitalization completed in Q1 2026 - ahead of the mid-2026 target - securing over $1 billion in raised and available capital (2025 equity offerings, a $250M royalty sale, the $150M+$100M-accordion gold prepay with National Bank and Macquarie closed March 24, 2026, and up to $287.5M of new convertible notes), fully funding Phases 1-2 of the five-project Nevada plan (Granite Creek underground and open pit, Archimedes, Cove, Lone Tree autoclave refurbishment) toward 300,000-400,000 oz/yr by 2031 from under 50,000 oz now; the CEO bought 1M shares in March 2026. What is NOT yet delivered is the operational half: production growth is entirely ahead, and the financing rescue left the assets carrying heavy encumbrances (royalty, gold delivery obligations from January 2028, converts) that a stumble would make punishing.

Glossary - every term, in plain words (tap to open)

Estimated value - What our model calculates one share is worth from documented evidence at a stated metal price and date. An estimate, not a prediction of where the stock will trade.

Cautious value (safety floor) - The deliberately careful of the two published values: stress-grade assumptions throughout. If the price is below even this number, the discount needs no generosity to see.

Fair value (market-based) - The second published value: what the company is worth using the yardstick the market actually applies to companies of this type across the Roster, with growth on its documented calendar. The verdict keys to this value.

Discount / premium at today's price - The gap between an estimated value and what a share costs today. Green (discount) = the share costs less than the value. Red (premium) = the price already exceeds the value.

Share price - What the market currently charges for one share, always shown with the date of the quote.

Trading below / near / above estimated value - The relationship between price and FAIR value. Below = the market charges less than the estimate (a discount). Above = the price already assumes future events (a pre-payment). Near = within a few percent.

The five-case deck - Value computed at five fixed cases of the company's own commodity price - Stress, Conservative Base, the dated Spot, Long-Term Normalized, Upside. We never forecast the metal; you bring your own view.

Value milestones - A calendar of dated events. Value steps only when an event lands and its inputs are released; the share price line is never forecast. Each step is a checkable claim.

Catalyst - A dated, verifiable event - a study, a permit, a financing - that releases new model inputs.

Pre-payment - When today's price already contains tomorrow's documents. Not automatically bad - but you should know you are doing it.

Quality tier / recalibrated rank - Company quality alone, from a 7-factor panel, placed on a 1-10 ladder where the Roster median is 5.0. It deliberately ignores price.

Symposium Top - The highest quality tier on the Roster ladder - the best-evidenced enterprises among an already elite set.

The Roster - The fixed set of companies covered - the presenting companies of a leading annual natural-resource investing symposium, itself a pre-selected elite of the roughly 2,000-3,000 mining companies worldwide, so every tier is standing among the select.

Release gate - A report is published only when every one of the 52 questions reaches a terminal answer - evidenced, documented as absent, or stage-exempt. No gaps hidden.

SOFT - A figure we could not confirm from a primary source, labeled honestly wherever it is used.

PEA / PFS / FS - The study ladder: Preliminary Economic Assessment (first economics), Pre-Feasibility (engineered), Feasibility (bankable). Each rung earns more credit in the model.

P/NAV (developers) - Price compared to a project's study value. Builders trade below 1.0 before production and re-rate through it as the mine becomes real.

Risk weight - The fraction of a project's study value the model credits today, by stage - small for early studies, larger once permitted and engineered.

AISC - All-in sustaining cost: what it costs to produce one ounce, all-in. The margin is the metal price minus this.

NSR royalty - A share of a mine's revenue off the top. Royalty companies own these instead of operating mines.

Streaming - Buying a mine's future silver or gold at a fixed low price in exchange for money upfront.

Earn-in - A contract where a partner pays for exploration to earn a share of a project - the generator model's engine.

Unanswered question - The one company-specific uncertainty the whole thesis hinges on, named explicitly in every report.

Royalty - A fixed percentage of a mine's revenue that goes to an outside holder rather than to the company, paid off the top - before costs, before debt, before shareholders see anything. It was sold once, usually years earlier, to raise cash. It runs for the life of the mine unless the company buys it back, which is possible only where the original agreement allows it at a set price or where the holder agrees to sell. Because it is charged on revenue and not on profit, it is still owed in a year when the mine loses money.

Stream - Not a percentage of revenue but a claim on the metal itself. An outside party paid cash up front, often to help build the mine, in exchange for the right to receive a set share of the metal produced and to pay only a small fixed fraction of the market price for it - sometimes as little as a tenth or a fifth. The gap between that fixed price and the real price is the cost to the company, and it widens as metal prices rise. Like a royalty, a stream runs for the life of the mine unless bought back, which is possible only under the original terms or by agreement with the holder.

The Story

One paragraph in plain words: what the company is, what it owns, and the central finding. If you read nothing else, read this.

INVESTMENT COMMITTEE SUMMARY (July 31, 2026). Ivanhoe Electric is a pre-revenue United States copper developer whose entire underwriting rests on one asset: the Santa Cruz Copper Project near Casa Grande, Arizona. The June 2025 Preliminary Feasibility Study defines a 20,000 tonne-per-day underground mine feeding a 100% heap-leach circuit that produces finished 99.99% LME Grade A cathode on site. Recommendation is driven by an unusual combination: a first-quartile cost asset on wholly private land in the United States, struck in a study whose base copper price sits roughly one third below the metal's actual July 31, 2026 level, set against a permanent project financing that was targeted for the first half of 2026 and had still not closed at the evidence cutoff. The equity is cheap against the study and expensive against the execution risk; the deciding variable is the financing, not the geology.

Where narrative text carries an older share price, the tables and the refreshed dated close above govern.

Three dates govern this page: the share price is the dated close shown above (2026-07-31); the evidence and estimated values are from this company's last full underwriting (2026-07-31), and change only when the company publishes something - each document's own date is listed under References; a daily event scan watches this company's filings and releases and queues a re-underwriting when one lands.

The Question the Thesis Hinges On

Single greatest company-specific uncertainty identified as macro/policy exposure layered onto construction execution risk: Santa Cruz's economics are directly sensitive to US copper tariff policy, with President Trump reported to be weighing a decision on refined copper tariffs, while the company simultaneously executes a real, capital-intensive construction ramp (tunnel-boring equipment acquisition, metric 16) - a real, live policy variable outside the company's control layered on top of ordinary construction risk.

The Full Underwriting Register - all 52 questions (tap to open)

The same 52 questions are asked of every company. Statuses: Complete = evidenced and scored; Not Available - Documented = the fact does not exist publicly and we say so; Stage-exempt = not applicable to this company type or stage. Figures not confirmed from a primary source are labeled SOFT.

3. Investment Committee decision summary [Complete · score 3 (of 10; 1 = best)]
INVESTMENT COMMITTEE SUMMARY (July 31, 2026). Ivanhoe Electric is a pre-revenue United States copper developer whose entire underwriting rests on one asset: the Santa Cruz Copper Project near Casa Grande, Arizona. The June 2025 Preliminary Feasibility Study defines a 20,000 tonne-per-day underground mine feeding a 100% heap-leach circuit that produces finished 99.99% LME Grade A cathode on site. Recommendation is driven by an unusual combination: a first-quartile cost asset on wholly private land in the United States, struck in a study whose base copper price sits roughly one third below the metal's actual July 31, 2026 level, set against a permanent project financing that was targeted for the first half of 2026 and had still not closed at the evidence cutoff. The equity is cheap against the study and expensive against the execution risk; the deciding variable is the financing, not the geology.

12. Principal uncertainty [Complete · score 1 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Single greatest company-specific uncertainty identified as macro/policy exposure layered onto construction execution risk: Santa Cruz's economics are directly sensitive to US copper tariff policy, with President Trump reported to be weighing a decision on refined copper tariffs, while the company simultaneously executes a real, capital-intensive construction ramp (tunnel-boring equipment acquisition, metric 16) - a real, live policy variable outside the company's control layered on top of ordinary construction risk.

16. Development-project underwriting [Complete · score 3 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Real, large, and currently-advancing development progress at Santa Cruz (Arizona): a June 2025 Preliminary Feasibility Study outlined strong economics, though the two sources reviewed showed some real inconsistency in reported mine life (15 years in one summary versus 23 years and 1.4 million tonnes of cathode over the project life per the company's own 10-K, with an after-tax NPV of $1.4 billion) - both figures logged rather than one silently chosen, since they may reflect different production phases or reporting bases; average annual production is targeted around 72,000 tonnes copper. Real, tangible construction-readiness evidence includes securing more than 3,000 acres of private land, clearing final payments for initial mine construction activities (November 2025, subject to permits), and acquiring a Robbins tunnel boring machine and material handling system specifically for mine access development (May 2026) - genuine physical procurement, not just planning documents.

17. Balance-sheet resilience [Complete · score 3 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Real, large, and diversified financing already secured: a $150 million equity raise (October 2025, at $15/share) and a $200 million bank credit facility (closed December 2025) provide real, dated liquidity; separately, the US Export-Import Bank has indicated potential support of up to $825 million - a real, government-backed financing signal distinct from anything else found in this project. The company also received a real $58.4 million cash distribution from its Cordoba Minerals Corp. holding (March 2026), a genuine non-core-asset monetization event. Months of cash runway and funding gap to the next milestone were not separately quantified as a distinct calculation this pass, per the sharpened requirement for this metric.

19. Run-rate normalization [Complete · score 2 (of 10; 1 = best)]
A real, distinctive feature not seen at any other company in this project: Ivanhoe Electric reports actual trailing-twelve-month revenue (approximately $2.9 million as of an August 2025 data point), attributable to its non-mining Data Processing and Energy Storage business segments rather than metal sales - genuine, if modest, revenue diversification well ahead of any mining production.

20. Formal scenario architecture [Complete · score 3 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Five named pricing cases are built on the SCENARIOS sheet rather than a generic bear/base/bull. Because Santa Cruz is a copper asset and the project's comparability deck is denominated in gold, each deck case is translated into a copper price by the ratio of that case to the deck's own spot level, so a reader comparing this company against a gold producer is reading the same column definition in both books. The value in each case is driven off the study's own disclosed price sensitivity rather than a rebuilt cash-flow model. REVISION (Aug 2, 2026): the gold-deck-to-copper translation convention described above is RETIRED - the deck is now stated natively in copper US$/lb at the shared deck ratios.

21. Valuation-to-action bridge [Complete · score 3 (of 10; 1 = best)]
The bridge from value to action is explicit on the SCENARIOS and CATALYST_TIMELINE sheets and is stated in both dollars and percent in every case. At the conservative base the modelled value sits essentially level with the traded price; at the dated spot copper price it sits materially above it; at the stress case it sits far below. The action therefore turns on whether the buyer is underwriting the metal at its current level or at a conservative long-run level, and the recommendation is written to say so rather than to average the two. REVISION (Aug 2, 2026, commodity-deck restatement): the five pricing cases in this workbook previously displayed gold-price levels as a project-wide scaling convention, which was mislabelled for this company - its commodity has no economic link to gold. The cases are now restated in the company's own commodity, Copper, US$/lb, anchored to COMEX copper US$6.49/lb at the July 31, 2026 close, at the same structural ratios as the shared deck (stress 0.64x, conservative base 0.84x, current 1.00x, long-term 1.04x, upside 1.33x of the dated current price). Per-share value outputs are unchanged; cross-company comparability survives because every company's five cases occupy identical positions relative to its own dated current price.

The clearest thesis-break condition is an adverse US copper tariff decision materially altering Santa Cruz's projected economics (metric 12), or a major construction delay/cost overrun given the project is now in physical construction-equipment procurement, not just planning.

26. Peer-group methodology [Complete · score 2 (of 10; 1 = best)]
The company is explicitly grouped alongside other copper-focused North American producers and developers (Ero Copper, Hudbay Minerals, Freeport-McMoRan, Arizona Sonoran Copper, First Quantum Minerals) by financial data providers - a real, sector-relevant peer set.

27. Jurisdiction, fiscal regime, and permitting [Complete · score 3 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Real, exceptionally high-profile, and directly government-linked jurisdictional context: Executive Chairman Robert Friedland joined US President Donald Trump at the White House for a critical-minerals stockpile announcement (February 3, 2026) - among the highest-profile, most directly verifiable instances of government engagement found at any company in this project. Santa Cruz itself sits on private land in Arizona, USA, simplifying surface-access risk; the company also holds a real, large-scale international joint venture with Ma'aden (Saudi Arabia's state mining company) covering approximately 50,000 km2 of exploration licenses, and a separate Typhoon-driven exploration collaboration with SQM in Chile (January 2026) - a genuinely global jurisdictional footprint for an otherwise US-focused developer.

28. Environmental liability, reclamation, closure, and tailings [Complete · score 3 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Santa Cruz's environmental profile is structurally lighter than a conventional copper mine of comparable scale, and for reasons that are disclosed rather than assumed. The processing route is 100% heap leach producing finished cathode on site, which removes the smelting step and its associated air-emissions and sulphur-handling liabilities entirely. The site development plan approval was received in March 2026; the Phase II Aquifer Protection Permit, which is the governing groundwater instrument for the leach operation, is expected by mid-2027 and remains outstanding at the evidence cutoff. Closure and reclamation obligations are borne on land the company owns outright rather than on federal ground with a separate bonding regime.

29. Reserve/resource quality [Complete · score 3 (of 10; 1 = best)]
The reserve base is real, dated and reconciled. The June 2025 Preliminary Feasibility Study supports Probable Mineral Reserves underpinning 1.4 million tonnes of contained copper cathode over a 23-year mine life at an average grade of approximately 1.08% copper. The apparent mine-life inconsistency carried in earlier drafts of this file is RESOLVED and was an artefact of reading two different disclosures as one: 23 years is the mine life, while the recurring '15 year' figure is the reference window the company uses for capital intensity and for its position on the industry cash-cost curve, not a shorter mine life. Indicated Resources exclusive of Reserves at Santa Cruz and East Ridge contain a further 1.5 million tonnes of copper, of which the heap-leachable portion is disclosed separately, and sit outside the current mine plan as near-mine expansion.

30. Exploration effectiveness [Complete · score 2 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Real, current, and multi-project exploration activity using the company's proprietary Typhoon geophysical technology: continuity of high-grade copper mineralization confirmed within the Verde Domain at Santa Cruz, widespread porphyry-style sulfide mineralization intersected at the Sunbeam area of Tintic, and step-out drilling extending mineralization at Hog Heaven (Montana) by 150+ metres - genuine, current, multi-site exploration progress, further supported by a real, named machine-learning partnership with CGI to improve Typhoon data-processing speed and quality.

31. Ownership, royalties, streams, and joint ventures [Complete · score 2 (of 10; 1 = best)]
A real, specific, and unusually complex ownership and partnership structure: 100% ownership of Santa Cruz and Tintic; a 50/50 exploration joint venture with Ma'aden in Saudi Arabia (Maaden Ivanhoe Electric Exploration and Development Limited Company, metric 27); and an equity stake in the separately-listed Cordoba Minerals Corp., itself embroiled in a real, complex sale of its remaining 50% interest in the Alacrán Copper Project to a consortium including JCHX Mining (up to $128 million, amended February 2026 to remove post-closing contingent payments) - genuinely one of the more layered corporate structures found in this project.

32. Commodity-price, FX, and inflation assumption governance [Complete · score 2 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Price-assumption governance is a genuine strength here and is testable against the market. The study was struck at a base case of US$4.25 per pound of copper and published alongside a life-of-mine copper price sensitivity table rather than a single point estimate, with a second headline case run at the then-prevailing COMEX price of approximately US$4.83 per pound as of June 20, 2025. COMEX copper settled at approximately US$6.49 per pound on July 31, 2026, so the governing study is anchored roughly one third below the metal's actual level at the valuation date. That is conservative assumption-setting, and it is the single most favourable structural feature of the file.

33. Tax, royalties, and fiscal losses [Complete · score 3 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Fiscal treatment is embedded in the disclosed economics rather than left open: the study's headline net present value figures are stated on an after-tax basis, so a corporate tax burden is modelled rather than ignored. The asset carries no third-party production royalty, because the company acquired 100% of both the mineral and the surface rights outright, completing the final option payment in August 2024 through its wholly-owned subsidiary Mesa Cobre and clearing the remaining land obligations with accelerated payments of US$39.3 million in November 2025. Federal incentive programs have been referenced as potential additional support but none is contracted.

36. Safety, workforce, and labor [Complete · score 4 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Workforce evidence is disclosed at the level appropriate to a pre-construction developer and no further. The company employs approximately 286 people and projects roughly 1,000 workers during the construction phase of Santa Cruz. The most substantive safety-relevant decision on record is the choice of mechanised tunnelling: management justified acquiring a refurbished Robbins Crossover tunnel boring machine explicitly on the grounds of safer and more reliable decline development through variable ground, delivering a permanent steel-reinforced sealed concrete tunnel in place of conventional roadheader advance. No injury-frequency statistics exist to review because no mine is operating, which is the honest ceiling on this score rather than a research gap.

37. Community relations and social licence [Complete · score 2 (of 10; 1 = best)]
The social-licence position is structurally unusual and is the reason the permitting path is short. The Santa Cruz resource lies entirely beneath approximately 6,000 acres of privately owned land that the company purchased outright, which removes the federal land-use process that has stalled comparable United States copper projects for a decade or more. Federal-level alignment is documented rather than inferred: the Executive Chairman appeared alongside the United States President at a White House minerals stockpile announcement on January 27, 2026. No organised local opposition to the project was identified in any source reviewed for this pass.

38. Disclosure quality, reporting integrity, and governance [Complete · score 3 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Governance process is documented and routine, with one real blemish. A proxy statement was filed on April 21, 2026 and shareholders approved director elections, executive compensation and auditor ratification on May 21, 2026. The company designates its investor-relations website as its Regulation FD distribution channel and reports on a quarterly cadence with accompanying slide decks. The blemish is a live disclosure inconsistency: the June 2025 study release and its syndicated copies continue to state first copper cathode in 2028, while the company's own current project webpage states the second quarter of 2029. Both are company disclosures, both remain public, and they cannot both be right.

Real, specific, and construction-relevant infrastructure procurement: acquisition of a Robbins tunnel boring machine and material handling system specifically for Santa Cruz mine access development (metric 16) - genuine, tangible, capital-equipment evidence of construction readiness, not merely planning language.
