41. Hedging, derivatives, and counterparty risk [Complete · score 3 (of 10; 1 = best)]
The company holds no metal hedges because it has no metal production, so the exposure that matters is financial rather than commodity. The material counterparty and rate exposure is the US$200 million senior secured multi-draw bridge facility closed in December 2025 at the Mesa Cobre subsidiary level, arranged by National Bank Capital Markets, Societe Generale and BMO Capital Markets, priced at three-month SOFR plus a 5.0% margin that steps up by a further 0.5% on each of the sixth, twelfth and eighteenth months after closing. That escalator is an unhedged floating-rate liability with a built-in cost ratchet, and it is designed to be refinanced rather than carried.

42. Working capital, cash conversion, and liquidity quality [Complete · score 4 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Liquidity was rebuilt substantially and then began to be consumed. The company added over US$360 million of liquidity in the fourth quarter of 2025 through a US$172.5 million equity offering priced at US$15.00 per share and the US$200 million bridge facility, and received a further US$58.4 million cash distribution from subsidiary Cordoba Minerals announced February 3, 2026 following the sale of the Alacran project. Against that, spending has accelerated into detailed engineering, the tunnel boring machine and site works, and third-party analysis published in July 2026 characterised the company as carrying less than a year of cash runway at then-current burn. An automatic mixed securities shelf was filed on April 15, 2026, which keeps further issuance available.

44. Debt structure, covenants, and refinancing [Complete · score 4 (of 10; 1 = best)]
REVISED THIS PASS. A US$200 million senior secured multi-draw bridge facility was closed in December 2025 at the wholly-owned Mesa Cobre subsidiary, arranged by National Bank Capital Markets, Societe Generale and BMO Capital Markets after extensive technical due diligence. The earlier score in this file rewarded the existence of the facility; the disclosed terms are less favourable than that implied. Pricing is three-month SOFR plus 5.0%, ratcheting a further 0.5% at each of the sixth, twelfth and eighteenth months from closing, which is bridge pricing with a deliberate escalator intended to force refinancing. The permanent package, including the non-binding Export-Import Bank Letter of Interest for up to US$825 million of 15-year project debt received April 15, 2025 and a contemplated project-level minority equity investment, was targeted to complete in the first half of 2026 and had not closed at the July 31, 2026 evidence cutoff.

45. Litigation, regulatory, and contingent liabilities [Complete · score 3 (of 10; 1 = best)]
No material litigation was identified in any source reviewed. The live regulatory contingency is trade policy rather than a claim: the United States Department of Commerce delivered its Section 232 follow-up report on refined copper on June 30, 2026, recommending a staged duty of 15% from January 2027 and 30% from January 2028, with no announced decision timeframe. For a domestic producer of finished cathode the exposure runs the favourable way, since a refined-copper tariff raises the domestic price this company would sell into. The outstanding Phase II Aquifer Protection Permit is the remaining regulatory condition on the operating plan.

48. Revenue realization, offtake, and payable metal [Complete · score 2 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Revenue realisation at Santa Cruz is structurally superior to a concentrate producer and this is the least-appreciated feature of the asset. The heap-leach and solvent-extraction route delivers 99.99% pure LME Grade A copper cathode at the mine site, so there is no concentrate to ship, no smelter to queue for, no treatment and refining charges to concede, no payable-metal deduction and no cross-border processing step. Approximately 3 billion pounds of finished copper metal are projected over the initial 23-year mine life. No long-term offtake contract is disclosed, which is consistent with selling finished metal into the domestic market rather than pre-committing concentrate.

49. Forecast governance and model governance [Complete · score 3 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Forecast governance is evidenced by behaviour rather than by policy language. The study was led by Fluor as principal engineering lead with named qualified persons, and the company labels its development plan as indicative and explicitly subject to project financing and receipt of permits. More tellingly, when the tunnel boring machine decision changed the mine-access method during 2026 the company re-dated the schedule publicly rather than holding a stale target, disclosing tunnel boring machine arrival and assembly in the first quarter of 2027, decline development from the third quarter of 2027, first ore to the leach pads in mid to late 2028 and first cathode in the second quarter of 2029.

50. Management incentives and conflicts [Complete · score 4 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Alignment carries a real and specific structural tension. Executive Chairman Robert Friedland simultaneously holds a founding and senior role at Ivanhoe Mines, a separate and much larger listed mining company, which is an attention and opportunity-allocation vector that no governance policy removes. Shareholders approved executive compensation and director elections on May 21, 2026 without incident. Insider dealing runs both directions and is dated: earlier open-market purchases by Chief Financial Officer Jordan Neeser are on record, and on March 6, 2026 both Neeser and Senior Vice President of Mine Development Glen Kuntz sold shares, 17,123 and 14,863 respectively, into a declining market.

A real, specific, and disclosed corporate structure: the Ma'aden joint venture operates through a named Saudi Arabian limited liability company (Maaden Ivanhoe Electric Exploration and Development Limited Company, metric 27/31); the company also holds an equity stake in the separately-listed Cordoba Minerals Corp. (metric 31) - genuinely well-documented multi-entity structure.

52. Reserve-price sensitivity, cut-off migration, and economic-envelope robustness [Complete · score 2 (of 10; 1 = best)]
The economic envelope is robust in the direction that matters and the study proves it rather than asserting it. The published life-of-mine sensitivity shows after-tax net present value rising from approximately US$1.4 billion at US$4.25 per pound to approximately US$1.9 billion at approximately US$4.83 per pound, an implied slope of roughly US$0.86 billion of value per additional dollar of copper price. Life-of-mine C1 unit cash costs of US$1.32 per pound sit in the first quartile of the global cost curve, which means the envelope does not close at any copper price a reasonable investor would model. At the July 31, 2026 copper price the asset is being valued outside the upper bound of the range the study actually tested.

53. Technical-report currency, competent-person reliance, and study obsolescence [Complete · score 4 (of 10; 1 = best)]
The governing technical study is current in date but is no longer a complete description of the execution plan, and that gap is the honest ding on this file. The Preliminary Feasibility Study carries a June 2025 effective date and was approximately thirteen months old at the valuation date, prepared under United States regulatory requirements with Fluor as principal lead and named qualified persons. Since publication the mine-access method has been changed to mechanised tunnel boring, the schedule has moved to a second-quarter-2029 first-cathode date, the final land payments have been made and the site development plan has been approved. A reader relying only on the study would materially misdate the project.

54. Geological reconciliation, grade control, metallurgical accounting, and reserve performance [Not Applicable - Operator's Risk]
There is no operating mine, no mill and no processing circuit, so there is nothing to reconcile: no mined-versus-modelled grade comparison, no metallurgical accounting, no reserve performance history. This is a stage fact about a pre-production developer rather than a gap in the research, consistent with the treatment of the other operating metrics in this workbook.

55. Water balance, water security, climate resilience, and extreme weather [Complete · score 2 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Water is both the principal environmental constraint and a disclosed company asset, which is a rare combination. The approximately 6,000-acre private land package at Santa Cruz explicitly includes associated water rights held by the company, which in Arizona is a materially stronger position than a permit-dependent allocation. The study was supported by hydrogeological testwork rather than assumption. The regulatory expression of the water risk is the Phase II Aquifer Protection Permit expected by mid-2027, and the mine-access design contributes directly to water management because the tunnel-bored decline is a permanent sealed steel-reinforced concrete structure rather than an unlined excavation.

56. Tailings-facility integrity, geotechnical stability, and emergency preparedness [Complete · score 1 (of 10; 1 = best)]
This metric resolves to the strongest score available for a structural reason rather than a management one. The processing route is 100% heap leach using a conventional on-off pad, so the project has no conventional wet tailings storage facility at all. The single largest catastrophic-loss category in modern mining, an upstream or centreline tailings dam and its geotechnical stability, is therefore absent from this asset by design rather than mitigated by procedure. No emergency-preparedness programme can match simply not having the structure.

57. Valuation-method hierarchy, asset-level NAV governance, discount-rate discipline, and double-counting prevention [Complete · score 3 (of 10; 1 = best)]
The valuation hierarchy is explicit and anti-double-counting. The primary instrument is the study's own after-tax net present value at an 8% discount rate, which is the only independently prepared economic assessment of the asset; the deck-scaled figures on the SCENARIOS sheet are derived from that study's disclosed price slope rather than from a rebuilt cash-flow model. Every other holding, being the Typhoon geophysical system and Computational Geosciences, the 50/50 Ma'aden joint venture in Saudi Arabia, Tintic in Utah, Hog Heaven and Gleeson, the SQM collaboration in Chile and the energy-storage segment, is carried at zero as a conservative offset. The published analyst mean target of US$21.42 is recorded as context and is deliberately not used as a valuation input. 59. Management track record and role-specific competence [Complete · score 2 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Real, exceptionally high-profile, and independently verifiable leadership: Executive Chairman Robert Friedland is a widely-recognized figure in global mining finance (also founder of the separately-listed Ivanhoe Mines Ltd.), and his direct engagement with the White House on critical-minerals policy (metric 27) is real, dated, and independently reported - among the highest-profile leadership findings in this entire project, though a full itemized track-record evaluation per the consultation document's standard was not performed this pass.

Glossary - every term, in plain words (tap to open)

Estimated value - What our model calculates one share is worth from documented evidence at a stated metal price and date. An estimate, not a prediction of where the stock will trade.

Cautious value (safety floor) - The deliberately careful of the two published values: stress-grade assumptions throughout. If the price is below even this number, the discount needs no generosity to see.

Fair value (market-based) - The second published value: what the company is worth using the yardstick the market actually applies to companies of this type across the Roster, with growth on its documented calendar. The verdict keys to this value.

Discount / premium at today's price - The gap between an estimated value and what a share costs today. Green (discount) = the share costs less than the value. Red (premium) = the price already exceeds the value.

Share price - What the market currently charges for one share, always shown with the date of the quote.

Trading below / near / above estimated value - The relationship between price and FAIR value. Below = the market charges less than the estimate (a discount). Above = the price already assumes future events (a pre-payment). Near = within a few percent.

The five-case deck - Value computed at five fixed cases of the company's own commodity price - Stress, Conservative Base, the dated Spot, Long-Term Normalized, Upside. We never forecast the metal; you bring your own view.

Value milestones - A calendar of dated events. Value steps only when an event lands and its inputs are released; the share price line is never forecast. Each step is a checkable claim.

Catalyst - A dated, verifiable event - a study, a permit, a financing - that releases new model inputs.

Pre-payment - When today's price already contains tomorrow's documents. Not automatically bad - but you should know you are doing it.

Quality tier / recalibrated rank - Company quality alone, from a 7-factor panel, placed on a 1-10 ladder where the Roster median is 5.0. It deliberately ignores price.

Symposium Top - The highest quality tier on the Roster ladder - the best-evidenced enterprises among an already elite set.

The Roster - The fixed set of companies covered - the presenting companies of a leading annual natural-resource investing symposium, itself a pre-selected elite of the roughly 2,000-3,000 mining companies worldwide, so every tier is standing among the select.

Release gate - A report is published only when every one of the 52 questions reaches a terminal answer - evidenced, documented as absent, or stage-exempt. No gaps hidden.

SOFT - A figure we could not confirm from a primary source, labeled honestly wherever it is used.

PEA / PFS / FS - The study ladder: Preliminary Economic Assessment (first economics), Pre-Feasibility (engineered), Feasibility (bankable). Each rung earns more credit in the model.

P/NAV (developers) - Price compared to a project's study value. Builders trade below 1.0 before production and re-rate through it as the mine becomes real.

Risk weight - The fraction of a project's study value the model credits today, by stage - small for early studies, larger once permitted and engineered.

AISC - All-in sustaining cost: what it costs to produce one ounce, all-in. The margin is the metal price minus this.

NSR royalty - A share of a mine's revenue off the top. Royalty companies own these instead of operating mines.

Streaming - Buying a mine's future silver or gold at a fixed low price in exchange for money upfront.

Earn-in - A contract where a partner pays for exploration to earn a share of a project - the generator model's engine.

Unanswered question - The one company-specific uncertainty the whole thesis hinges on, named explicitly in every report.

Royalty - A fixed percentage of a mine's revenue that goes to an outside holder rather than to the company, paid off the top - before costs, before debt, before shareholders see anything. It was sold once, usually years earlier, to raise cash. It runs for the life of the mine unless the company buys it back, which is possible only where the original agreement allows it at a set price or where the holder agrees to sell. Because it is charged on revenue and not on profit, it is still owed in a year when the mine loses money.

Stream - Not a percentage of revenue but a claim on the metal itself. An outside party paid cash up front, often to help build the mine, in exchange for the right to receive a set share of the metal produced and to pay only a small fixed fraction of the market price for it - sometimes as little as a tenth or a fifth. The gap between that fixed price and the real price is the cost to the company, and it widens as metal prices rise. Like a royalty, a stream runs for the life of the mine unless bought back, which is possible only under the original terms or by agreement with the holder.

The Story

One paragraph in plain words: what the company is, what it owns, and the central finding. If you read nothing else, read this.

IC summary: the industry's defining growth platform in its recovery-and-rebuild year - Kamoa-Kakula (39.6%) produced 64,328t of copper in Q2 2026 with full-year guidance of 290,000-330,000t MAINTAINED through the post-seismic recovery, Africa's largest copper smelter is running (112,307t of acid at ~$840/t July pricing), Kipushi (62%) printed its SEVENTH consecutive quarterly zinc record (70,177t at an extraordinary 38.7% feed grade), Platreef's Shaft #3 ramp is COMPLETE (hoisting capacity x5, first Flatreef stopes mined) with Phase 2 on target for Q4 2027, and the Western Forelands district resource update lands mid-July. The honest arithmetic: at conservative multiples the current attributable state supports ~C$2.36 at spot against C$10.59 - the market pre-pays the 2027-2031 growth wave AND a district premium; even the full staircase at 9x stays modestly below today's price. The third marquee expensive-quality verdict - with the counterweight that the DRC discount embedded in the 9x is itself contestable in both directions.

11. Reserve/resource movement bridge [Complete · score 2 (of 10; 1 = best)]
A real, current, quantified reserve/resource growth story at the Western Forelands: a 2,427 km2 exploration license package (54-100% owned, covering an area more than six times the adjacent Kamoa-Kakula complex) continues to expand the Makoko District copper discovery, with an updated Mineral Resource Estimate targeted for mid-2026; the company states a discovery cost below one cent per pound of copper at a 1% cut-off grade - a real, specific, company-stated efficiency claim worth treating as a superlative to verify rather than accept outright, though it is unusually precise for this kind of disclosure.

12. Principal uncertainty [Complete · score 1 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Single greatest company-specific uncertainty identified as recovery execution at Kamoa-Kakula following a real, disclosed 2025 seismic event: management's own language ("turning the corner... following the 2025 seismic event") confirms a real operational disruption occurred at the company's largest asset, and while 2025 copper production of 388,838 tonnes still met guidance, the pace and completeness of recovery remains the central operational question for the company's largest single asset.

13. Management guidance credibility [Complete · score 3 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Real, verified, multi-asset guidance delivery: Kamoa-Kakula produced 388,838 tonnes of copper in 2025, achieving guidance including a record production quarter from the Phase 3 concentrator; Kipushi has set a new zinc production record in four consecutive quarters reviewed (57,200t Q3 2025, 65,044t Q1 2026, 70,177t Q2 2026), with Q1 2026 cash costs tracking at the low end of full-year guidance - a genuinely strong, multi-period, multi-asset delivery record.

14. Mine-by-mine operating quality [Complete · score 3 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Real, current, asset-level detail across all three operations: Kamoa-Kakula's new on-site smelter is producing high-strength sulphuric acid averaging 1,350 tonnes/day at contract prices up more than 50% year-to-date to $725/tonne, a real and distinctive by-product revenue stream boosting margins; Kipushi's Q2 2026 record 70,177 tonnes of zinc came at a cash cost of $0.90/lb as zinc prices reached multi-year highs of $1.60/lb; Platreef's Shaft #3 was completed on schedule, increasing hoisting capacity five-fold and enabling first ore feed into the Phase 1 concentrator with first concentrate following shortly after (Q3 2025) - genuine, current, and specific operating detail at every asset.

15. Cost quality [Complete · score 2 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Real, quantified, and improving cost detail across two producing assets: Kipushi's cash cost (C1) improved from $1.13/lb (Q4 2025) to $0.86/lb (Q1 2026), tracking at the low end of full-year guidance ($0.85-0.95/lb); Kamoa-Kakula's margins are explicitly boosted by the new sulphuric acid by-product stream and lower logistics costs (metric 14) - real, disclosed, and favorable cost trends, not merely asserted.

16. Development-project underwriting [Complete · score 3 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Real, large, and currently-financed growth at Platreef: Phase 2 expansion (targeting a 400%+ increase in production from Phase 1, completion targeted Q4 2027) is being funded by a $700 million senior project finance facility, signed February 18, 2026 and reaching financial close April 30, 2026, amending and upsizing the original Phase 1 facility with approximately $600 million in net additional capital from a bank syndicate (Societe Generale, Absa Bank, and Nedbank) - real, dated, and already-closed project financing, not merely proposed.

17. Balance-sheet resilience [Complete · score 3 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Real, exceptionally large, and recently reinforced balance sheet: cash and short-term deposits of $885 million at December 31, 2025 (declining to $754 million by March 31, 2026 as Phase 2 capital was deployed), further strengthened by a real, notable $500 million strategic private placement from the Qatar Investment Authority (a sovereign wealth fund) - a genuinely large, named, and credible strategic investor not seen at any other company in this project. Months of cash runway and funding gap to the next milestone were not separately quantified this pass, per the sharpened requirement for this metric.

18. Capital allocation [Complete · score 3 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Capital allocation: no dividend has ever been paid - every dollar recycles into the growth pipeline (Platreef Phase 2 currently financed, solar build, Western Forelands drilling); correct for the platform's stage and stated openly.

19. Run-rate normalization [Complete · score 3 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Reported-to-sustainable: Q1 2026 carried the one-time $183M Kamoa Copper tax settlement - real, disclosed, excluded from run-rate; the sustainable engine is the maintained 290-330kt guide plus Kipushi's record cadence; H2 is guided stronger on mining rates and concentrate destocking, both named and measurable.

Shared five-case deck applied through the multi-metal attributable convention (copper, zinc, acid and early PGM scaled as gold-equivalent) - flagged as a comparability device; the base deliberately holds only the current state.

21. Valuation-to-action bridge [Complete · score 2 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Valuation-to-action bridge: current-state value C$2.36 at spot (-77.7%) and the FULL 2029-31 staircase C$5.81 (-45.1%) both sit below the C$10.59 price at this model's conservative 9x - the market pays a growth-and-district premium (Western Forelands as "the next Kamoa", the Friedland exploration franchise) beyond cautious arithmetic. 26. Peer-group methodology [Complete · score 3 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Peers: the copper growth class (Teck, First Quantum, Zijin - its own partner); on current attributable output IVN trades at a large premium to producing peers, and on 2030 output at a discount to what the platform would deserve in a tier-one jurisdiction - the DRC wedge in one sentence.

All three Tier-One assets sit in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (Kamoa-Kakula, Kipushi) and South Africa (Platreef), with further exploration exposure in Angola, Zambia, and a joint venture in Kazakhstan ($20 million and $20 million respectively of the $127 million 2026 group exploration budget, alongside $86 million for the DRC Western Forelands) - real, quantified geographic risk spread, though the DRC in particular carries real, well-known political and operational risk that was not independently assessed beyond the disclosed seismic event (metric 12).

The company's own characterization of Kamoa-Kakula as "the highest-grade major copper complex" globally is a real, specific claim; an updated independent technical report for Kamoa-Kakula was referenced as forthcoming in the Q1 2026 release - real, current, ongoing technical-basis maintenance for the flagship asset.

Real, current, and geographically broad exploration activity beyond the flagship Makoko District (metric 11): drilling during the period reviewed also tested new target areas including Tshipaya and Kamilli within the Western Forelands, alongside the separately-funded Kazakhstan JV and Angola/Zambia/South Africa programs (metric 27) - a genuinely large, multi-target, and well-funded exploration effort for a company already at production scale.

A real, specific, and disclosed mixed-ownership structure: the Western Forelands license package is held 54-100% by the company depending on the specific license (metric 11); Kamoa-Kakula operates through the Kamoa Holding joint venture structure, with all Kamoa-Kakula revenue recognized within that JV rather than directly on Ivanhoe's own books - a real, material structural detail for interpreting the company's consolidated financials.

Real, specific, and asset-attributed production guidance: Kamoa-Kakula and Kipushi both issued 2026 and 2027 guidance (December 3, 2025 and January 15, 2026 respectively); Platreef's Phase 2 expansion targets a 400%+ production increase from Q4 2027 (metric 16) - genuine, multi-year, asset-specific forward planning.

Real, strong, and repeatedly-verified operating reliability at two of three assets even while the third (Kamoa-Kakula) worked through a real disruption (metric 12): Kipushi has set new zinc production records in every quarter reviewed across this pass, and Platreef's Shaft #3 construction was completed on schedule - genuine evidence that operational execution has remained strong at the non-disrupted assets throughout the period.

Glossary - every term, in plain words (tap to open)

Estimated value - What our model calculates one share is worth from documented evidence at a stated metal price and date. An estimate, not a prediction of where the stock will trade.

Cautious value (safety floor) - The deliberately careful of the two published values: stress-grade assumptions throughout. If the price is below even this number, the discount needs no generosity to see.

Fair value (market-based) - The second published value: what the company is worth using the yardstick the market actually applies to companies of this type across the Roster, with growth on its documented calendar. The verdict keys to this value.

Discount / premium at today's price - The gap between an estimated value and what a share costs today. Green (discount) = the share costs less than the value. Red (premium) = the price already exceeds the value.

Share price - What the market currently charges for one share, always shown with the date of the quote.

Trading below / near / above estimated value - The relationship between price and FAIR value. Below = the market charges less than the estimate (a discount). Above = the price already assumes future events (a pre-payment). Near = within a few percent.

The five-case deck - Value computed at five fixed cases of the company's own commodity price - Stress, Conservative Base, the dated Spot, Long-Term Normalized, Upside. We never forecast the metal; you bring your own view.

Value milestones - A calendar of dated events. Value steps only when an event lands and its inputs are released; the share price line is never forecast. Each step is a checkable claim.

Catalyst - A dated, verifiable event - a study, a permit, a financing - that releases new model inputs.

Pre-payment - When today's price already contains tomorrow's documents. Not automatically bad - but you should know you are doing it.

Quality tier / recalibrated rank - Company quality alone, from a 7-factor panel, placed on a 1-10 ladder where the Roster median is 5.0. It deliberately ignores price.

Symposium Top - The highest quality tier on the Roster ladder - the best-evidenced enterprises among an already elite set.

The Roster - The fixed set of companies covered - the presenting companies of a leading annual natural-resource investing symposium, itself a pre-selected elite of the roughly 2,000-3,000 mining companies worldwide, so every tier is standing among the select.

Release gate - A report is published only when every one of the 52 questions reaches a terminal answer - evidenced, documented as absent, or stage-exempt. No gaps hidden.

SOFT - A figure we could not confirm from a primary source, labeled honestly wherever it is used.

PEA / PFS / FS - The study ladder: Preliminary Economic Assessment (first economics), Pre-Feasibility (engineered), Feasibility (bankable). Each rung earns more credit in the model.

P/NAV (developers) - Price compared to a project's study value. Builders trade below 1.0 before production and re-rate through it as the mine becomes real.

Risk weight - The fraction of a project's study value the model credits today, by stage - small for early studies, larger once permitted and engineered.

AISC - All-in sustaining cost: what it costs to produce one ounce, all-in. The margin is the metal price minus this.

NSR royalty - A share of a mine's revenue off the top. Royalty companies own these instead of operating mines.

Streaming - Buying a mine's future silver or gold at a fixed low price in exchange for money upfront.

Earn-in - A contract where a partner pays for exploration to earn a share of a project - the generator model's engine.

Unanswered question - The one company-specific uncertainty the whole thesis hinges on, named explicitly in every report.

Royalty - A fixed percentage of a mine's revenue that goes to an outside holder rather than to the company, paid off the top - before costs, before debt, before shareholders see anything. It was sold once, usually years earlier, to raise cash. It runs for the life of the mine unless the company buys it back, which is possible only where the original agreement allows it at a set price or where the holder agrees to sell. Because it is charged on revenue and not on profit, it is still owed in a year when the mine loses money.

Stream - Not a percentage of revenue but a claim on the metal itself. An outside party paid cash up front, often to help build the mine, in exchange for the right to receive a set share of the metal produced and to pay only a small fixed fraction of the market price for it - sometimes as little as a tenth or a fifth. The gap between that fixed price and the real price is the cost to the company, and it widens as metal prices rise. Like a royalty, a stream runs for the life of the mine unless bought back, which is possible only under the original terms or by agreement with the holder.

The Story

One paragraph in plain words: what the company is, what it owns, and the central finding. If you read nothing else, read this.

INVESTMENT COMMITTEE SUMMARY (July 31, 2026). Kincora is the campaign's fifth and final generator, caught mid-pivot and executing it cleanly: the Mongolian era is ending in a US$10 million staged divestment to Tumen Ail Coal (US$1.5 million option payment received May 19, definitive agreements EXECUTED July 2 triggering US$3.5 million within five business days, US$5 million to escrow for release on registration - all free and clear of taxes and fees), leaving a solely-Australian hybrid generator across NSW's Lachlan Fold Belt and the Condobolin field in the Cobar basin. The platform is already spinning: over $100 million of potential partner funding unlocked, 20,000-plus metres and A$10 million-plus of partner-funded drilling since late 2024 with management fees ramping, TWO programs drilling now (Nevertire South and Condobolin), a Lake Cowal-adjacent project expanded 40% on ex-Gold Fields ground, and quantum-gravity (Atomionics) and AI-targeting partnerships layered on. The company's own July page gives filing-grade numbers: 47.6 million shares, roughly $40 million capitalization, $13 million-plus cash before the pending tranches, and ~55% of the register insider-held or escrowed. At C$0.92 the file is NEAR-FAIR: treasury approaching sixty percent of the capitalization with the partner-funded portfolio nearly free - the TECT shape wearing a generator's clothes.

Glossary - every term, in plain words (tap to open)

Estimated value - What our model calculates one share is worth from documented evidence at a stated metal price and date. An estimate, not a prediction of where the stock will trade.

Cautious value (safety floor) - The deliberately careful of the two published values: stress-grade assumptions throughout. If the price is below even this number, the discount needs no generosity to see.

Fair value (market-based) - The second published value: what the company is worth using the yardstick the market actually applies to companies of this type across the Roster, with growth on its documented calendar. The verdict keys to this value.

Discount / premium at today's price - The gap between an estimated value and what a share costs today. Green (discount) = the share costs less than the value. Red (premium) = the price already exceeds the value.

Share price - What the market currently charges for one share, always shown with the date of the quote.

Trading below / near / above estimated value - The relationship between price and FAIR value. Below = the market charges less than the estimate (a discount). Above = the price already assumes future events (a pre-payment). Near = within a few percent.

The five-case deck - Value computed at five fixed cases of the company's own commodity price - Stress, Conservative Base, the dated Spot, Long-Term Normalized, Upside. We never forecast the metal; you bring your own view.

Value milestones - A calendar of dated events. Value steps only when an event lands and its inputs are released; the share price line is never forecast. Each step is a checkable claim.

Catalyst - A dated, verifiable event - a study, a permit, a financing - that releases new model inputs.

Pre-payment - When today's price already contains tomorrow's documents. Not automatically bad - but you should know you are doing it.

Quality tier / recalibrated rank - Company quality alone, from a 7-factor panel, placed on a 1-10 ladder where the Roster median is 5.0. It deliberately ignores price.

Symposium Top - The highest quality tier on the Roster ladder - the best-evidenced enterprises among an already elite set.

The Roster - The fixed set of companies covered - the presenting companies of a leading annual natural-resource investing symposium, itself a pre-selected elite of the roughly 2,000-3,000 mining companies worldwide, so every tier is standing among the select.

Release gate - A report is published only when every one of the 52 questions reaches a terminal answer - evidenced, documented as absent, or stage-exempt. No gaps hidden.

SOFT - A figure we could not confirm from a primary source, labeled honestly wherever it is used.

PEA / PFS / FS - The study ladder: Preliminary Economic Assessment (first economics), Pre-Feasibility (engineered), Feasibility (bankable). Each rung earns more credit in the model.

P/NAV (developers) - Price compared to a project's study value. Builders trade below 1.0 before production and re-rate through it as the mine becomes real.

Risk weight - The fraction of a project's study value the model credits today, by stage - small for early studies, larger once permitted and engineered.

AISC - All-in sustaining cost: what it costs to produce one ounce, all-in. The margin is the metal price minus this.

NSR royalty - A share of a mine's revenue off the top. Royalty companies own these instead of operating mines.

Streaming - Buying a mine's future silver or gold at a fixed low price in exchange for money upfront.

Earn-in - A contract where a partner pays for exploration to earn a share of a project - the generator model's engine.

Unanswered question - The one company-specific uncertainty the whole thesis hinges on, named explicitly in every report.

Royalty - A fixed percentage of a mine's revenue that goes to an outside holder rather than to the company, paid off the top - before costs, before debt, before shareholders see anything. It was sold once, usually years earlier, to raise cash. It runs for the life of the mine unless the company buys it back, which is possible only where the original agreement allows it at a set price or where the holder agrees to sell. Because it is charged on revenue and not on profit, it is still owed in a year when the mine loses money.

Stream - Not a percentage of revenue but a claim on the metal itself. An outside party paid cash up front, often to help build the mine, in exchange for the right to receive a set share of the metal produced and to pay only a small fixed fraction of the market price for it - sometimes as little as a tenth or a fifth. The gap between that fixed price and the real price is the cost to the company, and it widens as metal prices rise. Like a royalty, a stream runs for the life of the mine unless bought back, which is possible only under the original terms or by agreement with the holder.

The Story

One paragraph in plain words: what the company is, what it owns, and the central finding. If you read nothing else, read this.

IC summary: the purest project-generator success story in the universe - Kenorland staked Frotet greenfields in 2017, made the Regnault discovery with Sumitomo in 2020 through systematic surveys, and in February 2024 exchanged its 20% JV interest for a 4% NSR on the ENTIRE project; the maiden resource (December 2025) delivered 2.55 Moz Inferred at a remarkable 5.47 g/t, open in multiple directions with 19 high-grade shells still excluded, while Sumitomo funds everything and advances decline permitting. Sumitomo (10.1%) and Centerra (9.9%) sit on the register and repeatedly exercise top-up rights. At C$2.17 the model shows value above price in every deck case but stress - a costless royalty on a growing high-grade system, plus a working generator machine, priced as an ordinary junior.

Where narrative text carries an older share price, the tables and the refreshed dated close above govern.

Three dates govern this page: the share price is the dated close shown above (2026-07-22); the evidence and estimated values are from this company's last full underwriting (2026-07-31), and change only when the company publishes something - each document's own date is listed under References; a daily event scan watches this company's filings and releases and queues a re-underwriting when one lands.

Single greatest company-specific uncertainty identified as a real, disclosed divergence between growing revenue and worsening losses: FY2025 revenue grew 65% to CA$3.95 million, yet the net loss widened 174% to CA$10.1 million (loss per share deteriorating from CA$0.052 to CA$0.13) - a real, honest tension worth investigating directly rather than assuming the revenue growth alone tells the story.

Real, exceptionally high-grade, current, and specifically-dated exploration results at Regnault: 12.15 metres at 26.33 g/t gold, 7.80 metres at 13.98 g/t gold, and 4.50 metres at 18.06 g/t gold, from a 22,913-metre 2025 winter infill and step-out program that extended mineralization at depth along multiple named structural trends (R1, R5, R6, R9) - among the highest-grade intercepts found anywhere in this entire project. Glossary - every term, in plain words (tap to open)

Estimated value - What our model calculates one share is worth from documented evidence at a stated metal price and date. An estimate, not a prediction of where the stock will trade.

Cautious value (safety floor) - The deliberately careful of the two published values: stress-grade assumptions throughout. If the price is below even this number, the discount needs no generosity to see.

Fair value (market-based) - The second published value: what the company is worth using the yardstick the market actually applies to companies of this type across the Roster, with growth on its documented calendar. The verdict keys to this value.

Discount / premium at today's price - The gap between an estimated value and what a share costs today. Green (discount) = the share costs less than the value. Red (premium) = the price already exceeds the value.

Share price - What the market currently charges for one share, always shown with the date of the quote.

Trading below / near / above estimated value - The relationship between price and FAIR value. Below = the market charges less than the estimate (a discount). Above = the price already assumes future events (a pre-payment). Near = within a few percent.

The five-case deck - Value computed at five fixed cases of the company's own commodity price - Stress, Conservative Base, the dated Spot, Long-Term Normalized, Upside. We never forecast the metal; you bring your own view.

Value milestones - A calendar of dated events. Value steps only when an event lands and its inputs are released; the share price line is never forecast. Each step is a checkable claim.

Catalyst - A dated, verifiable event - a study, a permit, a financing - that releases new model inputs.

Pre-payment - When today's price already contains tomorrow's documents. Not automatically bad - but you should know you are doing it.

Quality tier / recalibrated rank - Company quality alone, from a 7-factor panel, placed on a 1-10 ladder where the Roster median is 5.0. It deliberately ignores price.

Symposium Top - The highest quality tier on the Roster ladder - the best-evidenced enterprises among an already elite set.

The Roster - The fixed set of companies covered - the presenting companies of a leading annual natural-resource investing symposium, itself a pre-selected elite of the roughly 2,000-3,000 mining companies worldwide, so every tier is standing among the select.

Release gate - A report is published only when every one of the 52 questions reaches a terminal answer - evidenced, documented as absent, or stage-exempt. No gaps hidden.

SOFT - A figure we could not confirm from a primary source, labeled honestly wherever it is used.

PEA / PFS / FS - The study ladder: Preliminary Economic Assessment (first economics), Pre-Feasibility (engineered), Feasibility (bankable). Each rung earns more credit in the model.

P/NAV (developers) - Price compared to a project's study value. Builders trade below 1.0 before production and re-rate through it as the mine becomes real.

Risk weight - The fraction of a project's study value the model credits today, by stage - small for early studies, larger once permitted and engineered.

AISC - All-in sustaining cost: what it costs to produce one ounce, all-in. The margin is the metal price minus this.

NSR royalty - A share of a mine's revenue off the top. Royalty companies own these instead of operating mines.

Streaming - Buying a mine's future silver or gold at a fixed low price in exchange for money upfront.

Earn-in - A contract where a partner pays for exploration to earn a share of a project - the generator model's engine.

Unanswered question - The one company-specific uncertainty the whole thesis hinges on, named explicitly in every report.

Royalty - A fixed percentage of a mine's revenue that goes to an outside holder rather than to the company, paid off the top - before costs, before debt, before shareholders see anything. It was sold once, usually years earlier, to raise cash. It runs for the life of the mine unless the company buys it back, which is possible only where the original agreement allows it at a set price or where the holder agrees to sell. Because it is charged on revenue and not on profit, it is still owed in a year when the mine loses money.

Stream - Not a percentage of revenue but a claim on the metal itself. An outside party paid cash up front, often to help build the mine, in exchange for the right to receive a set share of the metal produced and to pay only a small fixed fraction of the market price for it - sometimes as little as a tenth or a fifth. The gap between that fixed price and the real price is the cost to the company, and it widens as metal prices rise. Like a royalty, a stream runs for the life of the mine unless bought back, which is possible only under the original terms or by agreement with the holder.

The Story

One paragraph in plain words: what the company is, what it owns, and the central finding. If you read nothing else, read this.

INVESTMENT COMMITTEE SUMMARY (July 31, 2026). Latin Metals - the renamed Centenera - is the campaign's sixth and most structurally inventive generator: eighteen Argentine and Peruvian projects run on two to three million dollars a year under METER-BASED earn-ins (partners earn 70-75% by drilling metres, not spending dollars - an alignment innovation that pays the generator in the only currency that matters), with roughly $80 million of committed partner investment and a stated path toward $160-180 million as the book options out. The 2026 machine: Daura Gold drilling Cerro Bayo in the Deseado Massif (Phase One's 22 holes delivering high-grade intercepts and a confirmed large epithermal system in May, a US$250,000 milestone paid, La Flora sampling to 63.88 grams gold), Moxico Resources advancing the rebranded Zaha copper-gold toward a 15,000-metre program behind early-2026 permits, the LATIN EXPLORE spin-out launched carrying the 100%-owned Peruvian copper book (the RRI-Ravena pattern repeated), first systematic work inside a 500,000-hectare northwest-Argentina copper play, and February's full warrant exercise adding $750,000 without a raise. The honest ledger: AngloGold Ashanti TERMINATED its Organullo option after drilling 6,000 metres - the generator model's downside realized and disclosed, with the project back at 100% seeking its next partner. At C$0.16 on a micro-cap register the file prices near-fair - the family verdict, a sixth time.

Glossary - every term, in plain words (tap to open)

Estimated value - What our model calculates one share is worth from documented evidence at a stated metal price and date. An estimate, not a prediction of where the stock will trade.

Cautious value (safety floor) - The deliberately careful of the two published values: stress-grade assumptions throughout. If the price is below even this number, the discount needs no generosity to see.

Fair value (market-based) - The second published value: what the company is worth using the yardstick the market actually applies to companies of this type across the Roster, with growth on its documented calendar. The verdict keys to this value.

Discount / premium at today's price - The gap between an estimated value and what a share costs today. Green (discount) = the share costs less than the value. Red (premium) = the price already exceeds the value.

Share price - What the market currently charges for one share, always shown with the date of the quote.

Trading below / near / above estimated value - The relationship between price and FAIR value. Below = the market charges less than the estimate (a discount). Above = the price already assumes future events (a pre-payment). Near = within a few percent.

The five-case deck - Value computed at five fixed cases of the company's own commodity price - Stress, Conservative Base, the dated Spot, Long-Term Normalized, Upside. We never forecast the metal; you bring your own view.

Value milestones - A calendar of dated events. Value steps only when an event lands and its inputs are released; the share price line is never forecast. Each step is a checkable claim.

Catalyst - A dated, verifiable event - a study, a permit, a financing - that releases new model inputs.

Pre-payment - When today's price already contains tomorrow's documents. Not automatically bad - but you should know you are doing it.

Quality tier / recalibrated rank - Company quality alone, from a 7-factor panel, placed on a 1-10 ladder where the Roster median is 5.0. It deliberately ignores price.

Symposium Top - The highest quality tier on the Roster ladder - the best-evidenced enterprises among an already elite set.

The Roster - The fixed set of companies covered - the presenting companies of a leading annual natural-resource investing symposium, itself a pre-selected elite of the roughly 2,000-3,000 mining companies worldwide, so every tier is standing among the select.

Release gate - A report is published only when every one of the 52 questions reaches a terminal answer - evidenced, documented as absent, or stage-exempt. No gaps hidden.

SOFT - A figure we could not confirm from a primary source, labeled honestly wherever it is used.

PEA / PFS / FS - The study ladder: Preliminary Economic Assessment (first economics), Pre-Feasibility (engineered), Feasibility (bankable). Each rung earns more credit in the model.

P/NAV (developers) - Price compared to a project's study value. Builders trade below 1.0 before production and re-rate through it as the mine becomes real.

Risk weight - The fraction of a project's study value the model credits today, by stage - small for early studies, larger once permitted and engineered.

AISC - All-in sustaining cost: what it costs to produce one ounce, all-in. The margin is the metal price minus this.

NSR royalty - A share of a mine's revenue off the top. Royalty companies own these instead of operating mines.

Streaming - Buying a mine's future silver or gold at a fixed low price in exchange for money upfront.

Earn-in - A contract where a partner pays for exploration to earn a share of a project - the generator model's engine.

Unanswered question - The one company-specific uncertainty the whole thesis hinges on, named explicitly in every report.

Royalty - A fixed percentage of a mine's revenue that goes to an outside holder rather than to the company, paid off the top - before costs, before debt, before shareholders see anything. It was sold once, usually years earlier, to raise cash. It runs for the life of the mine unless the company buys it back, which is possible only where the original agreement allows it at a set price or where the holder agrees to sell. Because it is charged on revenue and not on profit, it is still owed in a year when the mine loses money.

Stream - Not a percentage of revenue but a claim on the metal itself. An outside party paid cash up front, often to help build the mine, in exchange for the right to receive a set share of the metal produced and to pay only a small fixed fraction of the market price for it - sometimes as little as a tenth or a fifth. The gap between that fixed price and the real price is the cost to the company, and it widens as metal prices rise. Like a royalty, a stream runs for the life of the mine unless bought back, which is possible only under the original terms or by agreement with the holder.

The Story

One paragraph in plain words: what the company is, what it owns, and the central finding. If you read nothing else, read this.

INVESTMENT COMMITTEE SUMMARY (July 31, 2026). Luca is the batch's small-cap turnaround-in-motion: two wholly-owned Mexican mines - Campo Morado, a VMS polymetallic underground in Guerrero running roughly 1,900 tonnes per day, and Tahuehueto, a newly built epithermal gold-silver operation in Durango now milling above 1,050 tonnes per day - that together printed a record 2025 (tonnes milled up 51% to 1.01 million, revenue up 103%, guidance exceeded) while retiring debt to US$1.4 million with FULL repayment expected in July 2026, among the cleanest deleveragings in this project. New leadership (CEO Dan Barnholden; COO Nick Shakesby from April 2026) has built a 63,000-tonne surface stockpile at Campo Morado - a five-fold increase - to optimize mill blend and recoveries, and a three-year US$25 million exploration program targets new gold resources at both mines. The underwriting's honest tension: cheap on enterprise-to-cash-flow screens, yet the payability-adjusted margin model puts value BELOW the C$0.87 quote at every case except upside - the Guerrero-state discount and the AuEq convention's flattery reconciling the two views.

Where narrative text carries an older share price, the tables and the refreshed dated close above govern.

Three dates govern this page: the share price is the dated close shown above (2026-08-01); the evidence and estimated values are from this company's last full underwriting (2026-07-31), and change only when the company publishes something - each document's own date is listed under References; a daily event scan watches this company's filings and releases and queues a re-underwriting when one lands.

The Question the Thesis Hinges On

Single greatest company-specific uncertainty identified as the disconnect between strong, real operating results and market valuation: 2025 revenue grew 103% and Adjusted EBITDA 226%, yet the share price sits near its 52-week low, down roughly 44% over the trailing twelve months - either the market is pricing in a risk not fully captured in the operating headlines, or the stock is genuinely mispriced relative to delivered performance; this gap needs real valuation work (metric 57) to resolve, not assumption in either direction.

2025 production exceeded the company's own revised guidance, with tonnes mined and milled up 53% and 51% respectively, and silver/zinc/lead/copper production up 69%/72%/53%/37% - a real, strong, multi-metal beat, not a single-metric headline.

14. Mine-by-mine operating quality [Complete · score 3 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Real, current, asset-level detail across two 100%-owned Mexican operations: Campo Morado (zinc-copper-lead with precious-metal by-products, processing 2,000+ tpd) and Tahuehueto (initiated commercial production March 2025, advancing toward its 1,000 tpd design capacity, tonnes milled up 12% in Q1 2026 alone, and produced its first copper concentrate that quarter).

15. Cost quality [Complete · score 5 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Jurisdictional exposure is single-country and includes the project's hardest state: both mines sit in Mexico, with Campo Morado - the larger revenue contributor - in Guerrero, a state whose security environment commands the sector's deepest operating discount, and Tahuehueto in Durango's more conventional mining country. The mines operate continuously and the record year happened IN this geography, which is the evidence for the licence metric; the discount the market applies for it is real, permanent at current conditions, and part of this workbook's reconciliation of value to price.

A real, sizable, multi-year growth commitment: a three-year, US$25 million exploration program (announced November 2025) targeting new gold resources at both Campo Morado and Tahuehueto, alongside a technical report targeted for H2 2026 to inform a Campo Morado expansion study.

Debt reduced to approximately $1.4 million as of the Q1 2026 report, with full repayment expected by July 2026 - real, near-complete deleveraging; cash declined from $36.4 million to $24.7 million in Q2 2026 due to continued mine investment, a real, disclosed trade-off rather than passive cash buildup. Months of cash runway and funding gap to the next milestone were not separately quantified this pass, per the sharpened requirement for this metric.

18. Capital allocation [Complete · score 2 (of 10; 1 = best)]
A normal course issuer bid (buyback) to repurchase up to 13.75 million common shares was announced - real, dated evidence of capital return alongside continued heavy reinvestment in mine development (metric 15), a genuinely balanced allocation approach for a company at this stage.

19. Run-rate normalization [Complete · score 3 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Run-rate normalization must resist the AuEq convention's flattery: 2025's record volumes came with LOWER precious-metal grades and modestly lower recoveries (disclosed plainly), and polymetallic silver-zinc-lead-copper revenue realizes at concentrate payabilities far below the gold-equivalent arithmetic - the model therefore normalizes to roughly 80,000 AuEq ounces (SOFT) realizing about 46% of the gold price per equivalent ounce, the ratio implied by reported revenue against reported equivalent production, rather than pretending dore economics.

20. Formal scenario architecture [Complete · score 3 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Five named pricing cases are built on the SCENARIOS sheet on the project's gold deck. The model is a REALIZED-MARGIN construction: equivalent ounces times (payability-adjusted realized price minus all-in cost), taxed and multiplied - because a naive gold-minus-AISC model would overstate a polymetallic producer's economics by nearly double. The stress case exposes the structure honestly: at deep-stress metal prices the margin goes negative and value collapses toward cash, which is the true shape of thin-margin polymetallic mining.

21. Valuation-to-action bridge [Complete · score 4 (of 10; 1 = best)]
The valuation-to-action bridge lands below the quote across most of the deck: roughly 25% below at the dated spot case, deeper below at base and stress, above only at the upside case - the market pre-paying the optimization story (new operators, the stockpile buffer, the blend program) about a year before its results print. The counter-reading is recorded honestly: on enterprise-to-cash-flow screens the company looks cheap near four times, and the two views reconcile through payability economics and the Guerrero discount. The action bridge is quarterly: recoveries and margins under the new blend regime, checkable each print.

The financial break is nearly retired along with the debt: with repayment complete, no covenant or maturity can force anything; the model's collapse mode is purely a metal-price one.

Glossary - every term, in plain words (tap to open)

Estimated value - What our model calculates one share is worth from documented evidence at a stated metal price and date. An estimate, not a prediction of where the stock will trade.

Cautious value (safety floor) - The deliberately careful of the two published values: stress-grade assumptions throughout. If the price is below even this number, the discount needs no generosity to see.

Fair value (market-based) - The second published value: what the company is worth using the yardstick the market actually applies to companies of this type across the Roster, with growth on its documented calendar. The verdict keys to this value.

Discount / premium at today's price - The gap between an estimated value and what a share costs today. Green (discount) = the share costs less than the value. Red (premium) = the price already exceeds the value.

Share price - What the market currently charges for one share, always shown with the date of the quote.

Trading below / near / above estimated value - The relationship between price and FAIR value. Below = the market charges less than the estimate (a discount). Above = the price already assumes future events (a pre-payment). Near = within a few percent.

The five-case deck - Value computed at five fixed cases of the company's own commodity price - Stress, Conservative Base, the dated Spot, Long-Term Normalized, Upside. We never forecast the metal; you bring your own view.

Value milestones - A calendar of dated events. Value steps only when an event lands and its inputs are released; the share price line is never forecast. Each step is a checkable claim.

Catalyst - A dated, verifiable event - a study, a permit, a financing - that releases new model inputs.

Pre-payment - When today's price already contains tomorrow's documents. Not automatically bad - but you should know you are doing it.

Quality tier / recalibrated rank - Company quality alone, from a 7-factor panel, placed on a 1-10 ladder where the Roster median is 5.0. It deliberately ignores price.

Symposium Top - The highest quality tier on the Roster ladder - the best-evidenced enterprises among an already elite set.

The Roster - The fixed set of companies covered - the presenting companies of a leading annual natural-resource investing symposium, itself a pre-selected elite of the roughly 2,000-3,000 mining companies worldwide, so every tier is standing among the select.

Release gate - A report is published only when every one of the 52 questions reaches a terminal answer - evidenced, documented as absent, or stage-exempt. No gaps hidden.

SOFT - A figure we could not confirm from a primary source, labeled honestly wherever it is used.

PEA / PFS / FS - The study ladder: Preliminary Economic Assessment (first economics), Pre-Feasibility (engineered), Feasibility (bankable). Each rung earns more credit in the model.

P/NAV (developers) - Price compared to a project's study value. Builders trade below 1.0 before production and re-rate through it as the mine becomes real.

Risk weight - The fraction of a project's study value the model credits today, by stage - small for early studies, larger once permitted and engineered.

AISC - All-in sustaining cost: what it costs to produce one ounce, all-in. The margin is the metal price minus this.

NSR royalty - A share of a mine's revenue off the top. Royalty companies own these instead of operating mines.

Streaming - Buying a mine's future silver or gold at a fixed low price in exchange for money upfront.

Earn-in - A contract where a partner pays for exploration to earn a share of a project - the generator model's engine.

Unanswered question - The one company-specific uncertainty the whole thesis hinges on, named explicitly in every report.

Royalty - A fixed percentage of a mine's revenue that goes to an outside holder rather than to the company, paid off the top - before costs, before debt, before shareholders see anything. It was sold once, usually years earlier, to raise cash. It runs for the life of the mine unless the company buys it back, which is possible only where the original agreement allows it at a set price or where the holder agrees to sell. Because it is charged on revenue and not on profit, it is still owed in a year when the mine loses money.

Stream - Not a percentage of revenue but a claim on the metal itself. An outside party paid cash up front, often to help build the mine, in exchange for the right to receive a set share of the metal produced and to pay only a small fixed fraction of the market price for it - sometimes as little as a tenth or a fifth. The gap between that fixed price and the real price is the cost to the company, and it widens as metal prices rise. Like a royalty, a stream runs for the life of the mine unless bought back, which is possible only under the original terms or by agreement with the holder.

The Story

One paragraph in plain words: what the company is, what it owns, and the central finding. If you read nothing else, read this.

IC summary: the West's answer to Chinese ionic-clay dominance, and the freshest document chain in the universe - the Caldeira Definitive Feasibility Study was released on THIS underwriting's valuation date (July 31, 2026): a 151 Mt Ore Reserve supporting a 23-year mine life, US$498M capex, and a post-tax NPV of US$847M with 24% IRR and four-year payback calculated AT CURRENT DEPRESSED SPOT RARE-EARTH PRICES - meaning the economics require no price recovery to work. Behind it: 90,000 m of drilling, 55,500 assays, three years of ANSTO testwork, five months of continuous pilot operations (~70%+ magnet-metal recoveries), Measured resources up 246% (July 9), the Preliminary Licence granted by Minas Gerais (December 2025), the Installation Licence targeted Q4 2026, non-binding offtake MOUs with POSCO International, Neo Performance Materials and Ucore, insiders holding ~19.4%, and 80%+ of the tenure still outside the study. Glossary - every term, in plain words (tap to open)

Estimated value - What our model calculates one share is worth from documented evidence at a stated metal price and date. An estimate, not a prediction of where the stock will trade.

Cautious value (safety floor) - The deliberately careful of the two published values: stress-grade assumptions throughout. If the price is below even this number, the discount needs no generosity to see.

Fair value (market-based) - The second published value: what the company is worth using the yardstick the market actually applies to companies of this type across the Roster, with growth on its documented calendar. The verdict keys to this value.

Discount / premium at today's price - The gap between an estimated value and what a share costs today. Green (discount) = the share costs less than the value. Red (premium) = the price already exceeds the value.

Share price - What the market currently charges for one share, always shown with the date of the quote.

Trading below / near / above estimated value - The relationship between price and FAIR value. Below = the market charges less than the estimate (a discount). Above = the price already assumes future events (a pre-payment). Near = within a few percent.

The five-case deck - Value computed at five fixed cases of the company's own commodity price - Stress, Conservative Base, the dated Spot, Long-Term Normalized, Upside. We never forecast the metal; you bring your own view.

Value milestones - A calendar of dated events. Value steps only when an event lands and its inputs are released; the share price line is never forecast. Each step is a checkable claim.

Catalyst - A dated, verifiable event - a study, a permit, a financing - that releases new model inputs.

Pre-payment - When today's price already contains tomorrow's documents. Not automatically bad - but you should know you are doing it.

Quality tier / recalibrated rank - Company quality alone, from a 7-factor panel, placed on a 1-10 ladder where the Roster median is 5.0. It deliberately ignores price.

Symposium Top - The highest quality tier on the Roster ladder - the best-evidenced enterprises among an already elite set.

The Roster - The fixed set of companies covered - the presenting companies of a leading annual natural-resource investing symposium, itself a pre-selected elite of the roughly 2,000-3,000 mining companies worldwide, so every tier is standing among the select.

Release gate - A report is published only when every one of the 52 questions reaches a terminal answer - evidenced, documented as absent, or stage-exempt. No gaps hidden.

SOFT - A figure we could not confirm from a primary source, labeled honestly wherever it is used.

PEA / PFS / FS - The study ladder: Preliminary Economic Assessment (first economics), Pre-Feasibility (engineered), Feasibility (bankable). Each rung earns more credit in the model.

P/NAV (developers) - Price compared to a project's study value. Builders trade below 1.0 before production and re-rate through it as the mine becomes real.

Risk weight - The fraction of a project's study value the model credits today, by stage - small for early studies, larger once permitted and engineered.

AISC - All-in sustaining cost: what it costs to produce one ounce, all-in. The margin is the metal price minus this.

NSR royalty - A share of a mine's revenue off the top. Royalty companies own these instead of operating mines.

Streaming - Buying a mine's future silver or gold at a fixed low price in exchange for money upfront.

Earn-in - A contract where a partner pays for exploration to earn a share of a project - the generator model's engine.

Unanswered question - The one company-specific uncertainty the whole thesis hinges on, named explicitly in every report.

Royalty - A fixed percentage of a mine's revenue that goes to an outside holder rather than to the company, paid off the top - before costs, before debt, before shareholders see anything. It was sold once, usually years earlier, to raise cash. It runs for the life of the mine unless the company buys it back, which is possible only where the original agreement allows it at a set price or where the holder agrees to sell. Because it is charged on revenue and not on profit, it is still owed in a year when the mine loses money.

Stream - Not a percentage of revenue but a claim on the metal itself. An outside party paid cash up front, often to help build the mine, in exchange for the right to receive a set share of the metal produced and to pay only a small fixed fraction of the market price for it - sometimes as little as a tenth or a fifth. The gap between that fixed price and the real price is the cost to the company, and it widens as metal prices rise. Like a royalty, a stream runs for the life of the mine unless bought back, which is possible only under the original terms or by agreement with the holder.

The Story

One paragraph in plain words: what the company is, what it owns, and the central finding. If you read nothing else, read this.

INVESTMENT COMMITTEE SUMMARY (July 31, 2026). Mineros is the project's quiet compounder: a 52-year-old Medellin institution running two cash machines - the Nechi alluvial dredging operation in Colombia and the Hemco underground-plus-artisanal complex in Nicaragua - that produced record 2025 results (US$800 million revenue, US$145 million net profit, US$138.6 million free cash flow) and just raised 2026 guidance to 220,000-240,000 ounces on an 11% second-quarter production increase. The distinguishing structure is the artisanal-partnership model: a large share of ounces is purchased from formalized small-scale miners at prices indexed to gold, making those ounces a margin business whose costs rise with the metal. The underwriting verdict: near-fair pricing for demonstrated cash flow in two hard jurisdictions, with the Porvenir polymetallic project, the Nicaragua expansion and the new Tolima entry as the un-paid-for pipeline.

Where narrative text carries an older share price, the tables and the refreshed dated close above govern.

Three dates govern this page: the share price is the dated close shown above (2026-07-30); the evidence and estimated values are from this company's last full underwriting (2026-07-31), and change only when the company publishes something - each document's own date is listed under References; a daily event scan watches this company's filings and releases and queues a re-underwriting when one lands.

The Question the Thesis Hinges On

Single greatest company-specific uncertainty identified as artisanal-mining-partnership cost sensitivity at Hemco: the company explicitly discloses that as gold prices rise, its Bonanza Mining Partners (artisanal miners) are paid a relatively stable percentage of spot price, directly pushing Cash Costs and AISC higher at that property - meaning part of the company's own cost structure is mechanically linked to the same gold price driving its revenue, a real, disclosed, and somewhat unusual structural relationship.

The Full Underwriting Register - all 52 questions (tap to open)

The same 52 questions are asked of every company. Statuses: Complete = evidenced and scored; Not Available - Documented = the fact does not exist publicly and we say so; Stage-exempt = not applicable to this company type or stage. Figures not confirmed from a primary source are labeled SOFT.

3. Investment Committee decision summary [Complete · score 3 (of 10; 1 = best)]
INVESTMENT COMMITTEE SUMMARY (July 31, 2026). Mineros is the project's quiet compounder: a 52-year-old Medellin institution running two cash machines - the Nechi alluvial dredging operation in Colombia and the Hemco underground-plus-artisanal complex in Nicaragua - that produced record 2025 results (US$800 million revenue, US$145 million net profit, US$138.6 million free cash flow) and just raised 2026 guidance to 220,000-240,000 ounces on an 11% second-quarter production increase. The distinguishing structure is the artisanal-partnership model: a large share of ounces is purchased from formalized small-scale miners at prices indexed to gold, making those ounces a margin business whose costs rise with the metal. The underwriting verdict: near-fair pricing for demonstrated cash flow in two hard jurisdictions, with the Porvenir polymetallic project, the Nicaragua expansion and the new Tolima entry as the un-paid-for pipeline.

11. Reserve/resource movement bridge [Complete · score 3 (of 10; 1 = best)]
The resource ledger advanced by drilling on both fronts this cycle: the 2025 Hemco campaign fed the new Guillermina resource area, July 2026 brought reported confirmation of a high-grade discovery at a new target with potential district expansion in Nicaragua, and the Nechi alluvial reserve depletes and re-proves on its long-established dredge-path model. No consolidated year-over-year movement bridge reconciling depletion against additions is published; the district-scale drilling disclosure makes the direction clear while leaving the arithmetic to the annual technical statements.
