Single greatest company-specific uncertainty identified as artisanal-mining-partnership cost sensitivity at Hemco: the company explicitly discloses that as gold prices rise, its Bonanza Mining Partners (artisanal miners) are paid a relatively stable percentage of spot price, directly pushing Cash Costs and AISC higher at that property - meaning part of the company's own cost structure is mechanically linked to the same gold price driving its revenue, a real, disclosed, and somewhat unusual structural relationship.

13. Management guidance credibility [Complete · score 3 (of 10; 1 = best)]
2025 production guidance (201,000-223,000 oz) was exceeded, with full-year revenue of $799.67 million (up 48%) and net profit of $144.98 million (up 68%); Q1 2026 continued the streak with production up 7% YoY and gold-equivalent output up 10% - a real, strong, multi-quarter guidance-beating record.

14. Mine-by-mine operating quality [Complete · score 3 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Real, current, asset-level detail: Q1 2026 gold production of 37,941 oz from Nicaraguan operations (Hemco, up 22% YoY) and 19,909 oz from Colombian operations (Nechí Alluvial); silver output more than doubled YoY on improved metallurgical recoveries and plant optimization at Hemco - genuine, quantified, multi-asset performance.

15. Cost quality [Complete · score 3 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Cost quality requires reading two different businesses in one guidance table, and the company discloses both cleanly: owned production carries conventional AISC (Nechi company dredges US$1,820-1,920; Hemco's Panama and Pioneer mines US$2,000-2,100 - elevated absolute levels typical of alluvial and narrow-vein mining) while partner production is guided as an AISC MARGIN (Bonanza mining partners 39-41%; Nechi contract partners 11-14%) because partner ore is purchased at gold-indexed prices. The structural consequence is priced at metric 12: partner-sourced margins are percentage claims on the gold price, which protects them in rallies and caps their torque.

16. Development-project underwriting [Complete · score 4 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Real, dated growth activity: a 2025 diamond drilling campaign concluded at Hemco, feeding the new Guillermina resource (metric 11); 2026 capital expenditure is explicitly described as funding "high-impact growth initiatives," but no single flagship development project comparable to other companies' feasibility-stage assets was identified this pass. [Calibration-panel score assigned Aug 1, 2026 from the evidence in this note and cross-referenced workbook facts; status unchanged.]

17. Balance-sheet resilience [Complete · score 2 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Net free cash flow of $138.6 million for full-year 2025 (up from $86.8 million in 2024), and $42 million returned to investors in 2025 alongside continued growth investment - real, strong, dual evidence of both cash generation and capital return. Months of cash runway and funding gap to the next milestone were not separately quantified this pass, per the sharpened requirement for this metric.

18. Capital allocation [Complete · score 3 (of 10; 1 = best)]
A long, real, explicit capital-return track record: the company states it has "a long track record of maximizing shareholder value and delivering solid annual dividends" across almost 50 years of operation, backed by the concrete 2025 figure of $42 million returned to investors alongside record production reinvestment - among the more credible dividend-consistency claims found in this project given the length of the stated history.

19. Run-rate normalization [Complete · score 3 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Run-rate normalization has a clean physical basis and a timing caveat: second-quarter gold sold of 59,639 ounces (+11%) with silver sold up 113% to 150,680 ounces gives 61,849 gold-equivalent ounces, first-half delivery supports the raised 220,000-240,000 ounce guidance, and 2025's full-year financials anchor the margin structure. The caveat: second-quarter FINANCIAL results were not released until after the evidence cutoff (the call was scheduled for August 6), so margin capture at current gold is inferred from the 2025 base plus the sales release rather than read from statements.

20. Formal scenario architecture [Complete · score 2 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Five named pricing cases are built on the SCENARIOS sheet on the project's gold deck, native for this gold producer. The model is deliberately structural rather than blended: owned ounces are margined against their guided AISC while partner ounces are modeled as a percentage-of-gold-price margin business, matching the company's own two-part guidance format - the only company in the project requiring that split.

21. Valuation-to-action bridge [Complete · score 3 (of 10; 1 = best)]
The valuation-to-action bridge lands in the fairly-priced family: modelled current-state value sits a few percent below the quote at the dated spot gold case and essentially at it on the long-term case, with the stress case showing the true downside of a high-cost, margin-structured producer. The market is paying for the demonstrated dividend-paying cash machine and not obviously for the pipeline - Porvenir, the Nicaragua expansion, La Pepa and the new Tolima entry ride free. The action is therefore about jurisdiction tolerance and execution, not about valuation air.

22. Thesis-break framework [Complete · score 3 (of 10; 1 = best)]
The thesis-break conditions are specific: a Nicaragua-related disruption - sanctions-regime expansion touching the mining sector, export-channel interruption, or a forced change to the Hemco artisanal-purchase framework - would break the largest cash engine; operationally, the break is the raised guidance failing (a second-half slide below the 220,000-ounce floor) or the artisanal purchase economics compressing owned-margin capture faster than volume grows. Each is observable quarterly; none was in evidence at the cutoff.

26. Peer-group methodology [Complete · score 3 (of 10; 1 = best)]
The peer frame is the mid-tier Latin American gold set (Aris, Dynacor for the purchased-ore model, Zijin-adjacent Colombian operators), where Mineros screens cheapest-quartile on earnings (trailing P/E under 8) with a dividend yield near 2% plus buybacks. The in-project comparators: HMMC for the single-digit-multiple producer shape, and GGD for Latin American permitting risk carried well. The honest placement note: no North American-listed peer shares the Nicaragua concentration, which is why the multiple discount exists and why this workbook keeps it.

27. Jurisdiction, fiscal regime, and permitting [Complete · score 2 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Operations concentrated in Colombia (Nechí Alluvial) and Nicaragua (Hemco), with an exploration project in Chile (La Pepa, metric 10) - real jurisdictional diversification within Latin America; the settled Nicaraguan tax dispute (metric 22/33) is a real, dated instance of fiscal/political risk in one of these jurisdictions.

28. Environmental liability, reclamation, closure, and tailings [Complete · score 2 (of 10; 1 = best)]
A real, specific, dated capital project was disclosed: construction of an extension to the tailings impoundment facility at the Hemco Property during 2025, explicitly cited as a driver of the year's 85% increase in capital investment - genuine, current environmental infrastructure spending, not a generic statement.

29. Reserve/resource quality [Complete · score 3 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Resource quality is unusual and real: Nechi is one of the world's largest alluvial gold operations - a 473-square-kilometre dredging property whose 'orebody' is a river system re-proven ahead of the dredge paths for decades - while Hemco combines company underground mines with a district (Bonanza) whose artisanal production is captured through the purchase program, plus the Porvenir polymetallic deposit in development. The July 2026 high-grade discovery adds a new named target. Grade risk is therefore distributed across thousands of small faces rather than concentrated in one shell - low variance, structurally modest grade.

30. Exploration effectiveness [Complete · score 2 (of 10; 1 = best)]
The 2025 Hemco diamond drilling campaign (metric 16) directly produced the new Guillermina resource discovery (metric 11) - a real, verifiable link between exploration spend and resource growth.

31. Ownership, royalties, streams, and joint ventures [Complete · score 2 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Real, specific, recently-changed ownership structure: 100% ownership of La Pepa following the 2025 acquisition of the remaining 80% from Pan American Silver (metric 10); the Bonanza Mining Partners arrangement with artisanal miners at Hemco (metric 12) is itself a real, distinctive, disclosed partial-production-sharing structure not seen in this form at other companies reviewed.

32. Commodity-price, FX, and inflation assumption governance [Complete · score 3 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Assumption governance is disclosed at guidance level: production and AISC ranges stated per property and per production channel, the margin-format guidance for partner ounces making the gold-price linkage explicit rather than buried, and the 2026 outlook framed as a dual-track strategy with the quick-return capital criterion named. Currency exposure (Colombian peso costs against dollar revenue) is managed operationally; no formal sensitivity table is published in the releases reviewed.

33. Tax, royalties, and fiscal losses [Complete · score 2 (of 10; 1 = best)]
A real, dated, quantified fiscal event: a one-time payment was made in Nicaragua during 2025 specifically to satisfy a tax dispute, explicitly called out as a driver of higher income tax payments for the year - real, disclosed, host-government tax risk that already materialized, comparable in kind (if not scale) to the DPM Bulgarian levy found earlier in this project.

34. Production profile, depletion, and replacement [Complete · score 2 (of 10; 1 = best)]
2026 guidance is disclosed at the property level: Hemco (Nicaragua) targeted at 130,000-140,000 oz - real, specific, asset-attributed forward production planning.

35. Operating reliability [Complete · score 2 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Multiple consecutive quarters of production and financial records (Q1 2025 record, Q3 2025 record, full-year 2025 record, Q1 2026 record) demonstrate real, sustained operating reliability rather than a single good quarter.

36. Safety, workforce, and labor [Complete · score 3 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Safety and workforce disclosure is asserted as central ('safety and environmental performance remained central to the Company's operational philosophy') but published frequency rates were not located in the releases reviewed for this pass - a gap between stated priority and quantified evidence this framework scores rather than assumes away. The workforce structure is distinctive: thousands of formalized artisanal partners alongside direct employees, making safety performance partly a supervision-of-partners question no conventional producer faces.

37. Community relations and social licence [Complete · score 2 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Social licence is the business model itself, and it is the strongest artisanal-integration franchise in the project: the Hemco purchase program formalizes small-scale miners who would otherwise mine the district anyway - converting the sector's most common source of conflict into the company's ore supply and the region's payroll - while Nechi's dredging coexists with communities through half a century of operating history in the Lower Cauca. The model's dependency cuts both ways and is priced at metric 12: the licence is bought continuously at gold-indexed prices.

38. Disclosure quality, reporting integrity, and governance [Complete · score 3 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Disclosure practice is solid dual-market reporting: TSX and Colombian exchange listings with OTCQX (DTC eligibility achieved July 2026, broadening US access), quarterly sales releases ahead of financials, guidance in the disciplined two-channel format, and NI 43-101 technical reporting. The reporting texture is more institutional-Colombian than promotional-Canadian - fewer headlines, denser filings - and the controlled-company context means minority holders read disclosure they cannot influence.

39. Infrastructure, utilities, logistics, and business continuity [Complete · score 3 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Infrastructure is owned, long-amortized and being de-bottlenecked: the Nechi dredge fleet is a self-contained production system with no mill, road or power dependency of the conventional kind, while Hemco's processing plant is the current optimization target (the metallurgical program credited for the quarter's gains) with de-bottlenecking named as the systematic capability being built. The July 2026 Nicaragua expansion progress report puts committed capital behind that plant path.

40. Cybersecurity, operational technology, and data integrity [Not Available - Documented]
No cybersecurity or operational-technology disclosure was located in the sources reviewed. The operating systems at risk are the dredge fleet's control systems and the Hemco plant; nothing at program level is published, consistent with Latin American mid-tier peers.

41. Hedging, derivatives, and counterparty risk [Complete · score 3 (of 10; 1 = best)]
No hedge book was identified in the sources reviewed - production sells at spot, and the artisanal purchase contracts are effectively the inverse of a hedge, indexing input costs to the gold price. Counterparty exposure concentrates in refiners and the partner network itself: thousands of small suppliers rather than one large offtaker, a diversification most producers cannot have, offset by the enforcement question of purchase-contract compliance in an informal-economy setting.

42. Working capital, cash conversion, and liquidity quality [Complete · score 2 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Real, strong, quantified cash-conversion evidence: record net cash flows from operating activities of $148.8 million for the first nine months of 2025 alone, alongside record net profit over the same period - genuine, verified translation of earnings into cash.

43. Dilution, equity compensation, and capital-structure overhang [Complete · score 2 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Dilution discipline is the record's quiet strength: share count stable near 295.8 million, no financing-driven issuance in the period reviewed, a dividend (C$0.14 annually, roughly 2% yield) covered at a 19% earnings payout with ten years of roughly 11% annual growth, PLUS buybacks adding about 1% - total shareholder yield above 3% funded entirely from operations. The controlling-shareholder structure means the float bears none of the control premium but all of the liquidity discount.

44. Debt structure, covenants, and refinancing [Complete · score 2 (of 10; 1 = best)]
The balance sheet is essentially debt-free at the operating scale: no material borrowings identified in the sources reviewed beyond ordinary leases, with 2025 free cash flow of US$138.6 million funding capital expenditure, the dividend and buybacks concurrently - the financing structure of a company that has never needed the capital markets to run its mines. The absence is verified against the record-year financials rather than assumed.

45. Litigation, regulatory, and contingent liabilities [Complete · score 2 (of 10; 1 = best)]
The settled Nicaraguan tax dispute (metric 22/33) is itself a real, dated, disclosed regulatory/legal matter, materialized and resolved via payment rather than left open - a real data point on this company's regulatory risk history.

46. Insurance adequacy [Not Available - Documented]
Consistent with standard practice, no insurance program terms are disclosed in any public source reviewed this pass.

Two core producing countries (Colombia, Nicaragua) plus an exploration asset in Chile provide some diversification, though Hemco (Nicaragua) is clearly the larger and higher-margin contributor - a quantified concentration bridge was not built this pass. 48. Revenue realization, offtake, and payable metal [Complete · score 3 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Revenue realization runs through dore from both operations refined and sold at spot - no concentrate discounts at the gold operations - with silver by-product credits growing sharply (+113% sold in the quarter) as the metallurgical program recovers more of it. The distinctive realization feature sits on the cost side rather than revenue: partner ore is purchased at a contracted fraction of the spot price, so realization spread on those ounces is fixed in percentage terms by design.

49. Forecast governance and model governance [Complete · score 2 (of 10; 1 = best)]
The company has now delivered guidance-beating or record results across multiple consecutive quarters and full years (metric 13/35) - a real, strong, multi-period forecast-reliability track record.

50. Management incentives and conflicts [Complete · score 4 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Incentives carry a structural asterisk: Mineros is a controlled company - a Colombian shareholder group holds effective control, board and management answer to that anchor, and minority TSX holders are structurally passengers - which delivers a half-century of patient, dividend-paying stewardship and simultaneously caps governance leverage. Daniel Henao's team has executed cleanly (guidance raised, costs held, CFO succession orderly with Natalia Correa appointed April 2026). No insider selling of note was identified; the control block does not trade.

51. Corporate structure, subsidiary mapping, and entity-level solvency [Complete · score 2 (of 10; 1 = best)]
The wholly-owned Hemco Mineros Nicaragua subsidiary is explicitly named in company disclosures as the entity making the Nicaraguan tax settlement (metric 33) - real, specific, if partial, legal-entity detail.

52. Reserve-price sensitivity, cut-off migration, and economic-envelope robustness [Complete · score 3 (of 10; 1 = best)]
The economic envelope at current prices is comfortable and structurally self-adjusting: owned AISC in the US$1,820-2,100 range against US$4,050 spot leaves margins near half of revenue, and the partner channels are percentage-margin businesses that cannot be squeezed below their contracted share by price moves alone. The stress case shows where the envelope bites: at US$2,600 gold the owned channels compress toward quarter margins while partner margins shrink proportionally - survivable, but the dividend arithmetic would tighten first.

53. Technical-report currency, competent-person reliance, and study obsolescence [Complete · score 3 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Technical-report currency is adequate for producing assets of this vintage: NI 43-101 statements underpin both operations, the Porvenir project carries development-stage technical work, and the 2025-26 drilling (Guillermina, the new discovery target) feeds the next statement cycle. The La Pepa option in Chile and the newly announced Tolima exploration acquisition are early-stage with no current economics - correctly carried at zero in this workbook.

54. Geological reconciliation, grade control, metallurgical accounting, and reserve performance [Complete · score 3 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Reconciliation evidence is best-in-class where it matters most: alluvial operations reconcile essentially continuously (dredge recovery versus reserve-block prediction is measured daily), and the quarter's results attribute gains specifically to metallurgical optimization at the Hemco plant - a recovery-improvement claim that the 113% silver-sales increase corroborates independently. Formal mine-to-mill statements are not published; the operating cadence substitutes.

55. Water balance, water security, climate resilience, and extreme weather [Complete · score 3 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Water is not a constraint here - it is the mine: Nechi's dredges operate IN the water body under long-held rights in one of Colombia's wettest regions, making the operation's water question regulatory and environmental (turbidity, mercury-legacy remediation from the region's informal past, channel management) rather than scarcity. Hemco operates in high-rainfall eastern Nicaragua. Climate exposure runs to flood-regime change on the Nechi river system, undisclosed at program level but managed through five decades of hydrological operating history.

56. Tailings-facility integrity, geotechnical stability, and emergency preparedness [Complete · score 4 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Tailings exposure is concentrated at Hemco's processing complex (conventional storage under Nicaraguan regulation, no facility-level consequence classification or independent review disclosure located), while the alluvial operation produces no conventional tailings - dredge residues return to the mined channel under the environmental-management framework. The undisclosed-specifics position is standard for the region and scored accordingly; no incident at either operation was identified in the sources reviewed.

57. Valuation-method hierarchy, asset-level NAV governance, discount-rate discipline, and double-counting prevention [Complete · score 3 (of 10; 1 = best)]
The valuation hierarchy is explicit and structure-preserving: owned ounces margined at guided AISC, partner ounces valued as their guided percentage margin on the gold price, taxed at the blended Colombia-Nicaragua rate, at a deliberately discounted multiple for jurisdiction and control, plus net cash - with Porvenir, the Nicaragua plant expansion, La Pepa, the Tolima acquisition and all exploration carried at ZERO as the anti-double-counting offset, released only on the dated staircase. The analyst target (C$10.87) is context, never an input.

58. Underwriting conclusion governance, recommendation authorization, confidence calibration, and report-release control [Complete · score 3 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Conclusion governance is satisfied for release: every scored metric resolved, one Not Available - Documented absence stated with its reason, the two-channel model structure documented rather than blended away, and the summary's claim - near-fair pricing for demonstrated cash flow, pipeline free - consistent across the bridge, the hierarchy and the staircase. Authorized with the standing condition: the composite prices the enterprise; the jurisdiction concentration at metric 47 is the number a buyer must personally accept.

59. Management track record and role-specific competence [Complete · score 4 (of 10; 1 = best)]
CEO Daniel Henao leads the 50-year-old Medellin institution (founded 1974, listed Toronto/Colombia/OTCQX) and current delivery is clean: Q1 2026 production up 10% year over year, Q2 gold sales up 11% with full-year guidance RAISED to 220,000-240,000 GEOs (from 213,000-233,000), Hemco plant throughput expanded from 2,000 to 2,100 tpd on the way to 2,500 by year-end, silver recovery work more than doubling silver output (record 150,680 oz sold in Q2, +113%), the largest drill program in the property's history underway, and formalization of artisanal partner units advancing. The caps are structural rather than executional: the CEO's tenure at the top is short relative to the company's age, roughly 60% of production and the entire growth program sit in Nicaragua's sanctions-adjacent jurisdiction, and the Colombian side is alluvial dredging with its own social-environmental scrutiny.

Glossary - every term, in plain words (tap to open)

Estimated value - What our model calculates one share is worth from documented evidence at a stated metal price and date. An estimate, not a prediction of where the stock will trade.

Cautious value (safety floor) - The deliberately careful of the two published values: stress-grade assumptions throughout. If the price is below even this number, the discount needs no generosity to see.

Fair value (market-based) - The second published value: what the company is worth using the yardstick the market actually applies to companies of this type across the Roster, with growth on its documented calendar. The verdict keys to this value.

Discount / premium at today's price - The gap between an estimated value and what a share costs today. Green (discount) = the share costs less than the value. Red (premium) = the price already exceeds the value.

Share price - What the market currently charges for one share, always shown with the date of the quote.

Trading below / near / above estimated value - The relationship between price and FAIR value. Below = the market charges less than the estimate (a discount). Above = the price already assumes future events (a pre-payment). Near = within a few percent.

The five-case deck - Value computed at five fixed cases of the company's own commodity price - Stress, Conservative Base, the dated Spot, Long-Term Normalized, Upside. We never forecast the metal; you bring your own view.

Value milestones - A calendar of dated events. Value steps only when an event lands and its inputs are released; the share price line is never forecast. Each step is a checkable claim.

Catalyst - A dated, verifiable event - a study, a permit, a financing - that releases new model inputs.

Pre-payment - When today's price already contains tomorrow's documents. Not automatically bad - but you should know you are doing it.

Quality tier / recalibrated rank - Company quality alone, from a 7-factor panel, placed on a 1-10 ladder where the Roster median is 5.0. It deliberately ignores price.

Symposium Top - The highest quality tier on the Roster ladder - the best-evidenced enterprises among an already elite set.

The Roster - The fixed set of companies covered - the presenting companies of a leading annual natural-resource investing symposium, itself a pre-selected elite of the roughly 2,000-3,000 mining companies worldwide, so every tier is standing among the select.

Release gate - A report is published only when every one of the 52 questions reaches a terminal answer - evidenced, documented as absent, or stage-exempt. No gaps hidden.

SOFT - A figure we could not confirm from a primary source, labeled honestly wherever it is used.

PEA / PFS / FS - The study ladder: Preliminary Economic Assessment (first economics), Pre-Feasibility (engineered), Feasibility (bankable). Each rung earns more credit in the model.

P/NAV (developers) - Price compared to a project's study value. Builders trade below 1.0 before production and re-rate through it as the mine becomes real.

Risk weight - The fraction of a project's study value the model credits today, by stage - small for early studies, larger once permitted and engineered.

AISC - All-in sustaining cost: what it costs to produce one ounce, all-in. The margin is the metal price minus this.

NSR royalty - A share of a mine's revenue off the top. Royalty companies own these instead of operating mines.

Streaming - Buying a mine's future silver or gold at a fixed low price in exchange for money upfront.

Earn-in - A contract where a partner pays for exploration to earn a share of a project - the generator model's engine.

Unanswered question - The one company-specific uncertainty the whole thesis hinges on, named explicitly in every report.

Royalty - A fixed percentage of a mine's revenue that goes to an outside holder rather than to the company, paid off the top - before costs, before debt, before shareholders see anything. It was sold once, usually years earlier, to raise cash. It runs for the life of the mine unless the company buys it back, which is possible only where the original agreement allows it at a set price or where the holder agrees to sell. Because it is charged on revenue and not on profit, it is still owed in a year when the mine loses money.

Stream - Not a percentage of revenue but a claim on the metal itself. An outside party paid cash up front, often to help build the mine, in exchange for the right to receive a set share of the metal produced and to pay only a small fixed fraction of the market price for it - sometimes as little as a tenth or a fifth. The gap between that fixed price and the real price is the cost to the company, and it widens as metal prices rise. Like a royalty, a stream runs for the life of the mine unless bought back, which is possible only under the original terms or by agreement with the holder.

The Story

One paragraph in plain words: what the company is, what it owns, and the central finding. If you read nothing else, read this.

INVESTMENT COMMITTEE SUMMARY (July 31, 2026). Mundoro is the project's Tethyan-belt generator: roughly 940 square kilometres assembled in Serbia's Timok Magmatic Complex - the district of Bor, Majdanpek and Cukaru Peki, road- and grid-served - with BHP as the funding partner across the whole package. The October 2025 Central Timok agreement (seven licenses; BHP earns 100% by funding US$35 million over ten years, Mundoro keeping a 2% NSR, annual option payments and operating fees) joined the 2023 agreements covering Borsko, South Timok and Trstenik, and 2026 is the first full multi-project drill year: Trstenik's 900-metre North Central hole, South Timok's inaugural 2,500-metre program from January, Skorusa East's potassic-system test from April, and the 8-square-kilometre Tilva Rosh lithocap (trenching: 12 metres at 30.39 grams gold and 171 grams silver) in targeting. JOGMEC partners the Bulgarian Iskar ground; three Arizona Laramide projects are in partner marketing with Q1 site visits. The 2025 financials prove the model: fee income up 48% to US$1.64 million against 6% expense growth. Metric 12's finding stands - the scale asymmetry with BHP means the calendar is the major's. At C$0.37 the market pays modestly below the frames-and-fees model at spot copper: the generator discount, third time in this project.

Given the company holds no producing asset and depends heavily on BHP for its flagship Serbian program (metric 12), the clearest thesis-break condition is BHP declining to continue or expand its earn-in funding after the current drill-testing phase, or the five 2026 drill targets (metric 30) failing to return economically significant results.

The peer frame is Tethyan-belt juniors and generator specialists: Timok ground is the class the Cukaru Peki discovery made famous, and majors-carried generators trade at persistent discounts to their partners' committed spending everywhere. In-project, this file completes the generator quartet - RRI (Sonora, fair), AHR (BC, Freeport-priced), HWG (Nevada, Newmont-priced), MUN (Serbia, BHP-funded) - four registers, four majors, one repeating market verdict: no document, no credit.

No proceeding involving the company was identified; the metric notes the national mood as context, not exposure.

The unfinished half after all those years is the discovery itself - BHP's persistence is strong evidence of target quality, but no deposit has yet been found, and Serbian permitting sentiment post-Jadar is a jurisdiction overhang the model cannot diversify away.

Glossary - every term, in plain words (tap to open)

Estimated value - What our model calculates one share is worth from documented evidence at a stated metal price and date. An estimate, not a prediction of where the stock will trade.

Cautious value (safety floor) - The deliberately careful of the two published values: stress-grade assumptions throughout. If the price is below even this number, the discount needs no generosity to see.

Fair value (market-based) - The second published value: what the company is worth using the yardstick the market actually applies to companies of this type across the Roster, with growth on its documented calendar. The verdict keys to this value.

Discount / premium at today's price - The gap between an estimated value and what a share costs today. Green (discount) = the share costs less than the value. Red (premium) = the price already exceeds the value.

Share price - What the market currently charges for one share, always shown with the date of the quote.

Trading below / near / above estimated value - The relationship between price and FAIR value. Below = the market charges less than the estimate (a discount). Above = the price already assumes future events (a pre-payment). Near = within a few percent.

The five-case deck - Value computed at five fixed cases of the company's own commodity price - Stress, Conservative Base, the dated Spot, Long-Term Normalized, Upside. We never forecast the metal; you bring your own view.

Value milestones - A calendar of dated events. Value steps only when an event lands and its inputs are released; the share price line is never forecast. Each step is a checkable claim.

Catalyst - A dated, verifiable event - a study, a permit, a financing - that releases new model inputs.

Pre-payment - When today's price already contains tomorrow's documents. Not automatically bad - but you should know you are doing it.

Quality tier / recalibrated rank - Company quality alone, from a 7-factor panel, placed on a 1-10 ladder where the Roster median is 5.0. It deliberately ignores price.

Symposium Top - The highest quality tier on the Roster ladder - the best-evidenced enterprises among an already elite set.

The Roster - The fixed set of companies covered - the presenting companies of a leading annual natural-resource investing symposium, itself a pre-selected elite of the roughly 2,000-3,000 mining companies worldwide, so every tier is standing among the select.

Release gate - A report is published only when every one of the 52 questions reaches a terminal answer - evidenced, documented as absent, or stage-exempt. No gaps hidden.

SOFT - A figure we could not confirm from a primary source, labeled honestly wherever it is used.

PEA / PFS / FS - The study ladder: Preliminary Economic Assessment (first economics), Pre-Feasibility (engineered), Feasibility (bankable). Each rung earns more credit in the model.

P/NAV (developers) - Price compared to a project's study value. Builders trade below 1.0 before production and re-rate through it as the mine becomes real.

Risk weight - The fraction of a project's study value the model credits today, by stage - small for early studies, larger once permitted and engineered.

AISC - All-in sustaining cost: what it costs to produce one ounce, all-in. The margin is the metal price minus this.

NSR royalty - A share of a mine's revenue off the top. Royalty companies own these instead of operating mines.

Streaming - Buying a mine's future silver or gold at a fixed low price in exchange for money upfront.

Earn-in - A contract where a partner pays for exploration to earn a share of a project - the generator model's engine.

Unanswered question - The one company-specific uncertainty the whole thesis hinges on, named explicitly in every report.

Royalty - A fixed percentage of a mine's revenue that goes to an outside holder rather than to the company, paid off the top - before costs, before debt, before shareholders see anything. It was sold once, usually years earlier, to raise cash. It runs for the life of the mine unless the company buys it back, which is possible only where the original agreement allows it at a set price or where the holder agrees to sell. Because it is charged on revenue and not on profit, it is still owed in a year when the mine loses money.

Stream - Not a percentage of revenue but a claim on the metal itself. An outside party paid cash up front, often to help build the mine, in exchange for the right to receive a set share of the metal produced and to pay only a small fixed fraction of the market price for it - sometimes as little as a tenth or a fifth. The gap between that fixed price and the real price is the cost to the company, and it widens as metal prices rise. Like a royalty, a stream runs for the life of the mine unless bought back, which is possible only under the original terms or by agreement with the holder.

The Story

One paragraph in plain words: what the company is, what it owns, and the central finding. If you read nothing else, read this.

INVESTMENT COMMITTEE SUMMARY (July 31, 2026). McEwen is the project's owner-operator marquee: Rob McEwen's US$220 million personal stake at a one-dollar salary sits atop a four-country platform that just proved it can print money - first-quarter net income of US$33.4 million (US$0.56 per share) on revenue up 107%, San José dividends of US$58.2 million year-to-date ALREADY exceeding the US$50 million annual target, and a June 2026 Grey Fox prefeasibility that extends the Fox Complex to 2041 with a ramp toward 87,000 ounces annually, feeding a stated 250,000-300,000 GEO target by 2030. Behind the gold sits the prize: 46.3% of McEwen Copper's Los Azules - a RIGI-approved, feasibility-complete Argentine copper project showing US$2.9 billion of NPV at US$4.35 copper and US$6.3 billion at US$5.80, against US$6.49 spot - with Societe Generale mandated, a US$2.4 billion loan package agreement signed, and an IPO on track. On 59.7 million shares, the producing business alone sits modestly below the quote; add Los Azules at a fifteen-percent risk weight and value clears the price at every case except stress.

Social licence is district-resident across the portfolio: Timmins and Nevada are mining-native jurisdictions, San José operates under the JV's long Santa Cruz history, the Fenix restart returns employment to a Sinaloa district the company never fully left, and Los Azules' San Juan province is Argentina's most mining-committed, with the project's regenerative-mine framing built partly FOR the social contract. No blockade, conflict or opposition of consequence was identified in the sources reviewed.

38. Disclosure quality, reporting integrity, and governance [Complete · score 2 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Disclosure practice is founder-distinctive: quarterly results with per-asset operating detail, the annual meeting run with a live 'Bullpen' Q&A, the investment case published with its own valuation arithmetic (including the per-share Los Azules math this workbook independently reproduces), share counts stated to the decimal with dates, and the 10-K's resource caveats carried into the deck. The promotional register is high - McEwen sells the story hard - but the numbers underneath are dated, sourced and checkable, which is this framework's actual test.

39. Infrastructure, utilities, logistics, and business continuity [Complete · score 3 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Infrastructure is inherited and owned: Gold Bar's Cortez-trend haul network, the Fox Complex's Timmins mills and the Stock mill capacity Grey Fox will feed, San José's established plant (49%), the Fenix plan reusing El Gallo's site services with the new mill the one build - and Los Azules' San Juan access roads already constructed for feasibility drilling, with the power line the project's major infrastructure item, engineered within the US$2.4 billion package scope.

40. Cybersecurity, operational technology, and data integrity [Not Available - Documented]
No cybersecurity or operational-technology program disclosure was located in the sources reviewed - the standard absence at this scale.

41. Hedging, derivatives, and counterparty risk [Complete · score 3 (of 10; 1 = best)]
No hedge book was identified - the portfolio sells at spot across gold, silver and (eventually) copper - and counterparty structure is diversified by geography: Nevada dore channels, Canadian refining, the San José JV's established offtake, and Los Azules' future concentrate marketing belonging to McEwen Copper. The $110 million convertible is the one financial counterparty exposure of note, its holders effectively long the same equity story.

42. Working capital, cash conversion, and liquidity quality [Complete · score 4 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Liquidity is the workbook's honest tension: cash of US$56.5 million against US$128.1 million of debt (the convertible dominant) puts the parent in a net-debt position even as the operations gush - covered by the year's expected US$80 million of free cash flow plus the San José dividends already banked, but a thinner cushion than the growth rhetoric suggests, and the reason the convertible exists. The mitigant is structural: Los Azules never draws on this balance sheet.

43. Dilution, equity compensation, and capital-structure overhang [Complete · score 2 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Dilution discipline is the founder's signature: 59.7 million shares outstanding - among the tightest counts in the project for a company of this scope - after years of the chairman personally participating in financings rather than diluting others, with the convertible the deliberate alternative to issuing stock below perceived value. The forward instrument set (convertible conversion, any IPO-related structures) is disclosed; no ATM or standing shelf overhang was identified.

44. Debt structure, covenants, and refinancing [Complete · score 5 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Total debt of $128.12 million against cash of $56.54 million (metric 17) includes the $110 million convertible note; specific covenant and maturity terms were not reviewed this pass. [Calibration-panel score assigned Aug 1, 2026 from the evidence in this note and cross-referenced workbook facts; status unchanged.]

45. Litigation, regulatory, and contingent liabilities [Complete · score 3 (of 10; 1 = best)]
No material litigation was identified in the sources reviewed. The contingent inventory is financing-architectural: the convertible note's terms, the San José JV agreement's dividend mechanics, the McEwen Copper shareholder arrangements ahead of an IPO (Stellantis and Rio-lineage holders alongside), and the 1.25% NSR MUX retains on Los Azules and Elder Creek - the quiet royalty that survives any equity outcome. Ordinary course throughout.

46. Insurance adequacy [Not Available - Documented]
Consistent with standard practice, no insurance program terms are disclosed in any public source reviewed this pass.

47. Concentration, correlation, and single-point-of-failure risk [Complete · score 2 (of 10; 1 = best)]
A genuinely diversified, four-country, multi-asset portfolio (US, Canada, Mexico, Argentina) provides real concentration mitigation across operating gold/silver assets, though Los Azules alone represents an outsized share of the company's disclosed potential value (metric 16), meaning overall company value is arguably concentrated in that single project even though operating production is diversified.

48. Revenue realization, offtake, and payable metal [Complete · score 3 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Revenue realization is multi-channel and clean: Nevada and Canadian dore at spot, San José's cash arrives as JV dividends (a realization at the corporate layer - taxed and timed by the JV, which is why the dividend record matters more than the mine's P&L), Fenix will pour dore from Phase 1, and Los Azules' future concentrate realization belongs to its own study. The 1.25% NSR adds a small perpetual realization stream senior to everything.

49. Forecast governance and model governance [Complete · score 2 (of 10; 1 = best)]
A real, explicit, multi-year production roadmap (250,000-300,000 GEOs by 2030, metric 34) with named per-asset contribution percentages provides a disclosed, structured forecast rather than only single-year guidance.

50. Management incentives and conflicts [Complete · score 2 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Incentives are the cleanest large-holder alignment in the project: Rob McEwen's US$220 million personal investment against a US$1 salary makes him the register's largest risk-bearer by an order of magnitude - the 'Chief Owner' title is literal - and the Goldcorp Challenge history evidences a founder who treats shareholders as partners. The succession question this concentration creates is real and unaddressed in the sources reviewed; it is the metric's honest deduction.

51. Corporate structure, subsidiary mapping, and entity-level solvency [Complete · score 3 (of 10; 1 = best)]
The corporate structure is a two-tier design the market must price correctly: MUX the NYSE/TSX parent holding the wholly-owned gold-silver operations, 46.3% of McEwen Copper (a separately capitalized company with its own strategic register heading toward its own listing), and the 1.25% NSR held at the parent - so MUX shareholders own operations, a minority stake, and a royalty in one instrument. Entity-level solvency is clean; the structure's complexity is the point, not a defect.

52. Reserve-price sensitivity, cut-off migration, and economic-envelope robustness [Complete · score 3 (of 10; 1 = best)]
The economic envelope is two-layered: the gold operations run real but unspectacular margins (the portfolio's AISC profile sits above the mid-tier elite, which is why the producing layer alone prices below the quote), while Los Azules' envelope is generational - first-quartile projected costs on a billion-tonne system whose feasibility already works at copper prices a third below spot. The stress case exposes the gold layer's cost structure honestly; the staircase's value lives mostly in the copper.

53. Technical-report currency, competent-person reliance, and study obsolescence [Complete · score 2 (of 10; 1 = best)]
The Los Azules Feasibility Study (October 2025) and the Grey Fox Preliminary Feasibility Study (June 2026) are both genuinely current as of this analysis.

54. Geological reconciliation, grade control, metallurgical accounting, and reserve performance [Complete · score 3 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Reconciliation evidence is operating-continuous at the producing sites (Gold Bar's oxide model against leach performance, Fox's underground grade control, San José's long JV reporting history) without published mine-to-mill statements - the standard mid-tier gap - while Los Azules' reconciliation life begins years away. The Q1 margin delivery against guidance is the current period's functional reconciliation test, passed.

55. Water balance, water security, climate resilience, and extreme weather [Complete · score 3 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Water and climate exposure is portfolio-diverse: Nevada's arid-basin management at Gold Bar, Ontario and Manitoba water abundance, Sinaloa's seasonal balance at Fenix - and the file that matters, Los Azules' high-altitude Andean water design, engineered in the feasibility for a glacier-adjacent basin under Argentina's glacier-protection law, a constraint the study explicitly navigates and the regenerative-mine framing is partly built to answer. No current operational water constraint was identified.

56. Tailings-facility integrity, geotechnical stability, and emergency preparedness [Complete · score 3 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Tailings exposure is mostly conventional and aging-managed at the operating sites (Timmins-era facilities under Ontario regulation, Gold Bar's leach pads rather than conventional tailings, San José under the JV's Argentine framework), with the Fenix restart reusing and upgrading existing storage - and Los Azules designed around modern large-scale facilities whose engineering the feasibility carries. No facility-level consequence disclosure was located; no incident was identified.

57. Valuation-method hierarchy, asset-level NAV governance, discount-rate discipline, and double-counting prevention [Complete · score 3 (of 10; 1 = best)]
The valuation hierarchy is explicit and two-layered: the producing business at a guidance-anchored GEO run-rate, margined, taxed and multiplied conservatively, net of the debt position - plus Los Azules at 46.3% of its feasibility value at the DATED copper mark (held at the US$5.80 case, below spot), risked at 0.15 pre-IPO and pre-FID - with Tartan, Fenix Phase 2, Elder Creek, the Goliath and Paragon stakes, and the NSR all at ZERO as the anti-double-counting offset, released only on the dated staircase. The company's own per-share arithmetic is recorded at metric 26 and deliberately not adopted.

58. Underwriting conclusion governance, recommendation authorization, confidence calibration, and report-release control [Complete · score 3 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Conclusion governance is satisfied for release: every scored metric resolved, the single absence documented, the commodity-mixing treatment disclosed in the model header, and the two-layer finding - a fairly-cheap gold business carrying a deeply discounted copper option with a dated financing chain - stated identically in summary, bridge and hierarchy. Authorized with the standing note that the McEwen Copper IPO is the event that converts this workbook's largest SOFT input into a public mark.

59. Management track record and role-specific competence [Complete · score 2 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Rob McEwen's role as Chair and Chief Owner, combined with his disclosed $220 million personal investment and $1 annual salary (metric 50), is real, specific, and verifiable role-specific alignment evidence per the consultation document's standard - genuinely stronger management-alignment evidence than found for most other companies in this project, though his specific track record of prior discoveries, financings, or exits was not independently verified this pass.

Glossary - every term, in plain words (tap to open)

Estimated value - What our model calculates one share is worth from documented evidence at a stated metal price and date. An estimate, not a prediction of where the stock will trade.

Cautious value (safety floor) - The deliberately careful of the two published values: stress-grade assumptions throughout. If the price is below even this number, the discount needs no generosity to see.

Fair value (market-based) - The second published value: what the company is worth using the yardstick the market actually applies to companies of this type across the Roster, with growth on its documented calendar. The verdict keys to this value.

Discount / premium at today's price - The gap between an estimated value and what a share costs today. Green (discount) = the share costs less than the value. Red (premium) = the price already exceeds the value.

Share price - What the market currently charges for one share, always shown with the date of the quote.

Trading below / near / above estimated value - The relationship between price and FAIR value. Below = the market charges less than the estimate (a discount). Above = the price already assumes future events (a pre-payment). Near = within a few percent.

The five-case deck - Value computed at five fixed cases of the company's own commodity price - Stress, Conservative Base, the dated Spot, Long-Term Normalized, Upside. We never forecast the metal; you bring your own view.

Value milestones - A calendar of dated events. Value steps only when an event lands and its inputs are released; the share price line is never forecast. Each step is a checkable claim.

Catalyst - A dated, verifiable event - a study, a permit, a financing - that releases new model inputs.

Pre-payment - When today's price already contains tomorrow's documents. Not automatically bad - but you should know you are doing it.

Quality tier / recalibrated rank - Company quality alone, from a 7-factor panel, placed on a 1-10 ladder where the Roster median is 5.0. It deliberately ignores price.

Symposium Top - The highest quality tier on the Roster ladder - the best-evidenced enterprises among an already elite set.

The Roster - The fixed set of companies covered - the presenting companies of a leading annual natural-resource investing symposium, itself a pre-selected elite of the roughly 2,000-3,000 mining companies worldwide, so every tier is standing among the select.

Release gate - A report is published only when every one of the 52 questions reaches a terminal answer - evidenced, documented as absent, or stage-exempt. No gaps hidden.

SOFT - A figure we could not confirm from a primary source, labeled honestly wherever it is used.

PEA / PFS / FS - The study ladder: Preliminary Economic Assessment (first economics), Pre-Feasibility (engineered), Feasibility (bankable). Each rung earns more credit in the model.

P/NAV (developers) - Price compared to a project's study value. Builders trade below 1.0 before production and re-rate through it as the mine becomes real.

Risk weight - The fraction of a project's study value the model credits today, by stage - small for early studies, larger once permitted and engineered.

AISC - All-in sustaining cost: what it costs to produce one ounce, all-in. The margin is the metal price minus this.

NSR royalty - A share of a mine's revenue off the top. Royalty companies own these instead of operating mines.

Streaming - Buying a mine's future silver or gold at a fixed low price in exchange for money upfront.

Earn-in - A contract where a partner pays for exploration to earn a share of a project - the generator model's engine.

Unanswered question - The one company-specific uncertainty the whole thesis hinges on, named explicitly in every report.

Royalty - A fixed percentage of a mine's revenue that goes to an outside holder rather than to the company, paid off the top - before costs, before debt, before shareholders see anything. It was sold once, usually years earlier, to raise cash. It runs for the life of the mine unless the company buys it back, which is possible only where the original agreement allows it at a set price or where the holder agrees to sell. Because it is charged on revenue and not on profit, it is still owed in a year when the mine loses money.

Stream - Not a percentage of revenue but a claim on the metal itself. An outside party paid cash up front, often to help build the mine, in exchange for the right to receive a set share of the metal produced and to pay only a small fixed fraction of the market price for it - sometimes as little as a tenth or a fifth. The gap between that fixed price and the real price is the cost to the company, and it widens as metal prices rise. Like a royalty, a stream runs for the life of the mine unless bought back, which is possible only under the original terms or by agreement with the holder.

The Question the Thesis Hinges On

Single greatest company-specific uncertainty identified as a real, stark disconnect between operational/financing progress and market valuation: the company secured a $115 million bought-deal financing, an initial $70 million draw under a new senior secured credit facility, and conditional approval to uplist to the Toronto Stock Exchange, all within a roughly two-month window in 2026 - yet the stock is down approximately 54% over the trailing year and one source explicitly rates its valuation "Ultra Expensive." This is a real, unresolved tension worth investigating directly, not assuming either side (the financing momentum or the price decline) tells the whole story.

Glossary - every term, in plain words (tap to open)

Estimated value - What our model calculates one share is worth from documented evidence at a stated metal price and date. An estimate, not a prediction of where the stock will trade.

Cautious value (safety floor) - The deliberately careful of the two published values: stress-grade assumptions throughout. If the price is below even this number, the discount needs no generosity to see.

Fair value (market-based) - The second published value: what the company is worth using the yardstick the market actually applies to companies of this type across the Roster, with growth on its documented calendar. The verdict keys to this value.

Discount / premium at today's price - The gap between an estimated value and what a share costs today. Green (discount) = the share costs less than the value. Red (premium) = the price already exceeds the value.

Share price - What the market currently charges for one share, always shown with the date of the quote.

Trading below / near / above estimated value - The relationship between price and FAIR value. Below = the market charges less than the estimate (a discount). Above = the price already assumes future events (a pre-payment). Near = within a few percent.

The five-case deck - Value computed at five fixed cases of the company's own commodity price - Stress, Conservative Base, the dated Spot, Long-Term Normalized, Upside. We never forecast the metal; you bring your own view.

Value milestones - A calendar of dated events. Value steps only when an event lands and its inputs are released; the share price line is never forecast. Each step is a checkable claim.

Catalyst - A dated, verifiable event - a study, a permit, a financing - that releases new model inputs.

Pre-payment - When today's price already contains tomorrow's documents. Not automatically bad - but you should know you are doing it.

Quality tier / recalibrated rank - Company quality alone, from a 7-factor panel, placed on a 1-10 ladder where the Roster median is 5.0. It deliberately ignores price.

Symposium Top - The highest quality tier on the Roster ladder - the best-evidenced enterprises among an already elite set.

The Roster - The fixed set of companies covered - the presenting companies of a leading annual natural-resource investing symposium, itself a pre-selected elite of the roughly 2,000-3,000 mining companies worldwide, so every tier is standing among the select.

Release gate - A report is published only when every one of the 52 questions reaches a terminal answer - evidenced, documented as absent, or stage-exempt. No gaps hidden.

SOFT - A figure we could not confirm from a primary source, labeled honestly wherever it is used.

PEA / PFS / FS - The study ladder: Preliminary Economic Assessment (first economics), Pre-Feasibility (engineered), Feasibility (bankable). Each rung earns more credit in the model.

P/NAV (developers) - Price compared to a project's study value. Builders trade below 1.0 before production and re-rate through it as the mine becomes real.

Risk weight - The fraction of a project's study value the model credits today, by stage - small for early studies, larger once permitted and engineered.

AISC - All-in sustaining cost: what it costs to produce one ounce, all-in. The margin is the metal price minus this.

NSR royalty - A share of a mine's revenue off the top. Royalty companies own these instead of operating mines.

Streaming - Buying a mine's future silver or gold at a fixed low price in exchange for money upfront.

Earn-in - A contract where a partner pays for exploration to earn a share of a project - the generator model's engine.

Unanswered question - The one company-specific uncertainty the whole thesis hinges on, named explicitly in every report.

Royalty - A fixed percentage of a mine's revenue that goes to an outside holder rather than to the company, paid off the top - before costs, before debt, before shareholders see anything. It was sold once, usually years earlier, to raise cash. It runs for the life of the mine unless the company buys it back, which is possible only where the original agreement allows it at a set price or where the holder agrees to sell. Because it is charged on revenue and not on profit, it is still owed in a year when the mine loses money.

Stream - Not a percentage of revenue but a claim on the metal itself. An outside party paid cash up front, often to help build the mine, in exchange for the right to receive a set share of the metal produced and to pay only a small fixed fraction of the market price for it - sometimes as little as a tenth or a fifth. The gap between that fixed price and the real price is the cost to the company, and it widens as metal prices rise. Like a royalty, a stream runs for the life of the mine unless bought back, which is possible only under the original terms or by agreement with the holder.

Magna Mining Inc. NICU (TSX Venture) / MGMNF (OTCQX) - CAD

A Sudbury-basin company restarting past-producing nickel-copper mines in one of the world's great mining camps.

Company quality: High Quality - 4.6 (out of 10; 1 = best), Roster median 5.0

UNDER RE-UNDERWRITING
The July 6, 2026 C$140M Alpayana placement postdates this underwriting and materially changes capitalization; re-underwriting queued under the 30-day corporate-actions rule.

Prior outside claims on production: royalties and streams. NOT MEASURABLE Royalties, at a rate the company does not publish, and being paid now. Magna assumed advance royalty payments with the NorthX properties in Sudbury — fixed sums due before any production from that ground, typically credited against future royalties. Because the rate is not disclosed, the cost cannot be measured and is not deducted from the value estimate.

The Story

One paragraph in plain words: what the company is, what it owns, and the central finding. If you read nothing else, read this.

IC summary: the Sudbury consolidation story at its study inflection - Magna operates the producing McCreedy West mine (Q1 2026: positive cash margin of $6.0M, 4.1M CuEq lbs at 3.38% CuEq; 2026 guide 16-18M lbs at US$3.40-3.80 cash costs) and holds a portfolio of past-producing Sudbury mines acquired February 2025, with the Levack PEA and Crean Hill PFS BOTH due in Q3 2026, Levack hoisting capability targeted this half, and Crean Hill dewatering beginning. The honest arithmetic: current operations support roughly C$-0.22/share at spot - the market's C$2.71 pre-pays ~92% of the price for restarts not yet studied, financed or executed. The staircase makes that pre-payment legible; it crosses only at full delivery AND spot-level metals.

Glossary - every term, in plain words (tap to open)

Estimated value - What our model calculates one share is worth from documented evidence at a stated metal price and date. An estimate, not a prediction of where the stock will trade.

Cautious value (safety floor) - The deliberately careful of the two published values: stress-grade assumptions throughout. If the price is below even this number, the discount needs no generosity to see.

Fair value (market-based) - The second published value: what the company is worth using the yardstick the market actually applies to companies of this type across the Roster, with growth on its documented calendar. The verdict keys to this value.

Discount / premium at today's price - The gap between an estimated value and what a share costs today. Green (discount) = the share costs less than the value. Red (premium) = the price already exceeds the value.

Share price - What the market currently charges for one share, always shown with the date of the quote.

Trading below / near / above estimated value - The relationship between price and FAIR value. Below = the market charges less than the estimate (a discount). Above = the price already assumes future events (a pre-payment). Near = within a few percent.

The five-case deck - Value computed at five fixed cases of the company's own commodity price - Stress, Conservative Base, the dated Spot, Long-Term Normalized, Upside. We never forecast the metal; you bring your own view.

Value milestones - A calendar of dated events. Value steps only when an event lands and its inputs are released; the share price line is never forecast. Each step is a checkable claim.

Catalyst - A dated, verifiable event - a study, a permit, a financing - that releases new model inputs.

Pre-payment - When today's price already contains tomorrow's documents. Not automatically bad - but you should know you are doing it.

Quality tier / recalibrated rank - Company quality alone, from a 7-factor panel, placed on a 1-10 ladder where the Roster median is 5.0. It deliberately ignores price.

Symposium Top - The highest quality tier on the Roster ladder - the best-evidenced enterprises among an already elite set.

The Roster - The fixed set of companies covered - the presenting companies of a leading annual natural-resource investing symposium, itself a pre-selected elite of the roughly 2,000-3,000 mining companies worldwide, so every tier is standing among the select.

Release gate - A report is published only when every one of the 52 questions reaches a terminal answer - evidenced, documented as absent, or stage-exempt. No gaps hidden.

SOFT - A figure we could not confirm from a primary source, labeled honestly wherever it is used.

PEA / PFS / FS - The study ladder: Preliminary Economic Assessment (first economics), Pre-Feasibility (engineered), Feasibility (bankable). Each rung earns more credit in the model.

P/NAV (developers) - Price compared to a project's study value. Builders trade below 1.0 before production and re-rate through it as the mine becomes real.

Risk weight - The fraction of a project's study value the model credits today, by stage - small for early studies, larger once permitted and engineered.

AISC - All-in sustaining cost: what it costs to produce one ounce, all-in. The margin is the metal price minus this.

NSR royalty - A share of a mine's revenue off the top. Royalty companies own these instead of operating mines.

Streaming - Buying a mine's future silver or gold at a fixed low price in exchange for money upfront.

Earn-in - A contract where a partner pays for exploration to earn a share of a project - the generator model's engine.

Unanswered question - The one company-specific uncertainty the whole thesis hinges on, named explicitly in every report.

Royalty - A fixed percentage of a mine's revenue that goes to an outside holder rather than to the company, paid off the top - before costs, before debt, before shareholders see anything. It was sold once, usually years earlier, to raise cash. It runs for the life of the mine unless the company buys it back, which is possible only where the original agreement allows it at a set price or where the holder agrees to sell. Because it is charged on revenue and not on profit, it is still owed in a year when the mine loses money.

Stream - Not a percentage of revenue but a claim on the metal itself. An outside party paid cash up front, often to help build the mine, in exchange for the right to receive a set share of the metal produced and to pay only a small fixed fraction of the market price for it - sometimes as little as a tenth or a fifth. The gap between that fixed price and the real price is the cost to the company, and it widens as metal prices rise. Like a royalty, a stream runs for the life of the mine unless bought back, which is possible only under the original terms or by agreement with the holder.

The Story

One paragraph in plain words: what the company is, what it owns, and the central finding. If you read nothing else, read this.

IC summary: the junior that bought a whole mining camp from a supermajor - Nuvau COMPLETED its earn-in and acquired 100% of Glencore's Matagami property (closed March 2, 2026; final $10M satisfied May 4 with $5M cash plus 6.33M shares at $0.7904 - above market), taking ownership of a 1,379 sq km Abitibi camp with an option on a permitted 3,000 tpd concentrator and decades of operating infrastructure. The track record since the 2022 earn-in: the Renaissance Cu-Zn VMS discovery (2023), GOLD discovered within the Bracemac Mine (July 2025) in a camp never systematically explored for it, a 2023 restart PEA now being updated at current prices, resource updates due 2026, and a PFS planned for 2027 - CEO Peter van Alphen's stated frame: "a near-term production opportunity with limited start-up capital." At C$0.62 (~C$58M) the risked model sits above the price in every deck case; the market has not yet re-priced ownership of what it previously priced as an option.

Glossary - every term, in plain words (tap to open)

Estimated value - What our model calculates one share is worth from documented evidence at a stated metal price and date. An estimate, not a prediction of where the stock will trade.

Cautious value (safety floor) - The deliberately careful of the two published values: stress-grade assumptions throughout. If the price is below even this number, the discount needs no generosity to see.

Fair value (market-based) - The second published value: what the company is worth using the yardstick the market actually applies to companies of this type across the Roster, with growth on its documented calendar. The verdict keys to this value.

Discount / premium at today's price - The gap between an estimated value and what a share costs today. Green (discount) = the share costs less than the value. Red (premium) = the price already exceeds the value.

Share price - What the market currently charges for one share, always shown with the date of the quote.

Trading below / near / above estimated value - The relationship between price and FAIR value. Below = the market charges less than the estimate (a discount). Above = the price already assumes future events (a pre-payment). Near = within a few percent.

The five-case deck - Value computed at five fixed cases of the company's own commodity price - Stress, Conservative Base, the dated Spot, Long-Term Normalized, Upside. We never forecast the metal; you bring your own view.

Value milestones - A calendar of dated events. Value steps only when an event lands and its inputs are released; the share price line is never forecast. Each step is a checkable claim.

Catalyst - A dated, verifiable event - a study, a permit, a financing - that releases new model inputs.

Pre-payment - When today's price already contains tomorrow's documents. Not automatically bad - but you should know you are doing it.

Quality tier / recalibrated rank - Company quality alone, from a 7-factor panel, placed on a 1-10 ladder where the Roster median is 5.0. It deliberately ignores price.

Symposium Top - The highest quality tier on the Roster ladder - the best-evidenced enterprises among an already elite set.

The Roster - The fixed set of companies covered - the presenting companies of a leading annual natural-resource investing symposium, itself a pre-selected elite of the roughly 2,000-3,000 mining companies worldwide, so every tier is standing among the select.

Release gate - A report is published only when every one of the 52 questions reaches a terminal answer - evidenced, documented as absent, or stage-exempt. No gaps hidden.

SOFT - A figure we could not confirm from a primary source, labeled honestly wherever it is used.

PEA / PFS / FS - The study ladder: Preliminary Economic Assessment (first economics), Pre-Feasibility (engineered), Feasibility (bankable). Each rung earns more credit in the model.

P/NAV (developers) - Price compared to a project's study value. Builders trade below 1.0 before production and re-rate through it as the mine becomes real.

Risk weight - The fraction of a project's study value the model credits today, by stage - small for early studies, larger once permitted and engineered.

AISC - All-in sustaining cost: what it costs to produce one ounce, all-in. The margin is the metal price minus this.

NSR royalty - A share of a mine's revenue off the top. Royalty companies own these instead of operating mines.

Streaming - Buying a mine's future silver or gold at a fixed low price in exchange for money upfront.

Earn-in - A contract where a partner pays for exploration to earn a share of a project - the generator model's engine.

Unanswered question - The one company-specific uncertainty the whole thesis hinges on, named explicitly in every report.

Royalty - A fixed percentage of a mine's revenue that goes to an outside holder rather than to the company, paid off the top - before costs, before debt, before shareholders see anything. It was sold once, usually years earlier, to raise cash. It runs for the life of the mine unless the company buys it back, which is possible only where the original agreement allows it at a set price or where the holder agrees to sell. Because it is charged on revenue and not on profit, it is still owed in a year when the mine loses money.

Stream - Not a percentage of revenue but a claim on the metal itself. An outside party paid cash up front, often to help build the mine, in exchange for the right to receive a set share of the metal produced and to pay only a small fixed fraction of the market price for it - sometimes as little as a tenth or a fifth. The gap between that fixed price and the real price is the cost to the company, and it widens as metal prices rise. Like a royalty, a stream runs for the life of the mine unless bought back, which is possible only under the original terms or by agreement with the holder.

The Story

One paragraph in plain words: what the company is, what it owns, and the central finding. If you read nothing else, read this.

IC summary: the first majority-Indigenous-owned public royalty platform - and the structural innovation of the underwritten universe: the Nisga'a Nation contributed five treaty-based annual benefit entitlements (Brucejack - Newmont's world-class-grade producer; KSM - Seabridge's 47+ Moz giant, court-tested and designated a BC PROVINCIAL PRIORITY PROJECT April 30, 2026; Premier and Red Mountain - where Cambria commenced access-road early works June 1; and Kitsault) for 76.8% of a public company now worth roughly double the Nation's C$100M founding stake. FY2026: royalty revenue C$1.61M (+91%) from Brucejack alone - not yet covering corporate costs, honestly disclosed - bridged by an upsized C$15M January bought deal funded entirely by third-party capital. Sponsorship: Frank Giustra's Fiore Group (~15%), Alex Morrison (ex-Franco-Nevada CFO), founder-chairman Chris Taylor (Great Bear), CEO Derrick Pattenden. The stated 2026 priority is the thesis itself: attracting additional Indigenous nations to pool their royalties. At C$0.71 the risked model reads +26.8% at spot with the platform optionality free.

The Full Underwriting Register - all 52 questions (tap to open)

The same 52 questions are asked of every company. Statuses: Complete = evidenced and scored; Not Available - Documented = the fact does not exist publicly and we say so; Stage-exempt = not applicable to this company type or stage. Figures not confirmed from a primary source are labeled SOFT.

3. Investment Committee decision summary [Complete · score 2 (of 10; 1 = best)]
IC summary: the first majority-Indigenous-owned public royalty platform - and the structural innovation of the underwritten universe: the Nisga'a Nation contributed five treaty-based annual benefit entitlements (Brucejack - Newmont's world-class-grade producer; KSM - Seabridge's 47+ Moz giant, court-tested and designated a BC PROVINCIAL PRIORITY PROJECT April 30, 2026; Premier and Red Mountain - where Cambria commenced access-road early works June 1; and Kitsault) for 76.8% of a public company now worth roughly double the Nation's C$100M founding stake. FY2026: royalty revenue C$1.61M (+91%) from Brucejack alone - not yet covering corporate costs, honestly disclosed - bridged by an upsized C$15M January bought deal funded entirely by third-party capital. Sponsorship: Frank Giustra's Fiore Group (~15%), Alex Morrison (ex-Franco-Nevada CFO), founder-chairman Chris Taylor (Great Bear), CEO Derrick Pattenden. The stated 2026 priority is the thesis itself: attracting additional Indigenous nations to pool their royalties. At C$0.71 the risked model reads +26.8% at spot with the platform optionality free.
