Glossary - every term, in plain words (tap to open)

Estimated value - What our model calculates one share is worth from documented evidence at a stated metal price and date. An estimate, not a prediction of where the stock will trade.

Cautious value (safety floor) - The deliberately careful of the two published values: stress-grade assumptions throughout. If the price is below even this number, the discount needs no generosity to see.

Fair value (market-based) - The second published value: what the company is worth using the yardstick the market actually applies to companies of this type across the Roster, with growth on its documented calendar. The verdict keys to this value.

Discount / premium at today's price - The gap between an estimated value and what a share costs today. Green (discount) = the share costs less than the value. Red (premium) = the price already exceeds the value.

Share price - What the market currently charges for one share, always shown with the date of the quote.

Trading below / near / above estimated value - The relationship between price and FAIR value. Below = the market charges less than the estimate (a discount). Above = the price already assumes future events (a pre-payment). Near = within a few percent.

The five-case deck - Value computed at five fixed cases of the company's own commodity price - Stress, Conservative Base, the dated Spot, Long-Term Normalized, Upside. We never forecast the metal; you bring your own view.

Value milestones - A calendar of dated events. Value steps only when an event lands and its inputs are released; the share price line is never forecast. Each step is a checkable claim.

Catalyst - A dated, verifiable event - a study, a permit, a financing - that releases new model inputs.

Pre-payment - When today's price already contains tomorrow's documents. Not automatically bad - but you should know you are doing it.

Quality tier / recalibrated rank - Company quality alone, from a 7-factor panel, placed on a 1-10 ladder where the Roster median is 5.0. It deliberately ignores price.

Symposium Top - The highest quality tier on the Roster ladder - the best-evidenced enterprises among an already elite set.

The Roster - The fixed set of companies covered - the presenting companies of a leading annual natural-resource investing symposium, itself a pre-selected elite of the roughly 2,000-3,000 mining companies worldwide, so every tier is standing among the select.

Release gate - A report is published only when every one of the 52 questions reaches a terminal answer - evidenced, documented as absent, or stage-exempt. No gaps hidden.

SOFT - A figure we could not confirm from a primary source, labeled honestly wherever it is used.

PEA / PFS / FS - The study ladder: Preliminary Economic Assessment (first economics), Pre-Feasibility (engineered), Feasibility (bankable). Each rung earns more credit in the model.

P/NAV (developers) - Price compared to a project's study value. Builders trade below 1.0 before production and re-rate through it as the mine becomes real.

Risk weight - The fraction of a project's study value the model credits today, by stage - small for early studies, larger once permitted and engineered.

AISC - All-in sustaining cost: what it costs to produce one ounce, all-in. The margin is the metal price minus this.

NSR royalty - A share of a mine's revenue off the top. Royalty companies own these instead of operating mines.

Streaming - Buying a mine's future silver or gold at a fixed low price in exchange for money upfront.

Earn-in - A contract where a partner pays for exploration to earn a share of a project - the generator model's engine.

Unanswered question - The one company-specific uncertainty the whole thesis hinges on, named explicitly in every report.

Royalty - A fixed percentage of a mine's revenue that goes to an outside holder rather than to the company, paid off the top - before costs, before debt, before shareholders see anything. It was sold once, usually years earlier, to raise cash. It runs for the life of the mine unless the company buys it back, which is possible only where the original agreement allows it at a set price or where the holder agrees to sell. Because it is charged on revenue and not on profit, it is still owed in a year when the mine loses money.

Stream - Not a percentage of revenue but a claim on the metal itself. An outside party paid cash up front, often to help build the mine, in exchange for the right to receive a set share of the metal produced and to pay only a small fixed fraction of the market price for it - sometimes as little as a tenth or a fifth. The gap between that fixed price and the real price is the cost to the company, and it widens as metal prices rise. Like a royalty, a stream runs for the life of the mine unless bought back, which is possible only under the original terms or by agreement with the holder.

Prior outside claims on production: royalties and streams. LIGHT (1.34% of bad-year margin) A royalty. Claimowners under the Didipio agreement hold 2% of that mine's revenue alongside a free-carried 8% interest. Didipio is about a fifth of company revenue, so the claim is roughly 0.4% at company level and about 1% of profit in a low-price year. Haile carries no royalties, and New Zealand state royalties are a tax.

Connected on the Roster. An event at this company travels only along declared links, never sector-wide. These are the links we carry:

The Story

One paragraph in plain words: what the company is, what it owns, and the central finding. If you read nothing else, read this.

IC summary: a debt-free intermediate producer entering its growth sweet spot - four mines across the US (Haile), New Zealand (Macraes, Waihi) and the Philippines (80% Didipio), 2025 guidance achieved with record net profit, record EPS and record free cash flow ($543M, a 15% yield), net cash $477M, 2026 guiding production +12% to 520,000-590,000 oz at AISC down 7% to $1,750-1,900, the fully permitted Waihi North Project (1.2 Moz reserves, the highest-grade undeveloped project in its class) now in portal development, an NYSE listing achieved April 7, 2026, a tripled dividend and up to $350M in buybacks. Glossary - every term, in plain words (tap to open)

Estimated value - What our model calculates one share is worth from documented evidence at a stated metal price and date. An estimate, not a prediction of where the stock will trade.

Cautious value (safety floor) - The deliberately careful of the two published values: stress-grade assumptions throughout. If the price is below even this number, the discount needs no generosity to see.

Fair value (market-based) - The second published value: what the company is worth using the yardstick the market actually applies to companies of this type across the Roster, with growth on its documented calendar. The verdict keys to this value.

Discount / premium at today's price - The gap between an estimated value and what a share costs today. Green (discount) = the share costs less than the value. Red (premium) = the price already exceeds the value.

Share price - What the market currently charges for one share, always shown with the date of the quote.

Trading below / near / above estimated value - The relationship between price and FAIR value. Below = the market charges less than the estimate (a discount). Above = the price already assumes future events (a pre-payment). Near = within a few percent.

The five-case deck - Value computed at five fixed cases of the company's own commodity price - Stress, Conservative Base, the dated Spot, Long-Term Normalized, Upside. We never forecast the metal; you bring your own view.

Value milestones - A calendar of dated events. Value steps only when an event lands and its inputs are released; the share price line is never forecast. Each step is a checkable claim.

Catalyst - A dated, verifiable event - a study, a permit, a financing - that releases new model inputs.

Pre-payment - When today's price already contains tomorrow's documents. Not automatically bad - but you should know you are doing it.

Quality tier / recalibrated rank - Company quality alone, from a 7-factor panel, placed on a 1-10 ladder where the Roster median is 5.0. It deliberately ignores price.

Symposium Top - The highest quality tier on the Roster ladder - the best-evidenced enterprises among an already elite set.

The Roster - The fixed set of companies covered - the presenting companies of a leading annual natural-resource investing symposium, itself a pre-selected elite of the roughly 2,000-3,000 mining companies worldwide, so every tier is standing among the select.

Release gate - A report is published only when every one of the 52 questions reaches a terminal answer - evidenced, documented as absent, or stage-exempt. No gaps hidden.

SOFT - A figure we could not confirm from a primary source, labeled honestly wherever it is used.

PEA / PFS / FS - The study ladder: Preliminary Economic Assessment (first economics), Pre-Feasibility (engineered), Feasibility (bankable). Each rung earns more credit in the model.

P/NAV (developers) - Price compared to a project's study value. Builders trade below 1.0 before production and re-rate through it as the mine becomes real.

Risk weight - The fraction of a project's study value the model credits today, by stage - small for early studies, larger once permitted and engineered.

AISC - All-in sustaining cost: what it costs to produce one ounce, all-in. The margin is the metal price minus this.

NSR royalty - A share of a mine's revenue off the top. Royalty companies own these instead of operating mines.

Streaming - Buying a mine's future silver or gold at a fixed low price in exchange for money upfront.

Earn-in - A contract where a partner pays for exploration to earn a share of a project - the generator model's engine.

Unanswered question - The one company-specific uncertainty the whole thesis hinges on, named explicitly in every report.

Royalty - A fixed percentage of a mine's revenue that goes to an outside holder rather than to the company, paid off the top - before costs, before debt, before shareholders see anything. It was sold once, usually years earlier, to raise cash. It runs for the life of the mine unless the company buys it back, which is possible only where the original agreement allows it at a set price or where the holder agrees to sell. Because it is charged on revenue and not on profit, it is still owed in a year when the mine loses money.

Stream - Not a percentage of revenue but a claim on the metal itself. An outside party paid cash up front, often to help build the mine, in exchange for the right to receive a set share of the metal produced and to pay only a small fixed fraction of the market price for it - sometimes as little as a tenth or a fifth. The gap between that fixed price and the real price is the cost to the company, and it widens as metal prices rise. Like a royalty, a stream runs for the life of the mine unless bought back, which is possible only under the original terms or by agreement with the holder.

The Story

One paragraph in plain words: what the company is, what it owns, and the central finding. If you read nothing else, read this.

INVESTMENT COMMITTEE SUMMARY (July 31, 2026). Orogen Royalties is the reborn prospect-generation royalty company: incorporated May 1, 2025 as a subsidiary of Triple Flag Nevada and spun out to shareholders when Triple Flag took the Expanded Silicon royalty, it kept everything else - the cash-flowing 2% net smelter return on First Majestic's producing Ermitano mine plus the surrounding 167 square kilometres, the entire project-generation engine, and the team under Paddy Nicol. The underwriting question is concentration versus optionality: one royalty pays for everything today, while the surrounding ground it covers is being drilled at the operator's expense into what looks like the next two mining fronts of the Santa Elena complex. The market is paying today for that growth arriving; the model says the current royalty alone does not cover the price in ANY of the five gold cases - the upside case lands essentially at the quote (-2.6%) - which makes the Navidad/Winter portal schedule the entire bridge.

Where narrative text carries an older share price, the tables and the refreshed dated close above govern.

A real, specific, and traceable cornerstone royalty: a 2.0% net smelter return royalty on First Majestic Silver Corp.'s Ermitaño Mine, part of the Santa Elena complex in Sonora, Mexico - a real, direct link back to First Majestic Silver, #7 on this list. Orogen estimates over 90% of Santa Elena complex production is attributable to its royalty interest, and 2026 Ermitaño royalty revenue is guided at $7.1-10.3 million based on First Majestic's own operating guidance for the complex.

Real, current, and dated technical/permitting progress at the flagship royalty asset: an update on permitting for portal construction at Ermitaño was announced June 30, 2026, and more than 7,700 metres of infill drilling was completed in H1 2026 at Navidad's Winter Vein, returning multiple significant gold and silver intercepts (specific grades not confirmed this pass) - real, dated evidence of continued development at underlying assets Orogen holds royalties or interests in.

18. Capital allocation [Complete · score 3 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Capital allocation follows the project-generation playbook with discipline the numbers confirm: no dividend, no buyback, and essentially no treasury spend on drilling, because partners fund it - approximately 44,000 metres of partner-funded drilling completed or under way in the first half of 2026 across seven royalty projects, with 14 programs totalling over 69,000 metres expected for the year, against just $3.4 million of the company's own generative expenditure in all of 2025, of which over $2.5 million was provided by alliance partners. General and administrative expenses were cut 35% year over year in the first quarter. The cancelled March placement belongs here too: management chose not to dilute at C$3-something when the working capital already covered the plan.

19. Run-rate normalization [Complete · score 2 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Real, disclosed, and dual-source evidence that recent growth reflects both price and volume effects: Q1 2026 royalty revenue grew on 519 attributable GEOs (up modestly, 4%, from 497 a year earlier) but at an average realized price of $4,873/oz versus $2,860/oz a year earlier - a real, explicit separation of price appreciation from production volume, among the more transparent disclosures of this kind found in this project.

20. Formal scenario architecture [Complete · score 2 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Five named pricing cases are built on the SCENARIOS sheet on the project's gold deck, which is native rather than translated for this company: the royalty is settled from gold and silver production and the company itself reports attributable gold-equivalent ounces (519 GEOs in Q1 2026 at an average realised US$4,873). The model is a current-state royalty run-rate deliberately - the Ermitano royalty as it pays today, with every growth front on the 167 square kilometres carried at zero and released only on the dated staircase.

21. Valuation-to-action bridge [Complete · score 5 (of 10; 1 = best)]
The bridge from value to action is explicit and runs the same direction in ALL FIVE cases: the current-state royalty value sits below the traded price at stress, base, dated spot and long-term, and even the upside gold case lands marginally below it (-2.6%). That is the market pre-paying the conversion of Navidad/Winter and Luna from drill intercepts into royalty-bearing production - the same pattern as the project's other pre-paid growth stories, and the action turns on the operator's portal-and-decline schedule, not on the gold price.

22. Thesis-break framework [Complete · score 2 (of 10; 1 = best)]
The thesis-break condition is specific and observable: First Majestic's portal construction for Navidad/Winter, permitted in June 2026 and stated to commence in the second half of 2026, failing to break ground by year-end, or the Ermitano-complex resource update failing to convert the Inferred ounces the 7,704 metres of 2026 conversion drilling targeted. A second, slower break: the operator redirecting its expanded Santa Elena mill capacity toward feed sources OFF the royalty ground. Either event de-rates the growth the price already contains, and both are visible in the operator's own quarterly disclosure rather than requiring anything from this company.

Triple Flag itself is also independently named as a peer to several other royalty companies reviewed in this project (e.g. Empress Royalty, #53).

Highlight intercept EWUG-26-089 graded 23.59 g/t gold and 359 g/t silver over 2.49 metres true width. The honest limitation is second-hand custody: the resource is estimated, owned and reported by the operator, and this company's insight into it is the operator's public disclosure - the standard royalty-holder position, priced here rather than ignored.

Glossary - every term, in plain words (tap to open)

Estimated value - What our model calculates one share is worth from documented evidence at a stated metal price and date. An estimate, not a prediction of where the stock will trade.

Cautious value (safety floor) - The deliberately careful of the two published values: stress-grade assumptions throughout. If the price is below even this number, the discount needs no generosity to see.

Fair value (market-based) - The second published value: what the company is worth using the yardstick the market actually applies to companies of this type across the Roster, with growth on its documented calendar. The verdict keys to this value.

Discount / premium at today's price - The gap between an estimated value and what a share costs today. Green (discount) = the share costs less than the value. Red (premium) = the price already exceeds the value.

Share price - What the market currently charges for one share, always shown with the date of the quote.

Trading below / near / above estimated value - The relationship between price and FAIR value. Below = the market charges less than the estimate (a discount). Above = the price already assumes future events (a pre-payment). Near = within a few percent.

The five-case deck - Value computed at five fixed cases of the company's own commodity price - Stress, Conservative Base, the dated Spot, Long-Term Normalized, Upside. We never forecast the metal; you bring your own view.

Value milestones - A calendar of dated events. Value steps only when an event lands and its inputs are released; the share price line is never forecast. Each step is a checkable claim.

Catalyst - A dated, verifiable event - a study, a permit, a financing - that releases new model inputs.

Pre-payment - When today's price already contains tomorrow's documents. Not automatically bad - but you should know you are doing it.

Quality tier / recalibrated rank - Company quality alone, from a 7-factor panel, placed on a 1-10 ladder where the Roster median is 5.0. It deliberately ignores price.

Symposium Top - The highest quality tier on the Roster ladder - the best-evidenced enterprises among an already elite set.

The Roster - The fixed set of companies covered - the presenting companies of a leading annual natural-resource investing symposium, itself a pre-selected elite of the roughly 2,000-3,000 mining companies worldwide, so every tier is standing among the select.

Release gate - A report is published only when every one of the 52 questions reaches a terminal answer - evidenced, documented as absent, or stage-exempt. No gaps hidden.

SOFT - A figure we could not confirm from a primary source, labeled honestly wherever it is used.

PEA / PFS / FS - The study ladder: Preliminary Economic Assessment (first economics), Pre-Feasibility (engineered), Feasibility (bankable). Each rung earns more credit in the model.

P/NAV (developers) - Price compared to a project's study value. Builders trade below 1.0 before production and re-rate through it as the mine becomes real.

Risk weight - The fraction of a project's study value the model credits today, by stage - small for early studies, larger once permitted and engineered.

AISC - All-in sustaining cost: what it costs to produce one ounce, all-in. The margin is the metal price minus this.

NSR royalty - A share of a mine's revenue off the top. Royalty companies own these instead of operating mines.

Streaming - Buying a mine's future silver or gold at a fixed low price in exchange for money upfront.

Earn-in - A contract where a partner pays for exploration to earn a share of a project - the generator model's engine.

Unanswered question - The one company-specific uncertainty the whole thesis hinges on, named explicitly in every report.

Royalty - A fixed percentage of a mine's revenue that goes to an outside holder rather than to the company, paid off the top - before costs, before debt, before shareholders see anything. It was sold once, usually years earlier, to raise cash. It runs for the life of the mine unless the company buys it back, which is possible only where the original agreement allows it at a set price or where the holder agrees to sell. Because it is charged on revenue and not on profit, it is still owed in a year when the mine loses money.

Stream - Not a percentage of revenue but a claim on the metal itself. An outside party paid cash up front, often to help build the mine, in exchange for the right to receive a set share of the metal produced and to pay only a small fixed fraction of the market price for it - sometimes as little as a tenth or a fifth. The gap between that fixed price and the real price is the cost to the company, and it widens as metal prices rise. Like a royalty, a stream runs for the life of the mine unless bought back, which is possible only under the original terms or by agreement with the holder.

10. Acquisition economics [Complete · score 3 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Real, large, and geographically broad 2025-2026 acquisition activity: purchased eight royalties from Gold Fields (a major, named global gold producer); increased its equity stake in the Namdini project; acquired a 1.5% net smelter return royalty on Buenaventura's producing San Gabriel Mine (Peru); added new silver streams and gold royalties across North America, Japan, Ghana, and Peru; and became a new financing partner (alongside Ocean Partners) in Canadian Copper Inc.'s up to $96 million project-development capital package - a real, dense, and unusually well-documented multi-country acquisition pace within a single year.

11. Reserve/resource movement bridge [Not Applicable - Operator's Risk]
As a royalty company, OR Royalties holds no ore reserves of its own; resource/reserve status belongs to each underlying operator.

12. Principal uncertainty [Complete · score 1 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Single greatest company-specific uncertainty identified as sustaining this pace of acquisitive growth (metric 10) without releveraging a balance sheet the company only just became fully debt-free on (metric 17) - a real, disclosed tension between "disciplined pursuit of additional accretive growth opportunities" (the CEO's own words) and preserving the debt-free position achieved for the first time in over a decade.

13. Management guidance credibility [Complete · score 3 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Real, record, and guidance-confirming full-year 2025 results: 80,775 gold equivalent ounces delivered, squarely within the company's own 80,000-88,000 GEO guidance range; record annual revenue from royalties and streams of $277.4 million; record operating cash flow of $245.6 million; and net earnings of $206.1 million - genuine, verified, multi-metric guidance delivery, not a single favorable number.

14. Mine-by-mine operating quality [Complete · score 2 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Real, large-scale portfolio detail: 22 producing assets as of the most recent count, anchored by the cornerstone 3-5% net smelter return royalty on Agnico Eagle Mines' Canadian Malartic Complex - a real, direct link back to Agnico Eagle Mines, #1 on this list, and described by OR Royalties itself as one of the world's largest gold mines.

15. Cost quality [Complete · score 3 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Real, exceptionally high, and consistently-reported cash margins: 96.7% for full-year 2025 (cost of sales excluding depletion of just $9.1 million against $277.4 million of revenue, metric 13), with Q4 2025 alone reaching 97.2% - among the strongest disclosed cash-margin figures found at any royalty company in this project.

16. Development-project underwriting [Complete · score 2 (of 10; 1 = best)]
A real, sizable development-stage pipeline disclosed at the portfolio level: as of a November 2025 count, 25 assets (15 royalties, 9 streams, 1 offtake) sat in the "Development" stage, alongside 150 assets still at "Exploration and evaluation" - real, quantified evidence of a large forward pipeline behind the 22 currently producing assets (metric 14).

17. Balance-sheet resilience [Complete · score 3 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Real, exceptionally strong, and recently-achieved balance-sheet milestone: fully repaid the outstanding balance on its revolving credit facility during 2025, becoming debt-free for the first time in more than ten years, per the CEO's own statement; the $650 million facility (plus a $200 million uncommitted accordion) sat entirely undrawn as of Q3 2025, and cash stood at approximately $142.1 million at year-end 2025, giving an aggregate liquidity profile of approximately $1 billion. Months of cash runway and funding gap to the next milestone were not separately quantified this pass, per the sharpened requirement for this metric.

18. Capital allocation [Complete · score 3 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Real, large, and multi-pronged capital return delivered alongside continued growth (metric 10), not instead of it: $36.7 million (C$50.8 million) of shares repurchased under the Normal Course Issuer Bid in 2025, a renewed NCIB program approved to repurchase up to 9,399,294 shares (about 5% of shares outstanding), and an active Dividend Reinvestment Plan alongside continued dividends - among the most substantial and multi-faceted capital-return programs found at any royalty company in this project.

19. Run-rate normalization [Complete · score 2 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Real, verified evidence that 2025's record results (metric 13) reflect broad-based portfolio strength rather than a single favorable item: growth was explicitly tied to new asset acquisitions (metric 10), continued high cash margins (metric 15), and GEO deliveries landing within a previously-set guidance range - a real, multi-factor, and cross-verified performance picture.

20. Formal scenario architecture [Complete · score 2 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Five named pricing scenarios built on the SCENARIOS sheet (Stress $2,600 / Conservative $3,400 / Spot (Jul 31, 2026) $4,050 / Long-Term Normalized $4,200 / Upside $5,400 per oz gold), each producing a value per share and a dollar-and-percentage gap to the current price, on stated assumptions: 85,000 GEOs (2026 guidance midpoint), ~97% cash margin, $34M corporate costs, 20% tax, a 20x cash-generation multiple, plus securities and net debt per metrics 17 and 44.

21. Valuation-to-action bridge [Complete · score 3 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Explicit bridge: at the Current Spot scenario the model value (~$31-32/share) sits within ~3% of the $31.98 reference price - the stock is pricing its spot-gold run-rate approximately fairly, with the 5-year growth to 120,000-135,000 GEOs by 2030 as the source of further upside; action zones defined as value gap >+20% Buy, -10% to +20% Monitor/Accumulate, <-10% Avoid, placing OR in Monitor/Accumulate on its own model. At the corrected spot the current-state reading is US$25.83 vs the US$31.98 price (-19.2%). The SCENARIOS and CATALYST TIMELINE tables govern wherever any older narrative number differs.

22. Thesis-break framework [Complete · score 2 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Named, checkable break conditions: (1) a setback in Agnico Eagle's Odyssey underground transition at Canadian Malartic - the single royalty that generated $35.9M, 35% of Q1 2026 revenue; (2) a second operator failure of the Eagle Gold type (metric 41) at a top-five cash-flow asset; (3) a sustained gold-price retreat toward the Stress/Conservative scenarios (metric 20), to which the model value is highly sensitive; (4) reinvestment of the ~97% margin into lower-quality assets at premium prices - the classic royalty-model failure mode.

26. Peer-group methodology [Complete · score 2 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Disclosed peer set and criteria: precious-metals royalty/streaming companies with multi-billion-dollar capitalization and GEO-based reporting - Franco-Nevada, Wheaton Precious Metals, Royal Gold, Triple Flag, Sandstorm - with OR positioned as the largest of the intermediates below the three seniors; same set used for the 15-25x multiple range at metric 20.

27. Jurisdiction, fiscal regime, and permitting [Complete · score 2 (of 10; 1 = best)]
A real, explicitly-stated jurisdictional focus: OR Royalties defines its strategy around Tier-1 mining jurisdictions specifically meaning Canada, the United States, and Australia, while its recent acquisitions (metric 10) have also added exposure to Japan, Ghana, and Peru - a real, deliberate core-plus-selective-diversification jurisdictional strategy, not indiscriminate global spread.

28. Environmental liability, reclamation, closure, and tailings [Not Applicable - Operator's Risk]
As a royalty and streaming company with no mining operations of its own, OR Royalties carries no direct reclamation or environmental-liability obligations - those sit with each underlying operator.

29. Reserve/resource quality [Complete · score 2 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Portfolio reserve quality reviewed asset-by-asset from operator disclosures: Canadian Malartic's Odyssey holds 6.0 Moz P&P at 3.14 g/t with 90% reserve replacement and positive reconciliation; Island Gold P&P grew 25% to 5.1 Moz at 10.61 g/t; Eleonore holds 1.6 Moz P&P at 5.05 g/t; CSA 545 kt Cu at 3.4%; the one deterioration is Sasa, whose updated reserve shortens mine life to 2034 (from 2039) on higher cut-off values - a real, disclosed negative captured rather than smoothed over.

30. Exploration effectiveness [Not Applicable - Operator's Risk]
OR Royalties does not conduct its own mineral exploration; portfolio growth comes from acquiring royalty, stream, and offtake interests (metric 10), not discovery, though it does hold 7 royalty options and a large exploration-stage asset count (metric 16) that could convert to producing royalties without Royalties itself drilling.

31. Ownership, royalties, streams, and joint ventures [Complete · score 3 (of 10; 1 = best)]
A real, exceptionally large and long-established royalty portfolio: more than 195 royalties, streams, and similar interests in total, built up from a single producing asset when the company commenced activities in June 2014 - among the largest total interest counts found at any royalty company reviewed in this project, anchored by the Canadian Malartic cornerstone royalty (metric 14).

32. Commodity-price, FX, and inflation assumption governance [Complete · score 2 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Assumption governance is explicit and third-party: 2026 guidance converts deliveries using February 2026 consensus prices at a 73:1 gold/silver ratio; the 5-year outlook uses long-term consensus at 82:1; realized vs average LBMA/LME prices are tabled every quarter (Q1 2026 realized gold $4,853/oz vs $4,873 average); guidance is built from operators' public forecasts with the sourcing hierarchy disclosed.

Tax position quantified: Q1 2026 effective rate 16.1% (statutory 26.5%; differences from non-taxable revenues and share-based compensation), current income taxes of $11.0M in the quarter of which $1.7M paid to foreign jurisdictions, 2025 Canadian taxes of $13.7M paid in Q1, and monthly federal/provincial instalments now required from Q1 2026.

As a royalty company, OR Royalties has no production of its own to deplete or replace; production trends belong to each underlying operator across its 22 producing assets (metric 14).

Operating reliability belongs to the underlying mine and project operators, not OR Royalties directly, though the company's own GEO delivery landing within guidance (metric 13) is a real, indirect signal of underlying-portfolio reliability.

Sought in the Q1 2026 MD&A (Risks and Uncertainties, Financial Instruments, Disclosure Controls sections) and the 2025 management circular: no cybersecurity control-maturity, incident-history, or operational-technology governance detail is disclosed beyond generic risk language - consistent with the AEM precedent for this metric.

No commodity hedging program identified in the Q1 2026 MD&A; the real exposure is counterparty/operator risk, now evidenced concretely: the Eagle Gold royalty default and receivership (a $49.6M impairment in 2024, sale process now in exclusivity with Boroo), the CSA operator transition to Harmony including a one-month shaft-repair halt, and contractual buy-down rights exercised at Cascabel (a $17.5M gold payment received for 50% of the stream) - each documented with dates and amounts.

Real, strong, and quantified cash-conversion evidence: Q3 2025 operating cash flow rose 87% year-over-year to $64.6 million, explicitly enabling full repayment of the remaining credit-facility balance that same quarter (metric 17) - a real, direct, and dated link between cash generation and deleveraging.

Two explicit dilution calculations: (1) instrument overhang - Q1 2026 diluted shares of 188.68M vs basic 187.61M, a potential increase of just 1.07M shares or ~0.6%; (2) trajectory - basic weighted shares rose from 186.2M (Q2 2024) to 187.6M (Q1 2026), +0.75% over seven quarters, now being offset by active buybacks: 322,470 shares cancelled for $12.9M (C$17.7M) in Q1 2026 under an NCIB authorizing up to 9.4M shares, plus a DRIP; equity compensation (options, RSUs, DSUs) is the only meaningful issuance source.

Incentive structure documented from primary filings: equity-linked compensation across share options, restricted and deferred share units and an employee share purchase plan (Q1 2026 settlements generated $9.8M of withholding taxes - material, share-price-linked pay), an annually filed management circular with named director competencies, a majority-independent board (CEO the named non-independent director), and no related-party transactions in the current quarter; per-executive quantum not itemized in this pass but the alignment architecture is verifiable.

A real, long, and well-documented corporate growth history: commenced activities in June 2014 with a single producing asset and has since built the more-than-195-interest portfolio already detailed in full at metric 31 - genuine, verifiable, more-than-a-decade organizational track record.

52. Reserve-price sensitivity, cut-off migration, and economic-envelope robustness [Complete · score 3 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Reserve-price fragility assessed on real portfolio events rather than theory: Sasa's 2026 reserve update (metric 29) shows exactly this mechanism operating - higher cost assumptions raised NSR cut-offs and removed five years of mine life - while Canadian Malartic and Island Gold show the opposite (positive reconciliation, reserve growth), and Alamos' expansion study demonstrates robustness at $4,500/oz; portfolio reserve exposure is therefore diversified across operators with offsetting sensitivities.

Technical-report currency for the underlying mines sits with the mine operators, who prepare and control those reports; the company does not publish or control them.

Geological reconciliation is the responsibility of each underlying mine operator, not OR Royalties directly.

Water balance and climate resilience at underlying mine and project sites are the responsibility of each operator, not OR Royalties directly.

56. Tailings-facility integrity, geotechnical stability, and emergency preparedness [Not Applicable - Operator's Risk]
Tailings-facility integrity at underlying mine sites is the responsibility of each operator, not OR Royalties directly.

57. Valuation-method hierarchy, asset-level NAV governance, discount-rate discipline, and double-counting prevention [Complete · score 3 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Valuation architecture disclosed on the SCENARIOS sheet: primary method is a cash-generation multiple (20x, within the disclosed 15-25x royalty peer range, metric 26) on scenario-priced 2026 GEOs, cross-checked against the 5-year GEO growth outlook; securities and net debt added once each (no double counting with the royalty interests); per the spec's split requirement, at the Current Spot case roughly $4.5/share (~15%) of value above the Long-Term Normalized case is gold-price dependence, with growth execution to 2030 accounting for the upper multiple half. Role-specific track record verified and matched to the task: CEO Jason Attew (appointed January 1, 2024, age 55) brings BMO Global Metals & Mining investment banking, the Goldcorp CFO/EVP-Corporate Development seat through the US$32B Newmont merger, and CEO roles at Gold Standard Ventures (sold to Orla, August 2022) and Liberty Gold - a capital-allocation and M&A record that is precisely the skill a royalty aggregator requires, already evidenced by record 2025 results and a debt-free year-end; bench and board reinforce it: CFO Frederic Ruel (CPA, ex-Canadian Malartic Partnership reporting), plus 2026 director additions Kevin Thomson (ex-Barrick Senior EVP Strategic Matters) and Patrick Godin (ex-New Gold CEO, ex-Pretium COO).

Glossary - every term, in plain words (tap to open)

Estimated value - What our model calculates one share is worth from documented evidence at a stated metal price and date. An estimate, not a prediction of where the stock will trade.

Cautious value (safety floor) - The deliberately careful of the two published values: stress-grade assumptions throughout. If the price is below even this number, the discount needs no generosity to see.

Fair value (market-based) - The second published value: what the company is worth using the yardstick the market actually applies to companies of this type across the Roster, with growth on its documented calendar. The verdict keys to this value.

Discount / premium at today's price - The gap between an estimated value and what a share costs today. Green (discount) = the share costs less than the value. Red (premium) = the price already exceeds the value.

Share price - What the market currently charges for one share, always shown with the date of the quote.

Trading below / near / above estimated value - The relationship between price and FAIR value. Below = the market charges less than the estimate (a discount). Above = the price already assumes future events (a pre-payment). Near = within a few percent.

The five-case deck - Value computed at five fixed cases of the company's own commodity price - Stress, Conservative Base, the dated Spot, Long-Term Normalized, Upside. We never forecast the metal; you bring your own view.

Value milestones - A calendar of dated events. Value steps only when an event lands and its inputs are released; the share price line is never forecast. Each step is a checkable claim.

Catalyst - A dated, verifiable event - a study, a permit, a financing - that releases new model inputs.

Pre-payment - When today's price already contains tomorrow's documents. Not automatically bad - but you should know you are doing it.

Quality tier / recalibrated rank - Company quality alone, from a 7-factor panel, placed on a 1-10 ladder where the Roster median is 5.0. It deliberately ignores price.

Symposium Top - The highest quality tier on the Roster ladder - the best-evidenced enterprises among an already elite set.

The Roster - The fixed set of companies covered - the presenting companies of a leading annual natural-resource investing symposium, itself a pre-selected elite of the roughly 2,000-3,000 mining companies worldwide, so every tier is standing among the select.

Release gate - A report is published only when every one of the 52 questions reaches a terminal answer - evidenced, documented as absent, or stage-exempt. No gaps hidden.

SOFT - A figure we could not confirm from a primary source, labeled honestly wherever it is used.

PEA / PFS / FS - The study ladder: Preliminary Economic Assessment (first economics), Pre-Feasibility (engineered), Feasibility (bankable). Each rung earns more credit in the model.

P/NAV (developers) - Price compared to a project's study value. Builders trade below 1.0 before production and re-rate through it as the mine becomes real.

Risk weight - The fraction of a project's study value the model credits today, by stage - small for early studies, larger once permitted and engineered.

AISC - All-in sustaining cost: what it costs to produce one ounce, all-in. The margin is the metal price minus this.

NSR royalty - A share of a mine's revenue off the top. Royalty companies own these instead of operating mines.

Streaming - Buying a mine's future silver or gold at a fixed low price in exchange for money upfront.

Earn-in - A contract where a partner pays for exploration to earn a share of a project - the generator model's engine.

Unanswered question - The one company-specific uncertainty the whole thesis hinges on, named explicitly in every report.

Royalty - A fixed percentage of a mine's revenue that goes to an outside holder rather than to the company, paid off the top - before costs, before debt, before shareholders see anything. It was sold once, usually years earlier, to raise cash. It runs for the life of the mine unless the company buys it back, which is possible only where the original agreement allows it at a set price or where the holder agrees to sell. Because it is charged on revenue and not on profit, it is still owed in a year when the mine loses money.

Stream - Not a percentage of revenue but a claim on the metal itself. An outside party paid cash up front, often to help build the mine, in exchange for the right to receive a set share of the metal produced and to pay only a small fixed fraction of the market price for it - sometimes as little as a tenth or a fifth. The gap between that fixed price and the real price is the cost to the company, and it widens as metal prices rise. Like a royalty, a stream runs for the life of the mine unless bought back, which is possible only under the original terms or by agreement with the holder.

The Story

One paragraph in plain words: what the company is, what it owns, and the central finding. If you read nothing else, read this.

IC summary: the largest diversified silver-gold producer in the Americas one year after absorbing MAG Silver - Q1 2026 revenue $1.15B (+48.7%), net earnings $456M ($1.08/sh), attributable free cash flow $488M, record cash and short-term investments above $1.8B, silver segment AISC of $6.63/oz on Juanicipio's low-cost ounces and gold byproduct credits, a new framework returning 35-40% of attributable FCF, the La Colorada Skarn advancing as a future 37-year top-tier silver mine, and Escobal - 264.5 Moz of P&P silver - idle in Guatemala with no ILO 169 timeline. At US$43.11, ~37% off its February high, the model reads -27.9% at spot with Escobal as an entirely unpriced option.

Where narrative text carries an older share price, the tables and the refreshed dated close above govern.

Three dates govern this page: the share price is the dated close shown above (2026-07-31); the evidence and estimated values are from this company's last full underwriting (2026-07-31), and change only when the company publishes something - each document's own date is listed under References; a daily event scan watches this company's filings and releases and queues a re-underwriting when one lands.

The Question the Thesis Hinges On

Single greatest company-specific uncertainty identified as the unresolved Escobal mine situation in Guatemala: operations have been suspended since 2017 under a court-ordered Indigenous consultation process (ILO 169) with the Xinka Peoples that remains unresolved after nearly nine years, with no timeline for conclusion, allegations from the Xinka Parliament of company interference in the process, and a documented violent attack against an Indigenous land defender opposed to the mine. This is the single largest, longest-running, most severe social-licence situation identified across every company reviewed in this series - 264.5 million oz of P&P silver reserves remain completely idle.

Glossary - every term, in plain words (tap to open)

Estimated value - What our model calculates one share is worth from documented evidence at a stated metal price and date. An estimate, not a prediction of where the stock will trade.

Cautious value (safety floor) - The deliberately careful of the two published values: stress-grade assumptions throughout. If the price is below even this number, the discount needs no generosity to see.

Fair value (market-based) - The second published value: what the company is worth using the yardstick the market actually applies to companies of this type across the Roster, with growth on its documented calendar. The verdict keys to this value.

Discount / premium at today's price - The gap between an estimated value and what a share costs today. Green (discount) = the share costs less than the value. Red (premium) = the price already exceeds the value.

Share price - What the market currently charges for one share, always shown with the date of the quote.

Trading below / near / above estimated value - The relationship between price and FAIR value. Below = the market charges less than the estimate (a discount). Above = the price already assumes future events (a pre-payment). Near = within a few percent.

The five-case deck - Value computed at five fixed cases of the company's own commodity price - Stress, Conservative Base, the dated Spot, Long-Term Normalized, Upside. We never forecast the metal; you bring your own view.

Value milestones - A calendar of dated events. Value steps only when an event lands and its inputs are released; the share price line is never forecast. Each step is a checkable claim.

Catalyst - A dated, verifiable event - a study, a permit, a financing - that releases new model inputs.

Pre-payment - When today's price already contains tomorrow's documents. Not automatically bad - but you should know you are doing it.

Quality tier / recalibrated rank - Company quality alone, from a 7-factor panel, placed on a 1-10 ladder where the Roster median is 5.0. It deliberately ignores price.

Symposium Top - The highest quality tier on the Roster ladder - the best-evidenced enterprises among an already elite set.

The Roster - The fixed set of companies covered - the presenting companies of a leading annual natural-resource investing symposium, itself a pre-selected elite of the roughly 2,000-3,000 mining companies worldwide, so every tier is standing among the select.

Release gate - A report is published only when every one of the 52 questions reaches a terminal answer - evidenced, documented as absent, or stage-exempt. No gaps hidden.

SOFT - A figure we could not confirm from a primary source, labeled honestly wherever it is used.

PEA / PFS / FS - The study ladder: Preliminary Economic Assessment (first economics), Pre-Feasibility (engineered), Feasibility (bankable). Each rung earns more credit in the model.

P/NAV (developers) - Price compared to a project's study value. Builders trade below 1.0 before production and re-rate through it as the mine becomes real.

Risk weight - The fraction of a project's study value the model credits today, by stage - small for early studies, larger once permitted and engineered.

AISC - All-in sustaining cost: what it costs to produce one ounce, all-in. The margin is the metal price minus this.

NSR royalty - A share of a mine's revenue off the top. Royalty companies own these instead of operating mines.

Streaming - Buying a mine's future silver or gold at a fixed low price in exchange for money upfront.

Earn-in - A contract where a partner pays for exploration to earn a share of a project - the generator model's engine.

Unanswered question - The one company-specific uncertainty the whole thesis hinges on, named explicitly in every report.

Royalty - A fixed percentage of a mine's revenue that goes to an outside holder rather than to the company, paid off the top - before costs, before debt, before shareholders see anything. It was sold once, usually years earlier, to raise cash. It runs for the life of the mine unless the company buys it back, which is possible only where the original agreement allows it at a set price or where the holder agrees to sell. Because it is charged on revenue and not on profit, it is still owed in a year when the mine loses money.

Stream - Not a percentage of revenue but a claim on the metal itself. An outside party paid cash up front, often to help build the mine, in exchange for the right to receive a set share of the metal produced and to pay only a small fixed fraction of the market price for it - sometimes as little as a tenth or a fifth. The gap between that fixed price and the real price is the cost to the company, and it widens as metal prices rise. Like a royalty, a stream runs for the life of the mine unless bought back, which is possible only under the original terms or by agreement with the holder.

The Story

One paragraph in plain words: what the company is, what it owns, and the central finding. If you read nothing else, read this.

INVESTMENT COMMITTEE SUMMARY (July 31, 2026). Riverside is the project's purest prospect-generator specimen: thirty-plus years of Mexican and now Canadian ground, a business model that has partners (a decade's roster includes BHP, Antofagasta, Centerra, Hochschild and Fortuna) pay for the drilling while shareholders keep royalties and spinout paper, roughly 93 million shares, no debt, and a December 2025 strategic placement of C$3.7 million that included the external practitioner personally alongside Sprott Wealth Management. The 2026 story is the THIRD spinout: Ravena Resources completed its first financing on July 13 ahead of a proposed TSX Venture listing, carrying the five Sonora projects (past-producing Los Cuarentas as flagship, plus Cecilia - back to 100% after Fortuna's termination with a six-month cost tail - Ariel, El Valle and Suaqui Grande), following the Capitan Silver and Blue Jay Gold precedents. At a roughly C$26 million capitalization, this is a machine for manufacturing small option positions - valued here as exactly that, nothing more.

20. Formal scenario architecture [Complete · score 3 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Five named pricing cases are built on the SCENARIOS sheet on the project's gold deck, native for this gold-focused generator. The model is deliberately the simplest in the project: cash plus a SOFT portfolio estimate (the Ravena distribution and retained stake, the royalty book, and the partner-carried interests) that scales linearly with the gold price - because a generator's paper and royalties are gold options, and pretending to more precision than that would be false accounting.

21. Valuation-to-action bridge [Complete · score 4 (of 10; 1 = best)]
The valuation-to-action bridge lands almost exactly at fair: the modelled value sits within a few percent of the quote at the dated spot gold case, modestly below at base and stress, and about 29% above only at the upside case - the market prices this generator at roughly the sum of its parts, which is the historically normal state for the model and the honest one. The action logic is therefore not a value gap but a manufacturing cadence: each spinout, royalty and partner deal adds a part, and the December placement's strategic names are betting the cadence continues. This is a position one holds for the machine, not for a re-rating.

22. Thesis-break framework [Complete · score 4 (of 10; 1 = best)]
The thesis-break conditions for a generator are structural rather than event-shaped: the model breaks if partners stop paying (a funding winter that idles the portfolio while overhead runs), if a spinout fails to list or trades poorly enough to impair the currency of the next one, or if the Mexican permitting and security environment degrades the very optionality being sold. The Fortuna termination at Cecilia is the live specimen - a partner walking is routine for the model, and the test is whether the asset re-partners or re-packages (it did: into Ravena) rather than strands.

26. Peer-group methodology [Complete · score 2 (of 10; 1 = best)]
The company is explicitly grouped alongside a real, named set of other small-cap explorers and royalty companies by financial data providers, including Empress Royalty Corp and Revival Gold Inc. - both already reviewed earlier in this project (#53 and #28 respectively) - a real, direct cross-reference.

27. Jurisdiction, fiscal regime, and permitting [Complete · score 2 (of 10; 1 = best)]
A real, genuinely diversified two-country, multi-commodity portfolio: exploration and drilling activity in Mexico (Cecilia, La Union), alongside gold and rare earth element properties in British Columbia, Canada (Deer Park, Revel, Taft) - a real, if less common, dual-commodity (precious metals plus REE) domestic exploration angle for a company otherwise known for its Mexican prospect-generator work.

28. Environmental liability, reclamation, closure, and tailings [Complete · score 4 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Environmental and closure obligations are structurally minimized by the model itself: partner-funded programs put operator obligations on the partner, the company's own ground carries early-stage disturbance only, and the past-producing sites in the portfolio (Los Cuarentas) hold historical footprints whose remediation obligations transfer with the Ravena reorganization - disclosed in structure though not quantified. No environmental proceeding, order or incident was identified in the sources reviewed.

There is no compliant mineral resource anywhere in the portfolio to assess - the honest score for a generator whose product is targets, not ounces: the value evidence is instead a decade of majors funding those targets (metric 31's roster), drill-confirmed mineralization at Cecilia and Union, and the past-producing character of Los Cuarentas. This framework scores the absence numerically rather than exempting it, because a buyer of the shares is buying pre-resource ground on purpose.

Glossary - every term, in plain words (tap to open)

Estimated value - What our model calculates one share is worth from documented evidence at a stated metal price and date. An estimate, not a prediction of where the stock will trade.

Cautious value (safety floor) - The deliberately careful of the two published values: stress-grade assumptions throughout. If the price is below even this number, the discount needs no generosity to see.

Fair value (market-based) - The second published value: what the company is worth using the yardstick the market actually applies to companies of this type across the Roster, with growth on its documented calendar. The verdict keys to this value.

Discount / premium at today's price - The gap between an estimated value and what a share costs today. Green (discount) = the share costs less than the value. Red (premium) = the price already exceeds the value.

Share price - What the market currently charges for one share, always shown with the date of the quote.

Trading below / near / above estimated value - The relationship between price and FAIR value. Below = the market charges less than the estimate (a discount). Above = the price already assumes future events (a pre-payment). Near = within a few percent.

The five-case deck - Value computed at five fixed cases of the company's own commodity price - Stress, Conservative Base, the dated Spot, Long-Term Normalized, Upside. We never forecast the metal; you bring your own view.

Value milestones - A calendar of dated events. Value steps only when an event lands and its inputs are released; the share price line is never forecast. Each step is a checkable claim.

Catalyst - A dated, verifiable event - a study, a permit, a financing - that releases new model inputs.

Pre-payment - When today's price already contains tomorrow's documents. Not automatically bad - but you should know you are doing it.

Quality tier / recalibrated rank - Company quality alone, from a 7-factor panel, placed on a 1-10 ladder where the Roster median is 5.0. It deliberately ignores price.

Symposium Top - The highest quality tier on the Roster ladder - the best-evidenced enterprises among an already elite set.

The Roster - The fixed set of companies covered - the presenting companies of a leading annual natural-resource investing symposium, itself a pre-selected elite of the roughly 2,000-3,000 mining companies worldwide, so every tier is standing among the select.

Release gate - A report is published only when every one of the 52 questions reaches a terminal answer - evidenced, documented as absent, or stage-exempt. No gaps hidden.

SOFT - A figure we could not confirm from a primary source, labeled honestly wherever it is used.

PEA / PFS / FS - The study ladder: Preliminary Economic Assessment (first economics), Pre-Feasibility (engineered), Feasibility (bankable). Each rung earns more credit in the model.

P/NAV (developers) - Price compared to a project's study value. Builders trade below 1.0 before production and re-rate through it as the mine becomes real.

Risk weight - The fraction of a project's study value the model credits today, by stage - small for early studies, larger once permitted and engineered.

AISC - All-in sustaining cost: what it costs to produce one ounce, all-in. The margin is the metal price minus this.

NSR royalty - A share of a mine's revenue off the top. Royalty companies own these instead of operating mines.

Streaming - Buying a mine's future silver or gold at a fixed low price in exchange for money upfront.

Earn-in - A contract where a partner pays for exploration to earn a share of a project - the generator model's engine.

Unanswered question - The one company-specific uncertainty the whole thesis hinges on, named explicitly in every report.

Royalty - A fixed percentage of a mine's revenue that goes to an outside holder rather than to the company, paid off the top - before costs, before debt, before shareholders see anything. It was sold once, usually years earlier, to raise cash. It runs for the life of the mine unless the company buys it back, which is possible only where the original agreement allows it at a set price or where the holder agrees to sell. Because it is charged on revenue and not on profit, it is still owed in a year when the mine loses money.

Stream - Not a percentage of revenue but a claim on the metal itself. An outside party paid cash up front, often to help build the mine, in exchange for the right to receive a set share of the metal produced and to pay only a small fixed fraction of the market price for it - sometimes as little as a tenth or a fifth. The gap between that fixed price and the real price is the cost to the company, and it widens as metal prices rise. Like a royalty, a stream runs for the life of the mine unless bought back, which is possible only under the original terms or by agreement with the holder.

The Story

One paragraph in plain words: what the company is, what it owns, and the central finding. If you read nothing else, read this.

INVESTMENT COMMITTEE SUMMARY (July 31, 2026). Revival Gold is the last developer in the universe and among the purest US-jurisdiction gold stories in it: two past-producing heap-leach projects totaling roughly six million ounces - Mercur in Utah (a former Barrick mine on largely PRIVATE land, sixty kilometres by paved road from Salt Lake City, with intact infrastructure and a stated two-year permitting horizon; PEA May 2025 at US$295 million NPV and roughly 95,600 ounces annually at a US$1,363 AISC) and Beartrack-Arnett in Idaho (a 4.6-million-ounce deposit with a completed 2023 heap-leach PFS, high-grade underground Joss drilling, and Stibnite's approval as the state's fresh permitting precedent). The company publishes its own NAV curve - US$521 million combined at US$2,175 gold rising to US$2.06 billion at US$4,000 - and the calendar is dated: Mercur PFS targeted Q1 2027, feasibility end-2027, construction decision 2028, startup 2029, financing talks from 2027. At C$0.70 on roughly 360 million fully diluted shares, the market pays about a ten-percent risk weight on the curve - a modest discount for a two-study, two-state US developer whose whole thesis is that American ounces re-rate.

Where narrative text carries an older share price, the tables and the refreshed dated close above govern.

Three dates govern this page: the share price is the dated close shown above (2026-07-14); the evidence and estimated values are from this company's last full underwriting (2026-07-31), and change only when the company publishes something - each document's own date is listed under References; a daily event scan watches this company's filings and releases and queues a re-underwriting when one lands.

The Question the Thesis Hinges On

Single greatest company-specific uncertainty identified as converting two real but differently-staged technical studies (a PEA at Mercur, a more advanced PFS at Beartrack-Arnett) into an actual phased restart, given both projects are past producers rather than new discoveries - the company's own thesis rests heavily on "past operating experience and extensive existing project information" reducing risk, which is a real, testable claim but not yet proven through an actual construction decision at either site.

The model adopts the company's own published NAV sensitivity - which is almost perfectly linear at roughly US$845 million per thousand dollars of gold - as the value curve, then applies this project's risk-weight discipline (0.10 blended: Mercur's PEA stage dominant in the NAV, Beartrack-Arnett's completed PFS partially offsetting) rather than the company's implicit 1.0. Adopting a company's curve while re-risking it is the framework's standard treatment of self-published NAV.

21. Valuation-to-action bridge [Complete · score 3 (of 10; 1 = best)]
The valuation-to-action bridge shows a modest developer discount: value about 21% ABOVE the quote at the dated spot gold case at a ten-percent risk weight, above at long-term and upside, slightly below at base, well below at stress - the market pricing the two studies at roughly nine cents on the NAV dollar while comparably-staged US peers (the Stibnite class) have re-rated on permits. The action logic is the dated Mercur chain: PFS Q1 2027, feasibility end-2027, decision 2028 - each document a risk-weight step on a curve the company itself publishes.

22. Thesis-break framework [Complete · score 1 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Given the company holds no current production, the clearest thesis-break condition is either project failing to advance from its current study stage (PEA at Mercur, PFS at Beartrack-Arnett) to an actual positive construction decision - a real, ongoing test given the company's relatively modest treasury (metric 17).

26. Peer-group methodology [Complete · score 3 (of 10; 1 = best)]
The peer frame is the Great Basin re-developer set the CEO himself names - Liberty Gold, Integra, Perpetua - where permitted or near-permitted heap-leach ounces command multiples of Revival's per-ounce mark, with Perpetua's Stibnite approval the class's proof that Idaho files clear. In-project, the instructive contrasts are CTGO (US producer stub, fair-priced) and TECT (Alaska explorer at treasury-cushioned near-fair): US jurisdiction is being paid for elsewhere in this universe; here it is still mostly free.

27. Jurisdiction, fiscal regime, and permitting [Complete · score 2 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Both core projects sit in the United States (Mercur in Utah, Beartrack-Arnett in Idaho) - real, low-political-risk, "top-tier" jurisdictions per the company's own characterization, with Mercur's mineralization primarily on privately-held patented claims, which the company states simplifies permitting relative to public-land projects.

28. Environmental liability, reclamation, closure, and tailings [Complete · score 2 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Environmental obligations are the portfolio's quiet advantage: both projects are PAST PRODUCERS - Mercur a reclaimed Barrick operation whose disturbance, roads and pads exist on private land, Beartrack a reclaimed heap-leach site with its permitting history in the record - so the environmental question is re-entry rather than greenfield. Baseline studies are running at Mercur under the stated two-year permitting plan; no proceeding was identified.

29. Reserve/resource quality [Complete · score 2 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Real, large, combined pit-constrained resource base: 3.2 million oz gold in the Measured & Indicated categories and 2.8 million oz Inferred, across 13,500 hectares of core claims - a genuinely large resource base for a company still at PEA/PFS stage.

30. Exploration effectiveness [Complete · score 3 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Real, current, high-grade, and specifically-dated exploration results at Joss (Beartrack-Arnett): hole BT26-254D intercepted 2.37 g/t gold over 147.2 metres, including 9.3 g/t over 3.5 metres and 14.9 g/t over 5.9 metres, extending the depth of known mineralization by 240 metres (announced June 25, 2026); a 2025-2026 winter drill program (3,900 metres planned) and a 13-kilometre drill program at Mercur were both real, dated, and actively delivering results.

31. Ownership, royalties, streams, and joint ventures [Complete · score 2 (of 10; 1 = best)]
A real, specific, and slightly unusual ownership structure: the company holds "the right to acquire" a 100% interest in Meridian Beartrack Co. (owner of Beartrack) rather than outright current ownership, alongside a 100% interest in the neighboring Arnett claims and a 51% interest in the unrelated Diamond Mountain Phosphate Project - a real, minor commodity-diversification data point (phosphate, an agricultural input, genuinely distinct from every other commodity reviewed in this project) though clearly non-core to the investment thesis.

32. Commodity-price, FX, and inflation assumption governance [Complete · score 2 (of 10; 1 = best)]
The combined-project NPV and Mercur PEA are both explicitly based on a $2,175/oz gold price assumption (metric 16) - real, specific, comparably transparent to several other companies reviewed in this project.

33. Tax, royalties, and fiscal losses [Complete · score 2 (of 10; 1 = best)]
The fiscal frame is domestic-simple: Utah and Idaho state regimes plus US federal tax, no royalty complexity of consequence identified, and accumulated losses sheltering the eventual income - the only two-project developer in this universe with zero sovereign, currency or stabilization question. The fiscal file is, deliberately, boring; that is the product being sold.

34. Production profile, depletion, and replacement [Not Applicable - Operator's Risk]
No current production exists, so there is no depletion/replacement bridge to build.

35. Operating reliability [Not Applicable - Operator's Risk]
No current operating history exists to assess operating reliability, though both projects have real historical operating records from their past-producing years, not independently reviewed this pass.

36. Safety, workforce, and labor [Not Applicable - Operator's Risk]
Pre-construction development and drilling stage: workforce exposure is program-scale under contractor management. The metric activates at construction.

37. Community relations and social licence [Complete · score 2 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Social licence is re-developer favorable: Mercur sits on private land in a historically mined Utah district with the state named by the company as supportive, Beartrack-Arnett carries decades of Lemhi County operating history with local employment memory, and Idaho's Stibnite approval evidences the state's current willingness to permit gold mines. No opposition was identified in the sources reviewed; the federal-land components at Beartrack are the eventual consultation file.

38. Disclosure quality, reporting integrity, and governance [Complete · score 2 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Disclosure practice is developer-institutional: both studies filed as NI 43-101 reports with named authors (Kappes Cassiday, RESPEC, IMC, WSP), the NAV sensitivity published with its price cases rather than hidden in fine print, the metallurgical program disclosed to the test count (twenty column leach tests under Kappes Cassiday), and the 2026 outlook stated as a dated objective list. The register communicates like the mid-tier it intends to become.

39. Infrastructure, utilities, logistics, and business continuity [Complete · score 2 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Real, specific, favorable infrastructure detail directly tied to the company's core strategy: both projects retain real, existing past-production infrastructure (roads, power, and ADR - adsorption/desorption/recovery - plants), explicitly cited by the company as reducing capital intensity and development timelines relative to a greenfield build.

40. Cybersecurity, operational technology, and data integrity [Not Available - Documented]
No cybersecurity or operational-technology disclosure was located in the sources reviewed - the standard absence at this scale.

41. Hedging, derivatives, and counterparty risk [Complete · score 3 (of 10; 1 = best)]
No hedging or streaming was identified - the realization slate is clean for the 2027-28 project financing, which is the point of keeping it so - and counterparty exposure is study-stage: the named engineering firms, the Dundee-anchored financing relationships, and the eventual lender set the 2027 talks will assemble. The clean slate is an asset the financing will spend; the model's staircase dilution reflects it.

42. Working capital, cash conversion, and liquidity quality [Complete · score 4 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Liquidity is the developer squeeze made visible: roughly C$19 million at December 2025 against two active drill programs, a PFS, baseline studies and a metallurgical campaign - real but modest, with the next raise a matter of sequencing rather than possibility. The mitigant is optionality: two separately financeable projects and a US-asset register in a market paying premiums for exactly that.

43. Dilution, equity compensation, and capital-structure overhang [Complete · score 4 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Dilution is the file's structural certainty: the 360-million-share count already reflects the assembly era, the PFS-to-construction chain will add more (the staircase models the count rising toward 430 million by startup), and the offset is that each document should raise NAV faster than the denominator - the race every developer runs, here with the advantage that both projects' studies already exist in some form.

44. Debt structure, covenants, and refinancing [Complete · score 1 (of 10; 1 = best)]
No debt identified this pass - there is no debt structure to assess.

45. Litigation, regulatory, and contingent liabilities [Complete · score 3 (of 10; 1 = best)]
No litigation was identified in the sources reviewed. The contingent inventory is transactional and ordinary: the Mercur acquisition's terms with its private-land package, Beartrack-Arnett's historical agreements and claims position, the financing instruments of the assembly era, and the engineering contracts of the current programs. The private-land structure at Mercur is the inventory's most valuable single item.

46. Insurance adequacy [Not Available - Documented]
Consistent with standard practice, no insurance program terms are disclosed in any public source reviewed this pass.

47. Concentration, correlation, and single-point-of-failure risk [Complete · score 5 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Two core gold projects (Mercur, Beartrack-Arnett) in two US states provide some geographic diversification, plus a minority (51%) non-core phosphate interest; a quantified concentration bridge between the two gold projects was not built this pass. [Calibration-panel score assigned Aug 1, 2026 from the evidence in this note and cross-referenced workbook facts; status unchanged.]

48. Revenue realization, offtake, and payable metal [Not Applicable - Operator's Risk]
No metal is being sold yet, so there are no revenue-realization or offtake terms to assess.

49. Forecast governance and model governance [Complete · score 3 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Forecast governance is publicly dated and so far kept: the Mercur PEA delivered in its stated window (May 2025), the 2026 outlook published as a checkable objective list (PFS substantially complete with Q1 2027 release, permitting on the two-year clock, financing talks 2027), and the drill programs executing as announced. The 2028-29 construction-and-startup targets are the long-dated promises this underwriting's staircase deliberately risks rather than adopts.

50. Management incentives and conflicts [Complete · score 2 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Real, exceptionally strong, disclosed alignment across two levels: Board, Management, and Advisors collectively own approximately 15% of shares outstanding, while two major institutional investors, EMR Capital and Dundee Corporation, together hold approximately 54% of shares - a real, verifiable, and unusually concentrated combined insider-plus-strategic-investor ownership structure.

51. Corporate structure, subsidiary mapping, and entity-level solvency [Complete · score 2 (of 10; 1 = best)]
A real, specific, disclosed corporate structure: subsidiaries include Revival Gold (Idaho) Inc. and Strata Minerals Pty Ltd., and the company itself was formerly known as Strata Minerals Inc. before renaming to Revival Gold in July 2017 - genuine, traceable entity history.

52. Reserve-price sensitivity, cut-off migration, and economic-envelope robustness [Complete · score 3 (of 10; 1 = best)]
The economic envelope is heap-leach honest: Mercur's PEA margins (a US$1,363 AISC against the deck) are real but not elite - oxide heap-leach economics are capital-light rather than cost-elite - and the NAV curve's steep gold slope is the envelope's true character: at US$4,000-class gold these are exceptional projects, at US$2,600 they are ordinary ones. The stress case says so plainly, which is why the risk-weighted model still clears the price only from base upward.

53. Technical-report currency, competent-person reliance, and study obsolescence [Complete · score 3 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Technical currency is dual-vintage: the Mercur PEA is current (May 2025) and feeding directly into the Q1 2027 PFS, while Beartrack-Arnett's PFS dates to August 2023 - serviceable but aging, with the current underground drilling aimed at a larger future restatement rather than at refreshing the heap-leach case. Nothing being paid for lacks a document; the Idaho document is the older of the two.

54. Geological reconciliation, grade control, metallurgical accounting, and reserve performance [Not Applicable - Operator's Risk]
No operating reconciliation exists pre-construction. Both projects' PAST-PRODUCER histories provide the stage's best analogue - orebodies that reconciled against real mills for years - carried qualitatively in the resource metrics.

55. Water balance, water security, climate resilience, and extreme weather [Complete · score 3 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Water and climate exposure is Great Basin standard: arid-region heap-leach water balances at both sites (a design discipline the region's operators have run for decades), established water access at the past-producing sites, and no scarcity conflict identified. Mercur's proximity to the Salt Lake urban shed makes water stewardship a permitting topic the baseline studies are built to answer.

56. Tailings-facility integrity, geotechnical stability, and emergency preparedness [Complete · score 3 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Tailings exposure is the heap-leach advantage: neither project requires a conventional tailings facility - spent leach pads are the storage question, both sites carry reclaimed historical pads under regulatory closure, and the new designs belong to the current studies. The absence of a wet tailings dam from the entire portfolio is a genuine risk-class exclusion few developers in this universe can claim.

57. Valuation-method hierarchy, asset-level NAV governance, discount-rate discipline, and double-counting prevention [Complete · score 3 (of 10; 1 = best)]
The valuation hierarchy is explicit: the company's own published combined NAV curve (adopted for its transparency, at its stated price cases), risked at 0.10 for blended study stage, plus the modest treasury - with the Joss underground upside, the three untested Idaho miles, the Mercur district targets, any US-premium re-rating and all post-study financing outcomes carried at ZERO as the anti-double-counting offset, released only on the dated staircase. The company's implicit 1.0 risk weight is recorded and deliberately not adopted.

58. Underwriting conclusion governance, recommendation authorization, confidence calibration, and report-release control [Complete · score 3 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Conclusion governance is satisfied for release: every scored metric resolved, the not-applicable items documented, the SOFT share count and adopted-curve treatment labeled, and the finding - the universe's last developer, a two-study US heap-leach story at nine cents on its own NAV dollar with a dated document chain - stated identically in summary, bridge and hierarchy. Authorized with the Q1 2027 Mercur PFS as the standing checkpoint.

59. Management track record and role-specific competence [Complete · score 5 (of 10; 1 = best)]
The company states its leadership team is "comprised of gold industry veterans who have decades of experience successfully financing, constructing, and responsibly operating gold mines" - a real, stated claim, and the same team's ~15% personal ownership (metric 50) is a real, concrete alignment signal; a full independently-verified, role-specific track-record evaluation per the consultation document's standard was not performed this pass.
