Glossary - every term, in plain words (tap to open)

Estimated value - What our model calculates one share is worth from documented evidence at a stated metal price and date. An estimate, not a prediction of where the stock will trade.

Cautious value (safety floor) - The deliberately careful of the two published values: stress-grade assumptions throughout. If the price is below even this number, the discount needs no generosity to see.

Fair value (market-based) - The second published value: what the company is worth using the yardstick the market actually applies to companies of this type across the Roster, with growth on its documented calendar. The verdict keys to this value.

Discount / premium at today's price - The gap between an estimated value and what a share costs today. Green (discount) = the share costs less than the value. Red (premium) = the price already exceeds the value.

Share price - What the market currently charges for one share, always shown with the date of the quote.

Trading below / near / above estimated value - The relationship between price and FAIR value. Below = the market charges less than the estimate (a discount). Above = the price already assumes future events (a pre-payment). Near = within a few percent.

The five-case deck - Value computed at five fixed cases of the company's own commodity price - Stress, Conservative Base, the dated Spot, Long-Term Normalized, Upside. We never forecast the metal; you bring your own view.

Value milestones - A calendar of dated events. Value steps only when an event lands and its inputs are released; the share price line is never forecast. Each step is a checkable claim.

Catalyst - A dated, verifiable event - a study, a permit, a financing - that releases new model inputs.

Pre-payment - When today's price already contains tomorrow's documents. Not automatically bad - but you should know you are doing it.

Quality tier / recalibrated rank - Company quality alone, from a 7-factor panel, placed on a 1-10 ladder where the Roster median is 5.0. It deliberately ignores price.

Symposium Top - The highest quality tier on the Roster ladder - the best-evidenced enterprises among an already elite set.

The Roster - The fixed set of companies covered - the presenting companies of a leading annual natural-resource investing symposium, itself a pre-selected elite of the roughly 2,000-3,000 mining companies worldwide, so every tier is standing among the select.

Release gate - A report is published only when every one of the 52 questions reaches a terminal answer - evidenced, documented as absent, or stage-exempt. No gaps hidden.

SOFT - A figure we could not confirm from a primary source, labeled honestly wherever it is used.

PEA / PFS / FS - The study ladder: Preliminary Economic Assessment (first economics), Pre-Feasibility (engineered), Feasibility (bankable). Each rung earns more credit in the model.

P/NAV (developers) - Price compared to a project's study value. Builders trade below 1.0 before production and re-rate through it as the mine becomes real.

Risk weight - The fraction of a project's study value the model credits today, by stage - small for early studies, larger once permitted and engineered.

AISC - All-in sustaining cost: what it costs to produce one ounce, all-in. The margin is the metal price minus this.

NSR royalty - A share of a mine's revenue off the top. Royalty companies own these instead of operating mines.

Streaming - Buying a mine's future silver or gold at a fixed low price in exchange for money upfront.

Earn-in - A contract where a partner pays for exploration to earn a share of a project - the generator model's engine.

Unanswered question - The one company-specific uncertainty the whole thesis hinges on, named explicitly in every report.

Royalty - A fixed percentage of a mine's revenue that goes to an outside holder rather than to the company, paid off the top - before costs, before debt, before shareholders see anything. It was sold once, usually years earlier, to raise cash. It runs for the life of the mine unless the company buys it back, which is possible only where the original agreement allows it at a set price or where the holder agrees to sell. Because it is charged on revenue and not on profit, it is still owed in a year when the mine loses money.

Stream - Not a percentage of revenue but a claim on the metal itself. An outside party paid cash up front, often to help build the mine, in exchange for the right to receive a set share of the metal produced and to pay only a small fixed fraction of the market price for it - sometimes as little as a tenth or a fifth. The gap between that fixed price and the real price is the cost to the company, and it widens as metal prices rise. Like a royalty, a stream runs for the life of the mine unless bought back, which is possible only under the original terms or by agreement with the holder.

The Story

INVESTMENT COMMITTEE SUMMARY (July 31, 2026). Royal Road closes the campaign as its most geopolitically-layered explorer: Dr. Tim Coughlin - AngloGold's former South American chief geologist and the Amulsar discoverer - holds roughly 1,840 square kilometres of Colombian titles and applications (among the country's largest positions), anchored by the GAM porphyry cluster in Antioquia: THREE porphyry systems with drilling restarted in 2026 on the first (historic intercepts of 181 metres at 1.1 grams gold-equivalent), a mining-concession TITLE GRANT secured in January, and early-2026 results showing evidence of scale - all while Colombia's May election replaced the administration whose permitting posture froze the sector, with the CEO's own words framing southern-project access as 'entirely political will.' Glossary - every term, in plain words (tap to open)

Estimated value - What our model calculates one share is worth from documented evidence at a stated metal price and date. An estimate, not a prediction of where the stock will trade.

Cautious value (safety floor) - The deliberately careful of the two published values: stress-grade assumptions throughout. If the price is below even this number, the discount needs no generosity to see.

Fair value (market-based) - The second published value: what the company is worth using the yardstick the market actually applies to companies of this type across the Roster, with growth on its documented calendar. The verdict keys to this value.

Discount / premium at today's price - The gap between an estimated value and what a share costs today. Green (discount) = the share costs less than the value. Red (premium) = the price already exceeds the value.

Share price - What the market currently charges for one share, always shown with the date of the quote.

Trading below / near / above estimated value - The relationship between price and FAIR value. Below = the market charges less than the estimate (a discount). Above = the price already assumes future events (a pre-payment). Near = within a few percent.

The five-case deck - Value computed at five fixed cases of the company's own commodity price - Stress, Conservative Base, the dated Spot, Long-Term Normalized, Upside. We never forecast the metal; you bring your own view.

Value milestones - A calendar of dated events. Value steps only when an event lands and its inputs are released; the share price line is never forecast. Each step is a checkable claim.

Catalyst - A dated, verifiable event - a study, a permit, a financing - that releases new model inputs.

Pre-payment - When today's price already contains tomorrow's documents. Not automatically bad - but you should know you are doing it.

Quality tier / recalibrated rank - Company quality alone, from a 7-factor panel, placed on a 1-10 ladder where the Roster median is 5.0. It deliberately ignores price.

Symposium Top - The highest quality tier on the Roster ladder - the best-evidenced enterprises among an already elite set.

The Roster - The fixed set of companies covered - the presenting companies of a leading annual natural-resource investing symposium, itself a pre-selected elite of the roughly 2,000-3,000 mining companies worldwide, so every tier is standing among the select.

Release gate - A report is published only when every one of the 52 questions reaches a terminal answer - evidenced, documented as absent, or stage-exempt. No gaps hidden.

SOFT - A figure we could not confirm from a primary source, labeled honestly wherever it is used.

PEA / PFS / FS - The study ladder: Preliminary Economic Assessment (first economics), Pre-Feasibility (engineered), Feasibility (bankable). Each rung earns more credit in the model.

P/NAV (developers) - Price compared to a project's study value. Builders trade below 1.0 before production and re-rate through it as the mine becomes real.

Risk weight - The fraction of a project's study value the model credits today, by stage - small for early studies, larger once permitted and engineered.

AISC - All-in sustaining cost: what it costs to produce one ounce, all-in. The margin is the metal price minus this.

NSR royalty - A share of a mine's revenue off the top. Royalty companies own these instead of operating mines.

Streaming - Buying a mine's future silver or gold at a fixed low price in exchange for money upfront.

Earn-in - A contract where a partner pays for exploration to earn a share of a project - the generator model's engine.

Unanswered question - The one company-specific uncertainty the whole thesis hinges on, named explicitly in every report.

Royalty - A fixed percentage of a mine's revenue that goes to an outside holder rather than to the company, paid off the top - before costs, before debt, before shareholders see anything. It was sold once, usually years earlier, to raise cash. It runs for the life of the mine unless the company buys it back, which is possible only where the original agreement allows it at a set price or where the holder agrees to sell. Because it is charged on revenue and not on profit, it is still owed in a year when the mine loses money.

Stream - Not a percentage of revenue but a claim on the metal itself. An outside party paid cash up front, often to help build the mine, in exchange for the right to receive a set share of the metal produced and to pay only a small fixed fraction of the market price for it - sometimes as little as a tenth or a fifth. The gap between that fixed price and the real price is the cost to the company, and it widens as metal prices rise. Like a royalty, a stream runs for the life of the mine unless bought back, which is possible only under the original terms or by agreement with the holder.

Glossary - every term, in plain words (tap to open)

Estimated value - What our model calculates one share is worth from documented evidence at a stated metal price and date. An estimate, not a prediction of where the stock will trade.

Cautious value (safety floor) - The deliberately careful of the two published values: stress-grade assumptions throughout. If the price is below even this number, the discount needs no generosity to see.

Fair value (market-based) - The second published value: what the company is worth using the yardstick the market actually applies to companies of this type across the Roster, with growth on its documented calendar. The verdict keys to this value.

Discount / premium at today's price - The gap between an estimated value and what a share costs today. Green (discount) = the share costs less than the value. Red (premium) = the price already exceeds the value.

Share price - What the market currently charges for one share, always shown with the date of the quote.

Trading below / near / above estimated value - The relationship between price and FAIR value. Below = the market charges less than the estimate (a discount). Above = the price already assumes future events (a pre-payment). Near = within a few percent.

The five-case deck - Value computed at five fixed cases of the company's own commodity price - Stress, Conservative Base, the dated Spot, Long-Term Normalized, Upside. We never forecast the metal; you bring your own view.

Value milestones - A calendar of dated events. Value steps only when an event lands and its inputs are released; the share price line is never forecast. Each step is a checkable claim.

Catalyst - A dated, verifiable event - a study, a permit, a financing - that releases new model inputs.

Pre-payment - When today's price already contains tomorrow's documents. Not automatically bad - but you should know you are doing it.

Quality tier / recalibrated rank - Company quality alone, from a 7-factor panel, placed on a 1-10 ladder where the Roster median is 5.0. It deliberately ignores price.

Symposium Top - The highest quality tier on the Roster ladder - the best-evidenced enterprises among an already elite set.

The Roster - The fixed set of companies covered - the presenting companies of a leading annual natural-resource investing symposium, itself a pre-selected elite of the roughly 2,000-3,000 mining companies worldwide, so every tier is standing among the select.

Release gate - A report is published only when every one of the 52 questions reaches a terminal answer - evidenced, documented as absent, or stage-exempt. No gaps hidden.

SOFT - A figure we could not confirm from a primary source, labeled honestly wherever it is used.

PEA / PFS / FS - The study ladder: Preliminary Economic Assessment (first economics), Pre-Feasibility (engineered), Feasibility (bankable). Each rung earns more credit in the model.

P/NAV (developers) - Price compared to a project's study value. Builders trade below 1.0 before production and re-rate through it as the mine becomes real.

Risk weight - The fraction of a project's study value the model credits today, by stage - small for early studies, larger once permitted and engineered.

AISC - All-in sustaining cost: what it costs to produce one ounce, all-in. The margin is the metal price minus this.

NSR royalty - A share of a mine's revenue off the top. Royalty companies own these instead of operating mines.

Streaming - Buying a mine's future silver or gold at a fixed low price in exchange for money upfront.

Earn-in - A contract where a partner pays for exploration to earn a share of a project - the generator model's engine.

Unanswered question - The one company-specific uncertainty the whole thesis hinges on, named explicitly in every report.

Royalty - A fixed percentage of a mine's revenue that goes to an outside holder rather than to the company, paid off the top - before costs, before debt, before shareholders see anything. It was sold once, usually years earlier, to raise cash. It runs for the life of the mine unless the company buys it back, which is possible only where the original agreement allows it at a set price or where the holder agrees to sell. Because it is charged on revenue and not on profit, it is still owed in a year when the mine loses money.

Stream - Not a percentage of revenue but a claim on the metal itself. An outside party paid cash up front, often to help build the mine, in exchange for the right to receive a set share of the metal produced and to pay only a small fixed fraction of the market price for it - sometimes as little as a tenth or a fifth. The gap between that fixed price and the real price is the cost to the company, and it widens as metal prices rise. Like a royalty, a stream runs for the life of the mine unless bought back, which is possible only under the original terms or by agreement with the holder.

The Story

One paragraph in plain words: what the company is, what it owns, and the central finding. If you read nothing else, read this.

IC summary: the Yukon's modern flagship discovery at its engineering moment - Valley on the Rogue Project holds 7.94 Moz Measured & Indicated at 1.21 g/t (a 96% M&I increase in the 2025 update) plus 0.89 Moz Inferred, with a maiden PEA outlining a 20-year conventional open-pit producing 6.81M payable ounces (averaging 340,500 oz/yr and 544,000 oz/yr in the high-grade years two through six) at an after-tax NPV5 of C$3.37 BILLION - calculated at US$2,150 gold, less than half today's spot. A fully funded PFS targets early 2027, the 2026 season is the company's largest ever, the safety record is spotless (zero lost-time injuries across 14,524 field days), the treasury holds ~C$105M, and - the variable that governs everything in the post-Eagle Yukon - the company is in CONTINUED collaboration and advanced project agreement discussions with the First Nation of Na-Cho Nyak Dun. At C$16.50 the model reads -8.0% at spot: the market has already paid for elite quality, and the staircase prices the de-risking ladder from here.

The Question the Thesis Hinges On

Glossary - every term, in plain words (tap to open)

Estimated value - What our model calculates one share is worth from documented evidence at a stated metal price and date. An estimate, not a prediction of where the stock will trade.

Cautious value (safety floor) - The deliberately careful of the two published values: stress-grade assumptions throughout. If the price is below even this number, the discount needs no generosity to see.

Fair value (market-based) - The second published value: what the company is worth using the yardstick the market actually applies to companies of this type across the Roster, with growth on its documented calendar. The verdict keys to this value.

Discount / premium at today's price - The gap between an estimated value and what a share costs today. Green (discount) = the share costs less than the value. Red (premium) = the price already exceeds the value.

Share price - What the market currently charges for one share, always shown with the date of the quote.

Trading below / near / above estimated value - The relationship between price and FAIR value. Below = the market charges less than the estimate (a discount). Above = the price already assumes future events (a pre-payment). Near = within a few percent.

The five-case deck - Value computed at five fixed cases of the company's own commodity price - Stress, Conservative Base, the dated Spot, Long-Term Normalized, Upside. We never forecast the metal; you bring your own view.

Value milestones - A calendar of dated events. Value steps only when an event lands and its inputs are released; the share price line is never forecast. Each step is a checkable claim.

Catalyst - A dated, verifiable event - a study, a permit, a financing - that releases new model inputs.

Pre-payment - When today's price already contains tomorrow's documents. Not automatically bad - but you should know you are doing it.

Quality tier / recalibrated rank - Company quality alone, from a 7-factor panel, placed on a 1-10 ladder where the Roster median is 5.0. It deliberately ignores price.

Symposium Top - The highest quality tier on the Roster ladder - the best-evidenced enterprises among an already elite set.

The Roster - The fixed set of companies covered - the presenting companies of a leading annual natural-resource investing symposium, itself a pre-selected elite of the roughly 2,000-3,000 mining companies worldwide, so every tier is standing among the select.

Release gate - A report is published only when every one of the 52 questions reaches a terminal answer - evidenced, documented as absent, or stage-exempt. No gaps hidden.

SOFT - A figure we could not confirm from a primary source, labeled honestly wherever it is used.

PEA / PFS / FS - The study ladder: Preliminary Economic Assessment (first economics), Pre-Feasibility (engineered), Feasibility (bankable). Each rung earns more credit in the model.

P/NAV (developers) - Price compared to a project's study value. Builders trade below 1.0 before production and re-rate through it as the mine becomes real.

Risk weight - The fraction of a project's study value the model credits today, by stage - small for early studies, larger once permitted and engineered.

AISC - All-in sustaining cost: what it costs to produce one ounce, all-in. The margin is the metal price minus this.

NSR royalty - A share of a mine's revenue off the top. Royalty companies own these instead of operating mines.

Streaming - Buying a mine's future silver or gold at a fixed low price in exchange for money upfront.

Earn-in - A contract where a partner pays for exploration to earn a share of a project - the generator model's engine.

Unanswered question - The one company-specific uncertainty the whole thesis hinges on, named explicitly in every report.

Royalty - A fixed percentage of a mine's revenue that goes to an outside holder rather than to the company, paid off the top - before costs, before debt, before shareholders see anything. It was sold once, usually years earlier, to raise cash. It runs for the life of the mine unless the company buys it back, which is possible only where the original agreement allows it at a set price or where the holder agrees to sell. Because it is charged on revenue and not on profit, it is still owed in a year when the mine loses money.

Stream - Not a percentage of revenue but a claim on the metal itself. An outside party paid cash up front, often to help build the mine, in exchange for the right to receive a set share of the metal produced and to pay only a small fixed fraction of the market price for it - sometimes as little as a tenth or a fifth. The gap between that fixed price and the real price is the cost to the company, and it widens as metal prices rise. Like a royalty, a stream runs for the life of the mine unless bought back, which is possible only under the original terms or by agreement with the holder.

The Story

One paragraph in plain words: what the company is, what it owns, and the central finding. If you read nothing else, read this.

Decision summary: a fully permitted, fully financed, half-built version of one of the world's highest-grade open-pit precious metals projects; quality rests on the asset (metric 29) and the demonstrated permitting/financing execution (metrics 27, 44), the honest risks are single-asset construction delivery (metric 12) and the leveraged capital structure (metric 17), and valuation (metric 57) shows the stock pricing most - not all - of the spot-gold case.

Where narrative text carries an older share price, the tables and the refreshed dated close above govern.

Three dates govern this page: the share price is the dated close shown above (2026-08-01); the evidence and estimated values are from this company's last full underwriting (2026-07-31), and change only when the company publishes something - each document's own date is listed under References; a daily event scan watches this company's filings and releases and queues a re-underwriting when one lands.

The Question the Thesis Hinges On

Single greatest company-specific uncertainty identified as construction/permitting execution risk on the single Eskay Creek project: the budget has already grown from $560M (2023 feasibility) to $659M (Feb 2026) due to inflation and stricter regulation, a permitting delay risk was explicitly flagged (a BC government employee strike), and the project's Indigenous impact-benefit agreement with the Tahltan Central Government was still pending negotiation as of the most recent evidence reviewed. As a pure developer, there is no operating cash flow yet to absorb a further delay or cost overrun.

DFS-level (2023) Proven and Probable reserves of 39.8 Mt containing 3.3 Moz gold and 88.0 Moz silver - 4.6 Moz gold-equivalent - with years 1-5 averaging 5.5 g/t AuEq at 455,000 oz per year: among the highest-grade open-pit precious metals reserves in the world, independently estimated for the November 2023 study.

Glossary - every term, in plain words (tap to open)

Estimated value - What our model calculates one share is worth from documented evidence at a stated metal price and date. An estimate, not a prediction of where the stock will trade.

Cautious value (safety floor) - The deliberately careful of the two published values: stress-grade assumptions throughout. If the price is below even this number, the discount needs no generosity to see.

Fair value (market-based) - The second published value: what the company is worth using the yardstick the market actually applies to companies of this type across the Roster, with growth on its documented calendar. The verdict keys to this value.

Discount / premium at today's price - The gap between an estimated value and what a share costs today. Green (discount) = the share costs less than the value. Red (premium) = the price already exceeds the value.

Share price - What the market currently charges for one share, always shown with the date of the quote.

Trading below / near / above estimated value - The relationship between price and FAIR value. Below = the market charges less than the estimate (a discount). Above = the price already assumes future events (a pre-payment). Near = within a few percent.

The five-case deck - Value computed at five fixed cases of the company's own commodity price - Stress, Conservative Base, the dated Spot, Long-Term Normalized, Upside. We never forecast the metal; you bring your own view.

Value milestones - A calendar of dated events. Value steps only when an event lands and its inputs are released; the share price line is never forecast. Each step is a checkable claim.

Catalyst - A dated, verifiable event - a study, a permit, a financing - that releases new model inputs.

Pre-payment - When today's price already contains tomorrow's documents. Not automatically bad - but you should know you are doing it.

Quality tier / recalibrated rank - Company quality alone, from a 7-factor panel, placed on a 1-10 ladder where the Roster median is 5.0. It deliberately ignores price.

Symposium Top - The highest quality tier on the Roster ladder - the best-evidenced enterprises among an already elite set.

The Roster - The fixed set of companies covered - the presenting companies of a leading annual natural-resource investing symposium, itself a pre-selected elite of the roughly 2,000-3,000 mining companies worldwide, so every tier is standing among the select.

Release gate - A report is published only when every one of the 52 questions reaches a terminal answer - evidenced, documented as absent, or stage-exempt. No gaps hidden.

SOFT - A figure we could not confirm from a primary source, labeled honestly wherever it is used.

PEA / PFS / FS - The study ladder: Preliminary Economic Assessment (first economics), Pre-Feasibility (engineered), Feasibility (bankable). Each rung earns more credit in the model.

P/NAV (developers) - Price compared to a project's study value. Builders trade below 1.0 before production and re-rate through it as the mine becomes real.

Risk weight - The fraction of a project's study value the model credits today, by stage - small for early studies, larger once permitted and engineered.

AISC - All-in sustaining cost: what it costs to produce one ounce, all-in. The margin is the metal price minus this.

NSR royalty - A share of a mine's revenue off the top. Royalty companies own these instead of operating mines.

Streaming - Buying a mine's future silver or gold at a fixed low price in exchange for money upfront.

Earn-in - A contract where a partner pays for exploration to earn a share of a project - the generator model's engine.

Unanswered question - The one company-specific uncertainty the whole thesis hinges on, named explicitly in every report.

Royalty - A fixed percentage of a mine's revenue that goes to an outside holder rather than to the company, paid off the top - before costs, before debt, before shareholders see anything. It was sold once, usually years earlier, to raise cash. It runs for the life of the mine unless the company buys it back, which is possible only where the original agreement allows it at a set price or where the holder agrees to sell. Because it is charged on revenue and not on profit, it is still owed in a year when the mine loses money.

Stream - Not a percentage of revenue but a claim on the metal itself. An outside party paid cash up front, often to help build the mine, in exchange for the right to receive a set share of the metal produced and to pay only a small fixed fraction of the market price for it - sometimes as little as a tenth or a fifth. The gap between that fixed price and the real price is the cost to the company, and it widens as metal prices rise. Like a royalty, a stream runs for the life of the mine unless bought back, which is possible only under the original terms or by agreement with the holder.

The Story

One paragraph in plain words: what the company is, what it owns, and the central finding. If you read nothing else, read this.

INVESTMENT COMMITTEE SUMMARY (July 31, 2026). Solaris is the developer the market has already started believing: Warintza - a 1.3-billion-tonne maiden-reserve copper porphyry in southeastern Ecuador with a November 2025 PFS showing US$4.6 billion of post-tax NPV, 26% IRR and 300,000-plus tonnes of copper-equivalent in the first five years - received its EIA TECHNICAL APPROVAL on April 9, 2026 after a multi-year government review, triggering the second US$50 million Royal Gold tranche, and now runs the government-led Shuar consultation toward Mining Exploitation Agreements and a targeted FULLY PERMITTED status by the end of 2026 with a construction decision by early 2027. The share price has re-rated roughly 250% in a year on exactly this momentum. The underwriting question is calibration, not direction: how much of a US$3.7 billion build in Ecuador - a jurisdiction with one large modern mine and a fresh consultation process - is fairly pre-paid at a C$2.2 billion capitalization, against a disclosed tension between fully-funded messaging and a deepening shareholder deficit.

27. Jurisdiction, fiscal regime, and permitting [Complete · score 3 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Real, specific, and unusually well-documented jurisdictional and social-license detail: Warintza sits in Morona Santiago province, southeastern Ecuador, described as an export-oriented nation with existing paved-highway infrastructure to port; the company established a formal Strategic Alliance with the Shuar communities of Warints and Yawi in 2019, leading to a long-term Impacts & Benefits Agreement signed in 2020 and later updated as the project grew - a genuinely long-standing, structured Indigenous-relations foundation predating the PFS by several years, a real contrast to the more recently-resolved or still-unresolved social-license situations found at several other companies in this project (e.g. Equinox Gold's Los Filos, #12; Pan American Silver's Escobal, #7). Ecuador's state-owned mining company, ENAMI EP, separately granted Solaris an option over ~40,000 hectares of adjacent concessions (Solaris 2, metric 30) - real, direct government-level land-access support.

28. Environmental liability, reclamation, closure, and tailings [Complete · score 3 (of 10; 1 = best)]

The 22-year mine life is explicitly TAILINGS-CONSTRAINED in the PFS, an honest disclosure that the storage design is the binding environmental envelope and the feasibility study's named optimization target.

Real, current, and district-expanding exploration activity: new copper anomalies with rock samples returning up to 8.38% Cu were reported at the "Solaris 1" concession (January 2026), alongside the real, government-granted "Solaris 2" option covering approximately 40,000 additional hectares immediately adjacent to Warintza (metric 27) - genuine, dated evidence the district-scale opportunity extends well beyond the currently-defined resource.

52. Reserve-price sensitivity, cut-off migration, and economic-envelope robustness [Complete · score 3 (of 10; 1 = best)]
The economic envelope is robust at study prices and generous at today's: a 26% post-tax IRR at US$4.00 copper against a US$6.49 spot means the margin of safety sits in the commodity itself; the maiden reserve's 0.41% CuEq grade is low in absolute terms but carried by scale, a low strip and first-quartile cost positioning per the study. The stress case (US$4.17) lands almost exactly on the study deck - the model's stress IS the study's base reality, and the project survives it by design. Cut-off and envelope refinement is precisely what the feasibility study is optimizing.

53. Technical-report currency, competent-person reliance, and study obsolescence [Complete · score 2 (of 10; 1 = best)]
The November 2025 PFS, prepared with named, credible consultants (Ausenco, Knight Piésold, AMC), is genuinely current, and a full Feasibility Study is already underway with the same firms (metric 16) - real, dated, and actively-advancing technical work.

54. Geological reconciliation, grade control, metallurgical accounting, and reserve performance [Not Applicable - Operator's Risk]
Reconciliation and metallurgical accounting require operations; Warintza is at feasibility. The 84% copper-recovery assumption and the grade model sit at metrics 16 and 29; performance reconciliation begins with commissioning, targeted for 2030.

55. Water balance, water security, climate resilience, and extreme weather [Complete · score 3 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Water and climate exposure is Amazonian-highland: high rainfall as a management task rather than scarcity as a constraint - the inverse of the Chilean copper problem - with Knight Piesold (the PFS water and tailings consultant) engineering for wet-season hydrology, and the tailings facility's water balance the design-critical item the feasibility study is refining. No water-availability constraint exists; water MANAGEMENT is the engineering. Formal climate-resilience disclosure is not yet published.

56. Tailings-facility integrity, geotechnical stability, and emergency preparedness [Complete · score 4 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Tailings is the project's stated binding constraint and its most consequential design item: the PFS mine life is explicitly limited by tailings storage capacity, the facility must be engineered for high-rainfall Amazonian-highland hydrology in a seismically active country, and refining the tailings solution is a named feasibility-study objective. Knight Piesold's involvement is the credibility anchor; no facility-level consequence classification or design disclosure is published yet at PFS stage. A real, named, well-consulted future obligation - scored as such.

57. Valuation-method hierarchy, asset-level NAV governance, discount-rate discipline, and double-counting prevention [Complete · score 3 (of 10; 1 = best)]
The valuation hierarchy is explicit: the PFS NPV scaled along a SOFT copper slope from the study's US$4.00 deck, risked at 0.20 for the pre-permit-completion, pre-FID, pre-financing position, plus available liquidity - with the district expansion (new anomalies to 8% copper), the Solaris 2 adjacent-concession options, La Verde, Tamarugo, the Peru assets and the Freeport farm-outs ALL at ZERO as the anti-double-counting offset, released only on the dated staircase. Nothing uses the share price's own momentum as an input.

58. Underwriting conclusion governance, recommendation authorization, confidence calibration, and report-release control [Complete · score 3 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Conclusion governance is satisfied for release: every scored metric resolved, the stage exemption justified, the SOFT slope labeled at source, and the central calibration finding - a disciplined premium for real permitting momentum, roughly fair at base copper and modestly cheap at spot - stated identically in the summary, bridge and hierarchy. Authorized with its condition named: the end-2026 permit target and early-2027 construction decision are the entire near-term case, and metric 12's funding-versus-deficit tension is the number to re-check at each milestone.

59. Management track record and role-specific competence [Complete · score 4 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Leadership changed mid-development - Matthew Rowlinson now President & CEO, succeeding Daniel Earle, within the Augusta Group lineage - and the current team's delivery cadence has been strong and dated: PFS with maiden mineral reserve published November 6, 2025 (US$4.6B NPV, extensive mine life, first-quartile cost position claimed), the US$200M Royal Gold financing signed May 2025 with its US$50M second tranche triggered exactly as designed by the EIA technical approval of April 9, 2026, feasibility underway with Ausenco/Knight Piesold/AMC, full permitting targeted H2 2026, a construction decision framed for early 2027, and the district expanded by ~40,000 ha in January 2026. The record also contains the sector's cautionary tale that management navigated rather than caused: the Zijin minority investment blocked under Canada's ICA review and terminated in 2024, forcing the pivot to royalty financing. Residuals: CEO turnover at the most capital-intensive moment, an FID and a financing package far beyond the Royal Gold facility still ahead, and Ecuadorian community-consultation complexity that the company's participatory model manages but can never fully retire.

Glossary - every term, in plain words (tap to open)

Estimated value - What our model calculates one share is worth from documented evidence at a stated metal price and date. An estimate, not a prediction of where the stock will trade.

Cautious value (safety floor) - The deliberately careful of the two published values: stress-grade assumptions throughout. If the price is below even this number, the discount needs no generosity to see.

Fair value (market-based) - The second published value: what the company is worth using the yardstick the market actually applies to companies of this type across the Roster, with growth on its documented calendar. The verdict keys to this value.

Discount / premium at today's price - The gap between an estimated value and what a share costs today. Green (discount) = the share costs less than the value. Red (premium) = the price already exceeds the value.

Share price - What the market currently charges for one share, always shown with the date of the quote.

Trading below / near / above estimated value - The relationship between price and FAIR value. Below = the market charges less than the estimate (a discount). Above = the price already assumes future events (a pre-payment). Near = within a few percent.

The five-case deck - Value computed at five fixed cases of the company's own commodity price - Stress, Conservative Base, the dated Spot, Long-Term Normalized, Upside. We never forecast the metal; you bring your own view.

Value milestones - A calendar of dated events. Value steps only when an event lands and its inputs are released; the share price line is never forecast. Each step is a checkable claim.

Catalyst - A dated, verifiable event - a study, a permit, a financing - that releases new model inputs.

Pre-payment - When today's price already contains tomorrow's documents. Not automatically bad - but you should know you are doing it.

Quality tier / recalibrated rank - Company quality alone, from a 7-factor panel, placed on a 1-10 ladder where the Roster median is 5.0. It deliberately ignores price.

Symposium Top - The highest quality tier on the Roster ladder - the best-evidenced enterprises among an already elite set.

The Roster - The fixed set of companies covered - the presenting companies of a leading annual natural-resource investing symposium, itself a pre-selected elite of the roughly 2,000-3,000 mining companies worldwide, so every tier is standing among the select.

Release gate - A report is published only when every one of the 52 questions reaches a terminal answer - evidenced, documented as absent, or stage-exempt. No gaps hidden.

SOFT - A figure we could not confirm from a primary source, labeled honestly wherever it is used.

PEA / PFS / FS - The study ladder: Preliminary Economic Assessment (first economics), Pre-Feasibility (engineered), Feasibility (bankable). Each rung earns more credit in the model.

P/NAV (developers) - Price compared to a project's study value. Builders trade below 1.0 before production and re-rate through it as the mine becomes real.

Risk weight - The fraction of a project's study value the model credits today, by stage - small for early studies, larger once permitted and engineered.

AISC - All-in sustaining cost: what it costs to produce one ounce, all-in. The margin is the metal price minus this.

NSR royalty - A share of a mine's revenue off the top. Royalty companies own these instead of operating mines.

Streaming - Buying a mine's future silver or gold at a fixed low price in exchange for money upfront.

Earn-in - A contract where a partner pays for exploration to earn a share of a project - the generator model's engine.

Unanswered question - The one company-specific uncertainty the whole thesis hinges on, named explicitly in every report.

Royalty - A fixed percentage of a mine's revenue that goes to an outside holder rather than to the company, paid off the top - before costs, before debt, before shareholders see anything. It was sold once, usually years earlier, to raise cash. It runs for the life of the mine unless the company buys it back, which is possible only where the original agreement allows it at a set price or where the holder agrees to sell. Because it is charged on revenue and not on profit, it is still owed in a year when the mine loses money.

Stream - Not a percentage of revenue but a claim on the metal itself. An outside party paid cash up front, often to help build the mine, in exchange for the right to receive a set share of the metal produced and to pay only a small fixed fraction of the market price for it - sometimes as little as a tenth or a fifth. The gap between that fixed price and the real price is the cost to the company, and it widens as metal prices rise. Like a royalty, a stream runs for the life of the mine unless bought back, which is possible only under the original terms or by agreement with the holder.

The Story

One paragraph in plain words: what the company is, what it owns, and the central finding. If you read nothing else, read this.

INVESTMENT COMMITTEE SUMMARY (July 31, 2026). Tectonic is the project's best-funded pre-resource explorer and its most institutionally validated one: the Flat Gold Project - 99,840 acres of Doyon-owned land in southwestern Alaska near Donlin, a twenty-plus-kilometre volcano-plutonic complex with six kilometre-scale intrusion targets, five gold-confirmed - anchored by Chicken Mountain's 100% drill success across 191 holes into a bulk-tonnage, heap-leachable, free-milling system with recoveries up to 96%. The 2026 campaign is the company's largest ever: 40,000 metres on five rigs behind a roughly C$100 million treasury, aimed at a MAIDEN RESOURCE at Chicken Mountain in the first quarter of 2027 and a preliminary economic assessment behind it. The structure is the deeper asset: Doyon - the Alaska Native regional corporation that OWNS the land - is one of the largest shareholders, and Crescat Capital leads the register. The underwriting prices a near-fair explorer whose treasury floors most of the quote and whose resource date answers the only question that matters.

Where narrative text carries an older share price, the tables and the refreshed dated close above govern.

The valuation-to-action bridge lands near fair with a cash floor: modelled value sits within a few percent of the quote at the dated spot and long-term cases, modestly below at base and stress, and above only at upside - while the treasury alone covers roughly 60% of the capitalization, making this the most downside-cushioned explorer in the project. The market is paying a modest premium over cash-plus-benchmark for the 191-hole success rate and the Doyon structure - a defensible price for optionality with a dated answer. The action bridge is the Q1 2027 maiden resource: the number that converts benchmark ounces into classified ones.

22. Thesis-break framework [Complete · score 3 (of 10; 1 = best)]
The thesis-break conditions are dated: the maiden resource disappointing against the bulk-tonnage framing (grade or contiguity below heap-leach viability), the Q1 2027 date slipping meaningfully (it has already moved once, from a 2026 target - disclosed, and priced here), or the 40,000-metre campaign burning the treasury without commensurate footprint growth. The structural break would be metallurgical: heap-leach recoveries failing to reproduce at resource scale would remove the low-capital pathway that IS the investment case.

26. Peer-group methodology [Complete · score 3 (of 10; 1 = best)]
The peer frame is pre-resource Alaska-Yukon gold systems and the RIRGS family specifically - the geological cousin of the team's own Coffee project - benchmarked between raw target acreage and BYN-class multi-million-ounce resources. In-project, the calibration pair is exact: BYN holds 8.62 million Yukon ounces at roughly C$53 of enterprise value per ounce, and this model's pre-resource benchmark sits deliberately below that, converging toward it only as classification arrives on the staircase.

27. Jurisdiction, fiscal regime, and permitting [Complete · score 3 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Real, exceptionally well-documented and distinctive land-tenure structure: the 99,800-99,840-acre Flat Gold Project sits on land predominantly owned by Doyon, Limited, one of Alaska's largest Native Regional Corporations - and Doyon is itself Tectonic's second-largest shareholder, a genuine landowner-shareholder alignment structure not seen in this exact form at any other company reviewed in this project, directly relevant to permitting and community-relations risk. Alaska itself is characterized by the company as "one of the world's most mining-friendly jurisdictions."

28. Environmental liability, reclamation, closure, and tailings [Complete · score 3 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Environmental obligations are early and being built deliberately: an integrated Environmental Baseline Study program was initiated with the 2025 season explicitly to support long-term planning - the correct pre-permitting move, started years early - and the private-land setting under Doyon ownership changes the eventual permitting architecture (Alaska Native corporation land involves ANCSA frameworks rather than purely federal public-land process). Placer-era historical disturbance exists in the district. No environmental proceeding or incident was identified.

29. Reserve/resource quality [Complete · score 4 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Resource quality is pre-classification by definition, and the drill evidence is unusually strong for the stage: 100% of 191 holes at Chicken Mountain mineralized, free-milling metallurgy with heap recoveries up to 96% in test work, Alpha Bowl adding a second style (65.5 metres at 1.2 g/t including 21.7 g/t; follow-up 41.15 metres at 2.23 including 13.25) - but no compliant resource exists until the first-quarter 2027 estimate, and this workbook's ounce assumptions are SOFT until then. The score is the honest average of exceptional drill statistics and zero classified ounces.

30. Exploration effectiveness [Complete · score 3 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Real, exceptionally extensive, high-grade, and multi-target 2025 exploration results: a record 18,372 metres drilled across 125 holes at Flat; a 4.05 g/t gold intercept over 30.48 metres (including 8.84 g/t over 13.72 metres) at the Adit Zone, part of a 550-metre-wide open mineralized corridor; a separate 4.50 g/t intercept over 48.77 metres (including 7.79 g/t over 24.38 metres) at a new target; and first-ever drilling at the Black Creek Intrusion, six kilometres north of Chicken Mountain, which returned high-grade gold and validated a genuine multi-intrusion gold system across the property - a real, dense, and geologically significant body of results.

Flat is 100%-owned by the company; the real, distinctive landowner relationship with Doyon, Limited (metric 27) is a surface/community arrangement rather than a mineral-rights encumbrance, and no material JV or royalty was identified this pass.

Social licence is the structure itself and the strongest explorer specimen in the project: the landowner IS a shareholder - Doyon, one of Alaska's largest Native regional corporations, owns the 99,840 acres AND sits among the company's largest holders, aligning the community's economics with the drill program at the capitalization level rather than through agreements alone. Consent is not being negotiated; it is capitalized. The obligation this creates is permanent performance in the relationship, and the joint public presentation of the project by both parties evidences its current health.

Disclosure practice is high-cadence explorer communication: assay-by-assay reporting with intercept detail, program launches with stated pillars and metreage, the resource-date change disclosed plainly, metallurgical results published with recovery figures, and dual TSXV/OTCQB reporting. The promotional register is strong ('The Shift', tier-one framing) and netted out by this framework; beneath it the operational disclosure is complete and dated.

Flat is located approximately 40 kilometres from Novagold's Donlin Gold Project, the fifth-largest undeveloped gold deposit - real, specific, favorable regional context suggesting some degree of shared district infrastructure and industry attention, though Tectonic's own site infrastructure needs were not independently reviewed this pass.

Glossary - every term, in plain words (tap to open)

Estimated value - What our model calculates one share is worth from documented evidence at a stated metal price and date. An estimate, not a prediction of where the stock will trade.

Cautious value (safety floor) - The deliberately careful of the two published values: stress-grade assumptions throughout. If the price is below even this number, the discount needs no generosity to see.

Fair value (market-based) - The second published value: what the company is worth using the yardstick the market actually applies to companies of this type across the Roster, with growth on its documented calendar. The verdict keys to this value.

Discount / premium at today's price - The gap between an estimated value and what a share costs today. Green (discount) = the share costs less than the value. Red (premium) = the price already exceeds the value.

Share price - What the market currently charges for one share, always shown with the date of the quote.

Trading below / near / above estimated value - The relationship between price and FAIR value. Below = the market charges less than the estimate (a discount). Above = the price already assumes future events (a pre-payment). Near = within a few percent.

The five-case deck - Value computed at five fixed cases of the company's own commodity price - Stress, Conservative Base, the dated Spot, Long-Term Normalized, Upside. We never forecast the metal; you bring your own view.

Value milestones - A calendar of dated events. Value steps only when an event lands and its inputs are released; the share price line is never forecast. Each step is a checkable claim.

Catalyst - A dated, verifiable event - a study, a permit, a financing - that releases new model inputs.

Pre-payment - When today's price already contains tomorrow's documents. Not automatically bad - but you should know you are doing it.

Quality tier / recalibrated rank - Company quality alone, from a 7-factor panel, placed on a 1-10 ladder where the Roster median is 5.0. It deliberately ignores price.

Symposium Top - The highest quality tier on the Roster ladder - the best-evidenced enterprises among an already elite set.

The Roster - The fixed set of companies covered - the presenting companies of a leading annual natural-resource investing symposium, itself a pre-selected elite of the roughly 2,000-3,000 mining companies worldwide, so every tier is standing among the select.

Release gate - A report is published only when every one of the 52 questions reaches a terminal answer - evidenced, documented as absent, or stage-exempt. No gaps hidden.

SOFT - A figure we could not confirm from a primary source, labeled honestly wherever it is used.

PEA / PFS / FS - The study ladder: Preliminary Economic Assessment (first economics), Pre-Feasibility (engineered), Feasibility (bankable). Each rung earns more credit in the model.

P/NAV (developers) - Price compared to a project's study value. Builders trade below 1.0 before production and re-rate through it as the mine becomes real.

Risk weight - The fraction of a project's study value the model credits today, by stage - small for early studies, larger once permitted and engineered.

AISC - All-in sustaining cost: what it costs to produce one ounce, all-in. The margin is the metal price minus this.

NSR royalty - A share of a mine's revenue off the top. Royalty companies own these instead of operating mines.

Streaming - Buying a mine's future silver or gold at a fixed low price in exchange for money upfront.

Earn-in - A contract where a partner pays for exploration to earn a share of a project - the generator model's engine.

Unanswered question - The one company-specific uncertainty the whole thesis hinges on, named explicitly in every report.

Royalty - A fixed percentage of a mine's revenue that goes to an outside holder rather than to the company, paid off the top - before costs, before debt, before shareholders see anything. It was sold once, usually years earlier, to raise cash. It runs for the life of the mine unless the company buys it back, which is possible only where the original agreement allows it at a set price or where the holder agrees to sell. Because it is charged on revenue and not on profit, it is still owed in a year when the mine loses money.

Stream - Not a percentage of revenue but a claim on the metal itself. An outside party paid cash up front, often to help build the mine, in exchange for the right to receive a set share of the metal produced and to pay only a small fixed fraction of the market price for it - sometimes as little as a tenth or a fifth. The gap between that fixed price and the real price is the cost to the company, and it widens as metal prices rise. Like a royalty, a stream runs for the life of the mine unless bought back, which is possible only under the original terms or by agreement with the holder.

The Story

One paragraph in plain words: what the company is, what it owns, and the central finding. If you read nothing else, read this.

INVESTMENT COMMITTEE SUMMARY (July 31, 2026). Honey Badger Silver just executed the tier's boldest move: in April it closed the acquisition of Canadian Zinc Corporation from Resource Capital Fund VI, taking 100% of PRAIRIE CREEK ('the PC Silver Mine') in the Northwest Territories - one of the world's highest-grade undeveloped silver-zinc-lead deposits, PERMITTED for underground mining, carrying decades of built infrastructure, Indigenous-government agreements along the project and its transport corridor, and a C$25 million federal National Trade Corridor road grant - funded by a C$11.5 million subscription-receipt raise at sixteen cents. JDS Energy & Mining is authoring an updated PEA and resource estimate targeted for Q3 2026, the study that converts a historic frame into current economics. Around it sit eight northern silver properties (Sunrise Lake, Plata's antimony-copper-tungsten, Clear Lake, Nanisivik, Hy's indium-bismuth) and 10,000 ounces of physical silver yielding 12% from Monetary Metals. The workbook's central finding is the metric-12 tension made explicit: the shares rose roughly 474% in a year against small financings, and the model sits BELOW the C$0.57 quote at every silver case - the deepest pre-document pre-payment in the explorer cohort, redeemed only if the Q3 study prints at the scale the price assumes.

Where narrative text carries an older share price, the tables and the refreshed dated close above govern.

Three dates govern this page: the share price is the dated close shown above (2026-07-24); the evidence and estimated values are from this company's last full underwriting (2026-07-31), and change only when the company publishes something - each document's own date is listed under References; a daily event scan watches this company's filings and releases and queues a re-underwriting when one lands.

The Question the Thesis Hinges On

Single greatest company-specific uncertainty identified as sustaining an extraordinary share-price run (roughly +474% over the trailing 12 months) against real, repeated, ongoing dilution from multiple financings in the same period - a real tension between rewarding early shareholders and continuing to fund a still pre-production, multi-pronged strategy.

In-project, the batch contrast is exact: AGAG offers the cohort's best grade at a one-document premium, this file offers a permitted mine at an all-cases premium - the same silver tape pricing two very different distances ahead of the documents.

Projects sit in Northern Canada (including the Northwest Territories, per the PC Silver Mine location) - a real, low-political-risk jurisdiction; the company itself describes its focus as areas "with a long history of mining in Northern Canada," though no material jurisdictional dispute or benefit was independently confirmed this pass.

28. Environmental liability, reclamation, closure, and tailings [Complete · score 3 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Environmental obligations are inherited-and-permitted: Prairie Creek carries operating-class permits (Type A water licence lineage) from the prior owners' completed processes within the Nahanni region's uniquely sensitive setting - the national park surrounds the property - making the file's environmental position simultaneously its strongest credential (permits exist where permitting is hardest) and its standing obligation set (care, maintenance and the road corridor's conditions). No proceeding was identified.

29. Reserve/resource quality [Complete · score 4 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Resource quality is world-class-by-history and uncurrent-by-category: Prairie Creek's historic base grades among the highest silver-zinc-lead endowments anywhere undeveloped, defined by decades of drilling and underground development - but the CURRENT compliant statement awaits the JDS update, and the portfolio properties (Sunrise Lake, Plata, Clear Lake, Nanisivik) carry historic figures of their own. Scored for the category gap the Q3 study exists to close; the geology itself is the acquisition's justification.

30. Exploration effectiveness [Complete · score 7 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Exploration effectiveness not reviewed this pass. [Calibration-panel score assigned Aug 1, 2026 from the evidence in this note and cross-referenced workbook facts; status unchanged.]

31. Ownership, royalties, streams, and joint ventures [Complete · score 2 (of 10; 1 = best)]
A real, genuinely distinctive and unusual business-model element beyond conventional exploration ownership: the company holds a 10,000 oz silver loan arrangement with Monetary Metals, yielding 12% annually paid in physical silver, with the underlying silver purchased at $52/oz - a real, specific, dated, yield-bearing silver-lending structure not seen at any other company reviewed in this entire project, positioning the company partly as a silver-linked financial-yield vehicle alongside its exploration and resource-management activities.

32. Commodity-price, FX, and inflation assumption governance [Complete · score 4 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Assumption governance strains at the tier's limits: historic figures are labeled historic and the study is properly commissioned with a named lead author and date - genuine discipline - while the promotional register (the physical-silver yield framing, the critical-minerals releases at early-stage properties, the acquisition superlatives) runs hotter than the document base beneath it. The workbook's SOFT labels on shares, frames and rates are its own governance response.

33. Tax, royalties, and fiscal losses [Complete · score 2 (of 10; 1 = best)]
The fiscal frame is northern-Canadian favorable: NWT territorial and federal tax, Indigenous-government agreements structuring benefit-sharing along the project and corridor, and the C$25 million National Trade Corridor grant as direct federal capital participation in the access road - a fiscal posture where government is a funding partner before it is a tax collector. No dispute was identified.

No production exists yet, so there is no depletion/replacement bridge to build.

No operating history exists yet to assess operating reliability.

36. Safety, workforce, and labor [Not Applicable - Operator's Risk]
Pre-restart study stage: workforce exposure is care-and-maintenance and program scale under contractor management. The metric activates at development.

37. Community relations and social licence [Complete · score 2 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Social licence is the acquisition's inherited crown: agreements with the Indigenous governments of the project area and the transportation corridor - negotiated over the prior owners' decades in the Nahanni region, among Canada's most consultation-intensive settings - transferred with the asset, alongside the federal road grant that itself evidences multi-government alignment. The current owner's task is stewardship of arrangements it did not build; no friction was identified in the sources reviewed.

38. Disclosure quality, reporting integrity, and governance [Complete · score 4 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Disclosure practice is promotional-forward with real documents underneath: the acquisition papered fully (consideration, receipts, warrants, escrow mechanics all published), the JDS engagement announced with author, scope and date, the physical-silver arrangement disclosed to its yield terms - while the news cadence (critical-minerals recognitions at multiple early properties within weeks) reads as momentum maintenance. The workbook scores the register's heat honestly and relies on the filed record.

39. Infrastructure, utilities, logistics, and business continuity [Complete · score 3 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Infrastructure is the acquisition's tangible core: Prairie Creek's built underground development, mill-site facilities and camp from the prior owners' construction era, the winter-road corridor with its Indigenous agreements, and the C$25 million federal grant advancing the all-season access solution that was always the project's binding constraint. Remote-NWT logistics remain the permanent cost fact; the difference between this file and greenfield peers is that the spending mostly already happened.

No cybersecurity or operational-technology disclosure was located in the sources reviewed - the standard absence at this scale.

No hedging was identified. The counterparty inventory is distinctive for the tier: Resource Capital Fund as acquisition counterparty (a sophisticated seller - a fact the price-setting metric weighs), Monetary Metals as the physical-silver yield counterparty (10,000 ounces at 12%, purchased near US$52 - an unusual instrument whose lease-yield mechanics the workbook flags rather than glorifies), the JDS study contract, and the federal grant's conditions. Each is disclosed; the seller's identity is the quiet diligence question.

No operating working capital cycle exists yet for a pre-revenue explorer.

Real, repeated, well-documented dilution across at least four separate financings identified within roughly a seven-month window (December 2025 through May 2026), with share count growth in the range of 24-51% depending on the exact comparison dates used across sources - a real, significant, and clearly disclosed pattern; value-creation-per-share and dilution-efficiency calculations per the sharpened requirement for this metric were not built this pass.

No metal is being sold yet from mining operations, so there are no revenue-realization or offtake terms to assess in the traditional sense, though the Monetary Metals silver loan (metric 31) does generate a real, physical-silver-denominated yield.

49. Forecast governance and model governance [Complete · score 4 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Forecast governance is one promise deep: the acquisition closed as announced (the record's kept promise), and everything else now hangs on the Q3 2026 JDS study date - publicly stated, externally authored, and the single test that matters. The prior operators' history is a cautionary archive of Prairie Creek timelines missed; the current owner's defense is that its promise is a study, not a mine. The workbook stakes its staircase entirely on that one date.

Real, specific, disclosed insider alignment: Executive Chairman Chad Williams personally participated in a December 2025 private placement for up to CAD $1,000,000 of units - a real, named, meaningful individual capital commitment by a senior insider, not merely a stated intention.

The corporate structure absorbed a transformation: the TSXV parent now holds Canadian Zinc Corporation (Prairie Creek) beneath it alongside the eight-property northern portfolio and the physical-silver position, with the receipt-and-warrant capital layers above. No debt was identified. The structure is young in its current form; the metric's watch item is how cleanly the CZC subsidiary's historical obligations were ring-fenced in the purchase.

52. Reserve-price sensitivity, cut-off migration, and economic-envelope robustness [Complete · score 4 (of 10; 1 = best)]
The economic envelope is entirely prospective: Prairie Creek's historic economics (prior-era studies showed robust high-grade underground margins repeatedly undone by capital and access costs) await the JDS restatement at current silver, zinc and lead prices - which is precisely the study's thesis, since the metals that broke past attempts have doubled and tripled. The envelope question is not grade; it is whether current prices finally clear the remoteness premium, and no current document yet says so.

53. Technical-report currency, competent-person reliance, and study obsolescence [Complete · score 5 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Technical currency is the discount's core: NO current compliant resource or economic study exists for the flagship this pass - the historic base and prior-era studies are superseded-in-waiting, and the JDS PEA-and-MRE (Q3 2026 target) is the file's entire document future compressed into one deliverable. Scored at the maximum currency deduction; the cure is dated and commissioned, which is the one mitigant.

No production exists yet, so there is no model-to-mine reconciliation to perform.

55. Water balance, water security, climate resilience, and extreme weather [Complete · score 3 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Water and climate exposure is Nahanni-northern: the permitted water-licence lineage governs discharge in a nationally sensitive watershed, winter-road climate dependence is the classic NWT operating risk the all-season road solution addresses, and the care-and-maintenance site carries established water management. The permits' existence in THIS watershed is the environmental file's proof of concept.

56. Tailings-facility integrity, geotechnical stability, and emergency preparedness [Complete · score 4 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Tailings and storage design belongs to the coming study: the built site includes the prior era's waste and water infrastructure under permit, the underground mining method limits surface tailings scale by design, and the JDS work will restate the storage plan to current standards. No facility-level consequence disclosure was located; the historic site's condition under care and maintenance was not independently evidenced this pass.

57. Valuation-method hierarchy, asset-level NAV governance, discount-rate discipline, and double-counting prevention [Complete · score 3 (of 10; 1 = best)]
The valuation hierarchy is explicit and deliberately severe: Prairie Creek's historic silver-equivalent frame at a SOFT per-ounce rate (elevated for permits and infrastructure, discounted for category), small portfolio frames, the physical silver, all scaling with the metal, plus treasury - with the road grant's value, the critical-minerals angles, the JDS study itself and every restart scenario carried at ZERO as the anti-double-counting offset, released only on the dated staircase. When the Q3 study lands, this model is designed to be discarded for its arithmetic.

58. Underwriting conclusion governance, recommendation authorization, confidence calibration, and report-release control [Complete · score 4 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Conclusion governance is satisfied for release with the cohort's heaviest caveat load: every scored metric resolved, the SOFT share count, frames and rates all labeled, the promotional-register and price-run findings stated rather than smoothed, and the verdict - a genuinely excellent asset acquired boldly, priced by the market at all-cases-above-model months before its first current document - carried identically in summary, bridge and hierarchy. Authorized with the Q3 2026 JDS delivery as the single standing checkpoint on which the entire underwriting turns.

59. Management track record and role-specific competence [Complete · score 7 (of 10; 1 = best)]
The weakest management-track-record evidence in the project, stated plainly. The pedigree at the top is real - Executive Chairman Chad Williams founded Red Cloud and previously ran Victoria Gold - but the company's own record is aggregation and promotion rather than delivery: eight 100%-owned northern Canada silver properties whose headline ounces are historical estimates, not current mineral resources (Sunrise Lake 12.8 Moz indicated + 13.9 Moz inferred historic; Clear Lake 5.5 Moz historic; Nanisivik a land position); the company's own materials describe the portfolio inconsistently (an estimated 500 Moz AgEq in one place, 150 Moz in another); the 2026 news flow consists largely of re-reading old assay data for critical-minerals angles (antimony at Plata in January, indium-bismuth-tungsten at Hy in February) rather than new drilling; the CEO seat has churned (Dusty Nicol appointed February 2024, releases now voiced by the Executive Chairman, and the January 2026 director slate does not include a standing CEO); and financing arrives in small tranches. A May 2026 acquisition of a permitted polymetallic project is the one recent asset-level step. Nothing here is improper - but on a metric that scores demonstrated delivery, a portfolio of un-validated historical ounces held by a promotion-forward micro-cap earns the bottom of this project's distribution.

Glossary - every term, in plain words (tap to open)

Estimated value - What our model calculates one share is worth from documented evidence at a stated metal price and date. An estimate, not a prediction of where the stock will trade.

Cautious value (safety floor) - The deliberately careful of the two published values: stress-grade assumptions throughout. If the price is below even this number, the discount needs no generosity to see.

Fair value (market-based) - The second published value: what the company is worth using the yardstick the market actually applies to companies of this type across the Roster, with growth on its documented calendar. The verdict keys to this value.

Discount / premium at today's price - The gap between an estimated value and what a share costs today. Green (discount) = the share costs less than the value. Red (premium) = the price already exceeds the value.

Share price - What the market currently charges for one share, always shown with the date of the quote.

Trading below / near / above estimated value - The relationship between price and FAIR value. Below = the market charges less than the estimate (a discount). Above = the price already assumes future events (a pre-payment). Near = within a few percent.

The five-case deck - Value computed at five fixed cases of the company's own commodity price - Stress, Conservative Base, the dated Spot, Long-Term Normalized, Upside. We never forecast the metal; you bring your own view.

Value milestones - A calendar of dated events. Value steps only when an event lands and its inputs are released; the share price line is never forecast. Each step is a checkable claim.

Catalyst - A dated, verifiable event - a study, a permit, a financing - that releases new model inputs.

Pre-payment - When today's price already contains tomorrow's documents. Not automatically bad - but you should know you are doing it.

Quality tier / recalibrated rank - Company quality alone, from a 7-factor panel, placed on a 1-10 ladder where the Roster median is 5.0. It deliberately ignores price.

Symposium Top - The highest quality tier on the Roster ladder - the best-evidenced enterprises among an already elite set.

The Roster - The fixed set of companies covered - the presenting companies of a leading annual natural-resource investing symposium, itself a pre-selected elite of the roughly 2,000-3,000 mining companies worldwide, so every tier is standing among the select.

Release gate - A report is published only when every one of the 52 questions reaches a terminal answer - evidenced, documented as absent, or stage-exempt. No gaps hidden.

SOFT - A figure we could not confirm from a primary source, labeled honestly wherever it is used.

PEA / PFS / FS - The study ladder: Preliminary Economic Assessment (first economics), Pre-Feasibility (engineered), Feasibility (bankable). Each rung earns more credit in the model.

P/NAV (developers) - Price compared to a project's study value. Builders trade below 1.0 before production and re-rate through it as the mine becomes real.

Risk weight - The fraction of a project's study value the model credits today, by stage - small for early studies, larger once permitted and engineered.

AISC - All-in sustaining cost: what it costs to produce one ounce, all-in. The margin is the metal price minus this.

NSR royalty - A share of a mine's revenue off the top. Royalty companies own these instead of operating mines.

Streaming - Buying a mine's future silver or gold at a fixed low price in exchange for money upfront.

Earn-in - A contract where a partner pays for exploration to earn a share of a project - the generator model's engine.

Unanswered question - The one company-specific uncertainty the whole thesis hinges on, named explicitly in every report.

Royalty - A fixed percentage of a mine's revenue that goes to an outside holder rather than to the company, paid off the top - before costs, before debt, before shareholders see anything. It was sold once, usually years earlier, to raise cash. It runs for the life of the mine unless the company buys it back, which is possible only where the original agreement allows it at a set price or where the holder agrees to sell. Because it is charged on revenue and not on profit, it is still owed in a year when the mine loses money.

Stream - Not a percentage of revenue but a claim on the metal itself. An outside party paid cash up front, often to help build the mine, in exchange for the right to receive a set share of the metal produced and to pay only a small fixed fraction of the market price for it - sometimes as little as a tenth or a fifth. The gap between that fixed price and the real price is the cost to the company, and it widens as metal prices rise. Like a royalty, a stream runs for the life of the mine unless bought back, which is possible only under the original terms or by agreement with the holder.

The Story

One paragraph in plain words: what the company is, what it owns, and the central finding. If you read nothing else, read this.

IC summary: America's uranium platform at its production inflection - fiscal Q3 2026 (ended April 30) delivered the commencement of production at Burke Hollow, the largest US greenfield ISR project to enter production in more than a decade, joining the ramping Christensen Ranch operation as the second of three hub-and-spoke platforms; the balance sheet holds $794M of liquid assets with NO debt; Sweetwater advances under the federal FAST-41 fast-track (Plan of Operations through BLM completeness and public comment); a 34,000 m conversion program feeds the Roughrider PFS in the Athabasca; and the UR&C launch positions the company as America's only vertically integrated miner-to-conversion platform. The honest arithmetic: quarterly output (32,195 lbs in Q3 at $54.61 total cost) remains a rounding error against 12.1M lbs/yr of licensed capacity and a $4.68B market cap - the market pays a strategic-American premium above conservative platform value in every deck case, and the staircase prices the ramp that must close the gap.

Where narrative text carries an older share price, the tables and the refreshed dated close above govern.

Three dates govern this page: the share price is the dated close shown above (2026-07-31); the evidence and estimated values are from this company's last full underwriting (2026-07-31), and change only when the company publishes something - each document's own date is listed under References; a daily event scan watches this company's filings and releases and queues a re-underwriting when one lands.

The Question the Thesis Hinges On

Single greatest company-specific uncertainty identified as U.S. trade/national-security policy risk: uranium was formally added to the U.S. Geological Survey Critical Minerals List in November 2025, and an active Section 232 investigation (with a status report due July 13, 2026) could result in import-price mechanisms or other trade remedies. Unlike any gold/silver company reviewed, UEC's commercial outlook is directly entangled with an active federal trade-policy process.
