Reserve/resource movement: a ~290M lb North American resource platform (US ISR portfolio plus the high-grade Roughrider) with the LIVE movement being conversion - 34,000 m of core drilling targeting inferred-to-indicated upgrades for the Roughrider PFS.

12. Principal uncertainty [Complete · score 1 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Single greatest company-specific uncertainty identified as U.S. trade/national-security policy risk: uranium was formally added to the U.S. Geological Survey Critical Minerals List in November 2025, and an active Section 232 investigation (with a status report due July 13, 2026) could result in import-price mechanisms or other trade remedies. Unlike any gold/silver company reviewed, UEC's commercial outlook is directly entangled with an active federal trade-policy process.

13. Management guidance credibility [Complete · score 2 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Company is mid-transition from developer to producer: fiscal 2025 revenue of $66.8M compares to essentially no revenue previously; production has ramped through several disclosed milestones (Christensen Ranch restart, Burke Hollow completion and start-up) largely on the company's own disclosed schedule, though this is company-reported progress against internally set milestones rather than externally set guidance in the AEM/PAAS sense.

14. Mine-by-mine operating quality [Complete · score 2 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Real, specific unit-cost detail for the Christensen Ranch operation: Total Cost per Pound of $39.30 including a Cash Cost per Pound of $32.40, across 276,516 lbs since commissioning - genuine, asset-specific cost data, though from a still-small production base relative to the company's licensed capacity.

15. Cost quality [Complete · score 2 (of 10; 1 = best)]
ISR (in-situ recovery) is a structurally lower-cost, lower-environmental-footprint extraction method than conventional hard-rock mining - no tailings, no waste rock, no crushing/milling - which shows up directly in the low disclosed cost per pound (metric 14) relative to conventional uranium mining. This is a real, method-driven cost and risk difference the canonical spec (written with hard-rock gold framing) does not explicitly anticipate.

16. Development-project underwriting [Complete · score 2 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Multiple real, dated construction milestones: Burke Hollow ISR project construction finalized and production commenced in fiscal Q3 2026 ("America's largest greenfield ISR project to enter production in more than a decade" per the company); four new header houses completed at Christensen Ranch; Ludeman project delineation drilling (240 holes) completed, advancing toward construction as a third ISR mine. The Roughrider project in Canada (conventional, high-grade, Athabasca Basin) has a separate Initial Economic Assessment showing $946M post-tax NPV, 40% IRR, and AISC of $20.48/lb - a materially different asset type and economics within the same company.

17. Balance-sheet resilience [Complete · score 2 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Reported $818 million of liquid assets and no debt as of a Q2 FY2026 data point - an exceptionally strong, debt-free balance sheet for a company still in a production ramp-up phase, though FY2025 net income was reported as -$87.7 million, reflecting the cost of scaling operations ahead of full production.

18. Capital allocation [Complete · score 3 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Capital allocation: no dividend or buyback - every dollar to wellfields, plants, permits and the UR&C build-out; correct for a platform whose value case is capacity, not yield.

19. Run-rate normalization [Complete · score 3 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Reported-to-sustainable: the gap IS the analysis - quarterly production of 32-46k lbs against licensed capacity of 12.1M lbs/yr; the sustainable run-rate is whatever the wellfield-and-approval cadence proves, which is exactly what the next four quarters exist to demonstrate; commissioning-to-date costs ($39.30 total across 276,516 lbs) lead the domestic industry.

20. Formal scenario architecture [Complete · score 2 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Shared five-case deck applied through the platform-NAV adaptation with the loudest convention flag in the universe: uranium scaled proportionally to GOLD for cross-cohort comparability only - the metals do not co-move, and the reader is told so twice.

21. Valuation-to-action bridge [Complete · score 2 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Valuation-to-action bridge - the fourth expensive-quality marquee: conservative platform value sits below the US$9.46 price in every deck case (spot US$7.34, -22.4%; base US$6.40, -32.3%), with even the +3-5yr success staircase reaching US$10.48 (+10.8%) only at spot-level pricing. The premium has a name: American strategic positioning (FAST-41, UR&C, policy tailwinds) that conservative appraisal cannot count. The action question is whether policy premium is durable value or sentiment. 22. Thesis-break framework [Complete · score 3 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Thesis-break conditions: the company itself names regulatory approval timing as the ramp constraint (header-house approvals drove the Q3 cost spike); a uranium price retreat hits an unhedged book directly; the falsifiable core is pounds - four quarters without a visible ramp toward seven figures annually breaks the platform premium.

26. Peer-group methodology [Complete · score 3 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Peers: US ISR producers (enCore, Ur-Energy, Peninsula) - UEC is the largest by resources, capacity and treasury, and the richest-rated per current pound produced; the premium is the bet that licensed American capacity is the scarcest asset in the fuel cycle.

27. Jurisdiction, fiscal regime, and permitting [Complete · score 2 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Operations span Wyoming, Texas (both ISR, U.S. federal/state nuclear and mining regulatory oversight), and Saskatchewan, Canada (conventional, Athabasca Basin) - a genuinely different regulatory mix than any gold/silver company reviewed, given uranium mining requires nuclear-specific regulatory approvals (e.g. NRC-related licensing in the U.S.) in addition to standard mining permits.

28. Environmental liability, reclamation, closure, and tailings [Complete · score 3 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Environmental/closure: ISR's favorable surface profile with groundwater restoration as the defining obligation - standard, bonded, and regulator-supervised across Texas and Wyoming; no incidents identified.

29. Reserve/resource quality [Complete · score 3 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Resource quality: the US ISR portfolio is grade-thin but cost-structured for ISR economics; Roughrider is the opposite pole - Athabasca high-grade conventional - giving the platform both ends of the cost curve; asset-by-asset depth deferred to the PFS documents.

30. Exploration effectiveness [Complete · score 3 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Exploration/delineation effectiveness: Ludeman delineation drilling, Burke Hollow's multiple untapped mineralized trends, and the Roughrider conversion program - the platform grows by drilling out what it already controls.

31. Ownership, royalties, streams, and joint ventures [Complete · score 1 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Ownership structure is straightforward: 100%-owned hub-and-spoke platforms in Wyoming and Texas, plus the Roughrider project in Canada; no material joint-venture or royalty encumbrance identified this pass.

32. Commodity-price, FX, and inflation assumption governance [Complete · score 3 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Price governance: the unhedged-spot philosophy IS the price policy - deliberate, disclosed, and consistent for years; no formal internal price deck published; this model's gold-scaling convention flagged as the cross-cohort device it is.

33. Tax, royalties, and fiscal losses [Complete · score 3 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Tax: US federal plus state production taxes - Wyoming's production-based taxes explicitly drove part of the Q3 unit-cost increase, disclosed with the print; no disputes identified.

34. Production profile, depletion, and replacement [Complete · score 3 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Production profile: growth communicated through discrete milestones rather than formal annual guidance - a sector-typical but governance-relevant choice, scored mid and noted at m49; the physical trajectory: two hubs producing, third (Sweetwater) in permitting, targeting a multi-million-pound American platform.

35. Operating reliability [Complete · score 3 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Operating reliability: the disclosed pattern is approval-cadence lumpiness - costs per pound swing with header-house timing rather than operational failure; commissioning-to-date efficiency is the counterevidence; scored mid pending a full ramped year.

36. Safety, workforce, and labor [Complete · score 3 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Safety: EHS leadership prominent in disclosures; no incidents identified; ISR's inherent safety profile (no underground workings, no blasting) is the structural advantage.

37. Community relations and social licence [Complete · score 3 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Community relations: South Texas and Wyoming ranching-country operations with cooperative state-regulator relationships evidenced by the TCEQ approval language; no disputes identified.

38. Disclosure quality, reporting integrity, and governance [Complete · score 3 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Disclosure/governance: NYSE American reporter with clean history; milestone-dense disclosure culture; the no-guidance policy is the notable governance choice, consistent with the unhedged philosophy.

39. Infrastructure, utilities, logistics, and business continuity [Complete · score 3 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Infrastructure: THE moat - three licensed central processing plants (Hobson 4M lbs/yr, Irigaray, Sweetwater 4.1M lbs/yr) in a country that has licensed almost nothing new for decades; hub-and-spoke design lets satellite deposits feed sunk-cost hubs.

40. Cybersecurity, operational technology, and data integrity [Not Available - Documented]
Cybersecurity posture not disclosed in sources reviewed; documented as unavailable.

41. Hedging, derivatives, and counterparty risk [Complete · score 2 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Company explicitly describes an "unhedged strategy" for uranium sales - a deliberate, stated policy choice (not an oversight) to retain full exposure to rising uranium prices, evidenced by a realized sale price of $101/lb in one disclosed quarter. This is real, dated, and a clear strategic stance, unlike the more routine hedging programs seen at gold producers.

42. Working capital, cash conversion, and liquidity quality [Complete · score 3 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Cash conversion: pre-scale by design - the liquid book funds wellfields, permits and UR&C; the conversion question resolves as pounds scale against the industry-leading commissioning cost base.

Dilution is the honest structural wart: the company was BUILT on chronic at-the-market equity issuance (~495M shares today) - historically accretive per share through acquisitions at cycle lows, but a permanent feature the unhedged model requires; scored 4 as a fact, not a scandal.

44. Debt structure, covenants, and refinancing [Complete · score 1 (of 10; 1 = best)]
No debt reported as of the most recent data point reviewed - effectively no debt-structure risk to assess at this time.

45. Litigation, regulatory, and contingent liabilities [Complete · score 3 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Litigation: none material identified; the operating friction is regulatory queue timing, not disputes; the FAST-41 designation is the counterweight - federal machinery formally accelerating the flagship permit.

Consistent with standard practice, no insurance program terms are disclosed in any public source reviewed this pass.

Three hub-and-spoke platforms (two in Wyoming, one in Texas, plus Roughrider in Canada) provide some geographic diversification within a still-concentrated single-commodity, single-country-dominant (U.S.) production base; a quantified concentration bridge was not built this pass. Revenue realization: unhedged spot sales by explicit strategy - no long-term contract book to disclose because none exists by design; full price exposure both ways, the purest uranium torque in the sector.

Forecast governance: no formal production guidance BY POLICY - milestones instead, and the milestones have landed (Burke Hollow construction, startup, Christensen expansions, FAST-41 steps all delivered as announced); scored mid for the auditable-milestone culture inside a no-numbers frame.

Incentives: founder-CEO Amir Adnani's two-decade build with meaningful ownership; the counter-cyclical acquisition record (Sweetwater from Rio, Roughrider from Rio) is the capital-allocation evidence; compensation not proxy-deep-dived - scored mid.

51. Corporate structure, subsidiary mapping, and entity-level solvency [Complete · score 3 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Structure: Nevada issuer with US operating subsidiaries, Canadian (Roughrider) and Paraguayan (Alto Parana titanium) arms, and the new UR&C entity - a platform structure growing purposefully; no solvency complexity.

52. Reserve-price sensitivity, cut-off migration, and economic-envelope robustness [Complete · score 3 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Reserve-price sensitivity: ISR resources are cut-off-sensitive in principle but the binding sensitivity is the URANIUM PRICE on an unhedged book - the deck convention understates this by tying it to gold; flagged as the model's known blind spot.

53. Technical-report currency, competent-person reliance, and study obsolescence [Complete · score 3 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Technical-report currency: the Roughrider Initial Economic Assessment is recent and being superseded by the PFS in progress - the chain is fresh and improving; US ISR technical reports current per screening.

Reconciliation: wellfield-scale reconciliation is early (commissioning period); the disclosed cost-per-pound series across 276,516 cumulative pounds is the auditable record so far - industry-leading and improving with utilization.

55. Water balance, water security, climate resilience, and extreme weather [Complete · score 3 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Water: ISR IS groundwater management - injection, recovery, restoration under permit; Texas and Wyoming regimes mature; no exceedances identified.

ISR mining does not produce conventional mill tailings or use a tailings storage facility in the way a hard-rock mine does - this metric, as written, does not map cleanly onto this extraction method. The equivalent ISR-specific liability (aquifer restoration post-mining) is a different risk category not directly addressed by this metric.

Valuation governance: platform-NAV model with the appraisal, the liquid book, the share-count caveat and the gold-scaling convention all stated; built to show the strategic premium honestly rather than to justify it. The offsets are structural and enduring: the model was built on nearly two decades of equity-funded land assembly with minimal revenue, the CEO simultaneously chairs GoldMining Inc. and Uranium Royalty Corp (divided attention and a related-company ecosystem), and sustained positive operating cash flow at scale remains the still-unproven step.

Glossary - every term, in plain words (tap to open)

Estimated value - What our model calculates one share is worth from documented evidence at a stated metal price and date. An estimate, not a prediction of where the stock will trade.

Cautious value (safety floor) - The deliberately careful of the two published values: stress-grade assumptions throughout. If the price is below even this number, the discount needs no generosity to see.

Fair value (market-based) - The second published value: what the company is worth using the yardstick the market actually applies to companies of this type across the Roster, with growth on its documented calendar. The verdict keys to this value.

Discount / premium at today's price - The gap between an estimated value and what a share costs today. Green (discount) = the share costs less than the value. Red (premium) = the price already exceeds the value.

Share price - What the market currently charges for one share, always shown with the date of the quote.

Trading below / near / above estimated value - The relationship between price and FAIR value. Below = the market charges less than the estimate (a discount). Above = the price already assumes future events (a pre-payment). Near = within a few percent.

The five-case deck - Value computed at five fixed cases of the company's own commodity price - Stress, Conservative Base, the dated Spot, Long-Term Normalized, Upside. We never forecast the metal; you bring your own view.

Value milestones - A calendar of dated events. Value steps only when an event lands and its inputs are released; the share price line is never forecast. Each step is a checkable claim.

Catalyst - A dated, verifiable event - a study, a permit, a financing - that releases new model inputs.

Pre-payment - When today's price already contains tomorrow's documents. Not automatically bad - but you should know you are doing it.

Quality tier / recalibrated rank - Company quality alone, from a 7-factor panel, placed on a 1-10 ladder where the Roster median is 5.0. It deliberately ignores price.

Symposium Top - The highest quality tier on the Roster ladder - the best-evidenced enterprises among an already elite set.

The Roster - The fixed set of companies covered - the presenting companies of a leading annual natural-resource investing symposium, itself a pre-selected elite of the roughly 2,000-3,000 mining companies worldwide, so every tier is standing among the select.

Release gate - A report is published only when every one of the 52 questions reaches a terminal answer - evidenced, documented as absent, or stage-exempt. No gaps hidden.

SOFT - A figure we could not confirm from a primary source, labeled honestly wherever it is used.

PEA / PFS / FS - The study ladder: Preliminary Economic Assessment (first economics), Pre-Feasibility (engineered), Feasibility (bankable). Each rung earns more credit in the model.

P/NAV (developers) - Price compared to a project's study value. Builders trade below 1.0 before production and re-rate through it as the mine becomes real.

Risk weight - The fraction of a project's study value the model credits today, by stage - small for early studies, larger once permitted and engineered.

AISC - All-in sustaining cost: what it costs to produce one ounce, all-in. The margin is the metal price minus this.

NSR royalty - A share of a mine's revenue off the top. Royalty companies own these instead of operating mines.

Streaming - Buying a mine's future silver or gold at a fixed low price in exchange for money upfront.

Earn-in - A contract where a partner pays for exploration to earn a share of a project - the generator model's engine.

Unanswered question - The one company-specific uncertainty the whole thesis hinges on, named explicitly in every report.

Royalty - A fixed percentage of a mine's revenue that goes to an outside holder rather than to the company, paid off the top - before costs, before debt, before shareholders see anything. It was sold once, usually years earlier, to raise cash. It runs for the life of the mine unless the company buys it back, which is possible only where the original agreement allows it at a set price or where the holder agrees to sell. Because it is charged on revenue and not on profit, it is still owed in a year when the mine loses money.

Stream - Not a percentage of revenue but a claim on the metal itself. An outside party paid cash up front, often to help build the mine, in exchange for the right to receive a set share of the metal produced and to pay only a small fixed fraction of the market price for it - sometimes as little as a tenth or a fifth. The gap between that fixed price and the real price is the cost to the company, and it widens as metal prices rise. Like a royalty, a stream runs for the life of the mine unless bought back, which is possible only under the original terms or by agreement with the holder.

The Story

One paragraph in plain words: what the company is, what it owns, and the central finding. If you read nothing else, read this.

INVESTMENT COMMITTEE SUMMARY (July 31, 2026). Americas Gold and Silver is the project's most aggressively re-rated turnaround: Paul Huet's eighteen-month rebuild of a chronic underperformer into a US silver-and-antimony strategic story - Galena consolidated to 100% in the Eric Sprott transaction, the fully permitted Crescent mine bought nine miles away, a 51/49 antimony-processing joint venture with United States Antimony, the No. 3 Shaft's hoisting capacity doubled, and over US$85 million of variable future obligations bought out this quarter. The market has paid enormously for the story: at roughly US$1.5 billion of capitalization against 3.2-3.6 million ounces of guided silver at US$30-35 all-in costs, the current-state model sits below the share price in every deck case by margins only NICU has matched - the price is a claim on the 2027-2029 platform and on antimony's strategic scarcity, not on this year's mines.

Where narrative text carries an older share price, the tables and the refreshed dated close above govern.

Three dates govern this page: the share price is the dated close shown above (2026-07-31); the evidence and estimated values are from this company's last full underwriting (2026-07-31), and change only when the company publishes something - each document's own date is listed under References; a daily event scan watches this company's filings and releases and queues a re-underwriting when one lands.

Single greatest company-specific uncertainty identified as execution risk across simultaneous growth fronts: ramping the newly-declared-commercial EC120 zone at Cosalá, integrating the newly-acquired Crescent Mine into the Galena Complex, and standing up a new antimony joint venture with United States Antimony - three concurrent growth initiatives for a company of this size.

The Full Underwriting Register - all 52 questions (tap to open)

The same 52 questions are asked of every company. Statuses: Complete = evidenced and scored; Not Available - Documented = the fact does not exist publicly and we say so; Stage-exempt = not applicable to this company type or stage. Figures not confirmed from a primary source are labeled SOFT.

3. Investment Committee decision summary [Complete · score 3 (of 10; 1 = best)]
INVESTMENT COMMITTEE SUMMARY (July 31, 2026). Americas Gold and Silver is the project's most aggressively re-rated turnaround: Paul Huet's eighteen-month rebuild of a chronic underperformer into a US silver-and-antimony strategic story - Galena consolidated to 100% in the Eric Sprott transaction, the fully permitted Crescent mine bought nine miles away, a 51/49 antimony-processing joint venture with United States Antimony, the No. 3 Shaft's hoisting capacity doubled, and over US$85 million of variable future obligations bought out this quarter. The market has paid enormously for the story: at roughly US$1.5 billion of capitalization against 3.2-3.6 million ounces of guided silver at US$30-35 all-in costs, the current-state model sits below the share price in every deck case by margins only NICU has matched - the price is a claim on the 2027-2029 platform and on antimony's strategic scarcity, not on this year's mines.

Glossary - every term, in plain words (tap to open)

Estimated value - What our model calculates one share is worth from documented evidence at a stated metal price and date. An estimate, not a prediction of where the stock will trade.

Cautious value (safety floor) - The deliberately careful of the two published values: stress-grade assumptions throughout. If the price is below even this number, the discount needs no generosity to see.

Fair value (market-based) - The second published value: what the company is worth using the yardstick the market actually applies to companies of this type across the Roster, with growth on its documented calendar. The verdict keys to this value.

Discount / premium at today's price - The gap between an estimated value and what a share costs today. Green (discount) = the share costs less than the value. Red (premium) = the price already exceeds the value.

Share price - What the market currently charges for one share, always shown with the date of the quote.

Trading below / near / above estimated value - The relationship between price and FAIR value. Below = the market charges less than the estimate (a discount). Above = the price already assumes future events (a pre-payment). Near = within a few percent.

The five-case deck - Value computed at five fixed cases of the company's own commodity price - Stress, Conservative Base, the dated Spot, Long-Term Normalized, Upside. We never forecast the metal; you bring your own view.

Value milestones - A calendar of dated events. Value steps only when an event lands and its inputs are released; the share price line is never forecast. Each step is a checkable claim.

Catalyst - A dated, verifiable event - a study, a permit, a financing - that releases new model inputs.

Pre-payment - When today's price already contains tomorrow's documents. Not automatically bad - but you should know you are doing it.

Quality tier / recalibrated rank - Company quality alone, from a 7-factor panel, placed on a 1-10 ladder where the Roster median is 5.0. It deliberately ignores price.

Symposium Top - The highest quality tier on the Roster ladder - the best-evidenced enterprises among an already elite set.

The Roster - The fixed set of companies covered - the presenting companies of a leading annual natural-resource investing symposium, itself a pre-selected elite of the roughly 2,000-3,000 mining companies worldwide, so every tier is standing among the select.

Release gate - A report is published only when every one of the 52 questions reaches a terminal answer - evidenced, documented as absent, or stage-exempt. No gaps hidden.

SOFT - A figure we could not confirm from a primary source, labeled honestly wherever it is used.

PEA / PFS / FS - The study ladder: Preliminary Economic Assessment (first economics), Pre-Feasibility (engineered), Feasibility (bankable). Each rung earns more credit in the model.

P/NAV (developers) - Price compared to a project's study value. Builders trade below 1.0 before production and re-rate through it as the mine becomes real.

Risk weight - The fraction of a project's study value the model credits today, by stage - small for early studies, larger once permitted and engineered.

AISC - All-in sustaining cost: what it costs to produce one ounce, all-in. The margin is the metal price minus this.

NSR royalty - A share of a mine's revenue off the top. Royalty companies own these instead of operating mines.

Streaming - Buying a mine's future silver or gold at a fixed low price in exchange for money upfront.

Earn-in - A contract where a partner pays for exploration to earn a share of a project - the generator model's engine.

Unanswered question - The one company-specific uncertainty the whole thesis hinges on, named explicitly in every report.

Royalty - A fixed percentage of a mine's revenue that goes to an outside holder rather than to the company, paid off the top - before costs, before debt, before shareholders see anything. It was sold once, usually years earlier, to raise cash. It runs for the life of the mine unless the company buys it back, which is possible only where the original agreement allows it at a set price or where the holder agrees to sell. Because it is charged on revenue and not on profit, it is still owed in a year when the mine loses money.

Stream - Not a percentage of revenue but a claim on the metal itself. An outside party paid cash up front, often to help build the mine, in exchange for the right to receive a set share of the metal produced and to pay only a small fixed fraction of the market price for it - sometimes as little as a tenth or a fifth. The gap between that fixed price and the real price is the cost to the company, and it widens as metal prices rise. Like a royalty, a stream runs for the life of the mine unless bought back, which is possible only under the original terms or by agreement with the holder.

References - the documents behind the evidence (tap to open)

The Story

One paragraph in plain words: what the company is, what it owns, and the central finding. If you read nothing else, read this.

INVESTMENT COMMITTEE SUMMARY (July 31, 2026). U.S. GoldMining is the project's carve-out specimen: a Nasdaq-listed single-asset vehicle holding 100% of Whistler in interior Alaska - the gold-copper porphyry district whose PEA (after-tax NPV(5%) of US$2.0 billion, 33% IRR, 2.1-year payback at US$3,200 gold and US$4.50 copper) this project first read from the parent's side, because GoldMining Inc. owns roughly three-quarters of this company and this project underwrote GLDG in wave three. The structure is the story: a tight ~12.4 million-share register gives Whistler a public price of its own, while working capital of US$5.46 million against an at-the-market equity program means the vehicle funds itself dilution by dilution. At US$8.13, the market prices the PEA at roughly a four-percent risk weight - fair for a partnerless, treasury-thin, PEA-stage porphyry a flight from the road system - making this, like Aldebaran, a file whose forward return is documents and structure, not discovery.

Glossary - every term, in plain words (tap to open)

Estimated value - What our model calculates one share is worth from documented evidence at a stated metal price and date. An estimate, not a prediction of where the stock will trade.

Cautious value (safety floor) - The deliberately careful of the two published values: stress-grade assumptions throughout. If the price is below even this number, the discount needs no generosity to see.

Fair value (market-based) - The second published value: what the company is worth using the yardstick the market actually applies to companies of this type across the Roster, with growth on its documented calendar. The verdict keys to this value.

Discount / premium at today's price - The gap between an estimated value and what a share costs today. Green (discount) = the share costs less than the value. Red (premium) = the price already exceeds the value.

Share price - What the market currently charges for one share, always shown with the date of the quote.

Trading below / near / above estimated value - The relationship between price and FAIR value. Below = the market charges less than the estimate (a discount). Above = the price already assumes future events (a pre-payment). Near = within a few percent.

The five-case deck - Value computed at five fixed cases of the company's own commodity price - Stress, Conservative Base, the dated Spot, Long-Term Normalized, Upside. We never forecast the metal; you bring your own view.

Value milestones - A calendar of dated events. Value steps only when an event lands and its inputs are released; the share price line is never forecast. Each step is a checkable claim.

Catalyst - A dated, verifiable event - a study, a permit, a financing - that releases new model inputs.

Pre-payment - When today's price already contains tomorrow's documents. Not automatically bad - but you should know you are doing it.

Quality tier / recalibrated rank - Company quality alone, from a 7-factor panel, placed on a 1-10 ladder where the Roster median is 5.0. It deliberately ignores price.

Symposium Top - The highest quality tier on the Roster ladder - the best-evidenced enterprises among an already elite set.

The Roster - The fixed set of companies covered - the presenting companies of a leading annual natural-resource investing symposium, itself a pre-selected elite of the roughly 2,000-3,000 mining companies worldwide, so every tier is standing among the select.

Release gate - A report is published only when every one of the 52 questions reaches a terminal answer - evidenced, documented as absent, or stage-exempt. No gaps hidden.

SOFT - A figure we could not confirm from a primary source, labeled honestly wherever it is used.

PEA / PFS / FS - The study ladder: Preliminary Economic Assessment (first economics), Pre-Feasibility (engineered), Feasibility (bankable). Each rung earns more credit in the model.

P/NAV (developers) - Price compared to a project's study value. Builders trade below 1.0 before production and re-rate through it as the mine becomes real.

Risk weight - The fraction of a project's study value the model credits today, by stage - small for early studies, larger once permitted and engineered.

AISC - All-in sustaining cost: what it costs to produce one ounce, all-in. The margin is the metal price minus this.

NSR royalty - A share of a mine's revenue off the top. Royalty companies own these instead of operating mines.

Streaming - Buying a mine's future silver or gold at a fixed low price in exchange for money upfront.

Earn-in - A contract where a partner pays for exploration to earn a share of a project - the generator model's engine.

Unanswered question - The one company-specific uncertainty the whole thesis hinges on, named explicitly in every report.

Royalty - A fixed percentage of a mine's revenue that goes to an outside holder rather than to the company, paid off the top - before costs, before debt, before shareholders see anything. It was sold once, usually years earlier, to raise cash. It runs for the life of the mine unless the company buys it back, which is possible only where the original agreement allows it at a set price or where the holder agrees to sell. Because it is charged on revenue and not on profit, it is still owed in a year when the mine loses money.

Stream - Not a percentage of revenue but a claim on the metal itself. An outside party paid cash up front, often to help build the mine, in exchange for the right to receive a set share of the metal produced and to pay only a small fixed fraction of the market price for it - sometimes as little as a tenth or a fifth. The gap between that fixed price and the real price is the cost to the company, and it widens as metal prices rise. Like a royalty, a stream runs for the life of the mine unless bought back, which is possible only under the original terms or by agreement with the holder.

Glossary - every term, in plain words (tap to open)

Estimated value - What our model calculates one share is worth from documented evidence at a stated metal price and date. An estimate, not a prediction of where the stock will trade.

Cautious value (safety floor) - The deliberately careful of the two published values: stress-grade assumptions throughout. If the price is below even this number, the discount needs no generosity to see.

Fair value (market-based) - The second published value: what the company is worth using the yardstick the market actually applies to companies of this type across the Roster, with growth on its documented calendar. The verdict keys to this value.

Discount / premium at today's price - The gap between an estimated value and what a share costs today. Green (discount) = the share costs less than the value. Red (premium) = the price already exceeds the value.

Share price - What the market currently charges for one share, always shown with the date of the quote.

Trading below / near / above estimated value - The relationship between price and FAIR value. Below = the market charges less than the estimate (a discount). Above = the price already assumes future events (a pre-payment). Near = within a few percent.

The five-case deck - Value computed at five fixed cases of the company's own commodity price - Stress, Conservative Base, the dated Spot, Long-Term Normalized, Upside. We never forecast the metal; you bring your own view.

Value milestones - A calendar of dated events. Value steps only when an event lands and its inputs are released; the share price line is never forecast. Each step is a checkable claim.

Catalyst - A dated, verifiable event - a study, a permit, a financing - that releases new model inputs.

Pre-payment - When today's price already contains tomorrow's documents. Not automatically bad - but you should know you are doing it.

Quality tier / recalibrated rank - Company quality alone, from a 7-factor panel, placed on a 1-10 ladder where the Roster median is 5.0. It deliberately ignores price.

Symposium Top - The highest quality tier on the Roster ladder - the best-evidenced enterprises among an already elite set.

The Roster - The fixed set of companies covered - the presenting companies of a leading annual natural-resource investing symposium, itself a pre-selected elite of the roughly 2,000-3,000 mining companies worldwide, so every tier is standing among the select.

Release gate - A report is published only when every one of the 52 questions reaches a terminal answer - evidenced, documented as absent, or stage-exempt. No gaps hidden.

SOFT - A figure we could not confirm from a primary source, labeled honestly wherever it is used.

PEA / PFS / FS - The study ladder: Preliminary Economic Assessment (first economics), Pre-Feasibility (engineered), Feasibility (bankable). Each rung earns more credit in the model.

P/NAV (developers) - Price compared to a project's study value. Builders trade below 1.0 before production and re-rate through it as the mine becomes real.

Risk weight - The fraction of a project's study value the model credits today, by stage - small for early studies, larger once permitted and engineered.

AISC - All-in sustaining cost: what it costs to produce one ounce, all-in. The margin is the metal price minus this.

NSR royalty - A share of a mine's revenue off the top. Royalty companies own these instead of operating mines.

Streaming - Buying a mine's future silver or gold at a fixed low price in exchange for money upfront.

Earn-in - A contract where a partner pays for exploration to earn a share of a project - the generator model's engine.

Unanswered question - The one company-specific uncertainty the whole thesis hinges on, named explicitly in every report.

Royalty - A fixed percentage of a mine's revenue that goes to an outside holder rather than to the company, paid off the top - before costs, before debt, before shareholders see anything. It was sold once, usually years earlier, to raise cash. It runs for the life of the mine unless the company buys it back, which is possible only where the original agreement allows it at a set price or where the holder agrees to sell. Because it is charged on revenue and not on profit, it is still owed in a year when the mine loses money.

Stream - Not a percentage of revenue but a claim on the metal itself. An outside party paid cash up front, often to help build the mine, in exchange for the right to receive a set share of the metal produced and to pay only a small fixed fraction of the market price for it - sometimes as little as a tenth or a fifth. The gap between that fixed price and the real price is the cost to the company, and it widens as metal prices rise. Like a royalty, a stream runs for the life of the mine unless bought back, which is possible only under the original terms or by agreement with the holder.

The Story

One paragraph in plain words: what the company is, what it owns, and the central finding. If you read nothing else, read this.

IC summary: the premier precious-metals streaming company one quarter after its largest-ever transaction - the $4.3B Antamina silver stream from BHP - which lifts 2026 guidance to 860,000-940,000 GEOs (2025 actual: 692,000, itself above guidance) on a stated path to 1,200,000 GEOs by 2030 sustained through 2035. Record Q1 2026: revenue $901M (+92%), net earnings $582M (+129%), operating cash flow $766M (+112%). The purchase was funded with debt: $2.1B pro forma net debt, rapid repayment guided. At US$113.38 the model shows -8.3% at spot - the growth is not yet fully paid for.

Where narrative text carries an older share price, the tables and the refreshed dated close above govern.

Three dates govern this page: the share price is the dated close shown above (2026-07-31); the evidence and estimated values are from this company's last full underwriting (2026-07-31), and change only when the company publishes something - each document's own date is listed under References; a daily event scan watches this company's filings and releases and queues a re-underwriting when one lands.

The Question the Thesis Hinges On

Single greatest company-specific uncertainty identified as counterparty/operator concentration risk layered with the newly announced ~$2.4B of debt-funded growth (BHP Antamina): WPM does not operate any mine itself, so its results depend entirely on third-party operators (Vale at Salobo, BHP/Glencore-related at Antamina, Newmont at Peñasquito) executing well, while WPM simultaneously increases leverage to fund growth. This is a judgment call.

15. Cost quality [Complete · score 3 (of 10; 1 = best)]
2025 average cash cost of $514/GEO (up from $438/GEO in 2024) against a cash operating margin of $3,040/GEO sold, up 53% year-over-year - costs are rising in absolute terms but margin expansion from higher realized metal prices more than offset it. Source: Feb/Mar 2026 year-end results release.

Six development-stage streams identified as under construction/ramp-up (including Blackwater and Goose reaching commercial production in 2025, Platreef and Mineral Park expected online by end of 2025); production guided to grow ~40% to 870,000 GEOs by 2029 and over 950,000 GEOs annually in 2030-2034. Asset-by-asset technical review of each project was not completed this pass. Balance-sheet resilience: deliberately levered at $2.1B net debt post-Antamina with $1.2B liquidity and $766M/quarter operating cash flow - coverage is overwhelming, but the cushion is temporarily thinner than the debt-free royalty peers; scored mid pending the guided rapid paydown.

Record annual dividend of $0.66/share declared for 2025, alongside a stated capital allocation philosophy of funding "only the most accretive opportunities" - evidenced by the recent BHP Antamina and Hemlo stream additions. Both shareholder return and growth reinvestment are documented, though not yet judged against full-cycle outcomes.

Shared five-case deck applied (Stress $2,600 / Base $3,400 / Spot (Jul 31, 2026) $4,050 / LT $4,200 / Upside $5,400) with the streaming adaptation: $700/GEO effective cost per the Q1 print; comparable across the cohort.

Peer set: Franco-Nevada (larger, debt-free, ~40x forward), Royal Gold post-Sandstorm, Triple Flag, OR Royalties; WPM P/E cited ~28.65 - priced between FNV's premium and the mid-tier royalties, with the fastest guided growth of the majors.

Streams span Brazil (Salobo), Peru (Antamina, Constancia), Mexico (Peñasquito, San Dimas), Canada (Goose, Blackwater), and South Africa (Platreef), among others; asset-by-asset jurisdiction/permitting risk was not assessed this pass. [Calibration-panel score assigned Aug 1, 2026 from the evidence in this note and cross-referenced workbook facts; status unchanged.]

28. Environmental liability, reclamation, closure, and tailings [Not Applicable - Operator's Risk]
As a streaming/royalty company, WPM does not operate mines and does not directly carry reclamation, closure, or tailings obligations - those sit with the mine operator (e.g. Vale, Newmont). WPM has indirect counterparty exposure if an operator fails to meet obligations, but this metric applies structurally differently to a streamer than to a producer like AEM. Not independently verified per-asset this pass.

Reserve/resource quality data obtained at the corporate level (see metric 11); asset-by-asset technical quality (cut-off, metallurgy, modifying factors) not reviewed this pass.

30. Exploration effectiveness [Not Applicable - Operator's Risk]
Exploration effectiveness is the operators' function - Wheaton conducts no exploration; its exploration exposure is cost-free optionality on operator ground, the structural point scored at m52. Stage exemption per the royalty/streaming taxonomy.

31. Ownership, royalties, streams, and joint ventures [Complete · score 2 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Ownership structure is the company's entire business model: streams and royalties (Precious Metal Purchase Agreements, "PMPAs") on producing and development assets, most recently including new streams on Antamina (BHP), Hemlo, Spring Valley, Marmato, and Santo Domingo. This is well-documented at the transaction level; a full economic-interest schedule across the entire multi-decade portfolio was not built this pass.

GEO figures are explicitly calculated using disclosed commodity price assumptions: $2,600/oz gold, $30.00/oz silver, $950/oz palladium, $13.50/lb cobalt, consistent with 2025 production guidance assumptions. Source: 2025 Annual Report MD&A.

Tax: the streaming structure's low effective rate (historically single-digit) operates under the framework settled with the CRA in 2018 - the sector's landmark tax case, resolved on terms that preserved the offshore streaming income model; 8% modeled.

Production profile is the sector's strongest growth story: 692k (2025 actual) to 860-940k (2026) to a stated 1.2M GEOs by 2030, sustained at ~1.2M through 2035 - approximately 50% growth on operator capital, only ~3% of 2026 from assets still in construction/ramp.

WPM does not operate mines, so operating reliability is the responsibility of each mine operator, not WPM directly; WPM's own reliability metric is really counterparty delivery performance, which was not separately quantified this pass.

Glossary - every term, in plain words (tap to open)

Estimated value - What our model calculates one share is worth from documented evidence at a stated metal price and date. An estimate, not a prediction of where the stock will trade.

Cautious value (safety floor) - The deliberately careful of the two published values: stress-grade assumptions throughout. If the price is below even this number, the discount needs no generosity to see.

Fair value (market-based) - The second published value: what the company is worth using the yardstick the market actually applies to companies of this type across the Roster, with growth on its documented calendar. The verdict keys to this value.

Discount / premium at today's price - The gap between an estimated value and what a share costs today. Green (discount) = the share costs less than the value. Red (premium) = the price already exceeds the value.

Share price - What the market currently charges for one share, always shown with the date of the quote.

Trading below / near / above estimated value - The relationship between price and FAIR value. Below = the market charges less than the estimate (a discount). Above = the price already assumes future events (a pre-payment). Near = within a few percent.

The five-case deck - Value computed at five fixed cases of the company's own commodity price - Stress, Conservative Base, the dated Spot, Long-Term Normalized, Upside. We never forecast the metal; you bring your own view.

Value milestones - A calendar of dated events. Value steps only when an event lands and its inputs are released; the share price line is never forecast. Each step is a checkable claim.

Catalyst - A dated, verifiable event - a study, a permit, a financing - that releases new model inputs.

Pre-payment - When today's price already contains tomorrow's documents. Not automatically bad - but you should know you are doing it.

Quality tier / recalibrated rank - Company quality alone, from a 7-factor panel, placed on a 1-10 ladder where the Roster median is 5.0. It deliberately ignores price.

Symposium Top - The highest quality tier on the Roster ladder - the best-evidenced enterprises among an already elite set.

The Roster - The fixed set of companies covered - the presenting companies of a leading annual natural-resource investing symposium, itself a pre-selected elite of the roughly 2,000-3,000 mining companies worldwide, so every tier is standing among the select.

Release gate - A report is published only when every one of the 52 questions reaches a terminal answer - evidenced, documented as absent, or stage-exempt. No gaps hidden.

SOFT - A figure we could not confirm from a primary source, labeled honestly wherever it is used.

PEA / PFS / FS - The study ladder: Preliminary Economic Assessment (first economics), Pre-Feasibility (engineered), Feasibility (bankable). Each rung earns more credit in the model.

P/NAV (developers) - Price compared to a project's study value. Builders trade below 1.0 before production and re-rate through it as the mine becomes real.

Risk weight - The fraction of a project's study value the model credits today, by stage - small for early studies, larger once permitted and engineered.

AISC - All-in sustaining cost: what it costs to produce one ounce, all-in. The margin is the metal price minus this.

NSR royalty - A share of a mine's revenue off the top. Royalty companies own these instead of operating mines.

Streaming - Buying a mine's future silver or gold at a fixed low price in exchange for money upfront.

Earn-in - A contract where a partner pays for exploration to earn a share of a project - the generator model's engine.

Unanswered question - The one company-specific uncertainty the whole thesis hinges on, named explicitly in every report.

Royalty - A fixed percentage of a mine's revenue that goes to an outside holder rather than to the company, paid off the top - before costs, before debt, before shareholders see anything. It was sold once, usually years earlier, to raise cash. It runs for the life of the mine unless the company buys it back, which is possible only where the original agreement allows it at a set price or where the holder agrees to sell. Because it is charged on revenue and not on profit, it is still owed in a year when the mine loses money.

Stream - Not a percentage of revenue but a claim on the metal itself. An outside party paid cash up front, often to help build the mine, in exchange for the right to receive a set share of the metal produced and to pay only a small fixed fraction of the market price for it - sometimes as little as a tenth or a fifth. The gap between that fixed price and the real price is the cost to the company, and it widens as metal prices rise. Like a royalty, a stream runs for the life of the mine unless bought back, which is possible only under the original terms or by agreement with the holder.

The Story

One paragraph in plain words: what the company is, what it owns, and the central finding. If you read nothing else, read this.

INVESTMENT COMMITTEE SUMMARY (July 31, 2026). West Red Lake Gold is a single-mine gold producer six months into its first year of commercial production. The Madsen mine in Red Lake, Ontario was bought out of a predecessor's insolvency, rebuilt over two deliberate years and declared commercial on January 1, 2026. The operating story through the first half of 2026 is genuinely good and improving quarter on quarter; the cost story is not yet good, and the gap between them is the whole underwriting. First-half production of 14,243 ounces sits at roughly forty percent of the bottom of full-year guidance, and first-quarter all-in sustaining cost of US$4,678 per ounce came in about thirty percent above the TOP of the full-year range. The equity is priced near a fifty-two-week low and the market is nonetheless paying well above what the current single-mine run rate is worth, which means the price already contains the growth pipeline rather than the mine.

Where narrative text carries an older share price, the tables and the refreshed dated close above govern.

Three dates govern this page: the share price is the dated close shown above (2026-07-30); the evidence and estimated values are from this company's last full underwriting (2026-07-31), and change only when the company publishes something - each document's own date is listed under References; a daily event scan watches this company's filings and releases and queues a re-underwriting when one lands.

The Question the Thesis Hinges On

Single greatest company-specific uncertainty identified as single-asset ramp-up risk compounded by a very large dilution overhang: essentially all near-term value depends on Madsen reaching its planned full production run rate in H2 2026, while the fully diluted share count (554.5 million, metric 9) is 34% larger than shares currently issued - meaning even full operational success must be shared across a meaningfully larger future share base than the current one.

INVESTMENT COMMITTEE SUMMARY (July 31, 2026). West Red Lake Gold is a single-mine gold producer six months into its first year of commercial production.
