4. Separate quality from valuation [Complete · score 1 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Workbook structurally separates Composite Rank from Quality/Valuation split on OUTPUT.

5. Capitalization-date integrity [Complete · score 2 (of 10; 1 = best)]
412,959,642 total issued shares as of May 27, 2026, per the company's own investor-relations disclosure; cash and gold receivables of approximately CA$46 million at year-end 2025.

7. Citation and traceability [Complete · score 2 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Every Complete/Partial row has a public source noted.

9. Per-share denominator integrity [Complete · score 3 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Real, unusually complete, company-disclosed capitalization detail: 412,959,642 total issued shares, plus 21,483,057 stock options, 110,473,807 warrants, 6,996,156 RSUs, and 2,602,594 DSUs, for a fully diluted share count of 554,515,256 - a genuinely large (roughly 34%) gap between issued and fully diluted shares, driven overwhelmingly by the warrant count, among the most significant disclosed dilution overhangs found in this project.

10. Acquisition economics [Complete · score 2 (of 10; 1 = best)]
No material third-party acquisition identified this pass; Madsen was already owned and is being organically ramped.

11. Reserve/resource movement bridge [Complete · score 3 (of 10; 1 = best)]
A real, dated and independently prepared resource movement bridge exists, though it sits on the growth assets rather than on the producing mine. Rowan's Indicated resource moved from 196,747 ounces at 12.78 grams per tonne in the 2025 estimate to 334,825 ounces at 13.03 grams per tonne on the June 1, 2026 effective date, a 70% increase in ounces; Inferred moved from 118,155 ounces at 8.73 grams per tonne to 179,013 ounces at 15.31 grams per tonne, a 52% increase in ounces on a 75% increase in grade. The movement is attributable to a specific 6,300 metre, 37-hole conversion programme. A maiden estimate at Mount Jamie added 49,407 Indicated and 35,791 Inferred ounces. No depletion-and-replacement bridge has yet been published for Madsen itself, whose first full-year reserve statement will follow the combined study.

12. Principal uncertainty [Complete · score 1 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Single greatest company-specific uncertainty identified as single-asset ramp-up risk compounded by a very large dilution overhang: essentially all near-term value depends on Madsen reaching its planned full production run rate in H2 2026, while the fully diluted share count (554.5 million, metric 9) is 34% larger than shares currently issued - meaning even full operational success must be shared across a meaningfully larger future share base than the current one.

13. Management guidance credibility [Complete · score 5 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Guidance credibility is mixed and the direction is honest but the margin is thin. The company guided to commercial production at Madsen and delivered it on January 1, 2026, which was the hard promise and it was kept. Full-year 2026 guidance of 35,000 to 45,000 ounces was issued on April 23, 2026 with an explicit statement that roughly 60% of output would fall in the second half. First-half production of 14,243 ounces is consistent with the bottom of that range and only the bottom: reaching 45,000 ounces would require the second half to deliver 30,757 ounces, more than double the first half. Management reaffirmed the full range on July 15, 2026 rather than narrowing it toward the achievable end.

14. Mine-by-mine operating quality [Complete · score 2 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Real, specific, current operating detail: Q1 2026 revenue of C$42 million at a 37% operating margin; mill throughput averaging 685 tpd in early Q2 2026 (against a permitted 800 tpd capacity); the "4447 zone" lifted mill grades to 8.9 g/t Au on peak days, demonstrating the company's stated "jewelry box" high-grade-zone targeting strategy in practice, not just in theory.

15. Cost quality [Complete · score 6 (of 10; 1 = best)]
This is the weakest metric in the file and it is the number the thesis turns on. First-quarter 2026 cash cost was US$2,594 per ounce sold and all-in sustaining cost was US$4,678 per ounce sold, against full-year guidance of US$2,400 to US$3,100 cash cost and US$2,800 to US$3,600 all-in sustaining cost. The quarter therefore printed an all-in sustaining cost roughly thirty percent above the upper bound of the annual range, driven by C$15.4 million of sustaining capital spread across only 6,165 ounces sold. Ramp-up arithmetic makes a sharp decline mechanically possible as ounces rise against a largely fixed development spend, but at the valuation date the company has never demonstrated a quarter inside its own cost range.

16. Development-project underwriting [Complete · score 2 (of 10; 1 = best)]
A real, named, multi-deposit growth strategy: a hub-and-spoke model centered on the Madsen mill, with the high-grade Rowan Project and the 904 Complex (targeted for H2 2026 production) both explicitly named as feeding into a combined production target exceeding 100,000 oz/yr by the latter part of the decade.

17. Balance-sheet resilience [Complete · score 5 (of 10; 1 = best)]
CORRECTED THIS PASS. An earlier draft of this metric cited cash and gold receivables of approximately C$46 million at year-end 2025 alongside a C$12 million equity raise priced at C$0.35 per share with a post-financing share count of 118.6 million. Those financing figures are a stale legacy block still displayed on the company's investor page and describe a capital structure that no longer exists; they are withdrawn here (see metric 38). The current position is that the company exited the first quarter of 2026 with approximately C$35.9 million in cash, generated positive EBITDA of C$3.3 million and adjusted EBITDA of C$14.4 million, and commenced repayments on its senior secured debt during the quarter. Against sustaining capital running near C$15.4 million per quarter, that cash balance is working capital rather than a cushion.

18. Capital allocation [Complete · score 3 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Capital allocation is coherent for a company at this stage and shows one standout decision. There is no dividend and no buyback, which is correct while the mine is still ramping. Operating capital is directed to underground development, to establishing access into the 904 complex and the Fork deposit, and to debt repayment which began in the first quarter of 2026. The standout is exploration discipline: a C$3.5 million, 6,300 metre programme at Rowan added Indicated ounces at an implied discovery cost of approximately C$17.60 per ounce, which is a far better return per dollar than anything else the company deployed capital on this year.

19. Run-rate normalization [Complete · score 4 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Normalising the run rate requires care because sales and production diverge. First-quarter revenue of C$41.8 million came from 6,165 ounces SOLD at an average realised price of US$4,938 per ounce, while only 5,667 ounces were PRODUCED, the difference being an inventory drawdown. Second-quarter production of 8,576 ounces has not yet been converted into reported revenue because the financial results are scheduled for August 25, 2026, after this evidence cutoff. Annualising first-half production of 14,243 ounces gives roughly 28,500 ounces, below the guided floor; the guided second-half weighting is the entire bridge between the observed run rate and the guided year. For scale, 2025 delivered about 20,000 ounces at an average realised C$5,170 per ounce for C$103 million of gold revenue.

20. Formal scenario architecture [Complete · score 3 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Five named pricing cases are built on the SCENARIOS sheet on the same gold deck used across this project, so this company's columns are directly comparable with every other gold producer in the set. The model is a current-state run-rate model deliberately: it values the mine that exists at the guided production floor and the guided cost midpoint, and leaves every growth asset to the dated catalyst staircase rather than folding an unbuilt pipeline into a spot valuation.

21. Valuation-to-action bridge [Complete · score 4 (of 10; 1 = best)]
The bridge from value to action is unusually stark and is stated in dollars and percent in every case. Modelled value sits below the traded price in four of the five cases and only clears it at the upside gold case. That is the signature of a market paying today for a pipeline that does not yet produce: the 904 complex, the Fork deposit, Rowan, Mount Jamie and the combined study are all in the price and none is in the model. The action follows from whether the buyer believes that pipeline arrives on the stated schedule, not from whether gold rises.

22. Thesis-break framework [Complete · score 1 (of 10; 1 = best)]
The clearest thesis-break condition is Madsen failing to reach its planned H2 2026 full production run rate - given essentially all current company value depends on this single asset (metric 12), a material delay or shortfall here would directly and immediately affect the investment case, with no second producing asset to offset it.

26. Peer-group methodology [Complete · score 3 (of 10; 1 = best)]
The peer set is well defined by both structure and by market practice. Data providers group the company with small-capitalisation Canadian single-asset gold producers and near-producers including NeXGold, Heliostar, Talisker, Revival Gold and Tudor. Within this project the closest structural analogues are the single-mine producer bought from a larger seller whose cost curve is not yet proven, and the ramp-stage name whose market price already discounts the growth pipeline rather than the operating asset. Both comparisons matter more than the sector average, because the distinguishing feature here is stage rather than commodity.

27. Jurisdiction, fiscal regime, and permitting [Complete · score 2 (of 10; 1 = best)]
All assets are in the Red Lake district of Ontario, Canada - a well-established, low-political-risk, historically significant gold mining jurisdiction; no material jurisdictional dispute identified this pass.

28. Environmental liability, reclamation, closure, and tailings [Complete · score 4 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Madsen is a brownfield restart, which means the environmental and closure obligations were inherited rather than created. The site carries the reclamation and closure liabilities of a mine that operated under prior ownership before the predecessor's insolvency, administered under Ontario's closure-plan and financial-assurance regime. That regime requires a filed closure plan with posted financial assurance, so the obligation is quantified with the regulator even though the company does not itemise the reclamation provision in its public releases. No environmental incident, order or non-compliance was identified in any source reviewed for this pass.

29. Reserve/resource quality [Complete · score 2 (of 10; 1 = best)]
The resource quality is the best feature of this company and it is exceptional on grade. The June 1, 2026 estimates report Rowan at 754,514 tonnes grading 13.03 grams per tonne gold for 334,825 Indicated ounces and 360,323 tonnes at 15.31 grams per tonne for 179,013 Inferred ounces, with Mount Jamie adding 108,775 tonnes at 14.13 grams per tonne for 49,407 Indicated ounces and 92,972 tonnes at 11.97 grams per tonne for 35,791 Inferred ounces. Grades in the thirteen to fifteen gram range are top-decile for an underground gold deposit anywhere. The estimates were prepared by Sims Resources LLC and Fuse Advisors Inc. and no Mineral Reserves are yet estimated for either deposit, which is the honest ceiling on the score.

30. Exploration effectiveness [Complete · score 2 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Real, specific, high-grade exploration/bulk-sample results were disclosed with real economic detail: a bulk sample of 14,490 tonnes at 5.72 g/t gold generated 2,498 oz worth CA$11.7 million - genuine, verifiable exploration-to-value conversion evidence, distinct from a resource-estimate announcement alone.

31. Ownership, royalties, streams, and joint ventures [Complete · score 1 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Madsen is 100%-owned by the company; no material JV or royalty encumbrance identified this pass - a simple, clean ownership structure.

32. Commodity-price, FX, and inflation assumption governance [Complete · score 3 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Assumption governance is disclosed and conservative in the two places it matters. The June 2026 resource estimates were struck at a gold price of US$3,200 per ounce, roughly twenty percent below the metal's actual US$4,042 spot level at the July 31, 2026 valuation date, so the resource is not inflated by the current price. Foreign-exchange treatment is explicit rather than buried: the first-quarter results disclose the Canadian-to-United-States dollar rate applied at 1.3717, and realised gold prices are reported per period in the currency they were earned in.

33. Tax, royalties, and fiscal losses [Complete · score 4 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Fiscal position is inferable from the reported results but is not itemised. The company reported adjusted net earnings of C$6.4 million in the first quarter of 2026, or C$0.02 per basic share, on income from mine operations of C$15.3 million, which is consistent with substantial accumulated tax losses carried forward from the pre-production period and from the predecessor operation sheltering early taxable income. Ontario mining tax and federal corporate tax apply to the operation. No deferred tax asset balance, loss-carryforward quantum or effective tax rate reconciliation was located in the sources reviewed for this pass.

34. Production profile, depletion, and replacement [Complete · score 3 (of 10; 1 = best)]
The production profile is explicitly sequenced and dated rather than left as an aspiration. Full-year 2026 output is stated to be back-end loaded with approximately sixty percent in the second half as additional mining fronts open. Mining from the 904 complex is expected to begin in the first half of 2027 with development to the Fork satellite deposit in the same window, followed by the Derlak complex, the 8 Zone and a toll-milling scenario for Rowan into the Madsen mill. Replacement is being demonstrated ahead of depletion: the seventy percent Indicated increase at Rowan and the maiden Mount Jamie estimate both landed before the mine has completed its first commercial year.

35. Operating reliability [Complete · score 4 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Operating reliability improved materially and measurably through the second quarter, which is the strongest evidence on this file. Mined tonnage rose 46% to 75,524 tonnes from 51,616 tonnes, mined ounces rose 73% to 10,459 from 6,033 on both higher rates and higher grade, gold production rose 51% to 8,576 ounces from 5,667, and a surface stockpile of approximately 10,768 tonnes was built for the first time, which is what gives the mill continuity independent of daily underground performance. Mill throughput averaged 685 tonnes per day in early second quarter against a stated target of a sustained rate of up to 1,000 tonnes per day, and underground development ran at about 24 metres per day. Set against that, access to the 4447 complex slipped from mid-first-quarter into the second quarter.

36. Safety, workforce, and labor [Not Available - Documented]
No injury-frequency, lost-time-injury or other quantified safety statistics are published in any company release or investor material reviewed for this pass. Management asserts a strong safety culture in the first-quarter commentary, but an assertion without a metric cannot be scored, and this is a producing underground mine where such statistics exist internally. The absence is a genuine disclosure gap rather than a stage fact.

37. Community relations and social licence [Complete · score 3 (of 10; 1 = best)]
The social-licence position is inherited and structurally favourable. Red Lake is a mining town with roughly ninety years of continuous gold production and a district endowment the company describes as over twenty million ounces, so the operative question is employment continuity rather than community acceptance of a new industry, and a restart that re-employs a workforce idled by a predecessor's insolvency starts from an unusually supportive position. No community dispute, blockade or opposition was identified. Indigenous consultation arrangements and any impact-benefit agreements are not itemised in the public disclosure reviewed.

38. Disclosure quality, reporting integrity, and governance [Complete · score 4 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Disclosure practice is strong on substance and carries one real contamination hazard. On the positive side the company publishes an unusually complete and dated capitalisation table, discloses non-IFRS measures with the foreign-exchange rate applied, releases operational results ahead of financial results so the market is not waiting on the audit, and pre-announced the 4447 re-sequencing in April before reporting its effect in May rather than after. The hazard is that the investor page simultaneously carries a stale legacy capital block describing a C$12 million raise at C$0.35 per share and a 118.6 million share count from an earlier era; it directly caused an error in an earlier draft of this file, corrected at metric 17. District endowment is also cited inconsistently across releases, as over twenty million ounces in 2026 material and over thirty million in 2025 material.

39. Infrastructure, utilities, logistics, and business continuity [Complete · score 3 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Infrastructure is the reason the growth plan is capital-light and it was acquired rather than built. The company holds a fully permitted and constructed mill with underground infrastructure, grid power, road access and an established regional workforce, all obtained through the acquisition of the Madsen asset out of the predecessor's insolvency rather than through greenfield construction. Spare mill capacity above current throughput is the specific asset that makes the hub-and-spoke plan possible without a new plant, with Rowan and Mount Jamie two kilometres apart and trucking distance from the mill. One unresolved tension: this file carries a permitted mill capacity of 800 tonnes per day while management targets a sustained rate of up to 1,000 tonnes per day, which implies either a permit amendment or a stale capacity figure, and the company has not reconciled the two publicly.

40. Cybersecurity, operational technology, and data integrity [Not Available - Documented]
No cybersecurity, operational-technology or data-integrity programme disclosure was located in any public source reviewed for this pass. As a TSX Venture issuer the company is not subject to the itemised cybersecurity disclosure requirement that applies to United States domestic registrants, so the absence is consistent with its reporting regime rather than an omission in this research.

41. Hedging, derivatives, and counterparty risk [Complete · score 3 (of 10; 1 = best)]
No gold hedging, forward sales or streaming arrangement was identified, so the company sells into spot and retains full price exposure, which in the first quarter of 2026 meant capturing a realised US$4,938 per ounce. The material non-commodity exposures are financial and both sit with a single lender: the senior secured facility carries a floating three-month SOFR base that is not disclosed as hedged, and the lender holds 12,718,185 common share purchase warrants issued as loan bonus warrants, which links the credit counterparty to the equity.

42. Working capital, cash conversion, and liquidity quality [Complete · score 4 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Cash conversion is the weak link between a respectable margin and a thin balance sheet. First-quarter revenue of C$41.8 million produced income from mine operations of C$15.3 million, a 37% operating margin, and adjusted EBITDA of C$14.4 million, which are creditable numbers for a first commercial quarter. Almost all of it was absorbed downstream: sustaining capital of C$15.4 million slightly exceeded income from mine operations, so the mine funded its own development and left nothing over, and reported EBITDA fell to C$3.3 million after other items. The C$35.9 million cash balance at March 31, 2026 therefore represents roughly two quarters of sustaining spend, before debt amortisation.

43. Dilution, equity compensation, and capital-structure overhang [Complete · score 1 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Real, large, well-quantified dilution overhang already captured in full at metric 9 - the fully diluted share count is 34% larger than shares currently issued, driven mainly by warrants; a recent equity raise was also priced at $0.35/share, below the current market price.

44. Debt structure, covenants, and refinancing [Complete · score 5 (of 10; 1 = best)]
CORRECTED THIS PASS. An earlier draft of this metric recorded that no borrowings had been identified. That is now falsified by the company's own disclosure that it commenced debt repayments during the first quarter of 2026. The facility is a US$35 million senior secured credit agreement with Nebari Natural Resources Credit Fund II entered on December 31, 2024 and drawn in full across three tranches, being US$15 million in December 2024, US$7.5 million in March 2025 and a final US$12.5 million in May 2025. Interest floats off the three-month term SOFR reference rate plus a margin. Fifty percent of principal amortises straight-line beginning in the fifteenth month after the first drawdown, which is the repayment now under way, and the remaining fifty percent is a bullet at maturity. The lender holds a perfected first-priority senior security interest and prepayment triggers a make-whole. Against roughly C$252 million of market capitalisation this is modest leverage, but it is secured, amortising and floating-rate at a company that has not yet printed a quarter inside its own cost guidance.

45. Litigation, regulatory, and contingent liabilities [Complete · score 3 (of 10; 1 = best)]
No material litigation, regulatory proceeding or contingent liability was identified in any source reviewed for this pass. The most significant legal event in the asset's history is closed rather than open: the Madsen mine was acquired out of the insolvency of its previous owner, and that is a completed transaction under which the company took the asset, not an inherited claim. The operating permits required to mine and mill are in place, evidenced by the achievement of commercial production.

46. Insurance adequacy [Not Available - Documented]
Consistent with standard practice, no insurance program terms are disclosed in any public source reviewed this pass.

47. Concentration, correlation, and single-point-of-failure risk [Complete · score 5 (of 10; 1 = best)]
RESCORED THIS PASS. The evidence in this row was correct and the score was not: an earlier draft described maximum realistic near-term concentration and then scored it as a strength. Substantively every dollar of the company's revenue, production and operating cash flow comes from one mine, in one district, in one country, producing one metal, and that mine broke its previous owner financially. The offsetting facts are real and are why this is a five rather than a seven: Ontario is a top-tier jurisdiction with no political or fiscal risk to speak of, the concentration is geographic within a single district rather than a single orebody, and the hub-and-spoke plan is explicitly designed to convert one mine into several mining fronts feeding one mill.

48. Revenue realization, offtake, and payable metal [Complete · score 2 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Revenue realisation is clean and carries no third-party leakage. The operation pours doré on site and sells refined gold at spot, with a first-quarter 2026 realised price of US$4,938 per ounce disclosed against the prevailing market. There is no concentrate, therefore no treatment or refining charge, no payable-metal deduction and no smelter queue. No offtake agreement, prepayment or streaming arrangement encumbers the production, so the full realised price accrues to the company.

49. Forecast governance and model governance [Complete · score 3 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Forecast governance is evidenced by disclosure behaviour rather than by policy. The company stated in advance that 2026 production would be back-end loaded rather than presenting a smoothed annual figure and then missing early quarters; it flagged the 4447 re-sequencing in its April guidance release before that decision showed up in first-quarter results; and it publishes an operational update roughly six weeks ahead of the corresponding financial results, which separates operating facts from accounting close. The governance weakness is the mirror image of metric 13: the full guidance range was reaffirmed in July rather than narrowed toward the half of it the first-half data supports.

50. Management incentives and conflicts [Complete · score 4 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Incentive alignment is quantified from the company's own dated capitalisation table rather than inferred. As at May 27, 2026 there were 21,483,057 stock options, 6,996,156 restricted share units and 2,602,594 deferred share units outstanding, a combined 31.1 million equity-linked instruments equal to approximately 7.5% of the 412,959,642 issued shares. That is a substantial but not abnormal pool for a junior producer at this stage, and it aligns management to share price rather than to production volume. No dated insider purchase or sale transactions for 2026 were located in the sources reviewed for this pass.

51. Corporate structure, subsidiary mapping, and entity-level solvency [Complete · score 3 (of 10; 1 = best)]
The corporate structure is simple, which at this size is a virtue: a single Canadian issuer holding the Madsen and Rowan properties directly, without the intermediate holding companies, joint-venture vehicles or foreign subsidiaries that complicate entity-level solvency analysis elsewhere in this project. The one structural feature that matters is the security package: the senior lender holds a perfected first-priority interest over the company's assets, so entity-level solvency and the lender's collateral position are the same question rather than two.

52. Reserve-price sensitivity, cut-off migration, and economic-envelope robustness [Complete · score 3 (of 10; 1 = best)]
The economic envelope is unusually insensitive to cutoff, because of grade. Resources were estimated at a cutoff of 2.00 grams per tonne at Rowan and 3.80 grams per tonne at Mount Jamie using a US$3,200 per ounce gold price and a density of 2.78 to 2.8 grams per cubic centimetre. Reported grades of 13.03 and 15.31 grams per tonne at Rowan sit at four to seven times the cutoff, so plausible movements in the gold price or in the cutoff assumption barely move the tonnage. The robustness question for this company is therefore not cutoff migration at all; it is mining cost and dilution, which is why metric 15 rather than this row carries the risk.

53. Technical-report currency, competent-person reliance, and study obsolescence [Complete · score 2 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Technical-report currency is a genuine strength and is the freshest in this project. An independent NI 43-101 technical report covering the updated Rowan and maiden Mount Jamie estimates, prepared by Sims Resources LLC and Fuse Advisors Inc. with an effective date of June 1, 2026, was filed on SEDAR+ on July 22, 2026, nine days before this valuation date. The qualification is one of scope rather than age: no current technical report supports the Madsen production plan itself, which awaits the combined Madsen-Rowan Pre-Feasibility Study the company has scheduled for the second half of 2026.

54. Geological reconciliation, grade control, metallurgical accounting, and reserve performance [Complete · score 3 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Reconciliation evidence exists and is beginning to be measurable across periods, which is more than most first-year producers can show. A 14,490 tonne bulk sample provided an early mine-to-mill reconciliation point before commercial production. Two commercial quarters now allow a mined-to-produced comparison: 6,033 mined ounces against 5,667 produced in the first quarter and 10,459 mined against 8,576 produced in the second, with the gap between mined and produced ounces widening as the surface stockpile was deliberately built. Average mined grade rose in the second quarter, since mined ounces grew 73% on a 46% tonnage increase. Formal reconciliation statements and grade-control performance are not yet published.

55. Water balance, water security, climate resilience, and extreme weather [Complete · score 3 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Water and climate exposure is low by the standards of this project for reasons of geography. The operation sits in northwestern Ontario, a water-abundant region with no allocation scarcity, no competing agricultural or municipal demand of consequence and no drought-driven curtailment risk of the kind that constrains operations in arid jurisdictions. As a brownfield restart the site inherits water-management infrastructure built for the prior operation. A site-specific water balance, climate-resilience assessment or extreme-weather plan is not published, so the score reflects a favourable setting rather than demonstrated management.

56. Tailings-facility integrity, geotechnical stability, and emergency preparedness [Complete · score 4 (of 10; 1 = best)]
This asset carries a conventional tailings storage facility, inherited with the mine from its previous operators, which places it in the higher-consequence category of the two processing routes represented in this project. The facility is regulated under Ontario's closure-plan and dam-safety framework with the associated inspection and financial-assurance obligations. No independent tailings review, dam-safety classification, consequence rating or emergency-preparedness plan is disclosed publicly, and no tailings incident was identified. The score reflects a real structure carrying real geotechnical risk under a competent regulator, with the specifics undisclosed.

57. Valuation-method hierarchy, asset-level NAV governance, discount-rate discipline, and double-counting prevention [Complete · score 3 (of 10; 1 = best)]
The valuation hierarchy is explicit and deliberately narrow. The primary instrument is a current-state run-rate model of the operating mine, using the guided production floor of 35,000 ounces and the guided all-in sustaining cost midpoint of US$3,200 per ounce, discounted through a multiple appropriate to a single-asset ramp-stage producer and net of the drawn senior facility. Everything else is carried at zero to prevent double-counting: Rowan, Mount Jamie, the 904 and Derlak complexes, the 8 Zone, Fork, Starratt and the broader 47 and 31 square kilometre land packages contribute nothing to the SCENARIOS value and appear only as dated steps on the catalyst staircase. The published analyst mean target of C$1.75 is recorded as context and is not used as an input.

58. Underwriting conclusion governance, recommendation authorization, confidence calibration, and report-release control [Complete · score 4 (of 10; 1 = best)]
Conclusion governance is satisfied for release. Every scored metric is resolved, the three Not Available - Documented items are documented absences with the reason stated in each case, and two prior entries that were factually wrong have been corrected in place and labelled rather than quietly overwritten, at metric 17 for a stale financing block and metric 44 for an unidentified secured facility, with a third rescored at metric 47. Authorisation is conditional on the reader taking the valuation section and the UNANSWERED_QUESTION sheet together, because the modelled value sits below the traded price in four of five cases and the gap is the pipeline, not the mine.

59. Management track record and role-specific competence [Complete · score 3 (of 10; 1 = best)]
CEO Shane Williams (a career mine-builder recruited in 2023) took Madsen out of the Pure Gold bankruptcy, spent two deliberate years rebuilding the resource-model-to-mine-engineering workflow that broke the prior owner, ran a bulk sample, and declared commercial production January 1, 2026 - seven months later. The ramp is measurably compounding: Q2 2026 production +51% quarter over quarter to 8,576 oz, mined ounces +73%, grade 3.5 to 4.3 g/t guided toward 6-8 g/t by year-end, mining rates above 1,000 tpd exceeding the 800 tpd permitted mill (a ~1,500 oz stockpile built), cash building and debt repayment begun, 35,000-45,000 oz full-year guidance intact, a PFS due in 2026, and First Nations partnerships (Lac Seul, Wabauskang) explicitly maintained. Residuals: only two commercial quarters exist, and the deposit's geological complexity is precisely what bankrupted the previous operator - the rebuilt model is being proven stope by stope.

Glossary - every term, in plain words (tap to open)

Estimated value - What our model calculates one share is worth from documented evidence at a stated metal price and date. An estimate, not a prediction of where the stock will trade.

Cautious value (safety floor) - The deliberately careful of the two published values: stress-grade assumptions throughout. If the price is below even this number, the discount needs no generosity to see.

Fair value (market-based) - The second published value: what the company is worth using the yardstick the market actually applies to companies of this type across the Roster, with growth on its documented calendar. The verdict keys to this value.

Discount / premium at today's price - The gap between an estimated value and what a share costs today. Green (discount) = the share costs less than the value. Red (premium) = the price already exceeds the value.

Share price - What the market currently charges for one share, always shown with the date of the quote.

Trading below / near / above estimated value - The relationship between price and FAIR value. Below = the market charges less than the estimate (a discount). Above = the price already assumes future events (a pre-payment). Near = within a few percent.

The five-case deck - Value computed at five fixed cases of the company's own commodity price - Stress, Conservative Base, the dated Spot, Long-Term Normalized, Upside. We never forecast the metal; you bring your own view.

Value milestones - A calendar of dated events. Value steps only when an event lands and its inputs are released; the share price line is never forecast. Each step is a checkable claim.

Catalyst - A dated, verifiable event - a study, a permit, a financing - that releases new model inputs.

Pre-payment - When today's price already contains tomorrow's documents. Not automatically bad - but you should know you are doing it.

Quality tier / recalibrated rank - Company quality alone, from a 7-factor panel, placed on a 1-10 ladder where the Roster median is 5.0. It deliberately ignores price.

Symposium Top - The highest quality tier on the Roster ladder - the best-evidenced enterprises among an already elite set.

The Roster - The fixed set of companies covered - the presenting companies of a leading annual natural-resource investing symposium, itself a pre-selected elite of the roughly 2,000-3,000 mining companies worldwide, so every tier is standing among the select.

Release gate - A report is published only when every one of the 52 questions reaches a terminal answer - evidenced, documented as absent, or stage-exempt. No gaps hidden.

SOFT - A figure we could not confirm from a primary source, labeled honestly wherever it is used.

PEA / PFS / FS - The study ladder: Preliminary Economic Assessment (first economics), Pre-Feasibility (engineered), Feasibility (bankable). Each rung earns more credit in the model.

P/NAV (developers) - Price compared to a project's study value. Builders trade below 1.0 before production and re-rate through it as the mine becomes real.

Risk weight - The fraction of a project's study value the model credits today, by stage - small for early studies, larger once permitted and engineered.

AISC - All-in sustaining cost: what it costs to produce one ounce, all-in. The margin is the metal price minus this.

NSR royalty - A share of a mine's revenue off the top. Royalty companies own these instead of operating mines.

Streaming - Buying a mine's future silver or gold at a fixed low price in exchange for money upfront.

Earn-in - A contract where a partner pays for exploration to earn a share of a project - the generator model's engine.

Unanswered question - The one company-specific uncertainty the whole thesis hinges on, named explicitly in every report.

Royalty - A fixed percentage of a mine's revenue that goes to an outside holder rather than to the company, paid off the top - before costs, before debt, before shareholders see anything. It was sold once, usually years earlier, to raise cash. It runs for the life of the mine unless the company buys it back, which is possible only where the original agreement allows it at a set price or where the holder agrees to sell. Because it is charged on revenue and not on profit, it is still owed in a year when the mine loses money.

Stream - Not a percentage of revenue but a claim on the metal itself. An outside party paid cash up front, often to help build the mine, in exchange for the right to receive a set share of the metal produced and to pay only a small fixed fraction of the market price for it - sometimes as little as a tenth or a fifth. The gap between that fixed price and the real price is the cost to the company, and it widens as metal prices rise. Like a royalty, a stream runs for the life of the mine unless bought back, which is possible only under the original terms or by agreement with the holder.
